title: Global seamount detection using machine learning
abstract: Volcanic in origin, seamounts are widely scattered throughout the world’s ocean basins. Research ships with single beam and multibeam echo-sounders have discovered many small seamounts and some large ones while satellite altimetry has found many large seamounts and some small ones. The exact number of seamounts in the world’s ocean basins is, however, unknown. Here we use machine learning in an attempt to locate all seamounts, to estimate their height, area and volume, and to speculate on their origin. In this study, the fillet fatty acid compositions of wild-caught gilthead sea bream and specimens produced under cage-reared and pond-reared aquaculture regimes in Northeast Atlantic waters were evaluated to (i) assess nutritional quality using lipid quality indices and (ii) test the traceability discrimination potential of fatty acids using machine-learning classification (Random Forest) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis. title: Ram.exe Has Entered the Chat: Synthetic Gods and the Rise of AI-Deity Agitprop in India
abstract: Abstract This article examines ‘theogonetic agitprop’: the use of divine avatars in India generated by artificial intelligence ( AI ) to fuse devotional affect with Hindutva political communication. Focusing on deepfake Ram and Ram Lalla videos, Krishna-style chatbots, violent goddess memes, and related social media reactions, it shows that generative tools make sacred figures programmable, iterable, and persuasive across WhatsApp, X (formerly Twitter), Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, and Telegram. title: El derecho de autor en obras generadas con inteligencia artificial: análisis de la jurisprudencia china
abstract: The expansion of artificial intelligence has posed new challenges for copyright law, particularly regarding the protection of content produced through such systems. This article examines Chinese case law on works generated with artificial intelligence based on six cases concerning images and documents created using technological tools. To address this issue, it develops a theoretical framework on originality and the degree of human intervention required in AI-assisted generation processes. abstract: ABSTRACT Developing methods to reliably recognize depositional processes and environments in unconsolidated materials is of broad interest to various Earth science fields, archaeology, engineering and life‐sciences. Recent decades have seen renewed interest in using grain‐size characteristics to reconstruct past depositional environments, driven by increased computing power and advanced analytical techniques like machine learning and artificial intelligence. title: Inteligencia sin comprensión. Magnifica Humanitas: de las dos ausencias de la máquina y la custodia de la persona
abstract: This article examines the central claim of the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas (2026), namely that artificial intelligence is fundamentally different from human intelligence and that, therefore, the human person requires special protection. Drawing on epistemology, philosophy of mind, and Kantian thought, the author argues that contemporary AI systems are marked by two fundamental limitations: they lack understanding and experience. title: Exploring Research Landscape of Global Green Finance via Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: The growing urgency of climate change and sustainable development has positioned green finance as a central mechanism for channeling capital toward low-carbon transitions and environmental protection. While research in this area has expanded rapidly, it remains unevenly distributed across regions, with a strong concentration in advanced economies and limited systematic evidence from emerging and climate-vulnerable regions such as Southeast Asia (SEA). title: A Review of Reverse Electrodialysis Process Simulation Approaches Applied to Concentrated Brines
abstract: Reverse electrodialysis (RED) is an emerging process intensification technology for sustainable energy generation from the salinity gradient between concentrated brines and dilute streams. Concentrated brines, generated in large volumes by seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) desalination, mining operations, and saltworks, represent an abundant and underutilised resource whose energetic valorisation via RED can simultaneously reduce brine disposal impacts and contribute to decarbonising the water-energy nexus. title: Image-Based Visual Identification of Coral Health Signs Using UPT and ROI-Based ImageJ Annotation in a Thermal-Discharge Coastal System
abstract: Image-based visual assessment provides a practical approach for documenting coral health signs in coastal systems where laboratory diagnosis is not available. This study applied a quadrat-based Underwater Photo Transect (UPT) method combined with Regions of Interest (ROI)-based ImageJ annotation to identify visually observable coral health signs, rather than laboratory-confirmed coral diseases, in the thermal-discharge coastal waters surrounding the Paiton Power Plant (PLTU Paiton), East Java, Indonesia. title: Sub-kilometer current divergence and vertical velocities in the macrotidal Iroise Sea from airborne radar interferometry and models
abstract: Fine-scale ocean dynamics strongly influence coastal mixing, sediment transport, and vertical exchange, yet remain difficult to observe at the spatial scales at which they occur. Here, we use total surface current vectors measured by the airborne Ocean Surface Current Airborne Radar (OSCAR) to investigate sub-kilometer divergence, vorticity, shear rate, and vertical velocities in the tidally dominated Iroise Sea around Ushant Island. title: Quantifying coastal ocean anthropogenic carbon changes and their uncertainties
abstract: Abstract Despite recent progress in quantifying anthropogenic carbon (C anth ) in global oceans, coastal regions remain understudied due to methodological and observational challenges. Here, we develop and generalize a Regional rEgression–based Coastal Anthropogenic carbon estimation algorithm (RECA) designed specifically for coastal environments. title: Rabbit production research in Southeast Asia: a bibliometric and systematic mapping review
abstract: Rabbit production remains relatively small, but has significant potential as a sustainable livestock in Southeast Asia. Despite a growing body of literature on it, there has been a lack of comprehensive analysis to synthesize these studies within the regional context. This study, therefore, addressed that gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis and a systematic mapping of rabbit production research in Southeast Asia using a specific search string. Results of the bibliometric analysis revealed 125 articles published between 1990 and mid-2025. Publication output showed a compound annual growth

title: PISA 2025 en Chile: más allá de los puntajes, el desafío de recuperar el aprendizaje profundo
abstract: The PISA 2025 results, released by the OECD in September 2026, place Chile below the OECD average in Science, Mathematics and Reading, with declines of 9 and 12 points in Mathematics and Reading respectively between 2022 and 2025. Some 59% of Chilean students fall below Level 2 in Mathematics, compared with 35% across the OECD. The article examines a central finding of the report: the rise of hasty reading and the sharper deterioration in tasks involving long texts and higher-order comprehension processes, which also affects mathematical problem solving. title: Laser-Induced Fluorescence Hyperspectral Imaging for Classification of Coastal Macroalgae, Eelgrass, and Mussels
abstract: This study explores the application of fluorescence hyperspectral imaging (FHSI) for marine ecosystem monitoring, combining laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) with hyperspectral imaging (HSI), an approach rarely applied in marine ecology. Photopigments such as chlorophylls, carotenoids, and phycobiliproteins emit distinct fluorescence signals when excited at specific wavelengths. title: Characterization and Forecasting of Future Drought in the Gambia River Basin at Kédougou Using Standardized Indices, Machine Learning, and Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Background: Drought is one of the most complex and damaging hydroclimatic hazards, particularly in West Africa where water resources are highly sensitive to climate variability and change. This study analyzes the future evolution of meteorological, climatic, and hydrological droughts in the Gambia River basin controlled at the Kédougou gauging station in southeastern Senegal. Methods: The approach combines precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, temperature, and simulated streamflow, and computes the SPI, SPEI, and SSI at 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month timescales. title: Improving reliability in rural microgrids through AI-powered predictive maintenance: A critical review of technology and community readiness
abstract: Reliable energy access remains a significant concern in rural Southeast Asia, particularly in off-grid communities marked by insufficient infrastructure, challenging geographic conditions, and limited technical expertise. Although renewable-energy microgrids, such as solar, biomass, hybrid photovoltaic-battery systems, and small hydropower, are increasingly deployed to reduce electrification gaps, inadequate maintenance strategies threaten the long-term reliability and sustainability of these systems. title: From ice hazards to system failures: analysis and prevention of catastrophic icebreaker escort accidents on the Northern Sea Route
abstract: The study examines catastrophic safety incidents in icebreaker escort operations on the Northern Sea Route (NSR). It develops strategies to prevent future accidents by analysing the Baikal–Vladivostok accident in the Yenisey Gulf of the Kara Sea in 2024 as a case study using the Swiss Cheese Model (SCM). The SCM-based analysis organised the documented factors associated with the Baikal–Vladivostok accident into multiple safety layers, including escort planning, safe-distance management, communication, operational coordination, and environmental conditions. title: Vibrio alginolyticus: an emerging marine pathogen at the intersection of aquaculture, public health, and antimicrobial resistance
abstract: Vibrio alginolyticus is a halophilic, Gram-negative marine bacterium that has emerged as a significant opportunistic pathogen affecting both marine animals and humans. As one of the most abundant vibrios in coastal and estuarine environments worldwide, V. alginolyticus causes substantial economic losses in aquaculture through vibriosis in fish, shrimp, and shellfish, while also being responsible for wound infections, otitis externa, and occasionally gastroenteritis in humans following seawater exposure or seafood consumption. title: Detection of Marine Litter on Arctic Beaches Based on Aerial Photography Using the YOLOv8s CNN
abstract: Marine litter beach accumulation is a pressing issue not only for urban coastal areas but also for remote and uninhabited regions such as the Arctic. Existing manual litter collection and identification methods remain labor-intensive. An assessment of the volume and composition of marine litter was conducted for the Russian Arctic coastlines using high-resolution airphotos. title: A Developed VMD-DMD Algorithm with Machine Learning Models for Improving Sea Level Predictions: A Case Study of the Mediterranean Coastlines
abstract: Accurate prediction of sea level change in the Mediterranean Sea is essential for coastal risk management; however, the nonstationary behavior of sea level makes this difficult. This study presents a hybrid framework that integrates variational mode decomposition (VMD) and dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) with long short-term memory (LSTM) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) to forecast monthly sea level anomaly (SLA). title: Interpretable machine learning for predicting cumulative plastic strain of marine soils under multi-factor coupling effects
abstract: Accurate prediction of cumulative plastic strain (CPS) is essential for assessing the deformation stability of marine strata subjected to artificial ground freezing (AGF). This study aims to clarify how variations in clay content and pore-water salinity regulate cyclic responses after freeze–thaw (FT) disturbance. Cyclic triaxial tests were conducted to investigate CPS under coupled effects of clay content, salinity, FT disturbance, and cyclic stress ratio (CSR). abstract: The port and logistics electromechanical industry underpins port production and supply chain operation, and its level of intelligentization is directly related to the improvement of operational efficiency and industrial capacity. title: Ocean acoustic field prediction method based on dual-branch physics-informed neural network under insufficient environmental parameters
abstract: Accurate computation of the ocean acoustic pressure field is crucial for underwater acoustic applications. Traditional numerical models depend on comprehensive environmental priors, such as full-depth sound speed profiles (SSPs) and bottom geoacoustic parameters. To address challenges posed by uncertain bottom geoacoustic parameters and depth-truncated SSPs, this study presents a Dual-Branch Physics-Informed Neural Network (DB-PINN) to predict the acoustic pressure field while simultaneously reconstructing the full-depth SSP. title: Data scarcity to strategic insight: monitoring global SDG progress using big earth data and AI
abstract: Evidence-informed sustainable development goals (SDGs) remain constrained by incomplete, geographically uneven and temporally sparse reporting. This study implements a systematic approach using 20 peer-reviewed Big Earth Data and artificial intelligence (AI)-derived datasets to address monitoring gaps across seven SDGs. By integrating multi-source geospatial datasets, AI-based methods, and established validation procedures, we assess regional imbalance and temporal patterns of SDG progress at the global scale. title: CHEMICAL APPROACHES TO MONITORING AND EVALUATING THE BIOREMEDIATION OF OIL CONTAMINATED DESERT SOILS: A REVIEW OF MODERN METHODS
abstract: Oil spills in deserts and other arid regions, including Kuwait, the Arava Valley in Israel, and Western Kazakhstan, have created extensive areas of chronically contaminated soil whose remediation is constrained by low moisture, nutrient deficiency, salinity, temperature fluctuations, and the ageing of petroleum residues. abstract: Rip currents pose significant threats to coastal safety and to autonomous marine vehicles operating nearshore. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework that combines a novel architecture and compression methodology. abstract: Stable isotopes are non-radioactive variants of the same element whose small mass differences produce predictable effects in chemical and biological systems. While medicine has mainly used the administration of enriched stable isotopes as tracers of physiological function, the natural sciences developed stable-isotope ratios into robust measures of source, transformation, and underlying mechanism across Earth and life history. abstract: Abstract The Pitzer model is widely used in process models for determining the thermodynamic properties of concentrated aqueous electrolytes. The main drawback is the need for experimentally determined parameters for each ion pair in the system. The estimation of unknown Pitzer parameters of electrolytes is thus an attractive prospect. This paper investigates machine learning-based models for the task of predicting the Pitzer parameters of binary electrolytes based on the properties of the constituent ions. abstract: BACKGROUND: The ocean is opaque to electromagnetic radiation, so underwater situational awareness over large areas remains a predominantly acoustic problem. Conventional underwater situational awareness means—active sonar, passive listening systems, and optical systems—offer either high resolution at short range or long range at low resolution. title: A practical approach to underwater depth and surface normals estimation
abstract: Monocular Depth and Surface Normals Estimation (MDSNE) is crucial for tasks such as three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction, autonomous navigation, and underwater exploration. Current methods rely either on discriminative models, which struggle with transparent or reflective surfaces, or generative models, which, while accurate, are computationally expensive. abstract: Living Research: Understanding Experience to Transform Reality introduces an original methodological and interpretive framework within contemporary qualitative research that integrates phenomenology and action research. The work posits that scientific inquiry is not complete merely by understanding a phenomenon, but when the constructed knowledge returns to its context to enable transformative and reflective action. abstract: In March 2026, the Wakashio-maru, a new training vessel for the National Institute of Technology, Toyama College, was completed. Operating primarily in Toyama Bay, which features deep-sea areas exceeding 1,000 metres, the vessel continues a tradition of marine surveys and observation activities carried out for many years by its predecessor. title: A Prompt Elastogravity Signal–Based Rapid Source Characterization Module for Tsunami Warning Support in Alaska
abstract: Abstract State-of-the-art earthquake early warning systems relying on seismic waves tend to underestimate the magnitude of large earthquakes, which typically results in dramatic underestimation of tsunami forecasts. Systems relying on other types of data (W phase, Global Navigation Satellite System) may provide more reliable magnitude estimates for very large seismic events but at the cost of slower warning. title: Seeing what students learn: assessing cognitive representations and academic outcomes via EEG image reconstruction
abstract: Abstract Understanding how humans process visual information during learning remains a central challenge in cognitive neuroscience. Traditional approaches typically rely on behavioral observations or indirect neural measures, which limits direct insight into learners’ internal cognitive representations. Recent advances in brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) and deep learning have enabled image reconstruction from electroencephalography (EEG), providing a promising pathway to decode latent cognitive states. title: Quantitative ultrasonic inversion of coating bond strength based on a physics-informed neural network
abstract: Abstract The nondestructive quantitative evaluation of the bond strength of metal coatings on marine equipment is crucial for ensuring their safe service. However, due to the inherent high acoustic attenuation of metal coatings and the limited number of destructive pull-off test samples, traditional ultrasonic techniques and purely data-driven deep learning models find it difficult to balance physical interpretability and high-fidelity prediction. title: Development of Artificial Intelligence Based Model to Predict Crop Yields of Biofertilizers
abstract: The research paper proposes the development and the analysis of an artificial intelligence model that can be used for predicting the crop yield under various biofertilizer treatment, types of soils and environmental conditions. The problem statement is the necessity of the prediction of the efficiency of biofertilizers taking into account the interaction of microbial strains, soil properties, inoculation rate, nutrients, crops, and climatic zones. title: Review of Applications, Technologies and Future Trends of Maritime UAV Systems for Smart Ocean Operations
abstract: Maritime unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly transforming ocean, coastal, port, and offshore operations through rapid sensing, intelligent communication, autonomous perception, and cooperative decision support. This trend-oriented review analyses 471 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and March 2026, supported by selected foundational pre-2020 studies, to examine the evolution, technological structure, methodological maturity, and deployment readiness of maritime UAV systems. title: A LITERATURE REVIEW OF RADIAL BASIS FUNCTION NEURAL NETWORKS FOR BLAST EXPLOSIVE PREDICTION
abstract: This review paper examines the development and application of Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (RBFNN) for predicting blast explosive effects. Addressing the complexities of nonlinear and multi-physics blast phenomena, it highlights the advantages of data-driven approaches over traditional analytical methods. The paper presents the fundamentals of RBF networks, including their architecture, training techniques, and optimization strategies, emphasizing their capacity for universal function approximation and adaptability. title: Bouncing Forward: A Company’s Three-Phase Playbook For True Resilience
abstract: Is your organisation’s approach to disruption one of ‘bounce back’ or ‘bounce forward’? When faced with an external disruption, most organisations try to absorb it and rebound to their previous state. While this ‘bounce back’ is an effective strategy for managing short-term disruptions, is there a better approach for responding to long-term disruptions such as rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI) or climate change? title: Stress corrosion cracking of 316 L stainless steel in simulated Arabian gulf seawater
abstract: Abstract Austenitic stainless steels are widely used in coastal and marine infrastructure for its corrosion resistance, yet failures associated with chloride-induced stress corrosion cracking (SCC) continue to be reported. In this work, the SCC susceptibility of 316L austenitic stainless steel was investigated using test solutions designed to simulate Arabian gulf seawater and compared with a reference standard brine. title: AI-Enabled Climate–Water Governance Linking Aquaculture and Irrigation in The Mekong Delta, Vietnam
abstract: The paper investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance integrated water governance and climate resilience in water-dependent production systems, specifically focusing on aquaculture and irrigation in the Mekong Delta, Vietnam. It addresses a gap in existing literature by integrating technical applications of AI with institutional analyses of water management and climate adaptation. abstract: Schizophrenia is a chronic and severe psychiatric disorder affecting nearly 1% of the global population, characterized by positive symptoms such as hallucinations and delusions, negative symptoms including avolition and affective flattening, and cognitive impairments that compromise social and occupational functioning. title: Toward interoperable bathymetric data in ocean observing systems: integrating hydrographic standards and FAIR data practices
abstract: Bathymetric data are a fundamental component of ocean observing systems, supporting applications in ocean modelling, coastal hazard assessment, marine spatial planning, and navigational safety. However, these datasets remain highly fragmented due to the diversity of acquisition platforms, including hydrographic surveys, autonomous vehicles, satellite-derived bathymetry, and legacy chart products, which often differ in spatial reference systems, vertical datums, resolution scales, and metadata quality. abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater continues to be managed predominantly as an abiotic resource for human use, a paradigm that overlooks the biological communities responsible for many indispensable ecosystem services and ultimately the integrity of the global water cycle. A shift towards a holistic ecological perspective is therefore essential but requires innovative techniques to monitor a challenging environment. abstract: Coral reefs support marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of coastal communities, yet their condition in Indonesia, including Bali, continues to decline due to coral bleaching. Bleaching monitoring still relies largely on manual surveys that are time-consuming, costly, and require trained experts. This study develops a YOLOv10-based object detection model with transfer learning to automatically detect and localize bleached areas in underwater images. abstract: This article proposes a reinterpretation of contemporary Spanish science fiction through the lens of postsecularity, understood not as a return of religion but as its functional redistribution within technoscientific dispositifs. Against dominant readings that frame the genre as inherently secularizing, it argues that works such as Jorge Carrión’s Membrana and Elia Barceló’s El efecto Frankenstein reconfigure traditionally religious functions—memory, creation, and identity—within narrative structures mediated by technology. title: Comparative evaluation of cycle-based and time history-based intelligent models for predicting the cyclic responses of liquefiable sand: Strengths, limitations, and prospects for advancement
abstract: In this study, an attempt is made to develop deep learning (DL) models using only cyclic laboratory test databases of Ottawa F65 sand to showcase its potential for predicting the cyclic response of soils. Two types of DL-based modelling strategies are proposed herein: (i) cycle-based models and (ii) time history-based models. title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for sustainable development and policy integration in the shipping industry
abstract: Shipping is a critical industry for global trade but is associated with environmental externalities like air, underwater noise, and light pollution. Transitioning to a sustainable future requires optimizing propulsion systems, which currently suffer from fossil fuel reliance and energy losses. This research develops an AI-assisted evidence-synthesis framework to examine sustainable shipping and propulsion technologies and support a policy framework for a sustainable maritime agenda. abstract: Background Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is amongst the commonest complications of pregnancy and an early marker of lifetime cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) risk. abstract: Smart nanocomposite packaging has emerged as a promising approach for enhancing food preservation by improving barrier performance, enabling active functionality, and supporting intelligent quality monitoring. title: Deep Learning-Based Monitoring of Tension and Fatigue in a Hybrid Mooring System of a Floating Offshore Wind Turbine
abstract: Mooring integrity monitoring of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) is constrained by the cost and limited reliability of subsea tension sensors. abstract: Abstract Decoupling strain magnitude and arbitrary orientation is a persistent challenge for wearable strain sensors, as conventional layered architectures and monolithic anisotropic networks suffer from issues of interfacial stress concentrations and irreversible signal drift under complex deformations. Inspired by the mechanogating mechanism of tactile sensory cells, we present a fluidic strain sensor with an orthogonal cross-shaped microchannel network and drum-shaped microstructures. abstract: Comprehending bioconvection facilitates the modelling of natural processes in aquatic environments and improves the efficacy of systems incorporating microorganism suspensions. It connects biology with fluid dynamics, providing insights into the impact of living creatures on fluid flow behaviour. The current study offers insights into the mechanisms of heat, microorganism and mass transfer in complex fluids, with potential applications in biomedical devices, chemical engineering and industrial processes involving non-Newtonian fluids under the influence of electromagnetic and thermal effects.

abstract: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remains a significant challenge in reproductive medicine, imposing substantial emotional, clinical, and financial burden on affected couples. RIF is generally defined as failure to achieve pregnancy after multiple transfers of good-quality embryos, yet progress in the field has been constrained by the absence of a universally accepted definition and by the inherent complexity of investigating the embryo–endometrial interface. abstract: Monitoring marine turbocharger condition under real-ship operation is complicated by operating-condition variability and limited labelled maintenance data. This study assesses whether mean-centred angle-domain rotational-speed fluctuations can discriminate between six recordings acquired before and after one turbocharger cleaning event. abstract: Holocene relative sea-level (RSL) reconstructions from far-field regions constrain past ice volume and global mean sea-level change, yet records from the South China Sea remain debated, particularly regarding the existence of a mid-Holocene highstand. Here, we present a revised RSL history for the Pearl River Delta based on six new radiocarbon-dated index points from an ancient Saccostrea cuccullata oyster reef, integrated into an updated, quality-controlled database of 292 data points. abstract: This study explores the polyphonic diversity of technopoetry and sound poetry, tracing their evolution within the expanded field of contemporary art. The 20th century was notably characterized by avant-garde movements—such as Dadaism, Surrealism, Russian Constructivism, Situationism, and Futurism—that influenced the poetic techno-scene. title: Quantifying Land–Sea Connectivity Through Remotely Sensed River Plumes
abstract: Abstract Coastal ecosystems are highly influenced by riverine freshwater inputs, but the nature of these influences is dynamic and hard to characterize. Here we present a method that leverages remote sensing data of river plumes to quantify land–sea connectivity. The method uses least‐cost routing across image‐derived cost surfaces, where connected paths have a directional water quality gradient characteristic of a fluvial plume. abstract: Understanding ecosystem recovery following flood events is critical for sustainable floodplain management, yet causal evidence linking flooding to vegetation recovery remains limited. This study investigated the causal impact of the 2022 flood on ecosystem recovery in the Chi River Basin, Thailand, using 232,172 spatial points with multi-temporal VCI data (2020–2024). We employed Propensity Score Matching (PSM) to control for confounding factors and Difference-in-Differences (DiD) to estimate the causal effect. title: Inter-strain diversity among coastal picocyanobacteria across salinity gradients
abstract: Strains of the picocyanobacteria genera Synechococcus and Cyanobium occur in cold-temperate zones, from coastal waters to the open ocean, spanning a range of salinities and water depths. To thrive across different salinities, picocyanobacteria strains acclimate internal turgor by expending metabolic energy to accumulate compatible solutes and extrude inorganic ions. We grew five picocyanobacterial strains, derived from a range of source habitat salinities, under a matrix of light and salinity levels. abstract: Abstract SST reconstruction from glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers (GDGT) preserved in marine sediments is an important tool in quantitative paleoclimatology. These reconstructions require calibration frameworks that provide mapping between sediment GDGT data and temperature values. Improvements in modeling and data coverage can reduce bias in existing calibrations, such as those based on the univariate TEX 86 index and other multivariate frameworks. abstract: In this article, we set out what we suggest are three key challenges for critical studies on men, masculinities and organizations in the context of the polycrisis. abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction offers a direct approach to utilizing biomass resources and converting them into biofuel by using water, which acts as a reactant, solvent and catalyst under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions. Hydrothermal liquefaction has been extensively studied to comprehend its mechanisms and kinetics across various batch operation scales. title: The Plant‐Microbe Alliance for Environmental Restoration: From Nature‐Inspired Solutions to Engineered Ecological Recovery
abstract: According to the United Nations, up to 40% of the world's terrestrial ecosystems are degraded and in need of ecological restoration. Here, we argue that ecosystem restoration requires not only the reintroduction of plant species but also the recovery of the biological interactions that sustain ecosystem functioning. Plants and their associated microbiomes form integrated functional units in which microorganisms contribute to nutrient cycling, stress tolerance, contaminant degradation and ecosystem resilience. abstract: [Purpose] This article analyzes the institutional barriers constraining the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain in Ecuador's notarial system, understood as components of the digital transformation of public services dependent on telecommunications infrastructure. It aims to identify and characterize such barriers, assess their comparative severity against the Brazilian case, and formulate analytical propositions on the viability conditions for notarial digital transformation. abstract: Accurate stratigraphic characterization is essential for offshore geotechnical engineering, where nearshore marine sediments commonly exhibit strong spatial variability and complex stratigraphic transitions. abstract: Nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions from marine diesel engines remain a major environmental concern in the maritime industry, requiring effective monitoring strategies under actual operating conditions. This study proposes a Random Forest-based approach for detecting anomalous operating conditions associated with NOx emissions using operational data collected from an actual merchant vessel during an 11-day voyage. abstract: Rapid urbanization in environmentally sensitive zones has intensified pressures on air, water, and soil systems, while regulatory agencies struggle to achieve timely detection of emerging risks and consistent compliance monitoring. This study proposes an Integrated Predictive and RemoteSensing Framework designed to support early warning, risk anticipation, and regulatory compliance in complex urban environments. abstract: Background Superficial fungal infections present a growing threat to global public health. Traditional diagnostic techniques, including microscopy and culture, are time-consuming and subjective, often limiting diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic tools offer a promising adjunct to improve efficiency and standardization of microscopic fungal detection. abstract: Underwater acoustic signals (UAS) in marine environments are often contaminated by noise from biological activity, ocean waves, and equipment. abstract: Introduction Carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (CP-KP) represents a major public health threat. The global dissemination of antimicrobial resistance is largely driven by high-risk clones (HRCs), such as ST307/OXA-48, ST11/OXA-48 and ST512/KPC-3, which currently dominate the epidemiology of CP-KP in Spain. abstract: Rapid and accurate prediction of radial power distribution is crucial for the design and operation of space nuclear reactors. However, traditional Monte Carlo methods incur prohibitively high computational costs, while conventional data-driven surrogate models face severe overfitting and insufficient generalization capabilities under small-sample and data distribution shift conditions. abstract: Abstract This present study introduces a cloud-based geospatial and machine learning framework for assessing coastal urban heat island (UHI) dynamics in Thoothukudi coastal region, Southern India, using 12 seasonal Landsat composites (2010–2025) processed through Google Earth Engine (GEE). abstract: Carbonate reservoirs are extremely heterogeneous owing to fractures, vugs, micropores, and karst features. abstract: Abstract Marine ecosystems are increasingly shaped by the combined effects of multiple environmental and anthropogenic stressors, generating non-linear, spatially heterogeneous patterns of risks to ecosystem functioning. abstract: Communal cattle farming in Sub-Saharan Africa continues to face destabilization from non-linear climate variability, yet insurance penetration remains negligible. abstract: Abstract The international community has committed to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, and satellite monitoring can now detect industrial fishing inside marine protected areas (MPAs) at near-global scale. abstract: Salt marshes are crucial coastal ecosystems that support biodiversity and provide a range of ecosystem services, including nutrient retention, shoreline erosion protection, and carbon storage, through the processes they maintain. abstract: This study aims to determine university students’ levels of artificial intelligence (AI) literacy and to examine the patterns of variation of this competence across individual and educational variables. abstract: The segmentation of spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) images for diabetic macular edema (DME) using deep learning technology has key challenges such as data privacy, computational cost, and information uncertainty. abstract: Drought is a natural disaster with serious impacts on agriculture, water resources management and ecosystem balance. Ongoing global warming and climate change exacerbate drought cases. abstract: As the global demand for sustainable energy grows, the importance of solar energy as a clean and inexhaustible source of energy has become increasingly prominent. However, the efficiency and yield of solar power generation are directly affected by the solar radiation intensity, so accurate prediction of solar radiation is crucial to improve the performance of solar power generation systems. abstract: The North Sea is among the largest and most productive shallow marine ecosystems, heavily influenced by historical and ongoing exploitation. Monitoring of North Sea biodiversity is vital for a better understanding of ecosystem responses to ongoing anthropogenic pressures and for informing effective management and conservation strategies. abstract: Reliable prediction of chloride convection-zone depth is important for service-life assessment of tidal-zone concrete, but most data-driven chloride studies focus on surface concentration or diffusion-related indicators. abstract: Global assessments project widespread coral reef degradation under continued ocean warming and acidification, underscoring the urgent need to identify and account for the full diversity of coral reef systems within conservation planning. abstract: Abstract This study presents a simulation-driven deep learning framework for vibration-based damage detection and localization in composite structures using mode shape images. abstract: This paper presents a virtual boundary integral neural network (VBINN) for three-dimensional exterior acoustic problems. title: Application of intelligent correction in ocean numerical forecasting based on spatiotemporal convolutional network (STCN)
abstract: Abstract Marine numerical forecasting is susceptible to complex spatiotemporal systematic errors, particularly during extreme weather events, such as typhoons, which majorly impede its efficacy in disaster prevention and mitigation. To address this challenge, the present study proposes an intelligent correction model based on a spatiotemporal convolutional network. title: Microplastic contamination in edible invertebrate from seafood markets along the Egyptian Red Sea and Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Marine environments contain plastic debris that potentially elicits adverse effects in aquatic organisms. In Egypt, microplastic pollution has been recognized as a significant issue; however, risks associated with human consumption have not been fully elucidated. Here, we evaluated the frequency of occurrence, abundance, and distribution of microplastics (MPs) in edible marine invertebrates (mussel, shrimp, and crab) sold at markets along the Mediterranean and Red Sea coasts of Egypt. title: Probabilistic corrosion prediction of marine steel under future climate change scenarios using physics-informed Gaussian process regression
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a framework of corrosion prediction by utilizing physics-informed Gaussian process regression (PI-GPR) and future climate change simulation. Long-term corrosion prediction of marine steel structures is routinely based on stationary environmental assumptions; however, future sea surface temperature (SST) changes should be taken into account as it may affect corrosion degradation over structural service life. institutions: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

title: Exploring pre-service teachers’ STEM readiness in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand: Comparative insights from teacher education programs
abstract: STEM education has become a central agenda for enhancing human resource quality and global competitiveness. This study explored pre-service teachers’ readiness to implement STEM teaching in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, with particular attention to their conceptual understanding, implementation ability and experience, perceived barriers and institutional support, and attitudes toward STEM education. title: Ecological recovery, maintenance-dependent protection: a synthesis of three nature-based solutions for coastal resilience in New Jersey
abstract: Hurricane Sandy in 2012 led to an extensive deployment of coastal nature-based solutions (NbS) in New Jersey, providing a unique opportunity to evaluate their physical and ecological performance under multi-year monitoring programs. This study presents a comparative synthesis of documented outcomes across three NbS categories implemented in New Jersey, including beach nourishment and dune restoration on the Atlantic coast, thin-layer placement (TLP) of dredged material for estuarine salt marsh restoration, and living shorelines based on constructed oyster reef systems in Delaware Bay. title: Propagation-physics-guided channel augmentation and temporal–spectral fusion for domain-robust underwater acoustic target recognition
abstract: Underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) is essential for ocean-intelligence sensing, but deep learning-based models often suffer from performance degradation under ocean acoustic domain shift. This problem arises because ship-radiated noise recorded under different propagation channels, vessel operating states, background noise levels, and recording configurations may exhibit substantial distribution discrepancies. title: Environment-conditioned deep learning for severe convection nowcasting
abstract: Severe convection produces localized hazards that often require warnings before radar echoes fully reveal storm development. Convective initiation and the maintenance of intense convection remain challenging for radar-only nowcasting because pre-convective signals may be absent from recent radar observations, and strong echoes often decay rapidly in forecasts. title: Internal Solitary Waves in the Xisha Areas: Evidence From SWOT Observations
abstract: Abstract The Xisha Islands, situated in the northwestern South China Sea, are characterized by diverse topography conducive to a wide range of oceanic dynamic processes. Internal solitary waves (ISWs), large‐amplitude nonlinear waves in continuously‐stratified oceans, are pivotal for oceanic energy transport, vertical seawater mixing, and material exchange. This research leverages Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission data to investigate ISWs near the Xisha Islands. title: Application of Machine Learning-Based Models in Early Detection of Production Anomalies in Oil and Gas Wells
abstract: The early detection of production anomalies in petroleum wells is critical for optimizing operational efficiency, reducing downtime, and mitigating environmental risks, particularly in complex and prolific regions like the Niger Delta. This study investigates the application of both unsupervised and supervised artificial intelligence models for anomaly detection using historical well production data. journal: Gazi University Journal of Science Part A Engineering and Innovation

title: How heterogeneous environmental regulations shape marine sustainable development: evidence from coastal China
abstract: Marine sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with environmental protection, making the design and selection of effective environmental regulatory instruments increasingly important under tightening marine ecological constraints. In this study, marine sustainable development is measured by marine green total factor productivity (MGTFP). Using panel data from 11 coastal provinces and municipalities in China from 2007 to 2021, this study examines the differential associations of command-and-control environmental regulation (CER) and market-incentive environmental regulation

title: Gigantes tecnológicos y poder en plataformas de inteligencia artificial: una revisión crítica
abstract: Estudios críticos, administrativos y técnicos de comunicación y de ciencias sociales suelen diagnosticar vínculos estrechos entre los gigantes tecnológicos (Big Tech) y el nuevo verano de la inteligencia artificial (IA). Ese consenso se sintetiza en la idea de Big AI y supone que los modelos subsimbólicos funcionan bajo la premisa “más grande es mejor” (bigger is better). Sin embargo, existen pocos análisis que sistematicen los principales argumentos de ese acuerdo tácito. title: Predicting long-term degradation of prestressed bridge girders using a hybrid finite element and deep learning approach
abstract: Prestressed concrete girders are widely used in bridge and railway infrastructure. However, their long-term performance is highly vulnerable to environmental effects, particularly corrosion, which significantly compromises structural serviceability and durability. Accurately quantifying corrosion-induced deterioration over extended periods remains challenging due to the substantial time and computational demands of conventional finite element analyses. title: SEMANTIC SEGMENTATION OF OIL-CONTAMINATED LAND FROM PLANETSCOPE IMAGERY USING NEURAL NETWORK MODELS
abstract: Monitoring of oil-contaminated land is a pressing challenge for Kazakhstan. During the Soviet era, oil production at a number of fields relied on the so-called pit method, whereby drilling waste, process fluids, and associated wastewater were collected in purpose-dug earthen pits adjacent to extraction sites, leaving a substantial legacy of oil-contaminated areas requiring remediation and systematic monitoring. title: Cleaner peri-urban agricultural transitions under nitrogen-related water constraints: A teacher-validated evaluation of land-use alternatives in Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands
abstract: Peri-urban agriculture is increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable urban development while reducing the environmental pressures associated with land-use change and water-quality degradation. A key challenge is how to compare alternative agricultural configurations that maintain productive land use while lowering nitrogen-related environmental burdens before implementation. This study develops a teacher-validated framework for evaluating cleaner peri-urban agricultural land-use alternatives, using Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands, as a living-lab case. title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Estimation With Spatiotemporal Features and Physical‐Persistence Adjustment
abstract: Abstract This study proposes SOPHIENet (TC Satellite‐Observed Physical‐Persistence and Spatiotemporal Hybrid Intensity Estimation Network), a hybrid framework for Tropical Cyclone (TC) intensity estimation. SOPHIENet integrates a convolutional neural network, the Convolutional Block Attention Module, and a physical‐persistence adjustment mechanism. By extracting spatiotemporal features from multi‐temporal satellite infrared (IR) imagery, SOPHIENet captures TC cloud‐structure evolution. journal: Journal of Geophysical Research Machine Learning and Computation

title: Environmental Controls of Soil Inorganic and Organic Carbon Revealed Through Multivariate Analysis and Machine Learning in the Eastern Black Sea Region of Türkiye
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the controls of soil organic carbon (SOC) and soil inorganic carbon (SIC) in humid mountainous landscapes is challenging because of strong topo‐climatic and land‐use heterogeneity. This study assessed SOC, SIC, soil pH and the SIC/SOC ratio across 5964 km 2 in the Eastern Black Sea region of Türkiye using 1310 topsoil samples collected at 0–30 cm depth. Soil observations were combined with climatic, topographic, hydrological, remote‐sensing, land‐use and legacy soil covariates. title: Flood susceptibility in a coastal backwater floodplain: a spatially validated multi-event SAR framework for Alappuzha, India
abstract: Flood susceptibility mapping (FSM) is dominated by studies of upland catchments. At the same time, near-sea-level coastal and backwater floodplains, where inundation is shaped by reclamation, land use, tidal influence and constrained drainage rather than relief, remain comparatively under-explored. Existing studies also commonly rely on single-event inventories and machine-learning models validated through random data partitioning, which can overestimate predictive skill in spatial data. title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON MARKETING PERFORMANCE, GUEST SATISFACTION AND LOYALTY: IMPLICATIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL HOTEL BUSINESS IN ABUJA, NIGERIA
abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping hotel marketing and guest-service delivery, yet empirical evidence on its implications for guest satisfaction and loyalty in developing hospitality markets remains limited. This study examined AI applications in selected international hotels in Abuja, Nigeria, focusing on their perceived contribution to marketing performance, guest satisfaction and loyalty, as well as barriers to adoption. A cross-sectional mixed-methods design was employed, involving hotel staff and guests from six selected hotels. Data were collected through s

title: A review of the effectiveness of solutions to achieve the good environmental status of the marine environment
abstract: Europe’s seas are at the nexus of a “triple crisis” of biodiversity and habitat loss, climate change, and pollution, increasingly eroding the ecosystems’ resilience and capacity to provide ecosystem services. Although essential, existing European Union policies, especially the Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD), proved insufficient. title: Transboundary marine radioactive pollution under China’s ecological and environmental code: implementation gaps and directions for reform
abstract: Marine radioactive contamination can cross national boundaries, limiting the effectiveness of legal responses confined to a single jurisdiction. China has responded by progressively developing its legal framework through successive revisions to the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China and the consolidation of relevant rules in the Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China (EEC). title: Redes neuronales artificiales en psiquiatría. Generalidades y aplicaciones
abstract: Desde sus primeros tiempos, la inteligencia artificial ha encontrado un campo fértil de aplicación en el dominio médico; quizá por la forma en que se modelan y abordan eventos, y por la apertura del personal sanitario. Lo importante es que ha ayudado a resolver de manera práctica problemas de interés; según la época, se han aplicado algoritmos de tendencia. El objetivo del presente artículo es describir de manera sintetizada la evolución de la inteligencia artificial, algunos detalles históricos, las diferencias entre aprendizaje automático y profundo, el concepto de redes neuronales y su apli

title: Performance of Two Beginner-Accessible AI Image Classifiers for Marine-Debris Identification on Beaches of the Texas Gulf Coast
abstract: Marine debris poses persistent environmental and human-health risks, while recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have expanded the accessibility of image-classification tools. This study investigated the extent to which two beginner-accessible AI image classifiers, trained by a high school student, could distinguish between oceanic debris and natural marine objects on beaches along the Gulf of Mexico coast in southern Texas. title: From track to impact: a review of multi-hazard typhoon forecasting and resilience
abstract: While recent advancements in tropical cyclone prediction have been extensively documented, existing review literature remains heavily fragmented into isolated academic domains, such as artificial intelligence, data assimilation, or coastal hydrodynamics. This fragmentation obscures the operational reality of disaster risk reduction. To address this critical gap, this paper presents a transdisciplinary systematic review of the entire end-to-end climate service value chain. title: Physics-guided Statistical Data Fusion for Reconstructing 3D Current Fields of Oceanic Eddies
abstract: Accurate reconstruction of three-dimensional ocean current fields is critical for understanding ocean dynamics and real-time conduct of modern oceanographic field campaigns, particularly for mesoscale eddy surveys. We propose a physics-guided modeling and learning framework for multi-source data fusion to estimate the three-dimensional (3D) current structure of oceanic eddies by integrating satellite altimetry and temperature data, ocean reanalysis data, and in situ drifting buoy observations. journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association

title: Terrain-Adaptive Hydrostatic-Pressure-Assisted Seawater Reverse Osmosis with Managed Brine Return and Conjunctive Groundwater Blending in the Qattara Depression, Egypt: A Screening-Level Conceptual Study
abstract: Inland desalination in arid regions involves trade-offs among seawater conveyance, desalination energy, brine management, and freshwater delivery. This study presents a screening-level conceptual assessment of a terrain-adaptive hydrostatic-pressure-assisted seawater reverse osmosis (HP-SWRO) corridor in the Qattara Depression, Egypt. title: Climate-driven habitat loss of Chinese sturgeon in the Northwestern Pacific and implications for marine protected area design
abstract: The conservation of endangered anadromous fishes depends on understanding their full-lifecycle habitat requirements, yet the marine phase of Chinese sturgeon ( Acipenser sinensis ) remains a critical knowledge gap despite over 90% of its lifespan occurring at sea. We integrated multi-source occurrence data (satellite tagging, bycatch records, environmental DNA, and online databases) and applied an ensemble modeling framework (Biomod2 with eleven algorithms) to predict habitat suitability across the Northwestern Pacific Ocean (100°E–150°E, 10°N–55°N). title: A Lagrangian Time‐Series Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Concentrations and Exploring Drivers of Atmospheric Aerosols: Model Development and Application to Cloud Condensation Nuclei in Marine Boundary Layer
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric aerosols play critical roles in climate and air quality. Accurately assessing their environmental impacts requires understanding aerosol abundance, distribution, and the key factors and processes that control them. Although machine learning is increasingly used in predicting aerosol concentrations, its application in exploring underlying processes remains limited, and existing studies often fail to capture processes occurring during preceding days that substantially shape aerosol populations. title: MACHINE LEARNING-AIDED GROUNDWATER LEVEL AND CO2 EMISSION ESTIMATIONS IN INDONESIAN TROPICAL PEATLAND
abstract: ABSTRACT Tropical peatlands store a large fraction of global soil carbon and emit large amounts of CO 2 from peat decomposition and root respiration. Accurate quantification of peatland carbon emissions requires a prediction that is sensitive to environmental gradients. This study estimated biweekly total and heterotrophic peat CO 2 emissions (Rs and Rh, respectively) in the peatland hydrological unit (PHU), which represents the whole peatland ecosystem on Rupat Island, Indonesia. title: Few Annotations, High Accuracy: Transfer Learning and Data Augmentation Improve Passive Acoustic Monitoring of the Vulnerable African Manatee
abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring elusive and threatened species remains a major challenge in ecology and conservation, particularly in turbid aquatic environments. The African manatee ( Trichechus senegalensis ), listed as Vulnerable by the IUCN, remains difficult to survey using visual methods, limiting reliable assessments of its distribution and population status. Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) offers a promising alternative monitoring tool, but the large volumes of audio data generated require efficient automated detection of vocalizations. title: Automatic grading of HER2 immunohistochemical whole-slide images based on a multi-scale hierarchical graph neural network
abstract: Objective The HER2 immunohistochemical (IHC) score of breast cancer is a critical precursor for determining eligibility for anti-HER2 targeted therapy, as the final HER2 status (positive/negative/low) is determined by IHC results combined with FISH confirmation for equivocal 2 + cases according to ASCO/CAP guidelines. title: Digital economy, green innovation, and high-quality development of the marine economy: evidence from China’s coastal regions
abstract: This study examines the association between the digital economy and high-quality marine economic development using panel data for 11 coastal provincial-level regions in China from 2014 to 2023. Composite indices of digital economy development (DIG) and high-quality marine economic development (MEHD) are constructed, and two-way fixed-effects and panel threshold models are used to examine the overall association and its variation across development conditions. title: Machine Learning–based Earthquake Probability Prediction for Istanbul Province
abstract: Earthquakes represent one of the most destructive natural hazards, causing severe social and economic losses, particularly in tectonically active regions. In this context, estimating the short-term probability of earthquake occurrence is of critical importance for disaster preparedness and risk mitigation. This study focuses on Istanbul province, located along the North Anatolian Fault Zone in the Marmara Region, which is considered one of the most seismically active areas in Türkiye. title: Materiales compuestos fabricados aditivamente bajo carga biaxial: revisión sistemática de su caracterización, modelado y predicción de falla
abstract: La fabricación aditiva de polímeros reforzados con fibras ofrece nuevas posibilidades para el diseño estructural; sin embargo, su respuesta bajo carga biaxial permanece dispersa y poco consolidada. Esta revisión sistemática analiza polímeros reforzados con fibras fabricados aditivamente y sometidos a cargas biaxiales. title: A Self‐Powered Ocean Energy Platform Enabling Green Hydrogen Production and Smart Ocean Monitoring From Irregular Wave Energy
abstract: ABSTRACT Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising for harvesting low‐frequency, stochastic ocean‐wave energy, yet their limited power output and inefficient energy utilization hinder practical marine applications. Here, we present an in‐phase dual‐layer oscillating float triboelectric nanogenerator (IDOF‐TENG) that directly converts irregular ocean‐wave energy into electricity for simultaneous green hydrogen production and smart ocean monitoring. title: Remotely sensed vegetation resilience in the four major estuarine ecosystems of eastern China
abstract: Introduction Estuarine wetlands are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth, but they have been experiencing severe degradation induced by human activities and climate change worldwide. Traditional assessments of degradation mostly rely on static indicators, which are insufficient to reflect dynamical ecosystem properties such as systemic resilience. title: Subsea pipeline vibration and integrity: a review of sensing technologies, mitigation mechanisms, and physics-integrated learning
abstract: Subsea pipeline systems constantly face harsh marine environments, where complex fluid-structure interactions and nonlinear seabed responses cause severe mechanical vibrations threatening long-term structural integrity. Consequently, continuous real-time monitoring is vital. Traditional high-fidelity numerical models remain highly computationally expensive for remote edge devices, while purely data-driven machine learning models lack physical interpretability and struggle generalizing in dynamic underwater conditions. title: Regime shifts in South Florida groundwater: distinguishing upstream recharge from coastal sea level influences (1997–2022)
abstract: Groundwater dynamics in South Florida play an important role in shaping the hydrologic balance of the region. This study investigated long-term trends in groundwater elevation, surface water stages, and their interactions across Water Conservation Areas 3A and 3B, Everglades National Park, coastal watersheds, and Florida Bay. Time series decomposition of long-term groundwater elevation (1997 to 2022) was used to identify trends, seasonal patterns, and anomalies. title: A CNN-ConvLSTM Deep Learning Model with Axial Attention for Radar Reflectivity-based Precipitation Nowcasting in Southern Vietnam
abstract: Precipitation nowcasting plays a critical role in early hazard warning, especially for rapidly evolving convective systems. This study proposes a radar-based deep learning model that combines convolutional neural networks (CNN) for spatial feature extraction, a recurrent spatiotemporal module (ConvLSTM) for image sequences, and axial attention to capture spatiotemporal context. title: First record of Trigonium zonatulatum (Greville) A. Mann (Bacillariophyta, Trigoniumaceae) from the tropical Atlantic Ocean (Caribbean Sea)
abstract: Trigonium zonatulatum (Greville) A. Mann, originally described as Triceratium zonatulatum Greville, was previously known solely from the Indo-Pacific, Indian Ocean, and Bering Sea. Here, we report the first record of this diatom species from the Atlantic Ocean (Caribbean Sea), based on material collected at Boca Chica Beach, Dominican Republic. A single valve was examined under light microscopy and agrees with Greville’s (1865) original and subsequent descriptions of T. zonatulum . title: Optimized machine learning models for identification of autism spectrum disorder
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) relies heavily on identifying critical behavioral and clinical markers within high-dimensional datasets. However, standard feature selection methods frequently struggle with premature convergence and suboptimal feature identification. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an approach based on an Improved White Shark Optimizer combined with Machine Learning classifiers (IWSO-ML). title: Artificial intelligence cooperation and domestic absorptive capacity: evidence from ASEAN economies
abstract: Cross-border artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation is expanding, but evidence on its effect on domestic technological capability in recipient economies is scarce. Drawing on absorptive capacity theory, we create a composite AI absorptive capacity index for 10 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) economies, encompassing innovation foundations, application foundations and industrial support. title: Diversity assessment of Western Indian Ocean whiprays (Himantura spp.) through a molecular species delimitation approach
abstract: Abstract The Himantura species complex consists of large demersal whiprays vulnerable to coastal fisheries, yet unresolved taxonomy within the genus hinders conservation efforts, making molecular assessments crucial for effective fishery management. This study clarified genetic relationships among Himantura species in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) using species delimitation techniques. title: Understanding Land Surface Temperature Patterns in Istanbul: The Role of Blue–Green and Built-Environment Predictors Using Explainable Machine Learning
abstract: Rapid urbanization and the replacement of vegetated surfaces by impervious materials can substantially alter urban thermal environments, while water bodies, topography, and coastal setting may further modify these patterns. Understanding how these factors contribute to land surface temperature (LST), particularly across large and geographically heterogeneous cities, is important for spatially targeted heat mitigation. title: A hybrid deep learning–based OCR model for handwritten medical prescriptions
abstract: The current trend involving the use of paper-based medical prescriptions and the exchange of such by the social media is a major problem in automated and accurate text extraction in healthcare processes. This paper suggests a complete smart pipeline to digitize the images of medical prescriptions with lightweight deep learning-based classification, specialized Optical Character Recognition (OCR) engines, and comparative benchmarking of results using a large language model (LLM). title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Teaching Support System for Personalized Learning in Higher Education
abstract: The aim of this study was to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence-driven teacher support system capable of translating multidimensional learning profiles into instructional and assessment recommendations for higher education. The proposal integrated five diagnostic dimensions: VARK, for preferences in accessing information; FSLSM, for processing and representation traits; ICAP, for levels of cognitive engagement; SRL, for self-regulated learning; and EBSI, for study habits. title: Machine learning-based Komodo dragon conservation planning using habitat suitability and wildfire risk
abstract: The conservation of Komodo dragons ( Varanus komodoensis ), an apex predator whose top-down regulation of ungulate prey helps sustain savanna ecosystem balance, and an iconic yet endangered species, requires a nuanced understanding of habitat suitability, wildfire susceptibility, and conservation zoning within Komodo National Park (KNP), Indonesia. title: Intelligent Surveillance System for Knife Detection Based on YOLOv8 Neural Networks
abstract: Cold weapon violence in urban environments represents a growing problem that demands innovative technological solutions for its prevention and control. This article presents the design and implementation of an intelligent surveillance system based on the YOLOv8nano architecture for real-time detection of sharp objects, specifically knives, in images and video streams. title: Storybooks and Wordwalls in Problem Based Learning to Improve Critical Thinking and Environmental Awareness
abstract: Exploration and reflection on problem-based learning building critical thinking. Implementation constrains problem-based learning in elementary schools, students' ability to understand problems is crucial. Media are needed to stimulate the ability to analyze real-world problems, express logical opinions, and implement solutions as critical thinking skills that foster an attitude of environmental concern. The purpose of this study was to analyze the influence of the use of storybooks and wordwall deep problem-based learning on critical thinking skills and environmental awareness simultaneously.

abstract: Este artículo presenta una revisión sistemática (PRISMA 2020) y bibliométrica de 157 documentos (Scopus/WoS) para determinar la estructura intelectual, las brechas de competencias y la arquitectura curricular en la educación universitaria. abstract: A adoção de ferramentas de inteligência artificial generativa na comunicação corporativa está a transformar a prática profissional e a gerar novos conflitos de natureza ética, estratégica e organizacional. abstract: Abstract Low‐frequency earthquakes (LFEs) provide key constraints on slow earthquake processes but remain difficult to detect because of their low signal‐to‐noise ratios (SNR) and emergent onsets, particularly in offshore environments where seismic networks are sparse. In this study, we develop a deep learning framework for LFE detection trained on a curated multi‐region data set spanning six tectonic environments. title: Coupled adaptive neural network control for active suspension of deep-sea mining tracked vehicles under hydrodynamic effects and multiple parametric uncertainties
abstract: Deep-sea mining tracked vehicles are subject to substantial parametric uncertainty from hydrodynamic effects, soft-seabed interaction, suspension nonlinearities, and actuator degradation. This paper proposes a coupled adaptive neural network (CANN) strategy for an 8-DOF six-wheel half-vehicle active suspension. title: Marine ecosystem ecology at a crossroads
abstract: Research in marine ecosystem ecology increasingly integrates biodiversity status and trends, ecosystem functioning, and human pressures. Understanding how marine biodiversity supports ecosystem functioning remains central to the field, while growing concern over ecosystem condition has shifted attention towards relationships between human pressures and ecological responses. These established questions are increasingly complemented by the need to anticipate climate-driven ecosystem transformations and translate ecological knowledge into effective conservation and management. abstract: Abstract Fish disease poses a substantial threat to the productivity and sustainability of Indian major carps (IMCs) in aquaculture. Early and accurate fish disease detection is crucial to minimizing economic losses and ensuring fish health management. In this study, we developed a lightweight deep learning model, FishMoViT, for real-time detection of seven major IMCs diseases. It integrates two state-of-the-art deep learning networks, MobileNetV2 and MobileViT-Small, as a dual backbone, leveraging an ensemble strategy to combine complementary feature representations. title: Análise de isótopos estáveis em ciências forenses: fundamentos teóricos, aplicações e avanços.
abstract: Os isótopos estáveis constituem importantes traçadores naturais utilizados em estudos ambientais, ecológicos e forenses, pois suas variações refletem processos físicos, químicos e biológicos que ocorrem no ambiente e nos organismos vivos. title: Nano clay mitigation of wind induced soil loss across aggregate sizes through wind tunnel experiments and explainable machine learning
abstract: This study aimed to investigate, under wind-tunnel conditions, the effects of different nano-clay application rates (0, 0.94, 1.88, and 3.75 g m⁻²) on wind-induced soil loss across different aggregate sizes (0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 mm) and wind speeds (8, 10, and 12 m s⁻¹). title: Recent advances in oil spill recovery technologies
abstract: Marine oil spills pose persistent threats to ecosystems and economies. This review systematically evaluates research advancements in marine oil spill recovery over the past decade, focusing on the last five years. After outlining oil spill impacts and traditional strategy evolution, the paper analyzes breakthroughs in three mainstream approaches: physical/mechanical methods (highlighting nanostructured adsorbents), chemical methods (emphasizing eco-friendly dispersants and gelling agents), and biological methods (focusing on nano-enhanced and enzymatic bioremediation). abstract: Abstract Changes in ice sheet mass manifest as changes in ice flow, ice thickness, and gravitational attraction. These parameters can be measured from space and used to track Greenland's contribution to sea level rise independently from each other. While an excellent level of agreement between these satellite techniques has been demonstrated at the ice sheet scale, less attention has been paid to whether this agreement is maintained at regional and local scales. abstract: High-resolution atmospheric modeling over topographically complex coastal zones requires multi-source spatial data fusion to bridge the scale gap between satellite-assimilated global reanalysis and localized surface boundary layer dynamics. abstract: Artificial intelligence tools are essential for effective time management. Given that many students work alongside their studies, saving and managing time effectively can significantly increase their efficiency. A total of 791 students from Ivane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University took part in the study. abstract: Molecular imprinted polymers (MIPs) have various applications such as chemical sensing and drug delivery systems because they can selectively attach molecules that fit the template. title: Economía azul e inteligencia artificial: innovación, sostenibilidad y nuevos mercados
abstract: La economía azul propone conciliar la actividad económica sin destruir los recursos marinos. En este contexto, el presente trabajo sostiene que la inteligencia artificial (IA) no debe verse solo como una herramienta de eficiencia, sino un elemento clave para redefinir las condiciones de viabilidad ambiental oceánica. A partir de una revisión crítica de la literatura reciente, se argumenta que la (IA) puede contribuir a la gestión sostenible de los ecosistemas marinos, aunque su impacto depende de marcos institucionales capaces de evitar la reproducción de desigualdades tecnológicas y prácticas

abstract: Marine engineering materials experience coupled and nonstationary environmental actions that cannot be fully reproduced by accelerated laboratory tests, making long-term field exposure necessary for reliable service-state assessment. title: Mapping disappearance: spatial analysis of vulnerable coastal destinations
abstract: Abstract Many coastal regions around the world face increasing risks from both natural and anthropogenic drivers, including climate change, rising sea levels, and rapid, unauthorized urbanization. This study presents an integrated geospatial approach to evaluate the coastal vulnerability of Visakhapatnam and Uppada Village, both located in coastal Andhra Pradesh, India. abstract: Abstract Traffic-related fatalities are among few leading causes of death worldwide. Crash severity prediction of traffic crashes has become a widespread research subject in recent years. Severity outcomes of crashes are usually influenced by factors such as humans, vehicles, roadway, weather, environment, and their interactions. abstract: Cities are central to global climate mitigation, yet existing projections often rely on coarse-grained assessment models that overlook the interplay between urban typology and socioeconomic dynamics. Here, we harness a context-aware deep learning framework combined with typological clustering to project CO₂ emissions for 46,833 cities in Annex I countries through 2050 under Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. abstract: This paper presents the results of an investigation into the feasibility of applying ensemble machine learning algorithms to predict the mechanical properties of nanofilled epoxy composites, aimed at enhancing the reliability of water transport facilities. abstract: Accurate urban land-use classification is essential for hydrological modeling, yet most studies evaluate classification schemes solely by pixel-level accuracy rather than their hydrological consequences. This study examines whether conventional classification accuracy is sufficient to identify land-use maps suitable for hydrological modeling. abstract: Accurately identifying whether a field of view of satellite hyperspectral infrared sounders is clear or cloudy is critical for geophysical parameter retrieval and meteorological applications. abstract: Single-pixel imaging (SPI) offers sensitivity for optical sensing, but dynamic scattering media severely degrade the captured 1D bucket signals, causing traditional image reconstruction algorithms to fail and hindering target recognition. To overcome the resulting sim-to-real gap, we propose a physics-enhanced dual-branch digital twin framework for single-pixel vision in highly scattering environments. abstract: Abstract Earth’s oceans cover 70% of the planet yet remain among the least observed regions. Underwater acoustics is a primary sensing modality, but recordings span biological, anthropogenic and natural sounds while labels remain sparse. abstract: The character of warfare is being reshaped by artificial intelligence, unmanned systems, and quantum computing at a pace that outstrips the doctrinal and institutional habits of most navies. abstract: This work presents a systematic, deployment-oriented evaluation of residential load forecasting models on resource-constrained embedded edge devices. In comparison to previous work, this study jointly analyses forecasting performance, memory footprint, inference latency, and directly measured on-device energy consumption. abstract: This article explored the perception of Information Systems Engineering students at the National University (UNA), Interuniversity Campus of Alajuela (SIUA), regarding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in their university learning. abstract: A incorporação da inteligência artificial (IA) nos sistemas de alerta precoce está transformando a antecipação de eventos extremos, a integração de informações de múltiplas fontes e a comunicação do risco. abstract: Precision Agriculture requires intelligent, adaptable and efficient technology that is capable of making decisions in agriculture at the right time, based on the condition of the plants and the environment. abstract: The global expansion of Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) under the "30×30" target necessitates rigorous effectiveness assessments. title: Fundamentos técnicos y dilemas éticos en los modelos de lenguaje natural en las Inteligencias Artificiales
abstract: El siguiente artículo tiene como objetivo mostrar los fundamentos de los generadores de lenguajes naturales dentro de las inteligencias artificiales, desde la elucidación de las Redes Neuronales hasta las arquitecturas Transformers de los modelos GPT. abstract: Abstract. Accurate identification of fish species is important for trade supervision, marine biology, and fisheries management. abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) require energy-efficient clustering and adaptive routing to maintain reliable communication and prolong network lifetime under varying node density, initial energy, communication range, packet size, residual energy, routing distance, latency, and mobile-sink conditions. abstract: This study integrates Ridge Regression (RR) and Random Forest (RF) machine learning (ML) models with geodetic and climatic datasets to investigate vertical land motion (VLM) patterns across the Ifewara-Zungeru fault zone. abstract: ABSTRACT Wastewater infrastructure must accommodate variable influent loads, complex contaminant mixtures, stringent discharge requirements, water reuse, and resource-recovery objectives within a single operational system. abstract: La praxis médica contemporánea se enfrenta a una encrucijada crítica: la integración de la inteligencia artificial (IA) no solo como herramienta diagnóstica, sino como arquitecta de una nueva realidad clínica.
