abstract: Countries across the world are leveraging the blue economy (BE) as a strategic framework for the sustainable exploitation of ocean resources, driving economic growth and creating employment. Economic activities emanating from marine and coastal environments are contributing significantly to the economies of the world. abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and rapid urbanization, island cities face increasing compound-flood risks due to their fragmented topography and limited terrestrial space, yet cross-scale modeling and high-resolution exposure assessment for archipelagic environments remain insufficient. Taking Zhoushan City, China, as a case study, this research develops an integrated compound-flood multi-receptor exposure assessment framework combining cross-scale hydrodynamic modeling with high-resolution spatialization. title: Seismic Deblending via an Adjacent‐CRG‐Assisted Multistep Deep Learning Framework
abstract: Abstract Dithered simultaneous‐source acquisition improves seismic survey efficiency but introduces complex overlapping blending noise that hinders subsequent processing and inversion. Therefore, deblending becomes an essential step for providing high‐quality data. While deep learning has shown promise for deblending in nonshot domains, existing methods often treat gathers in isolation, overlooking the potential of interrelationships between adjacent records. abstract: Sediment-linked benthic features provide evidence of ecological processes but remain difficult to analyse at scale because exhaustive box-level annotation is time-consuming and requires ecological expertise. We present a two-phase weakly supervised object detection framework that reduces reliance on dense manual annotations. abstract: To support urban decarbonization, XGBoost classifiers were developed to predict residential heating energy vectors in Spain using open cadastral, census, and Energy Performance Certificate data. title: Energy-efficient multimodal motion control of hybrid underwater gliders based on an optimized model predictive active disturbance rejection framework
abstract: Hybrid Underwater Glider (HUG) serve as critical platforms for extended and large-scale ocean observations. However, achieving precise trajectory tracking in complex and dynamic marine environment, remains a significant challenge. This paper addresses the multimodal trajectory tracking problem for HUG by proposing a composite control framework integrating Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC), Model Predictive Control (MPC), and Adaptive Line-of-Sight (ALOS). abstract: La expansión de la inteligencia artificial en ámbitos estratégicos plantea un problema específico para el derecho internacional público: dificulta identificar dónde ocurre un hecho jurídicamente relevante y, como consecuencia, qué conducta debe ser atribuida, a qué sujeto y en qué condiciones puede activarse la responsabilidad internacional. abstract: El auge y la penetración de los modelos de inteligencia artificial en todos los ámbitos de la vida humana constituyen un fenómeno continuo y dinámico.La investigación científica igualmente se ha visto permeada por el advenimiento y la democratización cada vez mayor de dichas tecnologías.Su implementación, desde el tratamiento de datos hasta su utilización en la redacción científica, hace que el uso de estos recursos deba observarse desde una perspectiva ética que nos permita reflexionar sobre hasta qué punto su uso resulta adecuado y si constituye o no un riesgo para las personas participantes

title: Markers of resilience to stony coral tissue loss disease and putative probiotic functions in the microbiomes of the coral, Orbicella faveolata
abstract: Abstract Stony coral tissue loss disease (SCTLD) is widespread within the Caribbean and affects at least 22 species of reef-building coral. Bacteria have been implicated in the etiology of SCTLD, but the community of bacteria and archaea may also contribute to SCTLD resistance. To identify potential mechanisms through which microbes contribute to SCTLD resistance, we sequenced metagenomes from 41 colonies of the threatened coral, Orbicella faveolata, in the lower Florida Keys. title: Cetacean acoustic occurrence in the Southern Ocean from biologged southern elephant seals
abstract: The Southern Ocean is a crucial habitat for multiple species of cetaceans, from mysticete species to odontocetes such as sperm whales and delphinids. However, their presence at high latitudes is still poorly known due to the remoteness of the area, with little literature on delphinid presence and sparse sampling along mysticete migration routes. title: El insustituible juicio humano: Desafíos de la revisión por pares frente a la Inteligencia Artificial en el Proceso Editorial de manuscritos científicos
abstract: En publicación científica se han probado distintos incentivos para optimizar el proceso de revisión por pares (RPP), sin lograr un impacto significativo en los tiempos y calidad de las revisiones. La irrupción de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) y de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM) prometen revolucionar el futuro de la RPP. Objetivo: Analizar los desafíos que plantea la IA en el proceso de RPP, revisar la evidencia y proponer lineamientos para el proceso editorial de Andes Pediatrica. abstract: Introduction Detection of underwater waste in freshwater environments remains a challenging task due to the scarcity of domain-specific annotated datasets and adverse visual conditions caused by poor visibility, inconsistent illumination, color degradation, and suspended particles. Unlike existing underwater debris datasets that primarily focus on marine environments, freshwater pond ecosystems remain relatively underrepresented. title: An Automated Deep Learning-Driven Data Analytics Approach for Silica Content Prediction in Potential Iron Flotation Using Real-World Mineral Processing Plant Operational Data
abstract: In the mineral sector, flotation is an extensively applied process to separate useful minerals from waste materials. On the other hand, it remains challenging due to numerous interacting physical and chemical components that complicate process control in real-time plant environments. Due to this, data-driven methods are applied to analyze and model flotation behavior. In iron flotation, predicting the silica content in iron ore concentrate is crucial for assessing final product quality and plant performance. title: Predicting Early Childhood Stunting and Associated Factors in Kenya Using Machine Learning
abstract: Background: Stunting in the first two years of life remains a major public health concern in Kenya, affecting about one in five children and leading to long-term consequences on cognitive development and economic productivity. Traditional, largely reactive approaches that rely on linear statistical models have a limited ability to capture the complex, non‑linear determinants of stunting. abstract: Abstract This work presents a machine learning approach for analyzing the corrosion behavior of AZ31 magnesium alloy using digital images acquired with a smartphone camera assembled to a homemade studio. A controlled imaging system combined with automated feature extraction enabled the quantification of surface color and texture changes associated with corrosion progression. abstract: According to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF), approximately 589 million adults are expected to be living with diabetes in 2025. This number continues to rise due to unhealthy eating habits and poor quality of life. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial to prevent organ damage and improve patient outcomes. This study aims to develop a method for predicting diabetes without requiring individuals to visit healthcare facilities or undergo laboratory tests, using machine learning (ML) techniques to enable early intervention. title: Expanding the global diversity of Nanobdellales from deep-sea hydrothermal vents
abstract: Abstract The archaeal symbiotic Nanobdellales have been isolated with their hosts from a shallow hot marine vent off Iceland and from terrestrial hot springs in Yellowstone National Park and Japan. They have highly reduced genomes and rely on their archaeal hosts for most of their metabolic needs. Here, to provide further insights into the ecology and evolution of this order, we greatly expand their phylogenomic distribution using metagenome assembled genomes from deep-sea hydrothermal vents in the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans, and the Gulf of California. abstract: Submarine stratum instability poses a potential threat to subsea tunnels and other marine infrastructure in geologically complex areas. This study develops an interpretable data-driven framework for assessing submarine stratum instability in the Miaodao Islands region of the Bohai Strait, China. A database of 120 borehole-derived and laboratory-tested submarine-soil samples was established using ten geological, physical, and mechanical indicators. abstract: Unmanned maritime vehicles (UMVs) are increasingly used in several maritime domain applications including seafloor mapping, mine countermeasures, pipeline and infrastructure inspection, and unexploded ordnance detection. abstract: The movement of European eels (Anguilla anguilla) has long been a mystery keeping scholars on their toes. Where European eels come from, for example, has been the source of some serious lateral thinking through the ages. title: Jornalismo de dados e Inteligência Artificial: Estudo de casos para compreender alcances e limitaçõesda automatização na América Latina
abstract: This paper analyzes ten cases of AI integration in data journalism (two global, eight Latin American). AI expands operational capacity (volume and speed) but does not replace epistemic decisions, which remain under editorial control. The automation gradient —signaling, predictive scoring, large‑scale classification, total output validation— is proposed as an alternative to the automatic/semiautomatic binary. In Latin America, the main constraint is data governance: the lack of public information in processable formats limits the reach of AI, regardless of the models’ capabilities.

abstract: Valve component tightness is critical for maintaining facility integrity and optimizing energy efficiency in power generation plants. Non-intrusive detection and quantification of internal leakages are essential for implementing condition-based maintenance. However, early detection and, in particular, accurate quantification—remains a major challenge. To address this need, the present study proposes a Cascading Feedforward Neural Network (CFNN)–Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework, which enables the prediction and control of complex nonlinear thermal behavior under soft constraints on useful heat gain and exergy gain. abstract: This study explores the use of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to simulate river hydrodynamics over complex varying bed elevations, as surrogate models for MIKE 21, enabling the reconstruction of high-resolution river flow fields from spatially sparse data. The PINN model was incorporated with the two-dimensional shallow water equations (2D SWEs) as physical constraints, and the topographic information of the riverbed for more effective convergence. abstract: Welded metal sheets are used across automotive, aerospace, marine, and civil infrastructure applications for their high strength and light weight, yet fatigue failure remains a persistent concern in relation to their long-term structural stability. Fatigue crack growth is strongly influenced by the interaction of weld geometry and manufacturing-related defects. abstract: Despite global coral reef degradation, Porites astreoides has become increasingly dominant on Florida and Caribbean reefs and is often considered climate-resilient. However, whether its apparent success reflects an increase in absolute abundance or simply a rise in relative abundance remains unclear, as does its ability to persist under continued climate stress. Finite-element-simulated acceleration responses are processed using Enhanced Frequency-Domain Decomposition (EFDD) to identify modal frequencies and damping ratios, which are then used as machine-learning input features. title: Advancing sustainable crab harvesting through intelligent technologies: a comprehensive review
abstract: Crab fisheries are important components of coastal food systems, but their sustainable development depends on selective fishing gear, reliable field information, and reduced ecological disturbance. This review synthesizes 173 studies published from 2002 to 2025 and retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and PubMed. abstract: Path planning for unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) formations in polar under-ice environments is fundamentally challenged by GNSS signal occlusion, severely degraded acoustic communication, dynamic ice obstacles, and the inherent tension between individual obstacle avoidance and formation integrity. abstract: Corrosion fatigue is a critical degradation mechanism that significantly limits the service life of high-performance structural steels and butt welds used in marine and coastal infrastructure. Traditional fatigue life assessment relies on extensive laboratory testing, which is costly, time-consuming, and insufficient to capture the complex interactions between cyclic loading and aggressive marine environments. abstract: Abstract Extensive, coherent circulations in the marine atmospheric boundary layer (MABL) are detected and classified using an automated image processing routine applied to synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images from Sentinel‐1 over subtropical oceans at sunrise and sunset. Circulations are inferred from patterns of capillary waves detected by the SAR. title: AI Governance and the MASS Code: the Law of the Sea and the Adoption of the Non-mandatory Code
abstract: Abstract The duties anchoring the law of the sea – the master’s search and rescue obligation and the flag State’s qualification duty under the Law of the Sea Convention, the Collision Regulations’ look-out and collision rules, and seafarer training and watchkeeping standards – are addressed to a human in command. title: Object-based image analysis supporting site selection in Posidonia oceanica restoration efforts
abstract: Posidonia oceanica meadows are a valuable yet vulnerable coastal ecosystem endemic to the Mediterranean Sea, providing key ecosystem services. However, these habitats have declined markedly over the last decades due to multiple anthropogenic stressors. Given their low natural recovery rates, active restoration through transplantation has become a widely adopted strategy to mitigate this loss. title: Regional climate risk assessment from climate models using probabilistic machine learning
abstract: Abstract Effective climate risk assessment is hindered by the resolution gap between coarse global climate models and the fine-scale information needed for regional decision making. Existing downscaling methods struggle to bridge this gap: physics-based methods are too computationally expensive for large ensemble sampling of extreme events, while traditional statistical methods fail to capture multivariate spatiotemporal dependencies crucial to compound risk estimation. abstract: Calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H), the primary hydration product of cement, governs the strength and durability of concrete but remains difficult to model due to its chemical heterogeneity and disordered nanostructure. Machine learning potentials (MLPs) offer a route to extend quantum accuracy to large-scale simulations, yet progress has been limited by the absence of representative datasets. abstract: Este artículo analiza, desde una perspectiva de economía política, cómo la revolución digital y la fragmentación geoeconómica obligan a replantear el papel de las instituciones en Europa. title: The impact of climate risk on forestry ecological total factor productivity: evidence from double machine learning
abstract: Extreme climate events associated with climate change pose a growing threat to forestry production efficiency, yet systematic empirical evidence on their effects on ecological total factor productivity in forestry (forestry TFP) and the underlying transmission pathways remains limited. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provinces from 2012 to 2023, we measure provincial physical climate risk, dominated by acute extreme events, with a composite physical climate risk index (CPRI) comprising exposure to extreme cold, extreme heat, extreme rainfall and extreme drought. title: Microbial community dynamics mediate rapid biomass loss and phosphorus recycling in pelagic Sargassum
abstract: Sargassum blooms in the tropical North Atlantic have surged to unprecedented levels, causing massive algal tides that severely impact coastal ecosystems. To improve the current understanding of Sargassum biomass dynamics and the contribution of this productive algal bloom to carbon and nutrient fluxes between the Atlantic and the Caribbean, we characterized the growth and decomposition rates of this pelagic alga, nutrient release rates during litter decay, and the bacterial microbiome at several stages of this decay. title: Learning the Path to Ion Separation: A Proof-of-Concept for Machine Learning-Assisted Inverse Design (MLAID) of Nanofiltration Membranes
abstract: Abstract Advancing the design of polymeric membranes through material screening and discovery offers a powerful strategy to guide future membrane fabrication tailored to a wide range of separation challenges. Traditional trial-and-error methods often fall short in navigating this large monomer and process-design space, whereas machine learning-assisted inverse design (MLAID) can provide an extensible workflow for translating literature-derived membrane knowledge into ranked experimental candidates. title: Explainable Machine Learning-Based Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment and Upazila-Level Intervention Prioritization in the Chattogram Region, Bangladesh
abstract: The increasing occurrence of natural hazards, either individually or in combination, has intensified disaster risk worldwide, with the Chattogram Region of Bangladesh representing a prominent multi-hazard hotspot where earthquakes, landslides, and floods frequently coexist. An interpretable GIS–ML-based multi-hazard risk assessment (MHRA) framework was developed to generate earthquake, landslide, and flood susceptibility zones (EQSZ, LSSZ, and FSZ) using ensemble machine learning algorithms, with model predictions explained through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). title: AI-Enabled Cultural Heritage Preservation and a Browser-Based Virtual Museum: Design and Implementation of a Kenya Coastal Heritage Platform
abstract: Coastal Kenya holds a wide-ranging cultural heritage expressed in material artefacts, oral traditions, indigenous and local languages, historical knowledge, and everyday community practices. Yet these resources are increasingly strained by modernisation and global circulation, shifting modes of cultural transmission, and gaps in systematic documentation. This study reports the design and implementation of the Kenya Coastal Heritage Digital Platform produced under the Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for the Preservation and Promotion of Coastal Cultural Heritage in Kenya (LAIPCH-K) project.

abstract: Abstract This study developed a spatially explicit framework to estimate household water consumption (HWC) and the number of household water subscribers in each consumption class (NHWSCC) using land surface temperature (LST), land value, and elevation. Three machine-learning (ML) models were applied: symbolic regression (SR), an extreme learning machine (ELM), and an ELM hybridized with the artificial bee colony algorithm (ELM-ABC). abstract: Abstract Ozone (O3) pollution in relatively high-latitude industrial cities shows spatiotemporal patterns associated with coupled meteorological, transport, and chemical processes, yet its dominant formation mechanisms remain unresolved. abstract: Accurate estimation of crop aboveground biomass (AGB) and aboveground carbon (AGC) across growth stages is pivotal for evaluating agroecosystem carbon sequestration. Nevertheless, the integration of feature selection, model optimization, and interpretability for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based crop AGB estimation remains underexplored. abstract: For matched field localization using ship radiated noise as sources of opportunity, replica libraries are often incomplete because vessel trajectories cannot fully cover the observation region. The completion problem can be formulated as recovering missing replica entries from partial observations, for which Bayesian matrix completion methods provide a probabilistic framework. title: Air–Water Greenhouse Gases Exchange in Surface Waters of Deception Island (South Shetland Archipelago, Antarctica): Assessment of Drivers of Spatial Variability
abstract: Abstract Greenhouse gases (GHGs) such as Carbon Dioxide (CO 2 ), Methane (CH 4 ), and Nitrous Oxide (N 2 O) play critical roles in global climate change. CO 2 dominates due to its high concentration and long atmospheric lifetime, while CH 4 and N 2 O also exert strong heat‐trapping effects despite shorter residence times. Deception Island, in the Southern Ocean, combines active volcanism with extensive penguin colonies, offering a unique setting to quantify natural GHG sources. title: Digital Innovation And The Blue Economy: Enhancing The Competitiveness Of Coastal Micro, Small, And Medium Enterprises
abstract: Purpose: This article aims to examine the role of digital innovation in enhancing the competitiveness of coastal Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) within the framework of the blue economy. Coastal MSMEs play an important role in generating employment, supporting local livelihoods, and utilizing marine and coastal resources. However, these enterprises frequently face challenges related to limited market access, low technological capabilities, inadequate infrastructure, environmental pressures, and intense competition. title: Warming Amplifies the Variability of Methane Emissions From a Coastal Wetland
abstract: Abstract Climate warming is expected to increase methane (CH 4 ) emissions from coastal wetlands, but its effects on the temporal dynamics of emissions remain poorly resolved. Because short‐lived high‐emission events are poorly captured by low‐frequency monitoring and by existing models, warming‐driven increases in variability could worsen a systematic bias in CH 4 budget estimates. title: Marine organic waste valorization on seafood-based industry development: A review on circular bioeconomy and Technology Readiness Level (TRL) perspectives
abstract: Marine organic waste, including fish processing byproducts, shellfish residues, aquaculture waste, aquatic plant biomass, and coastal beach wrack, represents an abundant yet underutilized biomass resource with significant potential for supporting a circular bioeconomy. This review comprehensively evaluates recent advances in the valorization of these marine waste streams through sustainable biotechnological and thermochemical approaches. abstract: Accurate solar irradiance prediction is a crucial step for the efficient planning and deployment of solar energy systems, particularly in tropical regions like Cameroon where solar resources remain largely untapped. Despite growing global interest in solar energy prediction using machine learning techniques, this remains a significant challenge. Similar studies exist in Cameroon, but they remain few compared to those in Asia, Europe, or North Africa. abstract: Accurate integrated water vapor (IWV) estimates are essential for atmospheric monitoring, yet reanalyses can retain systematic discrepancies relative to in situ observations. This study develops a radiosonde-informed machine learning framework to correct ERA5-derived IWV over Europe and assess spatial and temporal generalization. Radiosonde profiles from the University of Wyoming and the Integrated Global Radiosonde Archive were collocated with ERA5 and VMF3 products at 116 stations from November 2021 to November 2025. abstract: Control over reservoir water levels and gate settings at the spillways is key for preventing floods, protecting people living downstream, and efficient utilization of stored water especially when the reservoir is nearing its maximum capacity. This research project centers on the Shetrunji Reservoir in Gujarat, India, investigating the potential of machine learning to improve operations. title: Strong coral recovery indicates reefs in Laamu Atoll, Maldives, remain resilient following mass bleaching
abstract: Mass coral bleaching events linked to climate change are a major contributor to the global degradation of coral reefs. Recovery largely depends on the growth of survivors and successful coral recruitment; however, recruitment is highly variable and influenced by many factors. This study quantified the size structure of coral communities within Laamu Atoll, in southern Maldives, using colonies < 5 cm in diameter as a proxy for recent coral recruitment. abstract: The practical application of rechargeable zinc-air batteries (R-ZABs) is critically limited by high-performance bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, as their intrinsic activity directly governs the efficiency and longevity of air cathodes. Recently, biomass-derived carbon materials are compelling candidates for bifunctional electrocatalysts, benefiting from their renewable nature, low cost, inherently porous architecture, and naturally doped heteroatoms. abstract: Coastal subsea tunnels often traverse shallow heterogeneous strata, creating significant deformation risks. Deformation control is therefore essential for safe urban construction. This study integrates FLAC3D, SSA-LSSVM, and NSGA-II for multi-objective excavation-support optimization. The Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Second Subsea Tunnel serves as the case study. abstract: This study developed a risk-based integrity management strategy for aging marine pipelines, emphasizing corrosion degradation, structural reliability, failure risk, and life extension of the Uyeghe–Stubb Creek buried oil pipeline system in Rivers State, Nigeria. The study used a case-study approach, drawing on historical inspection data and operating parameters, along with Melchers tri-linear and Paik non-linear corrosion models, marine-growth modelling, time-dependent reliability analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation. abstract: Introduction Maritime transport carries the predominant share of cross-border agricultural trade, and geopolitical conflicts, climate anomalies, port congestion, and proliferating trade barriers have intensified uncertainty for the coastal enterprises that depend on seaborne logistics. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new pathways for building resilient supply chains through multi-source data fusion and risk prediction capabilities. However, these benefits depend on daily accessibility. In compact coastal metropolises, extensive nature may coexist with highly unequal residential access. abstract: The events such as earthquakes, tsunamis and underwater landslides occur; communication reliability becomes a big challenge in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs). abstract: The Koroshina Dolomite Formation is an important gas-bearing carbonate reservoir in the Sadad Gas Field, central Syria, where strong structural heterogeneity and limited well control make the prediction of reservoir properties challenging. This study aims to predict the spatial distribution of reservoir porosity within the Koroshina Dolomite Formation by integrating well-log data, two-dimensional (2D) post-stack seismic data, seismic inversion, and artificial neural network modeling. abstract: Marine litter remains a major global environmental challenge, and long-term mitigation depends not only on policy and waste management systems but also on public awareness and behavior change. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a school-based environmental education intervention in improving elementary school students’ knowledge, awareness, and behavioral intentions regarding marine litter. This study aims to classify material type, feed rate, and depth-of-cut using data-driven vibration signals obtained during CNC milling of Al6061 and Al7075 aluminum alloys. abstract: Deep learning, especially CNN- and transformer-based approaches, has significantly impacted computer vision techniques such as object detection, segmentation, and scene classification. Despite the many successful scene understanding pipelines currently in use, most still rely primarily on global image features or object-level predictions and have little capacity to explicitly model object relationships, spatial arrangements, and structured contextual dependencies. abstract: Marine litter (ML) has attracted attention from international and national regulatory bodies because of its impact on biodiversity, water quality and the blue economy. abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid advances in new urbanization and continued rural population contraction, the expansion of cropland non-grain use poses a potential challenge to national food security. abstract: Introduction Jellyfish possess the biochemical and physiological capabilities that enable them to survive from the beginning of the animal era to the impacts of global warming (ocean warming and deoxygenation) on the seas today. Despite their confirmed ability to bloom, significant gaps remain about the molecular basis of specific physiological responses, and limited data allow us to understand the metabolic pathways that enable medusozoans to transform energy and successfully cope with the challenges the marine environment imposes. abstract: The southwestern slope of the Mount Sirino (Basilicata, Southern Italy) is characterized by complex geological conditions favouring heterogeneous sinkhole phenomena. The most prominent geomorphological feature is Lake Sirino, formed on a large landslide deposit and frequently affected by piping-related sinkhole phenomena. abstract: Single-photon lidar possesses significant advantages in underwater weak-signal target detection. However, the complex underwater light propagation environment leads to highly random and non-uniform observation noise. Furthermore, the limited scale of real data, constrained by experimental conditions and acquisition costs, makes it difficult to meet the training requirements of deep learning detection models. abstract: Abstract This study compared four data-driven approaches, GMDH-GA, ANFIS-PSO, support vector machine (SVM), and pattern mining engine (PME), for predicting separation efficiency and diluate production flux in laboratory-scale electrodialysis treatment of Persian Gulf seawater. abstract: Due to climate change, changes in precipitation, temperature, evapotranspiration, runoff, groundwater recharge, drought and hydrological extremes are increasingly affecting the availability, distribution and dynamics of water resources. The review covers the evolution of geospatial and hydrological techniques for assessing water resources under changing climate conditions, with special emphasis on Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, hydrological and groundwater modeling, drought assessment, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and artificial intelligence. abstract: Carbon emission prediction of coastal port-industrial zones integrates industrial production, maritime logistics and spatial environmental governance. Existing models fail to simultaneously capture multi-scale temporal fluctuations and spatial correlations of industrial units under meteorological and policy interference. This paper constructs an interpretable dual-branch framework combining Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition–XGBoost (EEMD-XGBoost) and a Temporal Graph Neural Network (T-GNN). abstract: Abstract Seagrass meadows, composed of submerged marine angiosperms, provide a critical framework for studying biodiversity and ecological adaptations. The widely distributed genus Thalassia holds significant promise for sustainable environmental development. Moreover, a notable gap remains in the analysis of the Thalassia testudinum from the Caribbean, which is essential for accurately evaluating evolutionary distances between Thalassia species. abstract: Marine elasmobranchs' gut microbiota remains poorly characterized, despite its vital role in host health and ecosystem function, particularly for the longtail butterfly ray, Gymnura poecilura, a benthic predator in the Bay of Bengal. abstract: Acoustic coatings with low-frequency and broadband sound absorption are vital for underwater vehicle stealth. title: Spatial and temporal variability of Honduran benthic communities and reef functionality throughout the fourth global coral bleaching event
abstract: Mass coral bleaching events are intensifying under climate change, yet their ecological consequences remain highly context dependent. title: BIG DATA IN AGRONOMY: TECHNOLOGIES, APPLICATIONS, BENEFITS AND CHALLENGES
abstract: Big Data is becoming an important component of modern agronomy by enabling the integration, processing and analysis of large, diverse and continuously generated datasets for improved agricultural decision-making. Agricultural Big Data is generated from multiple sources, including remote sensing satellites, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, weather stations, farm machinery, field observations and historical databases. abstract: Interannual variability of Indian Summer Monsoon Rainfall (ISMR) is vital for South Asian water resources and agriculture, but its prediction is challenged by non-stationary ocean–monsoon interactions. This research develops a predictive and mapping framework for perceived soundscape quality in UGSs by integrating perceptual data collected through public participation geographic information systems, multi-scale environmental variables, and interpretable machine learning, using Hannover, Germany, as the case study. abstract: Abstract Urban heat stress is increasing in semi-arid Mediterranean towns, making the identification of Urban Cool Island (UCI) patterns essential for climate-resilient urban planning. This study developed an integrated remote sensing, GIS, and explainable machine-learning framework to map potential UCI locations in Oued Zenati, northeastern Algeria, using Landsat 9 imagery and geospatial environmental variables processed in Google Earth Engine. abstract: Oil spills pose significant threats to marine ecosystems and coastal economies; therefore, rapid and effective emergency response is critical. abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), smartphones and computer vision are expanding the use of non-contact approaches for measuring river surface velocity and estimating discharge. This review combines bibliometric analysis with a qualitative synthesis of video-based river hydrometry, with emphasis on sensing platforms, image-processing methods, validation procedures and sources of uncertainty. abstract: Abstract The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) has experienced intensive anthropogenic disturbance driven by rapid economic growth and accelerated urban expansion, resulting in increasing spatial heterogeneity of ecological processes and differentiated ecological risks. In this study, the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) was used to assess the spatiotemporal evolution of ecological environmental quality in the GBA from 2015 to 2024. abstract: Background Intestinal ischemia–reperfusion injury (IIRI) is driven by oxidative stress, excessive inflammation, Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress (ERS), and disruption of the intestinal epithelial barrier. abstract: Abstract While the basin-scale movements of North Pacific loggerheads are well documented, habitat use remains poorly understood for juveniles in the eastern North Pacific (ENP), including the exclusive economic zones (EEZs) of Mexico and the United States (U.S.). abstract: Early and correct detection of cancer regions in histopathology images is important for timely diagnosis and treatment. abstract: Abstract Coastal zones, particularly urban beaches, are dynamic social–ecological systems under growing cumulative pressures from mass tourism, urbanization, pollution, and unregulated land occupation. These stressors compromise ecological integrity and diminish nature’s contributions essential to human well-being. abstract: Introduction Biofouling is a serious problem in various industrial sectors such as shipping infrastructure, cooling water systems, and aquaculture. Biofilm formation by different types of microorganisms plays a very crucial role in this biofouling process. Biofouling on metallic surfaces accelerates aggressive corrosion processes. abstract: This study assesses the spatio-temporal evolution of the quality of groundwater intended for irrigation in the coastal aquifer of the Bay of Algiers (northern Algeria) during three sampling campaigns conducted in 2006, 2020 and 2025. abstract: Background Insulin resistance (IR) underlies many chronic diseases. While physical activity improves skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity (IS), the underlying molecular mechanisms and targeted drug strategies remain elusive. This hypothesis-generating study integrates bioinformatics and computational chemistry using public datasets; all findings are computational predictions requiring experimental validation. abstract: Deep-sea polymetallic nodule provinces host distinct benthic prokaryotic communities, yet viruses that regulate them remain largely unknown. Here, we established the viral genome dataset of the Clarion-Clipperton Fracture Zone, the world’s largest deep-sea mineral exploration region, to investigate viral diversity and ecological functions. abstract: Introduction Continental margin rift basins are characterized by highly variable present-day heat flow reflecting differential lithospheric extension. The East China Sea Shelf Basin, situated at the convergent boundary of multiple plates, represents a unique tectonic setting where Cenozoic rifting has produced an anomalously high thermal state that remains poorly documented. title: Objective wave breaker type classification from flume video using 3D CNNs across multiple plane slopes
abstract: Wave breaking is a complex and energy-intensive process in coastal hydrodynamics, yet breaker type classification remains largely subjective and discontinuous. This study enables more objective and consistent classification of breaker types through the Wave Breaker Video Classifier (WaBViC), a machine-learning framework. abstract: The report examines the evolution of risks and threats within the security environment of the Black Sea region, in the context of the shifting geopolitical landscape and the transformation of international relations. It analyses the processes shaping security dynamics -ranging from traditional military risks to contemporary hybrid, cyber, and cognitive threats. abstract: Abstract. Determining the climatic conditions under which the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) was smaller than present is important to quantify GrIS sensitivity to climate change. abstract: Marine steel structures endure cyclic loading throughout their service life. Acoustic emission (AE) is an effective passive non-destructive testing technique. title: Governance of dietary microplastic exposure risk in marine ranching in the context of climate change
abstract: Aquaculture facilities in marine ranches continuously fragment and release microplastics, which accumulate in filter-feeding shellfish and enter residents’ diets. Climate change intensifies this pathway. Warming and ultraviolet exposure accelerate the fragmentation of aquaculture plastics, while typhoons damage facilities and release microplastics in pulses and raise the health expenditure at stake for the government, enterprises, and households. abstract: Total Suspended Matter (TSM) is a primary indicator of water quality. abstract: Estuaries are subject to frequent stressors, including elevated nutrient loading and extreme hydrologic events, which impact water quality and disrupt ecosystem stability and function. The capacity of an estuary to resist changes in function in response to precipitation events is an important descriptor of ecosystem response dynamics, especially when interpreted within the context of baseline system condition and ecological state. abstract: This study addresses the early and accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, a key challenge in clinical neurology. We investigate an approach that combines morphometric biomarkers from magnetic resonance imaging with cognitive assessments, seeking to overcome the limitations of diagnostic methods that use these information sources in isolation. We analyzed data from 1,382 participants from the ADNI database, classified into cognitive controls, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer's. abstract: ABSTRACT The leader‐follower multi‐autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) fleet equipped with multi‐beam echo sounders (MBES) has become the most effective platform for large‐scale seabed topographic mapping and underwater target localization. Using kilometer‐level high‐speed underwater acoustic communication, compressed terrain data can be shared among multi‐AUV, and bathymetric SLAM (BSLAM) can then yield both precise location and consistent mapping results for the cooperative system. abstract: Medicinal plants provide an important source of structurally varied bioactive metabolites with medicinal potential; however, their effective extraction, characterization, and standardization present considerable analytical challenges. Counter-current separation (CCS) methods, such as centrifugal partition chromatography (CPC) and high-speed counter-current chromatography (HSCCC), represent advanced liquid-liquid chromatographic approaches that minimize irreversible adsorption of samples. abstract: Abstract Traditional directional regulation metasurfaces redirect reflected waves into prescribed directions, limiting their effectiveness in broadband and multistatic underwater detection. abstract: The application of machine learning to consumer neuroscience has made it possible, in principle, to predict consumer responses from media assets alone. However, the pursuit of model sophistication has outpaced attention to a foundational constraint: the quality of any predictive artificial intelligence (AI) system is bounded by the quality of the neurophysiological and biometric data used to train it, and by the rigor of the modeling procedures applied to those data. abstract: The Mar Menor, one of Europe's largest coastal lagoons, has experienced severe ecological crises over the past decade due to ongoing environmental degradation. These events, characterized by algal blooms and mass mortality of marine life have sparked widespread public concern and threaten the region's vital tourism industry. This study quantifies the impact of these environmental catastrophes on tourism across three key dimensions: economic, social, and mobility. abstract: Maritime domain awareness increasingly relies on satellite-based Earth observation (EO) for wide-area vessel monitoring. Low Earth orbit (LEO) platforms enable flexible acquisition, but optical imagery can be degraded by atmospheric turbulence and platform jitter. This paper presents a degradation-aware evaluation of deep learning-based maritime vessel detection that links algorithmic performance to the physical constraints of spaceborne optical imaging. title: Coastal Community Empowerment and Environmental Conservation Through the PALUH ASRI Social Innovation Program
abstract: Coastal ecosystems face increasing challenges due to environmental degradation, declining community welfare, and limited local capacity to manage natural resources sustainably. Social innovation-based empowerment programs are needed to integrate environmental conservation with social and economic development. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the PALUH ASRI Social Innovation Program as a model of coastal community empowerment through mangrove conservation and sustainable development approaches. abstract: With the entry into force of the Agreement on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (the Agreement), its interaction with existing institutional bodies has become an immediate governance challenge. title: Performance Evaluation of PID and AI-Based Controllers for Centrifugal Pump Operation Using Dynamic System Simulation at PT. Pelindo Energi Logistik (PEL)
abstract: The operation of centrifugal pump systems driven by AC motors is crucial for industrial fluid transportation, particularly in energy and logistics facilities where stable pressure and flow regulation are essential to maintaining operational efficiency. However, conventional control strategies often face limitations when dealing with nonlinear pump dynamics and fluctuating operating conditions. This study therefore evaluates the performance of proportional–integral–derivative (PID) and artificial intelligence (AI)-based controllers for centrifugal pump operation using dynamic system simulation.

abstract: Rural-coastal settlements in developing nations suffer from immense energy poverty, climate vulnerability and lack sustainable livelihood options. If problems of the blue economy are resolved, renewable energy deployment can be a viable solution. abstract: Food preservation challenges have positioned packaging as a rapidly evolving, innovation-driven field, with smart packaging offering transformative solutions. Among advanced materials, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have attracted growing attention due to their permanent porosity, structural tunability, high surface area, and chemical stability. abstract: The performance of the Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with chemistry (WRF-Chem) depends on the accuracy of input data and parameterisation schemes. abstract: Spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) has developed rapidly for ocean scatterometry over the past three decades. However, residual signal calibration errors, arising from inaccuracies in some key parameters and the complex space environment, degrade its performance. title: Reinforcement Failing guides the discovery of emergent physical dynamics in adaptive tumor therapy
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing scientific discovery in medicine, with reinforcement learning (RL) emerging as a promising tool for optimizing therapeutic strategies. Yet applying RL to complex scenarios such as therapy dynamics in solid tumors is constrained by the challenge of constructing training environments that are both computationally efficient and mechanistically interpretable. abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework for understanding the universe as a single continuous process of increasing complexity, operating through successive layers of organisation each built on the last. Here, we report a new katablepharid species, Katablepharis ulleungensis sp. nov., isolated from a black sandy beach in Ulleung-do, South Korea. abstract: Mediterranean coastal regions face increasingly interconnected climate risks that require adaptation across sectors and governance levels. Despite growing policy commitments and a widening portfolio of adaptation initiatives, implementation often remains fragmented. This study examines the governance conditions under which diverse climate adaptation initiatives can be integrated to support coordinated regional and local resilience. abstract: In a sea environment, the localization of ships is very important for traffic management. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) dataset is widely used to get information about ships. A detailed description of each specimen is provided, and situs inversus is discussed. Previously, reversed specimens in the family Bothidae were extremely rare, with only three reported cases, whereas the reversed condition was commonly found in the families Paralichthyidae and Pleuronectidae. title: Robust Peanut Size Grading via Scale-Augmented Ordinal Classification and Morphological Feature Fusion
abstract: Deep learning models classify peanut size accurately under fixed imaging conditions, but accuracy drops when apparent object scale changes, for example with camera-to-object distance. abstract: Global fisheries face an urgent crisis of biodiversity loss due to the unintentional capture of non-target species, known as by-catch. Traditional Electronic Monitoring (EM) systems rely on manual review of video footage, often resulting in data backlogs and delayed management responses. This research explores the integration of Edge AI—high-performance, localized artificial intelligence—onboard industrial fishing vessels to automate species identification and quantification in real time. abstract: Due to profound complexity of marine environments, significant challenges are posed to the reliability and service life of offshore wind turbine blades (WTBs). Existing structural health monitoring (SHM) techniques that are effective for land WTBs cannot directly apply to the offshore WTBs. abstract: This study investigates the relationships among overall service quality, customer satisfaction, customer engagement behaviors, and hotel brand loyalty within the sustainable tourism context of Western Thailand's accommodation sector. It further explores the roles of online reviews, hotel management responses, and artificial intelligence technology in shaping customer perceptions. title: Microplastic pollution across Bangladesh: A review of current evidence and research gaps
abstract: Pollution caused by microplastics (MP) has become an emerging environmental and public health concern in Bangladesh, which has a large number of people per square mile as well as an extensive system of rivers. This paper reviews a selection of the latest research regarding MP, including frequency and causes, routes through and methods of analysis, and environmental and human health consequences, for MP found in water, land and food in Bangladesh. abstract: B10 Cu Ni alloy is commonly subjected to both flow and external loading during marine service, but the influence of sub-yield elastic strain on its corrosion behavior and its dependence on flow velocity remain unclear. abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are spreading fast through higher education, reshaping how students learn. Yet what actually drives students to adopt these tools - especially in business schools, where ethical sensitivity and interpretive judgment matter as much as technical skill - is still not well understood. abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and the increasing frequency of extreme rainfall events, rainfall-triggered clustered landslides have become a major concern in mountainous disaster risk management due to their sudden occurrence, regional clustering, and high destructive potential. abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) has emerged as a non-intrusive method for detecting and classifying marine mammal vocalizations in near real time. Yet reliable classification from PAM remains challenging, particularly for whistles—transient, narrowband calls whose rapid temporal variations are difficult to capture from conventional spectral analyses alone. abstract: A small Mediterranean port can cut its electricity-related greenhouse-gas emissions by four fifths while paying less per kilowatt-hour than its retail tariff, provided its renewable supply is designed as an integrated portfolio. abstract: Gelatinous zooplankton (GZP) comprise a highly diverse group of marine taxa that play key ecological roles throughout the world’s oceans. However, their fragile bodies make them difficult to effectively study using traditional sampling methods such as net and optical surveys. While the recent advancements of non-invasive DNA metabarcoding techniques have become valuable tools in GZP biodiversity research, the performance of commonly used metabarcoding markers for these taxa remains poorly understood. title: Record of deep-sea Nephasoma constricticervix (Sipuncula, Golfingiidae) from the Guinea Basin (South-East Atlantic)
abstract: Six specimens of Nephasoma constricticervix are reported from the Guinea Basin from 5141–5171 m depth, collected during the Diva II expedition. This species was reported earlier from this region as “unpublished record”. Most characteristic are the long introvert hooks (up to 123 µm in our specimens), which decrease in size posteriorly and a constriction between introvert and trunk. An SEM investigation of the hooks shows their fine structure and the presence of papillae associated with the hooks.

abstract: Elasmobranchs play important ecological roles in coastal marine ecosystems, functioning as predators, mesopredators, and occasional scavengers. abstract: Abstract Reliable biomass and carbon assessments are essential for understanding mangrove forest dynamics and their role in global carbon cycling. However, field-based biomass estimation is time-consuming, labour-intensive, and costly. Remote sensing provides a practical and cost-effective alternative, particularly with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) that can capture high-resolution imagery. abstract: High interlaminar toughness is a critical requirement for 3D textile polymer composites, but its improvement remains challenging because of limited through-thickness reinforcement and the complexity of stitch-needle interactions. abstract: Strong winds and associated crosswind risks are frequent hazards that threaten vehicle stability, necessitating high-resolution wind monitoring and early warning. This study repurposes traffic surveillance cameras as the Intelligent Wind Ear (IWE), an audio-based framework for wind speed level (WSL) recognition that provides wind intensity information to support crosswind risk assessment. abstract: Diatom biomass has emerged as a promising biosorbent for removing dye pollutants from dye-bearing wastewater due to its low cost, sustainability, and abundant surface functional groups. abstract: The rapid evolution of decentralized finance (DeFi) has ushered in transformative opportunities for global financial inclusion, digital asset management, and permissionless transactions. However, the growth of DeFi also presents significant challenges related to data integrity, security, scalability, and regulatory compliance. abstract: Energy wells underpin critical technologies in the global energy transition, including geothermal energy extraction, carbon capture and storage, and underground hydrogen storage. abstract: High-resolution bathymetric digital elevation models (DEMs) support marine geoscience, but global grids can smooth fine-scale terrain where observations are sparse. abstract: Abstract To address the challenges of knowledge acquisition and low information utilization efficiency in marine diesel engine fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a question answering system integrating intent recognition and named entity recognition. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in land governance, reshaping how environmental pressures and sustainability goals are addressed. Yet the institutional processes through which human–AI collaboration takes shape remain largely unexplored. This study examines whether human–AI collaboration is emerging as a new governance paradigm in China’s land sector, and if so, through what institutional pathways and practical forms it is being articulated and implemented. abstract: This article argues that contemporary Western military innovation has become a strategic dead end. Tracing the evolution of military innovation from the Revolution in Military Affairs through counterinsurgency adaptation to today’s emphasis on disruptive innovation, experimentation and artificial intelligence, it shows how technological change has increasingly become an end in itself. abstract: Abstract The article illuminates the communicative power of graphic novels and the instructional rationale for their use for health professions education (HPE), particularly for enhancing critical thinking, empathy, and interpersonal skills. title: The Ascendance of Chinese Animation: An Analysis of Market Performance, Production Innovation, and Policy Support
abstract: This paper analyzes the recent evolution of the Chinese animation industry through the lenses of market performance, production innovation, and policy support. title: Integrated network toxicology and multiomics analyses reveal the mechanisms underlying trimethyltin chloride-induced epilepsy and the ameliorative effects of astaxanthin via NFKB1 and IL6
abstract: Trimethyltin chloride (TMT) is a ubiquitous neurotoxic organotin pollutant that induces epilepsy, while the natural marine product astaxanthin (AST) exerts potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects. However, the causal molecular mechanisms of TMT-induced epilepsy and the targeted intervention mechanism of AST remain unclear. title: Anchoring sustainability: A new paradigm for maritime clusters
abstract: The environmental footprint of maritime transport, combined with growing social and regulatory pressure to tackle pollution, has brought the shipping industry to the forefront of the sustainability agenda. The role of industry clusters is becoming increasingly relevant to this discourse, given their influence across all dimensions of sustainability. Surprisingly, although this profound relationship is well documented, it has not received sufficient scholarly attention. title: Using AI to assign building archetypes to individual buildings for enhanced resolution and accuracy in urban digital twin applications
abstract: Urban digital twins benefit from granular, building-level data, yet classifying city quarters into meaningful typologies remains a challenge. This paper presents a machine learning-based approach to automatically assign a building archetype to individual buildings using 3D CityGML data including building functions as the sole input. The archetypes range from detached single-family housing to industrial and business parks, and are defined by geometric properties and locational context rather than socio-economic factors, ensuring broad applicability across research domains. title: Advancing Nuclear Physics with Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) are becoming powerful tools in scientific research across various disciplines. In this review, we summarize recent progress in AI-assisted studies of nuclear structure and reaction observables, heavy-ion collisions and dense nuclear matter properties, many-body wave functions, experimental facilities and data analysis. This review focus on new progress since the last review in 2023, and machine learning in nuclear physics is evolving from purely data inferences to physics informed learning. title: Temporal Correlation between Ionospheric Storm-Enhanced Density Plume and Plasmaspheric Plume Occurrence
abstract: We present a statistical evidence of a temporal correlation between ionospheric storm-enhanced density (SED) and plasmaspheric plumes during magnetic storms. We identified SED plumes in 75 storms between 2010-2024 with sufficient total electron content (TEC) coverage. We also identified plasmaspheric plumes during these storms using a plasmapause asymmetry (PPA) index derived from the machine-learning-based DEN3D model. title: Competition-Aware CPC Forecasting with Near-Market Coverage
abstract: Cost-per-click (CPC) in paid search is an auction-generated outcome shaped by a competitive landscape that is only partially observable from any single advertiser’s history. From 1.66 billion Google Ads log records for a concentrated car-rental market (2021–2023), we construct a weekly panel of 1,811 keyword series over 127 weeks (218,924 keyword–week observations) and build competition-aware proxies from keyword text, CPC trajectories, and geographic market structure. title: Transversal Pooling Neural Networks
abstract: Many learning tasks require stability to small transformations while retaining sensitivity to larger ones. We introduce \emph{transversal pooling neural networks}, which generalize spatial max pooling to affine group actions. We establish equivariance to a chosen subgroup and derive explicit stability bounds for individual pooled wavelet coefficients under affine perturbations of the input. Experimentally, we demonstrate the utility of our networks in low-data environments and for predicting tropical cyclone intensification.

title: The limits of exactness: On the failure of automatic differentiation in physics-informed machine learning
abstract: Automatic differentiation (AD) lets neural networks compute derivatives of governing equations to machine precision, and this precision has made it the computational backbone of physics-informed machine learning. Yet exactness in the mathematical sense is not the same as fidelity to the physics. Here I argue that a derivative can be numerically perfect and still be the wrong derivative for the problem at hand, because AD, by construction, has no notion of the physical structure a solution must obey. title: Warm-starting PDE solvers with any-dimensional machine learning
abstract: Any-dimensional machine learning models, such as graph neural networks (GNNs), can be naturally trained and evaluated on inputs of different sizes and dimensions. Inspired by the GNN transferability literature, we show mathematical conditions under which a partial differential equation (PDE) learning-based solver can be trained in small dimensions and directly applied to solve a higher dimensional PDE in a zero-shot fashion. title: Well-posed by Design: Learning Constitutive Laws from Velocity Data using Convex Neural Network Potentials
abstract: Learning constitutive laws of complex fluids from velocity data (i.e. indirect observations) is a PDE-constrained inverse problem in which expressive neural parameterizations risk breaking the well-posedness of the forward physics model. We address this tension by learning, rather than the constitutive law itself, the dissipation potential: a scalar function whose convexity, frame-indifference, and dissipativity propagate into the underlying continuum mechanics and guarantee the structural properties needed for a well-posed and generalizable forward PDE. title: Toward Enhanced Water Detection in SWOT Pixel Clouds using Dynamic Graph Neural Networks
abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission offers unprecedented freshwater monitoring capabilities through its innovative wide-swath measurement system, which generates several data products, including the high-resolution pixel cloud (PIXC) product. However, the native PIXC water classification remains prone to systematic misclassification in urban environments, where strong radar returns from non-water surfaces are the predominant error sources. title: Real-world application of deep learning in large-scale seismic interference attenuation: A case study in the Camie field of Angola
abstract: In marine seismic acquisition, seismic interference (SI) occurs when energy from nearby external seismic source(s) is captured. It typically appears as coherent noise with linear or non-linear movement and varying amplitudes across different sail lines. SI is commonly observed and poses a challenge for seismic data processing. We present a case history of a previously proposed deep neural network (DNN)-based workflow applied for SI attenuation across a marine seismic block in the Camie Field of Angola. title: Nesterov-Accelerated Concurrent Learning for Lyapunov-Based Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Concurrent learning (CL) has recently been extended to Lyapunov-based deep neural networks (DNNs) to obtain parameter convergence under finite rather than persistent excitation. However, the existing first-order law converges slowly, especially for high-dimensional systems and overparameterized networks. To address this problem, this paper develops a Nesterov-accelerated concurrent learning (NACL) adaptation law for uncertain second-order control-affine systems. title: A Physics-Constrained Implicit Profile Network for Continuous Reconstruction of Tropical Cyclone Near-Surface Wind Profiles
abstract: Near the ocean surface, tropical cyclone winds change rapidly with height, but direct measurements are limited because aircraft dropsondes provide only sparse and irregular observations. Continuous wind profiles are important for understanding hurricane boundary-layer processes, improving storm-surge prediction, supporting offshore engineering, and assessing coastal hazards. In this study, we developed an artificial intelligence model that combines machine learning with physical principles to reconstruct continuous wind profiles from sparse observations. title: Fluorescence-enhanced Whisker Array with Vision-based Deformation Analysis for Underwater Source Localization
abstract: Deep-water biological observation is essential for understanding marine organisms and their interactions with the environment. However, conventional optical and acoustic approaches can introduce stimuli that alter animal behavior and bias biological observations. This paper proposes a fluorescence-enhanced whisker array sensing system that pinpoints underwater hydrodynamic sources through local optical readout rather than direct source imaging. title: Onboard Marine Anomaly Detection on $Φ$sat-2: From Simulation-Based Development to In-Orbit Demonstration
abstract: Onboard Artificial Intelligence can improve responsiveness and bandwidth efficiency of Earth Observation systems by processing data directly on the satellite. This paper presents the experience gained from the development, onboard integration, and post-launch adaptation of a lightweight marine anomaly detection pipeline deployed on the European Space Agency's $Φ$sat-2 mission. The application combines sea segmentation, self-supervised feature encoding of marine regions, generic anomaly detection based on deviations from a normal sea state, and optional characterization of selected anomaly type

title: Coral Grow-out Robotic Assessment System (CGRAS): Scaling Coral Recruit Monitoring Through Robotics and Computer Vision
abstract: Climate change is the largest threat to coral reefs, with increasing global impacts accelerating the need for scalable reef restoration technologies. Large-scale reef restoration depends on the mass production of corals, such as through coral aquaculture. Coral seeding with recruits grown in aquaculture facilities is a feasible restoration approach, but effective production requires consistent, high-frequency monitoring of tens of thousands of macroscopic (0.5-2mm diameter) recruits, making conventional manual assessment prohibitively labor-intensive. title: Operator-informed initialization for Fourier features physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) typically exhibit spectral bias, where some frequencies of the target function converge more slowly than others. In this work, we analyze the training dynamics of Fourier Feature PINNs in the Neural Tangent Kernel regime to address this limitation. We derive an explicit evolution equation to estimate the residual error in the frequency domain, demonstrating that the convergence rate of specific frequencies is primarily governed by the product of the differential operator's symbol and the spectral density of the initialization weights. title: BridgeCast: Bridging Ocean Wave Forecasts to Reanalysis via Flow Matching with Exogenous Variables
abstract: Ocean wave forecasting is essential for maritime safety, offshore operations, and coastal resilience, yet remains challenging due to systematic biases in physics-based models. Physical models, while widely used, rely on approximations and parameterizations that limit their accuracy under complex ocean-atmosphere conditions. To enhance ocean wave forecasting, we propose BridgeCast, within a physics-AI hybrid framework for bias correction. abstract: Hard signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) screening removes weak seismic records, but does retaining clearer waveforms improve learning enough to compensate for the discarded data? We test this question in phase picking and ambient-noise dispersion, first matching training counts and then restoring the full eligible dispersion pool at fixed compute. title: Explaining El Niño Forecasts with the Average Gradient Outer Product
abstract: An important and unresolved problem in the physical sciences is explaining the predictions made by neural networks. Several explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods have been proposed to address this problem, including gradient XAI, Integrated Gradients, and GradientSHAP. We evaluate the baseline XAI methods according to four scores: sensitivity (XAI patterns strongly affect predictions), attribution (XAI patterns reproduce the change in prediction relative to a baseline), robustness (XAI patterns remain stable for nearby inputs), and coherence (XAI patterns are spatially smooth). title: A Model-Agnostic Physics-Guided Adapter for Few-Shot Transfer of Coastal Flood Prediction Models to Unseen Regions
abstract: Deep learning surrogates can produce high-resolution coastal flood maps orders of magnitude faster than physics-based hydrodynamic simulators, yet transferring them to new coastal regions remains costly, since generating target-region data for fine-tuning typically requires numerous time-consuming simulations. To tackle this bottleneck, we introduce the Physics Adapter (PA), a compact, architecture-agnostic adaptation interface that enables efficient few-shot transfer of flood prediction models across diverse coastal regions. title: AquaWAM: A Dynamics-aware World Action Model for Underwater Embodied Agents
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) are becoming increasingly important and useful for embodied intelligence, as they enable robots to anticipate the consequences of candidate actions before interacting with the physical environment. However, underwater robots are usually subject to passive dynamics, such as inertia, buoyancy, hydrodynamic drag, and persistent drift, which can continue to affect the vehicle even after an action is completed. title: Textual Environmental Context and Spatial Graphs for LLM-Based Regional SST Forecasting
abstract: Sea surface temperature (SST) forecasting depends on local temporal persistence, regional spatial dependence, and environmental conditions that evolve with the forecast date. We study how these heterogeneous conditions can be presented to a large language model (LLM) for regional multi-step forecasting without serializing the full SST grid as text. title: PIC-UIE: Predicting Image-Adaptive Corrections for Lightweight Underwater Image Enhancement
abstract: Underwater image enhancement (UIE) aims to restore visibility, color fidelity, and structural detail from images degraded by wavelength-dependent attenuation and backscatter. State-of-the-art UIE methods often rely on large backbones and dense image-to-image prediction, limiting their practicality for edge deployment. title: Initial condition recovery in nonlinear damped viscous photoacoustic tomography using a convolutional neural network-guided gradient-free optimization framework
abstract: Photoacoustic tomography (PAT) is a hybrid imaging modality that combines high optical contrast with high ultrasonic resolution for biomedical imaging applications. In this work, we investigate the inverse problem of recovering the initial pressure distribution from boundary measurements in the presence of nonlinear acoustic propagation and viscous attenuation effects. title: Bilevel optimization for data-driven learning of Koopman embeddings using kernel-based autoencoders
abstract: Koopman operator theory provides a linear framework for analyzing nonlinear dynamical systems and has become a major tool for data-driven modeling. A central challenge, however, is that finite-dimensional approximations computed by methods such as extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) require the dictionary to be specified a priori. title: ClimateBench v2.0: Probabilistic Climate Model Benchmarking
abstract: We present ClimateBench v2, a standardized protocol for evaluating climate models on diagnostics expected to be informative for their skill in projecting mid-century regional temperature and precipitation changes. The protocol is designed to evaluate any physics-based, data-driven, or hybrid climate model on equal footing using a common set of observational and out-of-distribution tests. title: A PyTorch Library for Hyperspectral Image Models: Technical Report
abstract: Hyperspectral remote sensing has advanced across diverse deep learning paradigms, including spectral spatial CNNs, Vision Transformers, Mamba, graph neural networks, Kolmogorov Arnold networks, and self supervised masked autoencoding. Yet progress remains hindered by fragmented repositories, incompatible tensor conventions, and non standardized evaluation. title: DeepMIDE: A Multivariate Spatio-Temporal Method for Ultra-Scale Offshore Wind Energy Forecasting
abstract: To unlock access to stronger winds, the offshore wind industry is advancing with significantly larger and taller wind turbines. This massive upscaling motivates a departure from univariate wind forecasting methods that traditionally focused on a single representative height. To fill this gap, we propose DeepMIDE—a statistical deep learning method which jointly models the offshore wind speeds across space, time, and height. title: Detecting Nighttime Anomalies from NASA Black Marble Using a Generalized Spatio-Temporally Robust Framework of Machine Leaning Ensembles
abstract: Nighttime lights from NASA's Black Marble product suite capture thermal and light emission signals from anomalous events including fires, volcanic eruptions, and gas flaring. Existing detection approaches rely primarily on thermal bands, limiting sensitivity to weaker signals. We propose a novel machine learning framework that jointly models Black Marble M-band and Day/Night Band (DNB) signals to derive a generalized, spatio-temporally robust ensemble of anomaly detectors. title: Butterfly Effect Confirmed in Global AI Weather Models: Evidence from Tropical Cyclone Forecasting
abstract: A paradox recently emerged in artificial intelligence (AI) weather prediction research. While some claim AI weather models cannot simulate atmospheric butterfly effect, this conflicts with AI models' limited predictability and advances in AI ensemble forecasting. This study demonstrates via counterexamples that the butterfly effect does exist in AI weather predictions. For Super Typhoon Khanun, AI predictions are constrained by a double-attractor system. title: Coarse-to-fine multi-resolution hash encoding for implicit full waveform inversion
abstract: Implicit full waveform inversion (IFWI) reparameterizes the velocity model with a neural network, but it suffers from spectral bias and requires many iterations to converge. abstract: When recalling lists of concepts (e.g., animals) during the semantic fluency task (SFT), both humans and large language models (LLMs) organise their output into clusters of related items (e.g., sea animals) that are punctuated by strategic switches between clusters. title: Co-Designing Community-Centered AI Education for Adults: A Midwestern Case Study
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) education is increasingly important, yet adults outside higher education receive less attention. We report a case study of an AI education session with 54 adults (48 in-person and 6 virtual) in a predominantly African American community on the east side of a major Midwestern city. We ask: "What does AI education for adults outside formal educational systems look like in practice?" and "What does this AI education session reveal about AI literacy at the community level?" title: Low latency global carbon budget reveals strong land sink recovery in 2025
abstract: The atmospheric CO2 growth rate fell sharply in 2025, from a record 3.76 $\pm$ 0.09 ppm yr-1 in 2024 to 2.06 $\pm$ 0.09 ppm yr-1 (NOAA marine boundary layer observations), below the 2015-2022 mean of 2.47 ppm yr-1, even as fossil CO2 emissions rose by 0.7% to 10.38 GtC yr-1. abstract: Machine-learning models for physical systems are currently evaluated primarily through errors between predicted and reference states and, increasingly, through tests of physical consistency. These metrics assess whether predictions are accurate and satisfy selected physical requirements, but provide limited insight into whether learned trajectories reproduce the underlying dynamics. abstract: We present Video2SwimFish, an automated pipeline and benchmark for building controllable fish assets from real-fish videos for underwater embodied AI. abstract: Quantum federated learning (QFL) has emerged as a promising approach for collaboratively training compact quantum neural networks (QNNs) over distributed private data on resource-constrained devices. However, differences in device capabilities make a single shared QNN architecture unsuitable for all clients. title: Adjoint-based shape optimization of a ship hull using a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) assisted propulsion surrogate model
abstract: Adjoint-based shape optimization of ship hulls is a powerful tool for addressing high-dimensional design problems in naval architecture, particularly in minimizing the ship resistance. However, its application to vessels that employ complex propulsion systems introduces significant challenges. They arise from the need for transient simulations extending over long periods of time with small time steps and from the reverse temporal propagation of the primal and adjoint solutions. title: Tri-FusionNet: Enhancing image description generation with transformer-based fusion network and dual attention mechanism
abstract: Captioning of images is a crucial step towards helping artificial intelligence to perceive images and create relatable language descriptions. Nevertheless, most current captioning models are not very effective at integrating fine-grained visual information with global contextual information, also leading to high correspondence between visual and text representations. We suggest Tri-FusionNet to resolve these difficulties, a new transformer-based image description generation model. title: SonarVoxNet: Diver Detection in 3D Bounding Box using 3D Sonar
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) assisting human divers must continuously track not only the diver's 3D position but also their full-body orientation. However, vision-based perception is unreliable underwater, and forward-looking sonar -- despite being widely used -- discards the elevation information needed for orientation estimation, posing a fundamental limitation.
