title: Catching fire – On cremations in Late Iron Age Åland Islands, Baltic sea
abstract: The cremation was an important part of the mortuary rituals in Late Iron Age Åland Islands, c.550–1050 CE. More than 10 000 burial mounds with cremations found in c.440 farmstead cemeteries are known from the Åland Islands. The burial practice is characteristic of those common in Eastern Sweden. We here analyse how the cremation was carried out, considering detailed macroscopic analyses of the level of calcination of the cremated remains of humans and included animals. title: Cool‐Water Dolphins Have Larger Appendages Than Warm‐Water Dolphins
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Endothermic marine mammals face significant thermoregulatory challenges due to heat loss in the highly conductive marine environment. Allen's rule states that endothermic animals in cold environments have smaller appendages than those in warmer environments. While body size adaptations in marine mammals are well‐studied, the role of appendage size as an adaptation to different thermal habitats remains unclear. title: Contrasting nutritional proxies and methylmercury exposure in zooplankton delivered by little auks across Greenland and Svalbard
abstract: Zooplankton forms a key trophic interface in Arctic marine ecosystems, transferring both nutritional resources and contaminants to higher consumers. Yet these dimensions are rarely evaluated together in the prey actually selected and delivered by predators under natural foraging conditions. title: Regional Trends in Northern Hemisphere Summer Extratropical Cyclone Activity and Their Link to Precipitation and Temperature Trends
abstract: Abstract In recent years a robust weakening of the storm tracks has been identified in reanalysis data. This trend has been linked to coinciding changes in surface temperature extremes and precipitation over land. Here we use a surface‐based metric to quantify regional trends in the boreal summertime low‐level extratropical cyclone activity (ECA) and link this to surface impacts. abstract: The northern Tropical Americas (NTA) is influenced by multiple large-scale hydroclimate drivers, including the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), whose position and strength varied significantly during the Late Pleistocene (130–11.7 kyr BP). Since the 1960s, paleoclimate studies have provided valuable but often scattered insights into environmental changes and precipitation variability. abstract: The method of computing the euphotic depth, the depth horizon in the ocean above which light is sufficient for net primary production, has lacked consensus in the literature. Although many still use a % light level as a definition, a practice which dominates textbooks in oceanography, the modeling community uses a constant basal respiration to set the threshold. title: Predicting environmental health-related search patterns using freely available digital and reanalysis data: A critical evaluation of Google Trends and global datasets for Morocco
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation increasingly threaten urban public health, yet monitoring infrastructure is often unavailable in resource-constrained settings. This study develops and critically evaluates a machine learning framework that predicts environmental health-related search behavior , used as a low-cost digital proxy rather than a measure of clinical burden, in Morocco using exclusively open-access global datasets. title: TREND AND ANOMALY OF TEMPERATURE SERIES IN WEST AFRICAN COASTAL URBAN AREAS: THE CASE OF ABIDJAN, CÔTE D'IVOIRE (1985-2024)
abstract: Climate change is accompanied by a growing intensification of temperatures at the local scale, as observed in several cities of the sub-region, yet their evolution and trends remain insufficiently quantified. This study aims to examine the trends and anomalies of temperatures in the city of Abidjan over the period 1985-2024. abstract: Large-scale offshore aquaculture vessels provide an effective approach for expanding marine aquaculture; however, the complex flow characteristics induced by water circulation systems and vessel motion remain insufficiently understood. abstract: Abstract Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) formation plays a crucial role in the climate system by driving the lower branch of the global overturning circulation, redistributing heat and salt, storing anthropogenic carbon dioxide, and delivering oxygen to the deep ocean. title: Changing wind hazards for Mediterranean airports: the case of Cyclone Harry (2026)
abstract: Abstract Mediterranean storms and cyclones can generate hazardous wind conditions with major implications for aviation, yet the link between large-scale dynamics and airport-scale impacts remains poorly quantified. abstract: Abstract Bomb cyclones are high-impact extratropical cyclones characterized by rapid deepening. Although their climatology and long-term changes over the North Pacific (NP) have attracted considerable attention recently, it remains unclear whether bomb cyclone statistics are robust across different cyclone tracking algorithms. abstract: Abstract Relative sea surface temperature (SST), defined as local SST minus the tropical mean, is linked to tropical cyclone (TC) size growth, but its role in coupled size‐intensity evolution remains unclear. Using 23 years of global observations, we show that relative SST regulates very deep convection (infrared brightness temperature <208K), thereby modulating both TC intensification and size expansion. title: Multiscale ENSO–IOD–MJO Interactions Modulating Indian Summer Monsoon Rainfall Variability
abstract: The Indian Summer Monsoon Rainfall (ISMR) is strongly influenced by large-scale climate variability associated with the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), and the Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO). While the individual influences of these climate modes on the monsoon are well established, their combined impact across interannual and intraseasonal timescales remains insufficiently understood. title: Real-time sonar simulation for UUVs using rasterization and omnidirectional screen space reflections
abstract: Since real-world testing can be costly, risky, and difficult to reproduce, sonar simulation has become an important tool for developing and validating perception and navigation algorithms for unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs). This work introduces a real-time sonar simulation framework integrated into the NauSim platform. title: Nonlinear dynamics of time-variable slope circulation
abstract: Abstract. Bottom topography strongly constrains ocean circulation in the Arctic, and both theory and numerical modeling suggest that nonlinear flow–topography interactions influence slope-following currents. Yet, how such interactions modify the circulation response to time-variable surface forcing remains poorly understood. Using idealized shallow-water simulations of flow over a corrugated slope in a re-entrant channel, we investigate how nonlinear features arise and evolve under oscillatory forcing. title: Long-term spatio-temporal assessment of thermal comfort in Antalya (Türkiye) using the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI)
abstract: Climate change and the increasing frequency of extreme heat events have intensified thermal stress, particularly in Mediterranean regions, posing significant challenges to human health, quality of life, and sustainable urban development. Therefore, accurate assessment of outdoor thermal comfort has become increasingly important for supporting climate adaptation and planning strategies. This study aims to investigate the long-term (2000–2025) spatio-temporal changes of thermal comfort in Antalya (Türkiye) using the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI). title: Mitigating valvetrain noise and vibration in a medium-speed marine engine using electro-hydraulic fully variable valve actuation
abstract: Fully variable electro-hydraulic valve actuation (EHVA) is an enabling technology for next-generation internal combustion engines (ICE). The system provides in-cycle control strategies for ultra-efficient, fuel-flexible low temperature combustion (LTC) engines meeting the strictest emission norms. This study focuses on reducing the noise and vibration of EHVA systems, an aspect that remains less explored than performance and combustion optimisation. abstract: A multi-field coupled numerical model integrating fluid flow, convective heat transfer, and thermal stress is established for a shark-skin-inspired V-shaped micro-rib heat exchange tube. Using the shear stress transport (SST) k-ω model, its thermal–hydraulic performance is compared with a smooth tube, revealing the mechanism of vortex-induced thermal boundary layer disturbance. abstract: Antarctic ice mass loss has intensified in recent decades. However, short-term glacier velocity variability in Victoria Land, East Antarctica, remains poorly documented. This study used Sentinel-1 SLC data and environmental records from 2017 to 2025 to quantify glacier-velocity variability in Victoria Land and examine its model-based statistical associations with selected atmospheric and oceanic variables using XGBoost–SHAP. abstract: Abstract. title: Strategic roadmaps for Industry 4.0 implementation in smart manufacturing
abstract: Manufacturing is undergoing a profound transformation driven by digitalization, reshaping traditional processes into interconnected and intelligent systems. Industry 4.0, a contemporary strategy rooted in smart manufacturing principles, integrates advanced technologies such as cyber-physical systems (CPS), internet of things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins (DT), cloud computing, and big data analytics. abstract: Local erosion around foundation elements, generally referred to as ’scour’, is of major concern when designing hydraulic structures. When placed in natural open water systems, these structures influence the local dynamics of the flow and bed, which could result in lowering of the embedment level, with potentially severe consequences. abstract: This study evaluates the field performance of hatchery produced Asian green mussel, Perna viridis (Linnaeus, 1758) seed across three estuarine sites viz., Ashtamudi, Neendakara, and Vellimon in Kollam District, Kerala, south India, under varying stocking densities. title: A >100-million-year record of soft-sediment deformation structures in incoming-plate sediments of the Japan Trench Subduction Zone
abstract: Soft-sediment deformation structures (SSDS) are commonly used to infer past geological events, yet their long-term variability in marine sediment archives remains poorly constrained. We investigate the types, abundance, and temporal variations of SSDS throughout a 286.89-m sediment succession spanning >100 million years, recovered during the International Ocean Drilling Program (IODP) Expedition 405 at Site C0026 on the incoming Pacific Plate prior to the Japan Trench subduction. abstract: Remote sensing of intertidal seaweed habitats is challenged by overlapping spectral signals from multiple co-occurring species groups, making it difficult to predict their distributions. This study applies Hierarchical Modelling of Species Communities (HMSC), a joint species distribution framework that accounts for statistical dependencies and co-occurrence patterns among species groups, thereby improving prediction accuracy, particularly for groups that are otherwise difficult to model individually. abstract: Arctic atmospheric circulation and near-surface temperature are physically coupled, yet it remains unclear whether their spatial coherence changes in the same way across seasons. abstract: Abstract. As hydrological trends shift in response to a warming climate, accurate characterization of hydrologic conditions and hydrologic change are imperative for water resources management, which is particularly important in the Canadian Prairies. In the study herein, a HydroGeoSphere (HGS) fully integrated groundwater–surface water (GW–SW) model is employed to evaluate trends and drivers of surface and subsurface water storage changes in the South Saskatchewan River Basin (SSRB). title: Non-tidal ocean loading from Río de la Plata storm surges: empirical modeling at the Argentine–German Geodetic Observatory (AGGO) over its first decade of operation
abstract: Frequent storm surges in the Río de la Plata estuary produce non-tidal ocean loading signals detectable at the Argentine–German Geodetic Observatory (AGGO), affecting the space geodetic and gravimetric techniques co-located at the site. An empirical model of water level variations across the estuary is developed for the period 2016–2025, covering the first decade of operation of AGGO, using observations from seven tide gauge stations distributed along the Río de la Plata, complemented by two modeled stations derived from astronomical tidal predictions and a global storm surge model. title: Effect of hydrostatic pressure on transport-reaction processes of cement paste under sulfate attack
abstract: Cementitious materials in deep-sea environments may be simultaneously subjected to hydrostatic pressure and sulfate exposure, leading to coupled transport–reaction processes that differ from those under conventional sulfate attack. title: Beyond Land Titles: Rights Documentation, Boundary Clarity and Exposure to Community Land Conflicts in Kimbinga, Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract: In legally plural settings, land tenure security depends not only on the existence of a formal title but also on the ability to prove a right, identify and recognize its spatial boundaries, and coordinate the authorities that make it socially and institutionally enforceable. This article presents an analytical reanalysis of a cross-sectional household survey conducted in Kimbinga, Bulungu Territory, Kwilu Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), involving 384 households.

abstract: Abstract Precipitation variability in the MATOPIBA region, located in northern Northeast Brazil, exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity and is strongly influenced by large-scale ocean–atmosphere interactions. This study investigates trends, non-stationarity, and ocean–atmosphere teleconnections of daily precipitation over the period 1979–2020 using CPC/NOAA rainfall data and sea surface temperature (SST) fields from the Tropical Atlantic and Equatorial Pacific. abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) estimation from satellite-derived Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) is often biased in humid tropical environments because aerosol water uptake enhances optical extinction without a corresponding increase in dry particulate mass. This study develops a physics-informed, non-linear AOD-to-PM2.5 conversion framework that explicitly accounts for hygroscopic growth. In the third release version of the low‐resolution Energy Exascale Earth System Model (E3SMv3), the representation of the stratosphere is improved through vertical grid refinement in the lower stratosphere and the implementation of the linearized ozone scheme version 3 (Linozv3). abstract: Abstract Earth's rotation imposes a dynamical barrier on the free propagation of internal tides at high latitudes, raising questions about the fate of tidal energy poleward of the critical latitude. Satellite observations reveal spiral internal solitary waves (ISWs) along the continental slope of the South Orkney Plateau. abstract: Abstract This paper presents recent improvements in the cyber-physical test method for wind-assisted ships at SINTEF Ocean. In particular, a dynamic lifting line method, that interacts in real-time with the physical ship model, enables now modelling transient aerodynamic effects, sail-hull interaction, and sail-sail interactions. abstract: Abstract. title: Storm-Track Variability in Synoptic Forcing During Heavy Lake-Effect Snow Events over Lake Michigan
abstract: Lake-effect snow (LES) has traditionally been studied from a mesoscale perspective, with comparatively less attention devoted to the role of synoptic-scale forcing. This study quantifies the prevalence and magnitude of synoptic forcing during 116 heavy LES events affecting the eastern shore of Lake Michigan between 1997 and 2024. abstract: Abstract The Eastern Subpolar North Atlantic (E‐SPNA) upper ocean experiences pronounced interannual salinity variations that influence the global overturning circulation, yet a quantitative understanding of their life cycle remains lacking. Based on an ocean circulation state estimate, we combine budget analysis with particle tracking to quantify the generation and propagation of E‐SPNA salinity anomalies. abstract: The intensification of moist heat extremes under global warming represents a critical hazard to human health and ecosystem stability. However, the distinct spatiotemporal evolutionary patterns of moist heatwaves (MHWs; relative humidity ≥40%) versus extreme moist heatwaves (EMHWs; relative humidity ≥70%) across different latitudinal zones remain insufficiently understood. abstract: Mesh-free Lagrangian methods including smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) are ideal for complex ocean engineering involving large free-surface deformations, yet their high computational cost in 3D large-scale domains remains a barrier. abstract: Accurately forecasting reservoir water volumes is crucial for climate change adaptation, drought mitigation, and provides a basis for energy planning and management, particularly in continental basins, where hydrological variability poses challenges to traditional modeling. abstract: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) increasingly support long-duration ocean observation, yet their mission endurance remains constrained by limited onboard energy storage. abstract: Abstract Dynamic bedforms, such as sand waves, may pose a threat to offshore energy infrastructure. Due to their impact on seabed mobility, dredging is often required to reduce risks, for example, to avoid cable exposure. abstract: The safety of mooring systems is critical for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines (FOWTs), yet contact-based tension monitoring suffers from difficult installation, susceptibility to damage and limited long-term reliability. This study proposes a non-contact monitoring method based on the Vector Form Intrinsic Finite Element (VFIFE), which determines mooring tension from the measured motion of the floating platform. abstract: East Asian cold surges develop through several distinct spatiotemporal evolution patterns, each characterized by a different intensity and duration. abstract: Ports play a critical role in global trade infrastructure, however they are also a significant source of GHG emissions, energy use as well as marine environmental damage. abstract: The accurate and rapid estimation of tsunami sources immediately after an earthquake is essential for real-time tsunami forecasting. abstract: This study investigates the quantitative effects of external wake interactions and inter-farm spacing within a large-scale offshore wind cluster, focusing on the Shinan Cluster in Korea. abstract: Airborne microplastic (MP) particles are transported through the atmosphere, yet direct measurements at altitude remain scarce. We developed a novel uncrewed aerial system (UAS)-based method for in situ MP sampling within and above the atmospheric boundary layer. abstract: Environmental remediation has started to take advantage of all the advantages of Industry 5.0: sustainabililty, resilience and human-centric techologies. abstract: In the context of a changing climate, a comprehensive assessment is required of the impact of climatic conditions on the comfort of the living environment. This study evaluates changes in bioclimatic indices assessed on the basis of model reanalysis across the marine and land Arctic within the boundaries of the WMO Arctic Regional Climate Center — Network under ongoing climate change. abstract: Autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) are increasingly deployed for hydrographic survey, coastal observation, and unmanned maritime monitoring. abstract: The Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) is a crucial component of the global climate system, significantly influencing weather patterns, agriculture, and water resources across India. abstract: Coupled chloride–sulfate attack is a key cause of durability degradation in concrete structures in coastal and saline environments. abstract: Abstract Planetary boundary layer (PBL) turbulence modulates tropical cyclone (TC) intensity through competing mechanisms: (a) frictional dissipation that weakens TCs and (b) frictional convergence that drives stronger low‐level inflow and intensifies TCs. abstract: Abstract Lightning is an Essential Climate Variable, yet long‐term detection records may be compromised by changes in detection technology. abstract: Multistage centrifugal pumps operating as turbines (PATs) are important devices for hydraulic energy recovery. abstract: Climate change and extreme weather are increasing the vulnerability of power systems globally, particularly in emerging economies such as Indonesia. abstract: Shell structures are widely used in aerospace, automotive, marine, and civil engineering due to their high stiffness-to-weight ratio and efficient load-carrying capability. abstract: Abstract Rainfall-induced shallow landslides are typically attributed to short-term meteorological triggers such as rainfall intensity and duration. This study investigates the role of antecedent dry spells on landslide occurrence in the clay-rich terrains of the eastern Black Sea region of Türkiye. abstract: Abstract Three of Jupiter’s Galilean satellites—Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto—are of particular scientific interest due to their icy shells and suspected subsurface oceans. However, the radar properties of the icy satellites have not been measured since observations in 1987–1991. Because radio waves can penetrate pure ice to considerable depths, radar observations provide a powerful means of characterizing the subsurface properties of the icy shells of these satellites, offering key insights into planetary evolution. abstract: Compaction of soft subsurface layers occurs through different mechanisms, namely con- solidation, viscous compression, autocompaction, and shrinkage. title: Beyond the slip paradigm: Distributed inelastic deformation as a missing tsunami source class
abstract: Tsunami source models generally assume that tsunami-generating deformation is localized on fault surfaces and is therefore represented entirely by fault slip. abstract: The Weather and Climate Science for Service Partnership (WCSSP) India, launched in 2017, builds long-term research partnerships between the UK and India to strengthen weather and climate science. Building on an established history of collaboration, the programme focuses on improving risk-based forecasting of natural hazards through advances in scientific understanding, methods, and tools. abstract: In the context of the current digitalisation of education and the growing importance of research, special attention is being paid to developing students' competencies through interdisciplinary approaches. abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the feeding behavior of deformed and normal benthic foraminifera (Protista, Rhizaria) of the species Ammonia veneta . abstract: Abstract. The implementation of short-lived halogen (SLH) sources and atmospheric chemistry in the Community Earth System Model v1 (CESM1), has extended the capabilities of this state-of-the-art model to study how SLH chemistry alters the oxidative capacity of the atmosphere and, consequently, the Earth’s climate. abstract: Understanding regional wetting and drying under global warming remains challenging. Here we show, using global climate simulations and 191 records of past climate, that terrestrial moisture changes over the past 21,000 years follow a pronounced latitudinal pattern. abstract: Fatigue damage limits the service life of metallic structures, including mobile working machines. title: Tree-ring-derived April–July drought variability in the western Loess Plateau of China over the last four centuries and its linkage to the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation
abstract: Short instrumental records limit assessment of long-term drought variability on the western Loess Plateau of China. In this paper, we reconstructed April–July self-calibrating Palmer Drought Severity Index (scPDSI) variability for the last four centuries (1610–2016 CE) using a tree-ring width chronology obtained from Pinus tabuliformis in the Kongtong Mountains. title: Halogen behaviour during mantle melting and metasomatism recorded by peridotite xenoliths from Tariat, Mongolia
abstract: Peridotite xenoliths from the Tariat region of Mongolia are representative of the MORB-source mantle in terms of trace element patterns and radiogenic isotopic ratios, with rare metasomatic enrichments. A selection of 21 lherzolites with MgO of 37–44 wt% were analysed for halogens (F, Cl, Br, I) by a combination of ion microprobe in clinopyroxene (CPX) orthopyroxene (OPX), olivine (OL), and spinel (SP), and bulk rock methods. title: Precipitation nowcasting model based on multi-source data fusion and efficient additive attention
abstract: Short-term precipitation nowcasting serves as an indispensable technical support for the early warning and risk management of meteorological hazards. To improve the nowcasting accuracy by leveraging complementary information from multi-source data, this study proposes a precipitation nowcasting model based on multi-source data fusion and efficient additive attention (EAA-MNFP). title: Towards an optimisation of mooring design for floating offshore wind turbines: Mathematical formalisation of a novel physically-based motion-related constraint
abstract: Early-stage mooring design for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines (FOWTs) relies on empirical poorly standardised motion-related constraints that neglect system dynamics. This work proposes a novel performance-driven methodology that dynamically links allowable offsets to the physical response of the system. A validated OpenFAST model of the NREL 5 MW wind turbine on the OC3 Hywind spar-type floating platform, Magnitude-Squared Coherence, and Pearson’s correlation analyses, were used to investigate FOWT dynamics and identify key physical relationships underpinning the proposed motion-related desi

title: How Predictable Was the Extreme Precipitation Preceding the May 2019 Arkansas River Floods?
abstract: Abstract In May 2019, unprecedented extreme rainfall over the central United States (US) facilitated severe flooding along the Arkansas River. The well‐documented relationship between atmospheric rivers (ARs) and central US heavy precipitation motivated investigation into AR relevance to this event and its predictability on extended timescales. title: Offshore wind profile characteristics and their impact on floating wind turbine power production
abstract: Abstract. In this study, we investigate the impact of vertical wind shear and wind speed inversions on the power production of a floating offshore wind turbine. Using nacelle-mounted wind lidar data from a 6 MW turbine at the Hywind Scotland wind farm, we analyse inflow conditions and turbine performance during summer and autumn. The wind climatology shows that 33 % of examined cases exhibit non-standard wind profiles within the rotor-swept area, including negative shear and wind speed inversions. title: Finite-element analysis to assess the influence of cutback geometry on strain concentration in concrete-weight coated pipelines
abstract: Strain concentration at the field joints of concrete-weight coated (CWC) pipelines, driven by stiffness discontinuities between coated and uncoated sections, remains a key design challenge because the effects of cutback geometry are not fully understood, especially when different pipe stiffnesses are envisageable. This study introduces a stiffness-dependent framework to quantify how cutback geometry influences strain concentration across the investigated pipe configurations. A validated three-dimensional finite-element model is used within a Box-Behnken design (BBD) framework to quantify the i
journal: Journal of Ocean Engineering and Science
institutions: Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology

title: Anthropogenic aerosol reduction contributes to faster flash drought onset in a changing climate
abstract: Flash droughts have emerged as severe hazards, posing growing challenges to natural and socioeconomic systems, yet the influence of recent aerosol reductions on their onset remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impacts of aerosols and their underlying mechanisms using multi-source observations and large-ensemble climate simulations. Lower aerosol levels are increasingly linked to severe soil moisture deficits, with aerosol effects on onset-speed variability intensifying across 69.2% of regions. title: TYPOLOGY OF CALENDAR YEARS AND THERMAL REGIME DYNAMICS UNDER GLOBAL WARMING: RISK ASSESSMENT FOR ALMATY
abstract: The aim of this work was to develop a statistically substantiated typology of thermal conditions of calendar years for Almaty and a quantitative analysis of its transformation against the background of ongoing climate change. A two-stage approach was used for the study. The first stage: dimensionality reduction using principal component analysis (PCA) followed by k-means clustering to identify integral year types. title: European Climate Signals in Water Budget Dynamics
abstract: Monitoring the water budget helps us understand and manage the available water in a specific area, as well as track its use. Knowing the water budget (i.e., the difference between water inflow and outflow) allows us to predict water shortages or surpluses. In these times of climate change, the risk of extreme events such as droughts and floods is rising. The study considered the area of the European continent, classified according to the Koppen-Geiger climate zones, as it features a highly diverse climate. This research aims to evaluate the water budget across Europe and perform further analys

title: Rossby wave diversion as a source of subseasonal predictability for extreme Meiyu-Baiu events
abstract: Meiyu-Baiu, the distinct rainy season in subtropical East Asia, is characterized by a quasi-stationary Meiyu-Baiu Front (MBF) along which excessive rainfall and mega floods often occur. This study shows that the spatial stationarity of MBF, and thus its potential to generate catastrophic flooding is inherently modulated by synoptic-scale disturbances over northeastern East Asia. The activity of these disturbances is coupled with the Northern Annular Mode (NAM) and the subtropical westerly jet across the subseasosnal timescales. institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory (Zhuhai)

title: Simulating jökulhlaups from an ice-marginal lake within a 2D model of subglacial drainage and basal sliding
abstract: Abstract. Ice-marginal lakes are an increasingly common feature of glacierised landscapes, and their sudden drainage beneath glaciers (a jökulhlaup) can threaten downstream communities and infrastructure. Numerous efforts to model jökulhlaups have been made, however, because these models are 1D representations of a single channel connected to a lake, they cannot simulate lateral jökulhlaup propagation through the subglacial system. institutions: Centre for Polar Observation and Modelling

title: Anthropogenic aerosol forcing of European windstorms in CMIP6 climate models
abstract: A recently developed set of historical storm reconstructions were extensively validated by insurance loss data and revealed how European windstorm damages were three times higher in the 1980s and '90s compared to a few decades before and since. A better understanding of these slower fluctuations could improve how this costly risk is managed. Here, we explore the impacts of anthropogenic aerosols (AA) on European property damage using results from DAMIP (Detection and Attribution Model Intercomparison Project) climate model experiments. Multimodel mean DAMIP results indicate AA boosted European
journal: Natural hazards and earth system sciences

title: Dependence of Neutralized Charge Amount on Meteorological Conditions in Summertime Lightning Discharges in Japan
abstract: Abstract Lightning discharges in Gunma Prefecture, Japan, from June–September 2023 were analyzed to explore the dependence of the neutralized charge amount on cloud structures embedded in weather systems, mainly based on in situ measurements of the ground‐based electric field, radar and satellite remote sensing, and numerical simulations using a bulk lightning model. title: Assessing the Sustainability Performance of Fishing Harbors Under Uncertainty: A Gaussian‐Neutrosophic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Fishing harbors are increasingly required to meet sustainability expectations associated with the environmental, social, and economic development goals. Accordingly, assessing their sustainability performance has become an important concern for both policymakers, harbor operating organizations, and harbor managers. This study develops a decision support system (DSS) within a neutrosophic environment to evaluate the sustainability performance of small‐scale fishing harbors. title: Spaceborne multi-sensor tracking reveals hydrologic decoupling during the record-breaking Sahara flood
abstract: Satellite remote sensing enables large-scale quantification of extreme hydrologic events in data-scarce regions, yet the integration of multi-sensor observations to resolve hydrologic responses remains limited. The record-breaking 2024 Sahara flood presents a unique opportunity to evaluate satellite-based characterisation of hydrologic extremes in hyper-arid environments. By integrating multi-sensor satellite observations of precipitation, surface inundation, and terrestrial water storage, we provide a comprehensive assessment of this event’s hydrologic scope. institutions: Nanjing Institute of Geography and Limnology
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Interlocking, rearrangement and progressive failure in rubble‑mound breakwaters
abstract: Rubble-mound breakwater stability is commonly assessed through Hudson- and Van der Meer-type empirical formulae, which relate wave loading, armour properties and geometry to global stability and damage parameters. These formulae remain the design basis, but they do not explicitly describe how inter-block contacts reorganise under repeated wave loading. A testable contact-network interpretation of progressive rubble-mound failure is developed here. The armour layer is treated as a granular assembly whose load-carrying capacity depends on the redundancy and persistence of load-bearing contacts.

title: Intersections of climate and society: cold stress vulnerability in Northern Norway
abstract: Extreme cold profoundly shapes health, livelihoods, and social well-being in northern communities, yet research on social vulnerability to such conditions remains limited. This study provides a framework for integrating social, demographic, infrastructural, and institutional dimensions into an assessment of vulnerability to extreme cold in northern Norway. title: From concept to action: Driving impact through responsible research practices in the International Polar Year 2032–2033 An early career perspective
abstract: Regions at the poles are warming at rates two to four times higher than the global average, driving profound environmental, societal, and geopolitical changes. As Polar Early Career Researchers with careers extending into and beyond the 5th International Polar Year in 2032–2033, we have a responsibility to shape research practices that are impactful, ethical, and sustainable. We argue that current definitions of research impact often prioritize narrow, quantifiable metrics, overlooking cultural, environmental, and long-term consequences. institutions: Centre for Arctic Gas Hydrate, Environment and Climate

title: Implementation of a New Paradigm for Hydrometeorological Support for Enterprise Leaders and the Public for Adaptation Purposes
abstract: The aim of the article is to increase the efficiency of hydrometeorological support users for the population and enterprises leaders by implementing a new paradigm. The failure of enterprises to account for all climate and change-related risks, combined with the absence of systematized and formalized impact forecasts and recommendations for preventive actions, leads to increased losses. To establish a modern hydrometeorological support system, the paper proposes an implementation integrated approach of an end-to-end data processing scheme ‒ spanning from observation to decision support. title: Distilling complexity: stylized facts as explicit, auditable foundation for ecological theory and modeling
abstract: Ecological models routinely rely on broad empirical regularities to constrain theory and validate predictions, yet these regularities are typically applied implicitly under alternative labels such as "patterns", "laws", or "benchmarks." Such implicit applications obscure a model's empirical commitments, hide unverified assumptions, mask scale dependencies, and hinder transfer across systems. title: Quantifying Groundwater–Surface Water Exchange on a River Island: A Comparative Analysis of Direct and Indirect Methods
abstract: Abstract Groundwater–surface water exchange is a key hydrological process that governs river water quality and aquatic ecosystems. However, the quantification of such exchange remains uncertain, especially within river island aquifers where exchange processes are highly heterogeneous. In this study, direct seepage meter measurements and indirect Darcy‐based estimates of exchange fluxes were compared under consistent spatiotemporal conditions within the aquifer of Jungsa Island, a river island in the lower West Nakdong River, South Korea. title: Convectively Coupled Equatorial Waves in a Global Storm‐Resolving Model
abstract: Abstract We show how reducing the fall speeds of rain and ice leads to reduced biases of Convectively Coupled Equatorial Waves (CCEWs) in convection‐resolving configurations of the Icosahedral Non‐hydrostatic Model (ICON). In particular, reducing the fall speeds of rain and ice leads to stronger activity over the wavenumbers and frequencies associated with convectively coupled Kelvin waves, inertio‐gravity waves, mixed Rossby‐gravity waves, equatorial Rossby waves, and the Madden‐Julian oscillation, and to weaker activity of tropical depressions. title: Process based modelling of breaker bar evolution with submerged vegetation under regular waves
abstract: This study investigates how submerged vegetation influences breaker bar development using the process based IH2VOF-SED model, which couples a two-dimensional vertical Reynolds averaged Navier–Stokes solver with sediment transport and bed evolution. The model is evaluated against laboratory measurements for bare and vegetated beach profiles under regular erosive waves. It reproduces the principal measured features of wave transformation, pointwise velocity signals, and beach-profile evolution, although agreement varies among cases and variables. title: In Situ Measurement of Dust Particle Transport to the Tropopause Layer over the Northern Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Abstract Previous satellite observations and simulations have shown that dust particles can be transported to the upper troposphere, but there is very little evidence from in situ observations. This study provides the first balloon-borne measurements of dust particle transport to the tropopause layer during a dust event over the northern Tibetan Plateau (TP). title: The Growing Role of Evaporative Demand in Driving Record‐Breaking Droughts in the Amazon Basin
abstract: Abstract Amazon droughts have historically been driven by precipitation deficits, but recent escalating drought events highlight a regime shift toward “hot droughts.” By decomposing historical drought drivers (1979–2024), we show that rising evaporative demand (represented by potential evapotranspiration, PET) now acts as a primary driver of drought intensification. While rainfall deficits remain the dominant contributor to the record‐breaking 2024 drought, escalating atmospheric thirst almost doubled its severity. title: Hydro-morphological investigations on local scour around inclined piles under wave conditions
abstract: Scouring is a problem that should be considered while designing bridges; scour around inclined piles in the presence of waves has rarely been researched. However, in reality, many inclined braces are used for aesthetic reasons, which alters the flow properties depending on their exposure to the flow field. The purpose of this work is to numerically examine the flow behavior and local scour evolution around inclined piles downstream under wave conditions. title: Long-term climatology of vertical profiles of polarimetric variables and ice-microphysical retrievals at X-band – Part 1: Radar calibration
abstract: Abstract. In a two-part series of papers, a climatology of quasi-vertical profiles (QVPs) of polarimetric variables and ice-microphysical retrievals such as ice water content, total number concentration and mean volume diameter is presented. QVPs are generated from plan position indicator scans at 18° elevation angle measured with the X-band radar located in the city of Bonn in western Germany between 2013 and 2023. title: Mediterranean cyclones from pre-industrial to future climate: changes in extreme wind, precipitation and compound precipitation–wind events
abstract: Abstract. The Mediterranean storm track is characterized by small but intense cyclones that can cause extreme weather events across the region. Thus the aim of this study is to investigate the impact of future climate change on extreme wind, precipitation and compounding cyclones. Using a regional climate model simulation, we show that the mean cyclone frequency is reduced by roughly a third in the Mediterranean by the end of the 21st century under the representative concentration pathway RCP8.5. For precipitation-type extreme cyclones (EXCs), future projections show increased precipitation du
institutions: Oeschger Centre for Climate Change Research

title: Global climate impact of land-surface change driven by radiative effects
abstract: Abstract A robust proportionality between radiative forcing and global-mean temperature has been established for most climate drivers. However, land-surface changes are considered an exception due to their potential to alter surface hydrology, introducing non-radiative effects that may rival those from surface albedo changes. title: A State‐of‐the‐Art Study of Vortex‐Excited Vibration Problems in Large‐Span Flat Steel Box Girder Bridges
abstract: ABSTRACT Windborne vibration of large‐span bridges occurs from time to time, especially the abnormal windborne vibration of urban bridges, which often causes public panic. The paper consists of four parts. Specifically, the first part analyzes the wind challenges of large‐span bridges, including the formation mechanism of wind‐induced vibration disaster of large‐span bridges and typical cases, as well as the limitations of the current wind design codes. title: Chemical characterization and source apportionment of PM 10 in Belgrade, Serbia: influence of local and regional anthropogenic and natural sources
abstract: Abstract. Substantial efforts and improvements in air quality across Europe lowered levels of air pollutants including particulate matter (PM) in the last decades. However, significant proportion of the European population still lives in areas exceeding WHO recommendations, especially in Northern Italy, Balkans and Eastern Europe, including Serbia. Targeted PM mitigation strategies require extensive air quality monitoring and modelling including source apportionment (SA) studies. institutions: Institute of Environmental Assessment and Water Research

title: Invited perspective: Uncertainties in natural systems may be uncomfortable, but ignoring them would be absurd
abstract: Abstract. Uncertainties in natural systems are pervasive, varied, and unavoidable due to inherent open system complexity and limited knowledge. Therefore, the evolution of a natural system cannot be predicted deterministically and probabilistic forecasts are commonly used to account for these uncertainties. As the Voltaire-inspired title suggests, representing and quantifying all uncertainties in hazard and risk forecasting is difficult yet essential for an effective risk-cycle management and for a meaningful scientific evaluation of forecasting models. title: Satellite evidence of unequal basin-scale recovery from severe droughts
abstract: Abstract Severe droughts deplete terrestrial water storage, jeopardizing ecosystems and human well-being. Yet, the pace and extent to which large river basins recover from such events remain unknown at the global scale. Here, integrating GRACE/FO water storage observations with state-of-the-art water availability estimates, we disentangle hydrological recovery following 468 basin-scale severe droughts with discernible impacts globally from 2003 to 2025. title: Improved multi-class drought classification through climate data analysis and advanced imbalanced data handling
abstract: Study region The Urmia Lake Basin, a terminal endorheic system in semi-arid northwestern Iran, faces severe hydrological decline. 51 years of monthly precipitation records (1971–2021) from four upper sub-basin rain gauges are analyzed alongside 11 climate teleconnections. Study focus Detecting rare, extreme drought events in terminal basins is frequently hindered by class imbalance in historical hydroclimatic records, biasing machine learning classifiers toward normal conditions. title: Diverse coupling between climate change, socio-economic factors and climate potential productivity in Africa
abstract: Africa’s accelerating climate warming has rendered its climate potential productivity (CPP) increasingly vulnerable, raising global concerns over biodiversity, water resources, and food security. Understanding the long‑term evolution of CPP and its driving mechanisms has therefore become an urgent research priority. This study analyses the spatiotemporal patterns and correlates of CPP across Africa, using the Thornthwaite Memorial model in combination with trend detection, correlation, and econometric analyses. title: Probabilistic fatigue assessment and optimal heading design of FOWT mooring systems under wind–wave misalignment
abstract: Floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) mooring fatigue accumulates under ordinary operating conditions, where wind and waves are often misaligned. Previous studies typically represent this misalignment by a relative angle or a few fixed directional cases. Yet the three-line mooring is directionally anisotropic, making fairlead fatigue dependent on the absolute wind and wave directions. This study develops a probabilistic fatigue framework that preserves absolute directionality and exploits it to optimize platform heading. title: Macroscopic and mesoscopic mechanical behavior of the interface between piles and unsaturated sand under vertical cyclic loading
abstract: Understanding the degradation of pile bearing capacity under vertical cyclic loading requires an in-depth investigation of the pile–unsaturated sand interface. This study employs a multi-scale approach—combining visualized cyclic loading tests, particle image velocimetry (PIV), and discrete element method (DEM) simulations—to elucidate the underlying macro–meso evolutionary mechanisms. title: H2CHAIN: Integrated Web Platform for Energy-Balance-Constrained Planning of Green Hydrogen Value Chains
abstract: Planning a green hydrogen project couples siting, generation, electrolysis, storage, conversion and cost decisions that are usually assessed in separate tools. This paper presents an integrated web-based decision-support platform for the planning and analysis of green hydrogen value chains. The platform combines geospatial analysis, techno-economic modeling, and system-level scenario assessment within a modular architecture that is accessible through a standard web browser. title: Passive and semi-active nonlinear negative stiffness control of an offshore jacket platform under earthquake-induced hydrodynamic interaction
abstract: Earthquake-induced hydrodynamic interaction can substantially alter the seismic response and control performance of offshore platforms. This study investigates nonlinear negative stiffness control of a jacket platform considering motion-induced hydrodynamic feedback. A five-degree-of-freedom (5DOF) formulation is validated against a published benchmark and adapted to a lightweight-topside configuration. title: Impact of VR-based climate change education on awareness and water use behavior
abstract: Climate change has increased the need for effective educational approaches that can promote climate-related awareness and environmentally responsible behaviors. This study investigates the effects of a passive 360-degree virtual reality educational intervention on climate change awareness and operational water consumption in a real industrial setting. The study was conducted with 17 cafeteria workers at an operating factory in Türkiye. title: An approximately 70-year core-related modulation of Earth rotation and its implications for the leap second
abstract: Recent observations of Universal Time (UT1) indicate an acceleration in Earth’s rotation. If sustained under the current leap-second framework, this behavior could eventually prompt consideration of a negative leap second. We examine whether the recent acceleration is consistent with an approximately 70-year, core-related modulation of length of day (LOD). title: Salinity-driven controls on arsenic mobility in naturally coated sands: multi-mineral sorption, kinetic limitations, and metal-facilitated transport
abstract: Arsenic mobility in groundwater is sensitive to hydrodynamic and hydrochemical perturbations, yet the coupled mechanisms controlling arsenic transport in natural sands remain poorly constrained. This study uses a series of column experiments, combined with chemical extractions, surface microscopy, and reactive transport modeling, to explore how transient pore-water chemistry and co-existing mineral surfaces in sandy porous media control arsenate transport under oxic conditions. title: Prediction of Electric Arc Furnace End‐Point Temperature via Fusion of Physical Mechanism and Stacking Ensemble
abstract: Accurate endpoint temperature prediction in electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking is critical for energy efficiency and product quality; however, it remains fundamentally challenged by severe nonlinearity and dynamic variations. Traditional machine learning models lack interpretability and robustness against industrial noise, whereas purely mechanistic models fail to capture nonlinear deviations. title: Evaluation of different equations of state for simulating fluid-solid interaction with the material point method
abstract: The simulation fidelity of Fluid–Structure Interaction (FSI) is critical for predicting multi-phase (solid-liquid-gas) interactions that involve large deformations and failure evolution. While the Material Point Method (MPM) offers a robust numerical procedure for those problems, the choice of the Equation of State (EOS) for weakly compressible fluids remains a subject of compromise between computational accuracy and efficiency. title: The 2023–2024 El Niño as a Preview of Future Tropical Forest Climate
abstract: Abstract Tropical forests are an important component of the global carbon cycle. Increasingly frequent droughts and heatwaves are undermining their resilience, with far‐reaching impacts on local livelihoods and on regional and global hydrological cycles. El Niño events, recurring climate patterns that lead to dry and hot conditions across multiple tropical regions, have always influenced these dynamics, but the 2023–2024 El Niño produced extreme droughts and heatwaves that exceeded the typical El Niño footprint. title: Fire carbon emission constraints from space-based carbon monoxide retrievals during the 2019 intense burning season in Brazil
abstract: Abstract. In 2019, Brazil experienced an intensive fire season, despite the absence of major climate anomalies to enhance fire activity. Existing carbon monoxide (CO) emission estimates from state-of-the-art fire emission inventories differ by a factor two for the period and region. We provide a top-down estimate on CO emissions from these fires using the new CarbonTracker Europe – Long/Short Window (CTE-LW/SW) inverse modelling framework driven by column-averaged dry air CO mole fractions (XCO) from the MOPITT and TROPOMI satellite instruments. title: Enhanced WCSPH modelling of 2-D and 3-D granular flows using μ(I) rheology with rheology-aware boundary treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a weakly compressible smoothed particle hydrodynamics (WCSPH) framework for granular materials incorporating δ -SPH pressure stabilization, μ ( I ) rheology, a rheology-consistent extrapolated boundary condition (EBC), and a rheology-aware particle shifting technique (PST). title: Forest and bioenergy expansion amplifies climate warming by accelerating regional cloud loss
abstract: Abstract. Land use and land cover change (LUCC) can exacerbate cloud-mediated climate warming. However, the long-term response of cloud cover to LUCC remains underexplored, particularly regarding differences between idealized and realistic forest expansion scenarios, as well as between forest and bioenergy expansion. abstract: This study assessed flood hazard and risk in Semarang City, where increasing hydrometeorological pressures and rapid urban development have heightened flood impacts. abstract: While machine learning (ML) weather models are emerging as promising tools for predicting weather conditions on a global scale, their coarse resolution and systematic biases limit practical applicability in regional contexts. abstract: Abstract We present a revisited Cartesian-diver experiment in which a small air-filled balloon, loaded with a metal sphere and plasticine, undergoes a metastable sinking motion in a water column. abstract: Lake Qaroun is a closed saline lake located in Fayoum Depression in Egypt. abstract: Abstract The sixth assessment report (AR6) of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) presented regional summaries of the scientific knowledge of changing weather extremes and the human influence upon this. The hexagon figures, found in the Summary for Policymakers (SPM), were a key part of this presentation. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric non‐methane hydrocarbons (NMHCs) are important trace species with anthropogenic and natural sources including fugitive emissions from fossil fuel mining and distribution, biomass burning, biofuel combustion, and biogenic emissions from microbes and plants. abstract: This study explores how corrosion unfolds in aluminium hybrid structures created by integrating Selective Laser Melting (SLM) with conventional casting techniques. To better understand the impact of different fabrication routes, three sample configurations were considered: fully SLM-built components, cast aluminium substrates, and hybrid structures where an SLM layer was directly deposited onto a cast base. title: Relationship of tropical cyclone wind-field and cloud-band metrics with extreme rainfall events over Mexico
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) are the most important hydrometeorological phenomena affecting Mexico, accounting for approximately 86.5% of the country’s most costly disasters, where extreme rainfall is the main TC-associated hazard. This study analyzes two TC size metrics during the 2000–2024 period: R34, defined as the mean radius of 34-kt winds, and ROCLOUD, a satellite-derived metric that represents the spatial extent of TC cloud bands. abstract: Saudi Arabia’s infrastructure transformation under Vision 2030 is creating an exceptional need for environmental management systems that can operate at the scale, speed, complexity and ecological sensitivity of giga- and mega-project delivery. title: Observed sub-surface warming in the Northern Eurasia (1963-2022)
abstract: Abstract Long-term soil temperature changes in high-latitude regions have been reported mainly focusing on the near-surface air and sub-surface soil temperature because of limited observational data. This gap still obscures spatiotemporal changes and associated processes of vertical thermal changes at multiple soil layers over such climate-sensitive regions. abstract: Abstract Climate risk and socioeconomic development are increasingly reshaping tourism resilience, particularly in climate-sensitive and unevenly developed regions. Yet how climate risk and economic development jointly influence tourism, and how these effects vary across regions, remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Climate change is driving a sustained increase in global temperatures and an intensification of extreme events, including heatwaves. abstract: Accurate forecasting of net electrical power output (PE) in Combined Cycle Power Plants (CCPP) is a requisite for grid stability and strategic bidding in deregulated energy markets. abstract: Drought is a significant climate-related hazard in Sierra Leone due to the countrys reliance on seasonal rainfall, rain-fed agriculture, and climate-sensitive water resources. abstract: Sensitive skin is shaped by intrinsic physiology and environmental exposures, yet how concurrent lifestyle factors modulate its expression remains poorly characterized. This study examined how differing environmental and lifestyle conditions influence sensitive skin phenotypes through clinical evaluation, biophysical measurements, and biomarker profiling. title: Applications of Earth Observation for Monitoring and Management of Natural Hazards and Emergency Situations in Central Asia
abstract: Central Asia is highly vulnerable to a wide range of natural hazards due to its complex mountainous terrain, glacierized catchments, and highly variable climate. Hazards such as glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs), mudflows, snow avalanches, river floods, and droughts pose significant risks to communities, infrastructure, and water resources across the region. abstract: Paediatric asthma hospitalisations have marked seasonal peaks, but it remains unclear whether associations with environmental exposures vary under different local climatic conditions. abstract: Accurate and internally consistent radiosonde temperature and relative humidity profiles are fundamental to numerical weather prediction (NWP), boundary-layer studies, climate monitoring, and satellite data validation. abstract: Abstract While extreme precipitation is expected to intensify globally in a warming climate, changes in extreme precipitation on regional scales remain uncertain. abstract: ABSTRACT Vegetation growth is increasingly threatened by both extreme climate events and anthropogenic disturbances. Although considerable attention has been given to detecting large‐scale vegetation anomalies, comprehensive analyses of the spatiotemporal dynamics of negative extreme anomalies in vegetation growth (NEGs) and their underlying drivers remain limited. abstract: This study developed and evaluated a spatial consistency quality-control method for daily surface air temperature observations from 186 SYNOP stations across Vietnam during 1961–2023. abstract: Abstract Drought impacts in large river basins depend not only on precipitation deficits but also on how terrestrial water storage (TWS) buffers climate anomalies through hydrological memory, which is the persistence of past storage conditions. abstract: Sloshing dynamics in partially-filled rectangular tanks remains a computationally demanding phenomenon in applications such as tuned liquid dampers, largely due to high computational costs of using high-fidelity sloshing models. abstract: Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is a core indicator for quantifying atmospheric pollution, and its spatiotemporal variation is strongly influenced by meteorological factors, including water vapor, a critical driver of atmospheric moisture transport and energy balance. abstract: A variety of chemical and dynamical processes in the troposphere and stratosphere affect tropical total column ozone (TCO), the net effect of which may cause changes in surface UV radiation and impact human and ecosystem health. abstract: Abstract The Lancang–Mekong River Basin (LMRB), a crucial transboundary region that sustains millions of people across Southeast Asia, faces growing threats from compound hydrological extremes under climate change. abstract: This study investigates how alternative blade-root and blade-tip loss corrections influence steady aerodynamic predictions for a 200-kW horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT) within a Blade Element Momentum (BEM) framework. abstract: Abstract. Quantifying and understanding methane emissions of cities are of great importance given their role in current and future mitigation efforts to combat climate changing emissions. However, it remains challenging to routinely and accurately characterize and verify city-scale methane emission inventories. abstract: Recent urbanization and overexploitation have significantly degraded groundwater quality in the shallow unconfined aquifer in Barjisiyah. abstract: Brackish water offers compelling opportunities for agricultural use, especially in regions experiencing water scarcity and limited freshwater resources. However, its utilization requires careful supervision, considering factors such as crop salinity tolerance and soil composition to prevent adverse effects. abstract: ABSTRACT Lifetime estimation regarding leading‐edge erosion of wind turbine blades involves a series of mathematical and statistical procedures, including regression fitting, tolerance interval formulation, and weathering modeling approaches. This work investigates the intermediate steps in the fatigue assessment process and the associated sources of variability, using data from a whirling arm rain erosion test (RET) machine, time‐series liquid precipitation and wind data from two sites, and the IEA reference 15 MW wind turbine. abstract: Climate conditions can significantly affect plant dormancy and growing season, impacting crop development and its productivity. Temperature is considered the primary driver of grapevine phenology, with endodormancy and ecodormancy largely regulated by chilling and forcing accumulations, respectively. abstract: Abstract The resilience of human society to multiple climate disasters is crucial for supporting sustainable development progress and promoting human well‐being in an era of climate change. Yet little research has attempted to assess global spatial‐explicit capacity of communities to deal with compound extreme climate disasters simultaneously, and the relationship between resilience to different climate extremes remains unknown. abstract: Bridgmanite, the main mineralogical phase in the Earth's lower mantle, is intrinsically anisotropic and may therefore generate seismic anisotropy in actively-deforming regions, particularly subduction zones. Over 62,000 heat-related deaths were estimated to have occurred during the European summer of 2024, exemplifying the pressing need to develop effective early warning systems. abstract: In this research, the focus is on examining the occurrence of localized Cloudburst events in the Indian Himalayan region (IHR). abstract: ABSTRACT The transition from a linear to a circular economy necessitates systemic changes in product design, data sharing, and material flows. Applying a coevolutionary framework, this study shows how these three dimensions interact dynamically in circular economy transitions. title: The impact of climate change on human health and pharmaceuticals
abstract: Climate change and air pollution affect every major organ system, altering both the disease burden and patient responses to pharmaceutical treatments. However, current knowledge on how health systems, patients, healthcare professionals, and governments should prepare for these challenges remains fragmented. This review synthesises evidence on the potential impact of climate change on human health and pharmaceuticals, with the aim of identifying the diseases, populations, and medications most vulnerable, and assessing potential implications for pharmacotherapy. title: Digital Transformation for Enhancing Port Competitiveness, Resilience, and Sustainability: Evidence from Tanjung Perak Port, Surabaya
abstract: Indonesian ports are under sustained pressure to reduce dwelling time, logistics costs, and environmental exposure while maintaining operational resilience in the face of supply chain disruptions. This study examines digital transformation as a strategic intervention influencing port competitiveness, resilience, and sustainability. A qualitative case study was conducted at Tanjung Perak Port, Surabaya, using policy documents, operational reports, and observations of digital systems implemented during the 2019–2024 period. abstract: Wind disturbances at low altitudes increase energy consumption and safety risks for multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in densely built urban environments. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is too expensive for online path planning, while threshold methods represent hazardous regions as binary no-fly zones. abstract: Wastewater treatment and sustainable energy recovery are two key approaches to achieve circular water management and carbon neutral technologies. The semiconducting MXene-based materials have gained widespread attention as multifunctional platform materials because of their easily tunable electronic structures, high number of surface functional groups, and efficient charge-transfer properties. abstract: Urban heat stress poses an intensifying public health challenge in Australian cities, with Sydney facing increasingly severe summer thermal conditions. We present a reproducible framework for metropolitan-scale future heat risk assessment that integrates satellite-derived Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) with demographic projections to 2031. abstract: Abstract Subseasonal-to-seasonal precipitation forecasts are highly relevant for a wide range of practical applications and risk management, but their skill decreases substantially at longer lead times. title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of vegetation responses to compound drought and heatwave events in Central Asia
abstract: With climate warming intensifying, compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events have become more frequent and intense in arid Central Asia, severely affecting vegetation growth. However, systematic quantitative assessments of vegetation responses and their drivers under such compound extremes remain limited. Using meteorological and remote sensing data, we identified growing-season CDHW events across Central Asia from 1982 to 2023. abstract: This study integrates AMS 14C dating of 12 plant specimens, Bayesian modeling, and Tibetan texts to establish the first high-resolution construction chronology for key structures of the Guge ancient city in western Tibet. To ensure chronological precision and mitigate the old-wood effect, sampling prioritized short-lived annual plants and the outermost growth layers of small-diameter timber. title: Twenty years of Kilimanjaro observations across 5000 m reveal tropical elevation-dependent warming under clear-sky conditions
abstract: Abstract Mountain regions are experiencing rapid climate change. However, temperature trends along elevation gradients remain poorly understood in the tropics, where long-term high-elevation air temperature ( T air ) observations are sparse. Here, we examine elevation-dependent warming (EDW) on Mount Kilimanjaro by combining a unique long-term in situ T air transect with Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) land-surface temperature (LST), surface and topographic datasets. abstract: Implicit information on land use conflicts in territorial spatial planning texts directly affects the coordination and implementability of planning schemes. Traditional manual interpretation approaches have low efficiency, high omission rates, and inadequate standardization, making them difficult to use for full-process review of massive multi-source planning texts under multi-plan integration. title: Observation, analysis and numerical simulation of a low-level windshear case at Beijing Daxing International Airport
abstract: A case of low level windshear at Beijing Daxing International Airport is studied in the present paper. It is related to the synoptic scale/mesoscale changes of the airflow pattern over northern China. The shear was captured well by the Doppler LIDAR at the airport and timely alerts had been issued. This study considers the technical feasibility of forecasting the shear feature using a high resolution numerical weather prediction model with a lead time of several hours. It turns out that the shear feature could be forecast well, and is generally consistent with the actual observations.

abstract: The expansion of tourism in Saudi Arabia, under the Vision 2030 initiative, covers a wide variety of areas such as destination development, transport, utilities, heritage conservation, digital systems, the public realm, hospitality capacity and regional economic policy as part of a wider programme of transformation. abstract: The wildfire situation has become increasingly dangerous to the eastern Mediterranean’s forest lands and human life. abstract: Agricultural drainage networks increasingly function as distributed pollution control systems for mitigating non-point source phosphorus (P) export to aquatic ecosystems. abstract: Flood peak timing (FloPT) is a key indicator of hydrological responses to climate change. Yet global FloPT assessments is limited by sparse and uneven in-situ discharge observations. abstract: Acacia dealbata (Link) is enlisted as an invasive alien species in several regions where it was introduced. abstract: This work addresses a common problem: technology projects often run late, go over budget, or fail because risks are found too late. abstract: Mosquito-borne infectious disease is a major cause of mortality and a significant economic burden worldwide. Variable regional and seasonal patterns make proactive intervention challenging. abstract: The accelerated adoption of cloud computing by government institutions and financial organizations has transformed public service delivery, fiscal management, and financial intermediation. However, the migration of mission-critical information systems to cloud environments introduces complex reliability challenges with far-reaching implications for economic stability, public trust, and national security. abstract: Abstract Flood frequency analysis (FFA) forms the basis of many hydrological assessments and practical design calculations. Traditionally, FFA is based on the assumptions of stationary distributions and homogeneous samples. These assumptions are questionable in light of climate change and the wide variety of hydrological processes that lead to flooding. Furthermore, these assumptions can obscure important insights, including process‐specific changes. abstract: The increasing complexity of capacity expansion models underscores the need for time-series aggregation methods that balance accuracy with computational efficiency. abstract: Monitoring modern air pollution requires flexible but portable systems that can be used to gather real-time data in various settings. This paper describes a drone-based air quality monitoring platform with IoT-enabled sensors integrated into it. abstract: Dams in arid, data-scarce basins are designed to attenuate episodic flash floods, yet their performance under extreme operational stress or catastrophic failure is rarely evaluated against long-term observational records. This study presents an empirical and hydrodynamic assessment of Wadi Jazan Dam, Saudi Arabia, integrating nearly four decades of historical streamflow data with an integrated GIS, semi-distributed HEC-HMS, and 2D HEC-RAS modelling framework. abstract: Rapid urbanization and the expansion of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) in tropical megacities often overlook the microclimatic experience of pedestrians, leading to severe Urban Heat Island (UHI) effects and thermal discomfort. title: Self-Adaptive Edge-Intelligent IoT Framework for Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring and Predictive Control
abstract: Monitoring water quality is important for environmental safety and public health in places with fast-changing or unstable water conditions. Conventional monitoring approaches are slow to respond, not scalable, and lack real-time decision-making ability. To address these limitations, a research framework is proposed based on an intelligent edge-IoT architecture for real-time monitoring and assessment of water quality parameters. The system combines sensors such as temperature, pH, turbidity, and salinity with an ESP32 microcontroller for fast data sensing and processing. Edge computing is used

title: High-Precision Archaeological Recording of Jiajiang Thousand-Buddha Cliff Grottoes Using UAV Close-Range Photogrammetry
abstract: The digital documentation of riverside cliff grottoes has long been hindered by acquisition blind spots caused by steep terrain and irregular cliff faces. Conventional close‑range photogrammetry relies on preset flight paths, which are difficult to safely execute in complex scenarios with vegetation occlusion and no available space for setup along the riverbank. This paper proposes a two‑stage manually controlled acquisition strategy of “global cruising first, individual close‑up later” and acquires images on the Jiajiang Thousand‑Buddha Cliff Grottoes. title: Deformation-enhanced fluid evolution and skarn–IOCG transition in the Paleoproterozoic Elaine Dorothy Cu–Au system, Mount Isa Inlier, Australia
abstract: Abstract The Elaine Dorothy Cu-Au deposit, located in the Mary Kathleen Domain of the Mount Isa Inlier, Australia, records the interaction of Paleoproterozoic skarn metasomatism, fluid evolution, and deformation. The deposit is hosted by carbonate- and calc-silicate-rich rocks of the Corella Formation and comprises diopside–garnet–scapolite–wollastonite ± amphibole assemblages associated with pyrrhotite–chalcopyrite–pyrite mineralisation. title: Theory, technologies, and practice of oilfield-geothermal co-development in the Bohai Bay Basin
abstract: Abstract Driven by the global energy transition and China's dual-carbon goals, oil and gas field development faces challenges in achieving sustainable development. Oilfield-geothermal co-development (OGC) offers a pathway for revitalizing mature oilfields and supplying low-carbon energy. This article describes the resource endowment, genetic mechanisms, and oil-heat-water co-occurrence relationships of geothermal resources in oilfields, examines the theory and key technologies for OGC, and proposes an integrated technical system. title: Research on thermodynamic performance of a gas-steam combined cycle with rotating detonation combustion
abstract: Conventional gas-steam combined cycles are constrained by the substantial irreversibility of constant-pressure combustion, whereas integrating a rotating detonation combustor (RDC) may lower the turbine exhaust temperature and thereby impair the steam bottoming cycle. In this study, a thermodynamic model of a methane-fueled RDC-based gas-steam combined cycle is developed and compared with a conventional constant-pressure-combustion combined cycle. title: Dynamic Inference of Regional Traffic States in a Dense Waterway Using AIS Window Sequences
abstract: Regional vessel monitoring requires both a description of current traffic and an estimate of its near-term evolution. This study evaluates a lightweight approach to dynamic traffic-state inference using sequences of Automatic Identification System (AIS) observations. A lower Yangtze waterway case area is divided into spatial cells, and vessel-level observations are aggregated into 10-minute windows. title: Improved estimation of net ecosystem CO 2 exchange over North America using LSTM-based flux upscaling (2001–2021)
abstract: Abstract. Accurate estimation of regional-scale terrestrial carbon budgets is of great importance but remains challenging. With particular advantages, the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks method shows potential in improving regional carbon budget upscaling estimations. Here, based on LSTM, we upscale regional net ecosystem carbon exchange (NEE) with available flux tower measurements and satellite land surface observations in North America. title: From manual classification to transformer-based language models: assessing the quality and consistency of historical convective event records
abstract: Abstract. Historical text sources represent a central, yet methodologically challenging basis for the reconstruction of convective weather events. This study examines the extent to which historical reports on thunderstorms and hailstorms contain reliable climatological information, despite heterogeneous sources, varying degrees of detail and linguistic diversity. Based on a corpus prepared using source criticism, qualitative descriptions are converted into structured evidence levels and intensity classes and analysed using statistical methods and a multilingual BERT language model. title: HalifaxDT: A Wireless Digital Twin from Open Geospatial Data
abstract: Wireless digital twins can support site-specific analysis, planning, and experimentation for future wireless networks. However, constructing them at city scale remains challenging when accurate 3D city models are unavailable. This paper presents HalifaxDT, a wireless digital twin of the Halifax Peninsula in Nova Scotia, Canada, constructed from heterogeneous open geospatial and spectrum data. title: Baroclinic Annular Mode Modulates Global Atmospheric Rivers and Extreme Precipitation
abstract: The Baroclinic Annular Mode (BAM) strongly influences extratropical circulation, yet its role in the global hydrological cycle remains unclear. Using ERA5 reanalysis and a global atmospheric river (AR) database, we show that BAM systematically reorganizes AR occurrence and extreme precipitation in both hemispheres. During high-BAM states, AR frequency increases along the flanks of major storm tracks and decreases near their climatological cores, redistributing preferred AR corridors. title: Recent increase in near-perpendicular tropical cyclone landfall fraction projected to emerge under high-emissions warming
abstract: Tropical cyclone landfall angle strongly modulates storm-surge potential, but how it changes with climate remains unknown. From 1980 to 2024, the global fraction of near-perpendicular landfalls shows a weak, statistically insignificant increase, with no significant basin-scale trends. PepC-Global simulations driven by reanalyses reproduce observed landfall-angle and pre-landfall approach-angle distributions and broad geographic variations in the near-perpendicular fraction.
