title: Beyond gas dwarfs and water worlds: hybrid envelopes among the M-dwarf sub-Neptunes characterised with JWST
abstract: Sub-Neptunes orbiting M dwarfs are commonly interpreted either as rocky cores beneath primordial H/He envelopes (gas dwarfs) or as volatile-rich bodies formed beyond the water-ice line (water worlds). Because the two are degenerate in mass and radius once envelope evolution is treated self-consistently, the atmospheric mean molecular weight $μ$ is the more direct discriminant. title: Stochastic thermodynamics and predictability of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes: an application to the Madden-Julian Oscillation
abstract: Climate oscillations are intrinsically out-of-equilibrium phenomena, yet the connection between their predictability and nonequilibrium thermodynamic properties remains unexplored. We develop a coarse-grained stochastic thermodynamic framework for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) processes and apply this framework to climate data via linear inverse models (LIMs), linking predictability, entropy production, dynamical activity, and path action. title: Three-Dimensional Simulation of Flood Propagation at Syabrubesi, Nepal
abstract: Three-dimensional flood propagation through the Bhote Koshi--Langtang Khola junction at Syabrubesi, Nepal, is studied using an incompressible free-surface model. The calculation is motivated by the August 2026 flood and examines the passage of an imposed inflow through the local bends and changes in channel width. The Navier--Stokes equations and an interface transport equation are solved on unstructured tetrahedral meshes constructed from pre-event terrain data. title: Two-way actuator-line coupling of a geometrically exact finite-volume beam with incompressible and free-surface flow
abstract: Slender flexible structures such as mooring lines, aquaculture netting, and aquatic vegetation are too thin to be resolved economically by a body-fitted mesh, yet they exchange momentum with the flow in both directions. This paper presents a finite volume actuator-line formulation for the fluid--structure interaction of such structures, in which a geometrically exact Simo--Reissner beam, discretised by cell-centred finite volumes, is coupled two-way to an incompressible finite volume flow solver through conservative, parallel-consistent transfer operators. title: Morphology, interactions, and evolution of laminar thermal plumes revealed by time-resolved volumetric velocity measurements and analysis: Application to Earth's mantle
abstract: Plume-laden convection plays a fundamental role in thermal transport in geophysical and industrial flows. While the dynamics of isolated laminar plumes have been extensively studied, their collective interactions and evolution in a multi-plume system remains poorly quantified due to the lack of four-dimensional (4D, in space and time) flow measurements for viscous convection, common in the turbulence community. title: Non-stationary time series attribution for heatwaves over Europe
abstract: The increasing occurrence of extreme weather events since the beginning of the 21st century has led to the development of new methods to attribute extreme events to anthropogenic climate change. The way in which the extreme event is defined has a major influence on the attribution result. A frequently overlooked aspect concerns the temporal dependence of extremes. This study presents an approach for attributing complete time series during extreme events to anthropogenic forcing. title: Beyond Tomorrow -- Electrification of Hard-to-Abate Sectors
abstract: Reaching net-zero greenhouse-gas (GHG) emissions requires deep electrification beyond ground transportation, buildings, and conventional industry automation. This article discusses direct electrification pathways for hard-to-abate sectors, which today account for 30% of global GHG emissions and include steel, cement, chemicals, aviation, and shipping. abstract: Existing trajectory designs for covert communications with uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) typically rely on point-mass kinematics, which overlook the inherent coupling between flight maneuvers and antenna orientation. Motivated by recent studies linking UAV acceleration to attitude, we investigate dynamics-consistent trajectory and attitude co-design for rotary-wing UAV covert communications. title: Ab initio calculated diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility of carbonate minerals
abstract: The anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) is a widely used tool to infer rock fabrics, yet quantitative interpretation is limited by sparse single-crystal magnetic properties for rock-forming minerals and by the difficulty of separating intrinsic diamagnetism from impurity-related magnetism. Here we use density-functional theory (DFT) combined with perturbation theory to compute the diamagnetic susceptibility and AMS of calcite-group carbonates (calcite, magnesite, and dolomite) and to quantify the additional paramagnetic contribution from transition-metal doping. title: Spatial patterning and selection: How the environment shapes molecular complexity
abstract: Assembly theory predicts that a distinguishing signature of life is its ability to produce complex molecules in abundance, opening new possibilities for life detection. Experimental validation of this approach has so far relied on abiotic controls like meteoritic material, or simple, well-mixed chemical systems. title: Inclined surfaces bias bacterial swarming expansion and edge organization
abstract: Bacterial swarming is the collective expansion of dense populations of motile cells across hydrated soft surfaces, yet gravity is usually treated as a fixed background condition in standard horizontal assays. We used surface inclination to examine how agar-surface orientation relative to gravity affects the expansion of Enterobacter sp. SM3 swarms. title: Science of Nuclear Fusion: Insights and Ideas
abstract: Advances in several physics domains open up novel paths to smaller scale, higher energy density opportunities to advance small systems for nuclear fusion. Here we survey both legacy and several novel “table-top” approaches which attract current interest. title: StatD2GAN: When Calibration Masks Generator Quality in Held-Out Evaluation of Synthetic Weather Sequences
abstract: Generative models for multivariate weather series are routinely evaluated with pooled distributional metrics computed after marginal calibration. We show this practice can invalidate architectural conclusions, and rebuild the evaluation of StatD2GAN, a three-discriminator GAN with evolutionary weight adaptation, around a held-out protocol: the final two calendar years of each dataset are held out behind a 168 hour embargo, calibration is fitted on the training block only, and all metrics are computed on the held-out block. title: Rotational symmetry and common-mode phase drift in a counter-wound S-shaped Aharonov--Bohm interferometer
abstract: We study common flux offsets in a three-dimensional InAs Aharonov-Bohm waveguide formed by two quarter-circle bends of opposite curvature. title: Discrete Boltzmann model at Burnett level for compressible multicomponent flows under external forces
abstract: A discrete Boltzmann model at the Burnett level is established to investigate compressible multicomponent flows with external forces. A set of 25 discrete velocities is designed to provide high isotropy and numerical stability. Both the equilibrium discrete function and the force term are constructed using a moment-matching approach, ensuring that 25 independent kinetic moments are accurately recovered. abstract: The mixing-plane method plays a pivotal role in steady simulations of multiple turbomachinery components. With advances in computational power, a whole-engine gas turbine simulation is no longer an elusive approach. However, whole-engine simulations require simultaneous coupling of the compressor, turbine and combustor. title: Contact lens with stretchable distributed-feedback laser for intraocular pressure monitoring
abstract: Continuous monitoring of intraocular pressure (IOP) is essential for the diagnosis and management of glaucoma, yet existing clinical methods rely on intermittent in-clinic measurements that miss critical diurnal fluctuations. Smart contact lenses are an attractive platform for continuous IOP tracking, and optical strain sensors are particularly promising thanks to their high sensitivity and natural readout. title: Strategic Environmental Assessment for the Ukrainian Community Development Strategies: European Union Practice
abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is an important tool for integrating environmental considerations into territorial planning and sustainable development. This study compares SEA practices in the United Kingdom, Poland, Romania, and Ukraine to identify best European practices and formulate recommendations for Ukraine. The study used a comparative approach based on analysis of legal frameworks, consultation systems, and official SEA reports. title: DNA-based monitoring uncovers contrasting salinity-driven diversity patterns of bacterial and protist plankton in the Baltic Sea area
abstract: Salinity has been identified as a primary factor structuring community composition in global diversity assessments of free-living bacteria in non-extreme environments. It remains unknown whether the same is true for protists. Moreover, changes in alpha diversity of both bacteria and protists across the brackish salinity gradient remain elusive. abstract: There is now a growing recognition internationally that the impacts of Artificial Light at Night (ALAN) on marine biodiversity require regulation. How ALAN should be regulated and what constitutes ‘Good Environmental Status’ (GES) for underwater ALAN remain open questions that if resolved would accelerate the integration of ALAN management into existing policy instruments. abstract: Covering about 20 % of the global ocean, the polar ocean areas are among the most sensitive regions of the Earth climate system, where today climate change is reshaping processes that influence global circulation, sea level, and climate far beyond the poles. abstract: The Arctic Ocean (AO) is experiencing declining sea ice extent and thickness and increasing sea surface temperatures, with cascading consequences for the entire ecosystem. abstract: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing (RS) are now central tools forland resource mapping, administration and environmental management worldwide. abstract: Abstract Although foraminiferal oxygen isotope records (δ 18 O F ) have long been used to develop time‐continuous estimates of past global ice volume, growing evidence indicates that the ice volume and temperature contributions to δ 18 O F diverge considerably over the last glacial cycle. abstract: Introduction . The coastline of a reservoir is a complex natural object, which geometry has irregularity and signs of selfsimilarity, and the length depends on the scale of measurement. Despite the widespread study of its fractal properties, the transition to a digital representation of the coastline is a complex procedure and is a current topic of research. title: Ocean acidification pushes Mediterranean marine calcifiers toward a tipping point
abstract: Abstract The increasing emission of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is altering seawater chemistry, lowering ocean pH and threatening marine biodiversity. Predicting how marine biota will be adversely affected by ocean acidification (OA) remains a key challenge. Here, we document that functional morphological traits offer a more robust metric of calcifier sensitivity to OA than taxonomic diversity alone. title: Documented technology adoption in environmental impact assessment: a mixed-methods study of adoption–perception gaps in Korea
abstract: Despite rapid advances in AI, big data analytics, GIS, real-time monitoring, and predictive modeling, their integration into environmental impact assessment (EIA) practice remains poorly documented. This study employs a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design to examine documented technology adoption in Korean EIA and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA). abstract: E-commerce in emerging and fragile markets often develops faster than the physical logistics systems required to support reliable and efficient order fulfillment. This study develops an integrated geographic information system (GIS) and multi-criteria decision-making framework for evaluating candidate cities for e-commerce fulfillment hubs in Libya. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a pilot project exploring the integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into geography education in Zanzibar, Tanzania. Responding to systemic challenges such as overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages, and limited resources, the study developed and implemented a localized, GenAI‐assisted teaching platform. abstract: Context Edge effects at habitat boundaries can generate strong physicochemical gradients that structure coastal ecosystems. abstract: Organic alkalinity has been recognized as a potentially substantial fraction of total alkalinity in coastal waters. title: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN BANGLADESH: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
abstract: Bangladesh exemplifies a central paradox of sustainable development: how to maintain rapid economic and social progress without undermining the ecological systems upon which development depends. abstract: ABSTRACT Coastal protection infrastructure is routinely upgraded to address structural degradation and rising sea levels. abstract: Coastal zones provide recreational ecosystem services across land and sea, yet spatial data for ecosystem accounting is limited. We compared Strava activity data with survey-based public participation GIS (PPGIS) data across the Oslofjord, Norway, to assess spatial and sociodemographic biases in crowdsourced recreation accounting. title: Nonlinear longitudinal stress coupling in glacier and ice sheet flow
abstract: Abstract The Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets exhibit high variability in flow speed, over multiple orders of magnitude. This flow integrates forcings from complex, multi-scale and spatially heterogeneous pressure gradient and friction fields into smooth and continuous flow fields, over a finite scale known as the longitudinal coupling length (LCL). The strongly nonlinear, shear-thinning rheology of ice complicates the stress transmission, but previous work has relied on either linear (Newtonian) models or linearized, small-perturbation models, to determine the coupling length. title: Genomic insights into the metabolic complementarity of a synthetic marine consortium for hydrocarbon degradation in coastal sand microcosms
abstract: Microbial consortia are essential for the degradation of complex hydrocarbon mixtures in coastal environments, yet the functional basis of consortium performance rarely resolved at strain level. In this study, we employed a Plackett–Burman experimental design to rationally assemble and optimize a synthetic consortium for the degradation of medium-grade crude oil in a sand–seawater microcosm. Six strains were selected: Stutzerimonas stutzeri CBC1 and CBC2, S. balearica GOM11, Pseudomonas sp. CBC3, Halomonas litopenaei GOM23 and Enterobacter kobei GOM24. title: Cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in juvenile green and loggerhead sea turtles: an exploratory biologging study
abstract: Anthropogenic underwater noise is an increasing concern in marine environments, yet physiological responses of sea turtles remain poorly understood. We examined cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in three juvenile green turtles (Chelonia mydas) and four juvenile loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta) maintained after incidental capture. Electrocardiogram, acceleration, depth, and turtle-borne acoustic data were recorded during 44 trials. abstract: Kegiatan ini dilatarbelakangi oleh kebutuhan BPJS Kesehatan Cabang Samarinda sebagai mitra dalam memanfaatkan data pelayanan Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional (JKN) agar dapat disajikan secara lebih informatif berdasarkan aspek wilayah. title: Multilocus phylogeny and historical biogeography of the pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris (Diplopoda, Glomerida) in Thailand
abstract: Abstract Southeast Asia is widely recognized as a global biodiversity hotspot with a complex geological history and high species richness across multiple taxa. The pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris Verhoeff, 1906 has received increasing taxonomic attention in recent years, with several new species described, particularly from western Southeast Asia, including Thailand and Myanmar. However, its historical biogeography has remained insufficiently understood. title: Measurements of the Size and Physical Properties of Marine Particles Using Atomic Force Microscopy: Implications for Marine Biogeochemical Cycles
abstract: Abstract Particle size and physical properties such as stiffness and adhesiveness affect sinking velocity and flux in the ocean, yet conventional two‐dimensional measurements lack accuracy and mechanical information. In this study, we applied atomic force microscopy (AFM) to quantify three‐dimensional size and physical properties of marine particles. Three hundred and sixty‐eight particles were collected using a marine snow catcher from the pycnocline and benthic boundary layer at three coastal‐to‐offshore stations in the northwestern Pacific. title: Status of Sea Bamboo (Isis hippuris Linnaeus, 1758) in Bunaken National Park, North Sulawesi, Indonesia
abstract: Isis hippuris Linnaeus, 1758, commonly known as sea bamboo, is a gorgonian octocoral of the family Isididae that plays a vital structural and ecological role in coral reef ecosystems. It is also recognised for producing unique bioactive secondary metabolites, particularly hippuristanol, which exhibits potent antiviral and cytotoxic properties. Despite its conservation and pharmacological importance, baseline demographic data for I. hippuris across North Sulawesi marine protected areas remain scarce. This study assessed the distribution, abundance, and population density of I. hippuris within B

title: Silicate accumulation in taxonomically diverse seaweeds: morphology, uptake, visualization and environmental responses
abstract: Abstract Silicon is required by some microalgae but use and accumulation by seaweeds has been quantified in few taxa. This study aimed to examine biogenic Si (bSi) in taxonomically and morphologically diverse seaweeds, measure Si uptake rates, assess the effects of environmental conditions on bSi, and visualize Si within seaweed tissues. bSi was determined in 57 seaweed taxa across 17 taxonomic orders collected around Tasmania, Australia. institutions: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

title: Spatial disparities in surf-resource sustainability: Implications for coastal policy and marine education in Taiwan
abstract: This study situates global surf sustainability within the Taiwanese context, where recreational surfing has developed since the 1980s and expanded internationally after 2010, yet region-wide assessments of surf-resource sustainability remain limited. Little is known about how sustainability conditions vary across Taiwan’s coastal regions, which sustainability dimensions contribute most strongly to these disparities, and what implications such patterns have for coastal governance and marine education policy. institutions: National Pingtung University of Science and Technology

title: Combined effects of elevated temperature and fluoxetine exposure on early development of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus
abstract: Temperature rise associated with climate change increases the vulnerability of coastal species, which are also exposed to pharmaceuticals. We investigated the effects of thermal stress and fluoxetine (FLX), alone and in combination, on early developmental stages of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus, a key coastal species. Gametes, zygotes and embryos were exposed to ambient (18°C) and near-future projections (21°C, 24°C) to identify the most sensitive developmental stage to warming. In parallel, environmentally relevant FLX concentrations were tested under near-future temperature scenarios.

title: Projecting Impacts of Marine Heatwaves and Their Effects on Long‐Term Changes in Marine Ecosystems Over the 21st Century
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasing in frequency, duration and intensity under climate change. Although current MHWs trigger broad ecological impacts, such as coral bleaching, mass mortality of seagrass meadows, and declines in important fish stocks, the cascading effects of MHWs on ecosystem structure and functions in the 21st century remain unclear. In this study, we utilise a global biomass flow modelling framework to analyse these impacts. Leveraging climate projections from two Earth system models (ESMs), we project marine food webs dynamics at a spatial resolution of 1° latitude and l
institutions: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

title: ANOVATS: a subsampling-based test to detect differences among short time series in marine studies
abstract: Assessing marine ecosystems is important for understanding the impacts of climate change and human activity, as well as for maintaining healthy oceans and ecosystems. In marine science, it is common for biologists and geologists to identify regional differences based on expert knowledge, frequently through data visualization. However, time series data collected through surveys in marine studies typically span only a few decades, limiting the applicability of classical time series methods. title: Navigating coastal futures: Harnessing GIS and multi-criteria decision analysis for sustainable resilience in Kerala's vulnerable Shores
abstract: Extreme weather occurrences, particularly in densely populated coastal places like India, cause loss and devastation, hindering disaster preparedness and long-term viability of vulnerable populations. Research shows that hybrid models, such as Bayesian Networks and Coastal Vulnerability frameworks, outperform traditional methods for measuring coastal vulnerability to Sea Level Rise (SLR). However, their extensive geographical coverage has considerable limitations, including data scarcity and challenges in effectively capturing differences in tiny locations. title: Environmental occurrence and source apportionment of synthetic phenolic antioxidants in typical coastal bays: Drivers and source-specific risk assessment
abstract: Synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) are emerging contaminants whose occurrence, sources, and risks in marine ecosystems remain poorly understood. This study assessed the occurrence, associated factors, potential sources, and ecological and human health risks of 16 SPAs in seawater, sediments, and clams from coastal bays of the Shandong Peninsula based on a single sampling campaign conducted in August 2024. Given the limited data available for SPAs, the driver, source, and risk analyses were exploratory and aimed to identify potential environmental and health implications. Σ₁₆ SPA concentrat

title: Where do the monsters come from? Visualizing marine pollution through biological mutation and game threat design
abstract: Marine pollution is difficult to communicate because much of it is gradual, distributed, and hidden below the surface. Plastic fragments, chemical residues, and damaged habitats may be present long before the sea looks visibly different. This creates a problem for games: players need to understand danger quickly, while the process itself is slow and difficult to see. This paper examines biological mutation as a design language for making that hidden damage visible. title: Environmental Factors Have a Stronger Influence on the Coral Holobiont in Comparison to Geographic Distance Along a 15,000‐km East‐to‐West Transect Through the Coral Triangle, Pacific and Indian Oceans
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To determine the factors that structure coral‐associated microbial communities (bacteria and Symbiodiniaceae). These microbial communities play critical roles in reef ecosystem function, yet the relative importance of environmental versus geographic drivers in structuring these communities across large spatial scales remains poorly understood, particularly across broad Indo‐Pacific gradients that include biodiversity hotspots such as the Coral Triangle. title: Tecnologías de información geográfica y gerencia pública en salud: hacia una vigilancia epidemiológica territorial de la enfermedad diarreica aguda en Perú y América Latina
abstract: La enfermedad diarreica aguda (EDA) persiste como problema prioritario de salud pública en Perú y América Latina. Mediante una revisión sistemática PRISMA de 30 estudios (Scopus y SciELO, 2000-2026), se analizó cómo las Tecnologías de Información Geográfica (TIG) —autocorrelación espacial e indicadores LISA— identifican clústeres de riesgo de EDA. Se concluye que estas herramientas constituyen activos estratégicos de gerencia pública en salud, con potencial para optimizar la planificación territorial, la asignación presupuestaria y la capacidad de respuesta institucional ante brotes.

title: Analisis Kesesuaian Lahan Budidaya Minapadi Berbasis SIG dan AHP di Kecamatan Tanjungkerta, Kabupaten Sumedang
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kesesuaian lahan budidaya Minapadi di Kecamatan Tanjungkerta, Kabupaten Sumedang, melalui integrasi Sistem Informasi Geografis (SIG) dan metode Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), serta mengevaluasi kualitas air pada lima lokasi sampel sebagai pendukung pengembangan minapadi. Data primer meliputi pH, suhu, oksigen terlarut (DO), Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), dan amoniak, sedangkan data sekunder meliputi sumber air, jenis tanah, topografi, tutupan lahan, kerentanan gerakan tanah, dan kerawanan gempa. title: Tracing Groundwater–Seawater exchanges using geochemical tracers (radon, radium, stable isotopes of water) in a seasonally frozen beach
abstract: Groundwater–seawater exchanges remain poorly documented in subarctic and arctic regions, particularly during winter, when coastal ice alters hydrogeology conditions and limits sampling opportunities. This study investigates winter groundwater dynamics at a seasonally frozen beach by combining the use of various geochemical tracers. title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. title: 4-MBC in Australian sunscreens as an unmonitored discharge pathway into Great Barrier Reef coastal waters
abstract: Abstract 4-Methylbenzylidene camphor (4-MBC, also known as enzacamene), a chemical UV filter prohibited or never permitted across the EU, UK, China, ASEAN, US, and Japan, remains legal in Australian therapeutic sunscreens at concentrations up to 4% w/w. The European Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety concluded in 2022 that no safe concentration could be established, and the UK Scientific Advisory Group on Chemical Safety confirmed this in 2025. title: Constraint-Based Adaptive Grids for Compact Representation of Marine Scalar Fields
abstract: Fixed-block representations can obscure heterogeneous local variability in marine scalar fields. We present a deterministic adaptive representation in which anchored dyadic tiles merge under a field-normalized local-range rule and a realized-tile diameter cap. Area-weighted tile values provide lossy reconstruction, whereas exact tile-to-cell membership preserves the link to the authoritative source grid. title: Rheumatic Heart Disease Burden and Sex Differences in China and ASEAN Countries, 1990–2030: A Comparative Analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
abstract: Background: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) remains a major public health concern in low‑ and middle‑income countries. Systematic comparisons between China and the ten ASEAN member states examining sex disparities are scarce. Methods: Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 data, we analyzed RHD burden in China and ten ASEAN countries from 1990 to 2023. Key measures included age‑standardized prevalence (ASPR), mortality (ASMR), and disability‑adjusted life‑years rates (ASDR). title: Marine habitat use and movement of sympatric anadromous Dolly Varden and Arctic Char in the Canadian Arctic
abstract: Abstract Objective Inuit subsistence fishers in Kugluktuk, Nunavut, Canada, have noticed changes in the timing and locations of their catches of Arctic Char Salvelinus alpinus and northern form Dolly Varden S. malma malma (collectively referred to by the community as “char”) in the past ∼20 years. In response, an ongoing research program was formed to study char in partnership with the Kugluktuk Hunters and Trappers Organization. title: Mathematics anxiety and problem-solving ability in numerical methods courses: A repeated cross-sectional study across two Southeast Asian universities
abstract: Mathematics anxiety (MA) impedes mathematical learning by taxing cognitive resources, negatively affecting problem-solving ability (PSA). Some evidence suggests that the strength and nature of this negative association may vary across educational and cultural contexts. However, cross-cultural studies on MA and PSA, especially in Southeast Asia, remain limited. This study investigated cohort-level patterns of MA and PSA in a transnational Numerical Methods course at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) and Universitas Pahlawan (UP), Indonesia. title: Landscape of Targetable Genetic Alterations in Advanced Cholangiocarcinoma among Patients in Southeast Asia
abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a heterogeneous form of biliary tract cancer, for which treatment options remain limited; however, molecular profiling technology has helped in uncovering genomic mutations that can be used in precision oncology. This molecular profiling study has been carried out retrospectively in order to investigate the genomic alterations that are targetable in advanced cholangiocarcinomas of Southeast Asia. Samples from 126 patients were analyzed through targeted next generation sequencing in order to identify somatic mutations, copy number alterations, and gene fusions. Ident
institutions: Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology

title: Three decades of marine bioregions evolution through analysis of phytoplankton phenology
abstract: Abstract. Ocean biogeochemistry is undergoing significant modification in response to climate change. To better understand these evolution, we present a novel ocean monitoring indicator approach that tracks the temporal evolution of marine bioregions of similar phytoplankton phenologies. Chlorophyll-a concentration observations from remotely sensed ocean color describe seven distinct marine bioregions characterized by their unique patterns of phytoplankton biomass seasonality. title: Winter disturbances drive community change in subarctic eelgrass meadows
abstract: The dynamics of winter sea ice and icefoot play a fundamental role in structuring intertidal ecosystems in subarctic environments. However, ongoing climate warming is altering ice regimes across northern shorelines. In the St. Lawrence marine estuary (Canada), reduced formation of icefoot increasingly exposes benthic habitats to winter-related disturbances. We investigated how such disturbance influences eelgrass ( Zostera marina L.) meadows and associated benthic communities using a before-and-after comparison spanning the 2024-2025 winter season. title: Experimental snowball earth viscosity drives the evolution of motile multicellularity
abstract: During the 70-million-year Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity over 3-fold. Unicellular eukaryotes in this environment would have faced severe constraints on movement and nutrient uptake, while nascent multicellular organisms, with larger size and collective mobility, could have gained an adaptive advantage. We experimentally tested whether viscosity-induced metabolic constraints could have selected for multicellular phenotypes, potentially driving the origin or early diversification of multicellularity. title: Assessment of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion Potential in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia: Energy Performance, Techno-Economic Feasibility, and Environmental Considerations
abstract: This study evaluated the potential of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion as a renewable electricity source in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia. Ocean temperature data from the World Ocean Atlas for 1955-2018 at station 21576 were analyzed to characterize the surface and deep-water thermal conditions and to assess the performance of an open-cycle Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion system. The assessment covered thermodynamic efficiency, electrical power generation, production cost, freshwater production, and potential environmental impacts. title: Remobilized volcanogenic sediments boost photophysiological activity in three symbiotic reef-building coral species
abstract: Abstract Coral reefs that surround volcanic islands are continually influenced by run-off carrying remobilized volcanogenic sediments. Although unaltered volcanic ash is known to supply trace metals that enhance coral holobiont productivity, the impacts of long-term exposure to weathered tephra, a far more likely scenario in island settings, are less understood. title: Pyropia haitanensis cultivation enhances water quality and reshapes microbial communities in coastal water and connected aquaculture ponds
abstract: Seaweed cultivation offers nature-based bioremediation for aquaculture effluents, yet its cascading effects on microbial ecosystems remain poorly understood. This study evaluated Pyropia haitanensis cultivation impacts across four phenological stages in nearshore marine (Cultivation Area, PS; Control Sea, CS) and connected aquaculture ponds (Influenced Pond, PA; Control Pond, CA). Results showed that P. haitanensis cultivation significantly improved water quality in PS and PA by increasing dissolved oxygen and pH while reducing NH₄⁺-N, TN, TC, and TOC. title: Meandering shorelines: The potential for multi-level habitat complexity to ecologically enhance artificial coastal defences
abstract: Artificial coastal defences simplify, linearize, and homogenize the coast, leading to reduced species diversity, ecological functioning, and ecosystem services. Previous active management research has shown that greater habitat complexity at millimeter to decimeter scales increases the diversity of fauna and flora living on constructed shores, however, little is known regarding the potential effects of increasing the scale of complexity on larger marine species. title: Global triazine herbicide pollution impairs marine phytoplankton nutrition through disruption of acetyl-CoA-related metabolism
abstract: Herbicide contamination impairs marine primary productivity, yet its subcellular impact on phytoplankton carbon allocation remains poorly understood. Global monitoring (1990–2023) revealed triazine herbicides as the dominant coastal pollutants, with atrazine and simazine exceeding 80% detection frequency; their combined toxicity corresponded to a median atrazine-equivalent concentration of 0.68 nmol L −1 . title: From shark hunters to sea guardians: Environmental literacy transformation and socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people in Sapeken Islands, East Java-Indonesia
abstract: The Bajo people are known for their closeness to and dependence on the sea. Over the past few decades, the Bajo people have undergone significant changes that are worth examining. This study aims to analyze the socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people who inhabit Sadulang Besar Island, Sapeken Archipelago, East Java, with particular attention to how environmental literacy, intergenerational learning, and shifting livelihood strategies have contributed to changes in marine practices and ecological identity. title: Hydrodynamics of bio-mimetic sponge arrays with non-uniform triangular arrangement under wave actions
abstract: Bio-inspired marine structures have attracted increasing attention as nature-based solutions for modifying coastal hydrodynamics and enhancing momentum exchange. Previous studies on isolated and dual sponge-inspired elements have shown limited hydrodynamic effectiveness under relatively low-height waves, where velocity redistribution and turbulence generation remain weak. To address this limitation, the present study proposes and experimentally fabricates a bio-mimetic pillar coral composed of non-uniform triangular sponge elements arranged in a progressive three-line configuration. title: Macrobenthic community turnover along a compressed depth gradient in the East Sea
abstract: The East Sea of Korea is a semi-enclosed marginal sea characterized by a steep bathymetric gradient, creating a compressed environmental gradient that provides an ideal study area for investigating benthic macrofaunal communities. Still, quantitative assessments of community patterns across the continuous coastal-to-deep-sea gradient remain limited in the East Sea of Korea. This study analyzed the distribution and community transition patterns of macrobenthic communities along the continuous coastal-to-deep-sea depth gradient in the East Sea. title: Biomass and Carbon Allocation in Tree Components of Beech-Chestnut Mixed Forests in Coastal Western Black Sea Region
abstract: Aim of study: Estimating C storage using biomass data is a widely used method for forest ecosystems. In most studies, the content of biomass is calculated by destructive methods such as cutting and sampling of trees on sampling plots. However, tree biomass can be estimated using diameter and height data without disturbing the site. The aim of this study is to determine the content of above-and below-ground biomass and their carbon (C) stocks in an eastern beech (Fagus orientalis Lipsky) and Anatolian chestnut (Castanea sativa Mill.) mixed forest. title: Environmental assessment of shrimp farming in coastal Tamil Nadu of India: a case study of Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai districts
abstract: Shrimp aquaculture is a major economic activity in Tamil Nadu, with the Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai districts together accounting for nearly 45% of the state’s licensed shrimp farms. Although the sector has periodically attracted concern regarding its environmental sustainability particularly with respect to shrimp farm discharge water quality and coastal ecosystem health there remains a paucity of empirical, field-based assessments from this region. institutions: Tamil Nadu Dr. J Jayalalitha Fisheries University

title: Advanced Assessment of the Agro-Silvo-Pastoral Coherence in Transboundary Transitional Water Regions
abstract: Transitional waters play a vital role in the ecological health and sustainability of coastal areas. According to European Union legislation, transitional waters are coastal water bodies influenced by freshwater flows but are partly saline due to their proximity to the sea. This study focuses on agricultural and forestry regions adjacent to transboundary transitional waters—i.e., areas where two or more countries share an estuary, tidal inlet, delta, or lagoon and have a contiguous border in their territorial waters. title: Phosphate-Modified Co/BaTiO₃@Vulcan Nanocomposite for Stable Seawater Oxygen Evolution
abstract: This study presents a design strategy for developing corrosion-resistant anode materials, establishing a successful baseline for further optimization in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) during direct seawater splitting. Cobalt nanocomposites supported on BaTiO₃ and Vulcan XC72R carbon black were synthesized via a combined sol-gel and microwave-assisted methodology using cellulose phosphate (CP) as a structural template and phosphorus source. title: Environmental Security of the Gulf During Armed Conflict: Marine Pollution Risks, GCC Preparedness, and a Regional Emergency-Response Framework
abstract: The Gulf is a strategically crucial and environmentally vulnerable semi-enclosed marine system supporting petroleum industries, international shipping, desalination facilities, coastal ecosystems, and urban centers. Alongside chronic industrial and maritime pressures, armed conflict introduces severe risks via direct military operations, targeting of energy infrastructure, drone and missile strikes, hazardous material releases, and disruption of monitoring networks. This review evaluates the potential marine pollution consequences of armed conflict in the region, examining historical precedent
journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: Seascape genomics reveals high genetic diversity and apparent panmixia in endemic Southern Ocean phytoplankton
abstract: Abstract The adaptive potential and resilience of cold‐adapted phytoplankton to climate change have the potential to impact polar marine food webs and global biogeochemical cycles. Two central but poorly constrained facets of adaptive potential in polar phytoplankton are standing genetic diversity and its spatial structure. Here, we partially sequenced 30 field isolate genomes of a commonly‐occurring endemic Southern Ocean (SO) phytoplankton, the diatom Actinocyclus actinochilus , and analyzed patterns in standing genetic diversity and geographic structure. title: Marine renewable energy and cumulative effects assessments: Summary of the state of play
abstract: Cumulative effects result from interacting human activities across space or time, potentially involving multiple sectors, which can affect ecosystem components. Cumulative effects assessments (CEAs) systematically identify and evaluate the compound effects of multiple pressures that may occur within and across industries (and via interaction with climate change induced ecosystem shifts), causing large-scale environmental change. title: Industry-led mitigation of seal bycatch in North Sea pelagic trawl fisheries: Evaluating excluder device effectiveness and policy implications
abstract: Bycatch of marine mammals in commercial fisheries presents conservation, operational, and regulatory challenges, particularly in the Greater North Sea where trawl fisheries targeting forage fish overlap with seal foraging habitats. This study evaluates the effectiveness of two seal excluder devices—the DPPO’s excluder tube and the PFA’s excluder grid—designed to reduce incidental seal captures in sandeel and herring fisheries, respectively. Reproductive thermoregulation in marine mammals: mechanisms, adaptations and evolutionary implications
abstract: Marine mammals inhabit thermally challenging environments in which maintaining internal body temperature is essential for survival, metabolic function, and reproductive success. Unlike terrestrial mammals, many marine male species lack external reproductive structures (e.g. scrotum), raising questions about how reproductive temperatures are regulated in the absence of conventional cooling mechanisms. This review synthesizes current knowledge of reproductive thermoregulation in marine mammals, with a focus on cetaceans and pinnipeds, and highlights key anatomical and physiological adaptations.

title: Distribution-based assessment reveals structural shifts in a protected estuarine gastropod, Clithon retropictus (Mollusca: Gastropoda)
abstract: Understanding temporal variation in estuarine populations is essential for conserving species inhabiting environmentally heterogeneous coastal habitats. Clithon retropictus is a protected brackish-water gastropod in South Korea that inhabits algae-covered stones in small tidal rivers and is vulnerable to changes in salinity gradients, substrate structure, and fragmentation of estuarine habitats. We evaluated long-term changes in the abundance structure of this species using national-scale ecological monitoring data collected from 2016 to 2024. title: Anthropized environments as reservoirs of hidden and exotic diversity in marine annelids: sicilian ports as a case study
abstract: Marine annelids are key components of benthic ecosystems, yet their diversity remains unevenly documented, particularly in anthropized habitats. In Sicily (Mediterranean Sea), significant knowledge gaps persist regarding port benthic communities and their role in the spread of non-indigenous species (NIS). This study provides the first characterization of polychaete assemblages in Sicilian ports in over three decades, with a specific focus on biodiversity patterns and NIS occurrence. title: Shell characteristics and Sr–Nd–Pb isotope signatures of Creseis acicula during its 2020 outbreak near Daya Bay Nuclear Power Station
abstract: Abstract China ranks second in the world in terms of nuclear power generation, making significant contributions to China’s green economic and social development. Chinese nuclear power plants are located in coastal areas, which are prone to frequent outbreaks of marine organisms due to inputs from terrestrial sources. These outbreaks have led to shutdowns of varying severity at nuclear power plants. However, there is currently limited research on the processes involved in marine-organism outbreaks. Daya Bay Nuclear Power Station (DBNPS) is the first large-scale commercial nuclear power station

title: Intra-annual dynamics of larval fish assemblages and their environmental associations in the central Southern Black Sea
abstract: Larval fish assemblages are crucial indicators for monitoring marine ecosystem dynamics and the recruitment potential of fishery stocks. This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics of larval fish assemblages in the central Southern Black Sea (Sinop) and the environmental parameters shaping these patterns. An intra-annual monthly sampling survey identified 35 species across 20 families; the assemblage structure was dominated by Engraulis encrasicolus, Gobius niger, Sprattus sprattus, Mullus barbatus and Trachurus mediterraneus. title: No effect of short‐term exposure to ocean acidification on individual‐level variation in behaviour and susceptibility to predation in a Great Barrier Reef damselfish
abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification, caused by rising carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) in the atmosphere, has been reported to negatively impact a wide variety of behaviours in fishes, including activity, exploration, and predator avoidance. These effects have been documented at the population level, but many animal species naturally show large and repeatable individual‐level differences in behaviour. How environmental stressors, such as ocean acidification, affect behavioural variation at the individual level remains largely unknown but is vital in understanding adaptation given natural selection operates on

title: Determination of seasonal groundwater recharge potential in the coastal mining town of Jose Panganiban, Philippines
abstract: Coastal groundwater resources are highly vulnerable to the combined risks of heavy metal contamination and saltwater intrusion where artisanal small-scale gold mining is active. This study used a GIS-based analysis to identify susceptible coastal aquifers in the municipality of Jose Panganiban, Philippines, by examining the reduction in groundwater potential coincident with the seasonal oscillation of precipitation, the main driver of recharge. journal: Journal of Degraded and Mining Lands Management

title: Effects of the summer season and religious holiday periods on tropospheric NO₂ levels in Türkiye’s coastal tourism destinations: A Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI and GIS-based analysis (2023–2025)
abstract: This study investigates tropospheric NO2 variations observed in the Mediterranean and Aegean regions—Türkiye’s prominent coastal tourism hubs—during the 2023–2025 period, within the context of seasonal summer intensity and short-term mobility during Eid al-Fitr (Ramadan Feast) and Eid al-Adha (Feast of Sacrifice). The study utilizes Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI tropospheric NO2 data to generate daily regional median values for selected coastal tourism districts. title: Dashboard e Indicatori sul Climate Change per i Planning Decision Support Systems
abstract: What are geospatial dashboards, and how can they support planning and Planning Decision Support Systems (PDSS) addressing Climate Change (CC)? Starting from the literature, the paper analyses dashboards and their indicators as used in planning, proposing criteria for an integrated, dynamic, and operational PDSS for diverse plan recipients at local and global scales. title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
abstract: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. title: Fin whale movement patterns from the Mediterranean sea reveal summer habitat use in the North Atlantic and potential feeding behavior
abstract: Abstract Understanding the movements of highly mobile marine species is essential for identifying critical habitats and developing effective conservation measures. Although occasional movements of fin whales ( Balaenoptera physalus ) between the Mediterranean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean have been reported, the extent to which these movements represent a recurrent component of Mediterranean fin whale ecology remains unclear. institutions: Instituto de Instrumentación para Imagen Molecular

title: Functional Identity Drives Directional Shifts in Freshwater Plankton Biomass–Size Relationships
abstract: Body size is a master variable in ecology that can predict ecosystem-level processes and reflect environmental conditions across diverse ecosystems. In freshwater ecosystems, the relationship between body size and biomass provides a powerful tool for characterizing community structure and trophic transfer efficiency. While these relationships are well established at the whole-community level, responses within plankton functional groups with distinct ecological characteristics have yet to be explored. In this study, we analysed plankton biomass-size relationships across > 550 Canadian lakes. Fo

title: Visualizing the Nuclear: Visibility and Invisibility in U.S. Photographic Representations from the Pacific
abstract: This article examines the visual culture of U.S. nuclear imperialism in the Pacific through an analysis of several widely circulated photographs: two images of atomic testing at Bikini Atoll published in Life magazine in 1946, and a photograph of the nuclear-powered USS Enterprise produced during Operation Sea Orbit in 1964. Drawing on theories of coloniality, whiteness, and militourism, this article traces the shift from the hypervisibility of the atomic explosion to the increasing invisibility of nuclear power within Cold War visual discourse. title: Stronger Together: Isograft Fusion Accelerates Recovery and May Facilitate Heat‐Evolved Symbiont Transmission in Bleached Adult Corals
abstract: Experimentally evolved, heat-tolerant algal symbionts (heat-evolved; HE) offer a promising means of enhancing coral holobiont thermotolerance under warming oceans. However, translating their benefits into restoration practices requires scalable delivery methods. Coral tissue fusion may provide one such pathway by facilitating HE symbiont transfer to wild corals; however, its feasibility remains largely untested. title: Development of A Composite Sustainability Index Within An Integrated Coastal Zone Management Framework: A Case Study of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
abstract: Coastal regions are increasingly under compounded pressures from climate change and rapid socioeconomic development, and integrated approaches to sustainability assessment are needed. This study assesses coastal sustainability in Ho Chi Minh City by developing a composite sustainability index (CSI) structured around three key dimensions: socioeconomic, ecoenvironmental, and institutional management. institutions: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

title: Spatial prioritization of urban green infrastructure for heat mitigation: a gis-mcda approach in Chennai, India
abstract: Urbanization and loss of vegetated land have amplified the Urban Heat Island (UHI) phenomenon which severely worsens urban climate in the main cities of the developing nations. This research develops a GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis (GIs-MCDA) framework to quantify green space shortfalls, surface thermal exposure, and urban microclimates across the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC), India. High-resolution Landsat 8/9 TIRS and OLI data were processed to generate Land Surface Temperature (LST) and NDVI layers for illustrating microclimatic surface temperature and vegetation patterns,
institutions: School of Planning and Architecture Delhi

title: Self-reporting alkalinity-responsive hydrogel for visual monitoring and microenvironment remodeling of seawater-immersed infected wounds
abstract: Seawater-associated infected wounds involve alkaline and hyperosmotic stress, polymicrobial contamination, biofilms, and persistent inflammation, collectively delaying healing. Herein, we developed QCB-Au@SPG, a pH-responsive hydrogel integrating fluorescent antibacterial QCB-Au, an alkali-sensitive SA-PBA network, and photocrosslinkable GelMA. QCB-Au@SPG exhibited a linear fluorescence response across pH 4–8 (R² = 0.998), enabling semi-quantitative visualization of pH variation, while alkaline conditions moderately enhanced QCB-Au release. institutions: First Affiliated Hospital of Jiangxi Medical College

title: Visualizing Reversible Uranyl (UO 2 2+ ) Capture and Release With Self‐Indicating Porous Organic Polymers
abstract: Seawater uranium extraction is a promising sustainable energy pathway; however, practical application requires advanced adsorbents that combine reversible, high uranium‐uptake capacity with the ability to track sorption cycles. Herein, we report self‐indicating porous organic polymers (POPs), Sal‐POP and Im‐POP , containing uranyl (UO 2 2+ ) ion‐coordinating salphen and o ‐hydroxy imine cores with UO 2 2+ binding energies up to −71.94 kcal mol −1 as uranium adsorbents, and demonstrate their reversible, high uranium extraction capacities up to 0.114 g g −1 h −1 . title: Cultivation of Cladophora glomerata Under Low‐Salinity Conditions: Ecological Controls, Production Constraints and Baltic Sea Deployment
abstract: ABSTRACT Brackish and freshwater coastal systems often combine nutrient enrichment with proximity to wastewater, aquaculture and coastal infrastructure, yet macroalgal cultivation under low‐salinity conditions remains poorly validated. This review evaluates whether Cladophora glomerata , commonly managed as nuisance biomass, can be developed as a seasonal crop and nutrient‐recovery tool in low‐salinity systems, with emphasis on the Baltic Sea. A structured evidence synthesis used 80 sources selected from a broad evidence register, separating direct C. glomerata evidence from mechanistically tr

title: Spatial Variability and Long‐Term Trends in Winter Phytoplankton of the Warming Eastern Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Abstract The Eastern Mediterranean Sea (EMS) is among the fastest‐warming ocean regions, but the impacts of this warming on phytoplankton are unclear. Here, wintertime field observations were conducted across the EMS. These observations showed that small photosynthetic eukaryotes (<20 μm) dominated phytoplankton communities, collectively accounting for >60% of total chlorophyll a (Chl‐a) despite severe nitrate‐ and phosphate‐depleted conditions. institutions: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel

title: Measuring Dry Deposition of Sea Spray Aerosol and Height of Aerosol Plume Using a Controlled Wave Pool
abstract: Abstract Deposition of sea spray aerosols facilitates atmospheric corrosion of materials, requiring maintenance and replacement over time. However, the dimensions of sea spray aerosol plumes produced from breaking waves have not been well‐characterized, limiting useful prediction of particle transport downwind and atmospheric corrosion. Therefore, this project aimed to measure sea spray aerosol production from breaking waves in a controlled environment at several elevations to obtain the height profile of an aerosol plume. title: Ocean predators as indicators of nano- and microplastic prevalence in pelagic food webs
abstract: Quantifying nano- and microplastics (NMPs) in ocean predators is fundamental to understanding the prevalence of these contaminants and potential impacts on ecosystem health. Pyrolysis gas chromatography tandem mass spectrometry with lipid correction was used to determine NMP concentrations and polymer composition in the muscle tissue of two pelagic predators (dolphinfish [ Coryphaena hippurus ], yellowfin tuna [ Thunnus albacares ]) across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. title: A review on visualization of flexible VOC sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are ubiquitously present in the natural environment and are produced by human activities, serving as key indicators of the chemical state of substances. The integration of flexible sensors and visualization technologies offers novel solutions for on-site, in-situ, and real-time VOC detection. institutions: Khalifa University of Science and Technology

title: Climate change and biological traits: interglacial stability and higher glacial functional diversity in Late Quaternary molluscan assemblages of the Adriatic Sea (Italy)
abstract: Abstract Studies on the effects of long-term climate change on marine communities are crucial to our understanding of ecosystem resilience. The Late Quaternary fossil record, dominated by extant taxa, provides a valuable archive of past biotic responses to major climate fluctuations. While most studies on faunal turnover so far have focused on taxonomic identity, trait-based approaches are becoming increasingly common as they provide a stronger link to ecosystem functioning. title: Prorocentrum pseudonux sp. nov. ( Prorocentrales, Dinophyceae ): A new nanoplanktonic dinoflagellate from the open tropical Pacific Ocean
abstract: SUMMARY While phytoplankton from the coasts of temperate seas has received considerable attention, phytoplankton from the open tropical ocean, especially the smallest fraction, remains understudied. Here, we describe a new nanoplanktonic dinoflagellate from the tropical Pacific Ocean. Prorocentrum pseudonux sp. nov. is slightly oval in thecal view, measuring 6–9 μm long and 5–8 μm deep. The theca is smooth with a few pores of different size classes. title: Small‐Scale Topographic Variability Shapes Molecular Diversity of Organic Matter in Coastal Dune Soils
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays a crucial role in carbon and nutrient cycling across terrestrial, aquatic, and marine ecosystems. Most terrestrial OM originates from litter and soils, where it is mobilized by percolating rainwater before entering the groundwater. Consequently, groundwater OM composition can be influenced by soil processes such as organic matter processing above the groundwater surface. title: Application of eDNA metabarcoding for high-resolution reconstruction of the trophic web of an Arctic fjord
abstract: Abstract In a rapidly changing Arctic, the Kongsfjorden marine ecosystem was investigated to explore its community composition and structural dynamics using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding. Samples were collected with metaprobes , passive eDNA samplers deployed within fish traps in the coastal zone and towed along a transect in the mid-fjord zone. Mitochondrial COI and ribosomal 18 S SSU (V8-V9 region) genes were amplified to characterize metazoan and protist communities, respectively. title: Assessment of groundwater quality using GWQI and an AHP-Developed Health-Risk-Oriented Index (HR-GWQI): evidence from the Mitidja Plain (Algeria)
abstract: Groundwater quality assessment in the alluvial aquifer system of the Mitidja Plain during the 2019 low-water period was conducted using an integrated approach combining the conventional Groundwater Quality Index (GWQI) with an innovative Human Risk-Groundwater Quality Index (HR-GWQI) developed through Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) weighting and GIS-based spatial analysis. title: Território quilombola e fragilidades ambientais
abstract: Coastal systems are dynamic spaces where natural elements and human actions interact in complex ways, generating varying degrees of environmental fragility. Thus, this paper aims to assess the environmental fragility of the Quilombo do Cumbe Territory, using the sub-watershed in which the territory is located as the spatial unit of analysis. The methodological approach is based on an integrated analysis, supported by General Systems Theory (Bertalanffy, 1975) and an adaptation of Ross’s proposal (1994, 2012). title: Carbon fluxes within an Arctica islandica habitat in the German Baltic Sea
abstract: Ongoing climate change and rising CO 2 emissions highlight the need to understand ecosystem carbon cycling to guide the conservation of carbon-rich, biodiverse habitats. We investigated organic carbon cycling and storage associated with the long-lived bivalve Arctica islandica in the German Baltic Sea. Through filtration and bioturbation, A. islandica may enhance the burial of organic carbon in deeper sediment layers. institutions: Leibniz Institute for Baltic Sea Research Warnemünde

title: Visualizing the penetration behavior of tapered thread piles via transparent soil: Effects of thread design
abstract: With superior construction efficiency and load-bearing performance, precast tapered thread piles hold significant potential for offshore and coastal infrastructure. However, their installation mechanics remain poorly understood, and visual experimental investigations are scarce. To address this knowledge gap, this study utilizes a developed optomechanically coupled testing system to investigate the continuous penetration process of tapered thread piles. title: Volcanic stratigraphy offshore East Montserrat: Selective preservation and subaqueous remobilisation in marine records
abstract: Abstract In tectonically active regions, volcanic eruptions generate large volumes of material that are transported offshore through processes such as pyroclastic density currents, turbidity currents, and secondary sediment remobilisation. These deposits form key stratigraphic markers for reconstructing eruptive histories, yet their preservation, correlation with onshore events, and modification by mass wasting remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the effectiveness of marine sedimentary sequences in recording eruptive and mass-transport events from Soufrière Hills Volcano offs

title: Quantitative Text-based Shrinking-society Risk Index for Multidimensional Assessment in Coastal Regions

title: PREFERENCES OF DIGITAL NOMADS: ANALYZING POPULAR DESTINATIONS AND DECISION-MAKING FACTORS THROUGH INTERACTIVE DATA VISUALIZATIONS USING PUBLIC ACCESS DATABASES
abstract: Digital nomadism is a rapidly spreading form of location-independent work that is fundamentally transforming the global labour market, economy, and tourism. The aim of this study is to quantitatively explore and model the destination preferences of digital nomads and to present an innovative, interactive data visualization framework. Our research analyses the structural changes of the period 2021-2024 following the logic of the PEST model (Political, Economical, Social, Technological). title: Antifungal potential and ecological perspectives of selected seagrass species from tropical coastal meadows
abstract: Seagrasses have gathered increasing attention due to their multifaceted ecological roles. Apart from their ecological significance, seagrasses have exhibited potent antifungal properties, indicating potential for diverse applications. The antifungal efficacy of methanolic extracts derived from five seagrass species ( Cymodocea serrulata , Cymodocea rotundata , Halodule pinifolia , Halophila ovalis , and Syringodium isoetifolium ) was assessed against pathogenic fungal strains using the agar well diffusion method. title: Epistemic justice and deep-sea mining: UNCLOS’s facilitation of epistemic diversity the International Seabed Authority’s decision-making process
abstract: The paper discusses epistemic justice as a central justice framework to be considered in the regulatory process of exploitative deep sea mining, with the aim of bringing attention to the relevance of epistemic justice and diversity to deep sea mining scholarship. Epistemic justice is here understood as deeply connected to a broader social equity, and entails the fair treatment of different ’knowers’ and a creation, sharing, and validation of knowledge that is fundamentally diverse rather than based on one dominant knowledge-tradition. title: New evidence of the early stages of establishment of the parrotfish Sparisoma cretense (Teleostei: Labridae) following northward and westward range expansion in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Abstract Sparisoma cretense is undergoing a range expansion across the Mediterranean Sea, yet its establishment at northern latitudes of the westernmost Mediterranean remains uncertain. During July 2025, patterns consistent with the establishment of S. cretense in Cabrera National Park (39º 09’ N; 2º 57’ E) were assessed, and habitat features associated with its occurrence were identified. Underwater visual censuses were conducted, recording abundance, total length, sex, habitat composition, and the hydrodynamic exposure level of each locality. title: Integrating Environmental DNA ( eDNA ) Approaches to Enhance Fisheries Advisories Through Marine Food Web Reconstruction: Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental DNA (eDNA) transforms marine ecological research through non‐invasive assessment of ecosystem structure with higher taxonomic resolution. This study explores the potential of eDNA metabarcoding to enhance fisheries advisories through food web reconstruction, bridging ecological insights with ecosystem‐based fisheries management. This review elucidates the concepts of eDNA and explores its applications in food web studies and Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) dynamics. title: Molecular approaches to phylogeny and species boundaries in Lethrinus (Teleostei, Lethrinidae): insights from a taxonomic complex along Mozambique coast
abstract: Abstract Accurate species delimitation is essential for understanding the evolutionary processes that generate and maintain biodiversity, particularly in marine systems characterized by high connectivity and widespread distributions. Reef-associated fishes of the Indo–West Pacific provide an ideal framework to investigate these dynamics, yet many taxa remain poorly resolved due to morphological conservatism and cryptic diversity. title: Environmental and economic assessment of alternative marine energy pathways using integrated life cycle analysis
abstract: The maritime sector faces increasing pressure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while maintaining economic feasibility. In response to the International Maritime Organization’s decarbonization targets, alternative marine fuels have gained significant attention as potential pathways toward low-carbon shipping. This study presents an integrated well-to-wake life cycle assessment (LCA) and life cycle cost assessment (LCCA) of marine diesel oil (MDO), liquefied natural gas (LNG), biodiesel, methanol, E-methanol, E-diesel, E-ammonia, and hydrogen using real operational data from a 6177 GT general

title: Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Surface Water and Fluvial Sediments of a Rural Gulf Coast Watershed: A Year-long Spatiotemporal Assessment
abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants of significant health concern. This study quantified the spatiotemporal occurrence of 40 PFAS in surface water and fluvial sediments across the Lavaca Watershed and Lavaca Bay, Texas, a rural Gulf Coast system with limited potential point sources. Monthly sampling was conducted at 12 sites from January to December 2025, and samples were analyzed following U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Method 1633A. title: Shear strength evolution and multi-factor coupling friction model of coral sand-structure interface
abstract: The shear strength of coral sand-pile interface affects the bearing capacity of pile foundation in island and reef engineering. However, there is still a lack of interface shear strength prediction model that can comprehensively consider the influence of multiple factors. In this paper, the influence of roughness of pile (concrete, steel and aluminum alloy), normal stress and relative density of soil on the shear characteristics of pile-soil contact interface is systematically studied by using a large-scale interface shear apparatus developed independently. title: Metabolomic profiling and anticancer effects of Red Sea sponges Liosina granularis and Callyspongia crassa on prostate and ovarian cancer cells
abstract: Abstract Marine sponges are rich sources of bioactive secondary metabolites with potential relevance to anticancer drug discovery. This study investigated the metabolomic profiles and preliminary anticancer activity of methanolic extracts from two Red Sea sponge species, Liosina granularis (LGE) and Callyspongia crassa (CCE), using prostate (PC3) and ovarian (SKOV-3) cancer cell models. LC-MS/MS analysis annotated 44 metabolites, including alkaloids, long-chain amides, fatty acids, polyketides, and terpenoids. title: A coupled water-quality–Ecopath with Ecosim model incorporating sand-lance aestivation dynamics in the Harima-Nada Sea
abstract: Sand lance ( Ammodytes japonicus ) is an important forage fish in the Harima-Nada Sea, Japan, but its stock has declined markedly in recent decades under concurrent changes in nutrient availability and water temperature. To clarify the mechanisms underlying these changes, we developed a region-specific coupled water-quality–Ecopath with Ecosim (EwE) model that explicitly incorporates sand-lance aestivation dynamics. title: Self-organized hummock-hollow patterns redistribute salinity stress in coastal meadows
abstract: Self-organization theory predicts that ecosystem functioning and resilience can emerge from feedbacks that generate spatial patterns. These emergent properties have commonly been explained by local positive feedbacks that concentrate limiting resources within productive patches. Here, we identify a stress-redistribution feedback underlying self-organized hummock-hollow patterning. title: Web-Based Extreme Weather Monitoring and Early Warning System for Traditional Fishermen Using IoT Sensor Data
abstract: Extreme weather can disrupt traditional fishing activities and increase safety risks, particularly when local weather information is difficult to access before departure. This study develops a web-based extreme weather monitoring and early warning system for traditional fishermen using Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data. The system integrates an ESP32 microcontroller with a DHT22 sensor, rain sensor, and anemometer to acquire temperature, humidity, rainfall, and wind-speed data at ten-second intervals. title: Thermal resource characterization for regional OTEC site screening in the Caribbean using AHP–TOPSIS
abstract: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) offers a sustainable option for improving energy security in the hurricane-prone Caribbean region. This study established a regional screening framework for identifying offshore OTEC candidate sites based on a high-resolution (∼1 km) characterization of the Mean Sea Water Temperature Difference (ΔT m ) and thermal persistence over a 19-year period under hurricane and non-hurricane seasons. title: Spatial patterns and environmental associations of plankton communities in the Karst free-flowing Chishui river: Insights from eDNA metabarcoding and network analysis
abstract: Understanding the mechanisms governing plankton community assembly and spatial heterogeneity is fundamental for freshwater ecosystem conservation, yet such knowledge remains scarce for free - flowing rivers in Karst regions facing compounding anthropogenic pressures. Here, we investigated the spatial patterns, community – environment relationships, and co-occurrence network architecture of phytoplankton and zooplankton communities along the mainstem of the Chishui River, the last undammed tributary of the upper Yangtze River and a biodiversity hotspot of global conservation significance. title: Softening mechanism and fatigue performance analysis of heat affected zone in welding of microalloyed submarine flexible pipes
abstract: Subsea flexible pipelines are key equipment in deep-sea resource development, serving as the "lifeline" connecting underwater production systems with surface treatment facilities. Its core function is to safely and efficiently transport various marine resources. The welding Heat Affected Zone (HAZ) is a weak link in the welding joints of submarine flexible pipelines. title: Sea Turtle Nesting Beach Fidelity Revealed by Satellite Tracking
abstract: ABSTRACT Site fidelity describes the tendency to return to or reuse familiar sites, yet some animals may use alternative sites while maintaining fidelity to primary locations, with consequences for population estimates as well as resilience to changing environments. Here we assessed and compared nesting beach fidelity of hawksbill turtles ( Eretmochelys imbricata ) on Frégate Island, Seychelles using data from beach foot patrols (2017–2025; n = 575 turtles) and satellite telemetry (2023; n = 10 turtles) and then examined the implications of fidelity strategies for population estimates. title: Delta morphology reveals timings of early ocean regression and hydrologic shift on ancient Mars
abstract: Abstract Mars’ ancient hydrologic history remains a subject of debate, with competing interpretations suggesting either a large ocean or scattered lacustrine environments. Here, we show that delta morphology on Mars records a shift between these hydrologic regimes. Through controlled tank experiments, we identify two distinct delta types: “lobe-extruding deltas” formed during water-level falls and “stepped fan-deltas” formed during rising water levels. title: Modulation of ETCCDI-based extreme rainfall indices by ENSO and the Indian Ocean Dipole over topographically complex North Sumatra, Indonesia
abstract: This study examines the characteristics of extreme rainfall in North Sumatra Province, Indonesia, and its teleconnections with the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). The analysis uses a blended daily rainfall dataset from 1990 to 2024, combining station observations from the Indonesian Agency for Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics (BMKG) with the Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station (CHIRPS) satellite data. title: Rooftop photovoltaic potential in data-scarce regions using open-source geospatial information: Scenario-based approach for a Mediterranean coastal city
abstract: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems can support urban decarbonization, yet data scarcity limits city-scale assessments in developing regions. This study develops an open-source 2D GIS workflow for five central districts of Antalya, Turkiye, using Overture Maps building footprints. A three-stage procedure combined spatial and size filters, geometry and land-use screening, and targeted image inspection to retain the continuous urban building stock while excluding rural settlements, greenhouses, and structures smaller than 60 m 2 . journal: Energy Sustainable Development/Energy for sustainable development

title: Spatial organization and coordinated development of offshore wind industrial chains under governance decentralization: evidence from China's coastal provinces
abstract: Offshore wind industrial chains, encompassing upstream component manufacturing, midstream project development and operation, and downstream grid integration, underpin large-scale utilization, yet their spatial organization, structural linkages, and coordinated development remain underexamined. This study examines offshore wind industrial chains in China's 11 coastal provinces during 2010 − 2023, a period characterized by globally leading capacity expansion and governance transition from national centralization to provincial decentralization, through a stepwise analytical framework integrating

title: Fluid–substrate coupled controls on mineral‑phase selection in the Kunlun hydrothermal system
abstract: Abstract Mineral precipitation at submarine hydrothermal vents transfers redox‑sensitive elements from the lithosphere to the ocean. However, conventional plume and sediment‑trap sampling poorly preserves particle‑scale signatures generated at reactive interfaces, hindering robust interpretation of near‑vent mineralization. Here, we deployed open‑cell Fe, Ni, Cu, and Fe–Ni foams within diffuse low‑temperature alkaline fluids of the serpentinization‑driven Kunlun hydrothermal field. title: Mosaic Accumulation of Somatic Genetic Variation and Estimates of Age in the Long‐Lived Reef‐Building Coral Acropora palmata
abstract: Somatic genetic variation (SoGV) accumulates during an organism's lifetime and is traditionally viewed as detrimental rather than adaptive due to links with cancer and senescence. However, in modular organisms like corals, deleterious mutations can be purged at the cellular or polyp level, while adaptive mutations may rise in frequency as polyps create genetically distinct modules. Quantifying the somatic genetic landscape in corals is necessary to understand the role these mutations may have in coral and clonal animal development and evolution. title: Design and Implementation of a Centralized Vessel Monitoring System Using API Harmonization
abstract: Vessel tracking is critical for ensuring the safety and operational efficiency of the maritime industry. However, the reliance on tracking devices from disparate commercial vendors (e.g., Vendor A, Vendor B, and G-Track) introduces severe data fragmentation, forcing operators to navigate multiple proprietary dashboards. Furthermore, custom-built Internet of Things (IoT) tracking devices lack interoperability with these existing commercial platforms.
