title: Hydrometeorological and hydrogeological trends and drought dynamics in a cold-humid, coastal region
abstract: Quantifying groundwater response to droughts remains challenging, as aquifers typically respond to meteorological conditions with delays, and long-term groundwater records remain limited. This study investigated statistical relationships among meteorological, hydrogeological, and hydrological datasets in the Canadian province of Nova Scotia. title: Ontogenetic shifts, trophic differentiation, and predator–prey size relationships in Oxyrhopus false coral snakes from Bahia, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Although snakes of the genus Oxyrhopus are generally regarded as opportunistic predators, the relative roles of interspecific dietary differentiation, ontogenetic variation, and predator morphology in their feeding ecology remain poorly understood. We analyzed the diet of 253 preserved specimens representing four Oxyrhopus species from Bahia, Brazil. title: Assessment of water quality and anthropogenic impacts on surface and groundwater in the Zhambyl region using GIS-technology
abstract: An integrated hydrochemical and geospatial assessment was performed to access the water quality of wastewater accumulation basins and adjacent aquatic systems in the Zhambyl region (southern Kazakhstan) under conditions of increasing anthropogenic impact. Monitoring was carried out at eight sampling points (P1-P8) during three seasonal campaigns (September 2025, November 2025, and January 2026). The measured parameters included pH, oxidation-reduction potential (ORP), dissolved oxygen (DO), salinity, total dissolved solids (TDS), electrical conductivity (EC), and chemical oxygen demand (COD).

abstract: Abstract Magma oceans represent a pivotal stage in the early evolution of terrestrial planets. title: Local Environmental Habitat Templates and Hydroperiod Contingency Jointly Shape Benthic Macroinvertebrate Dynamics in Tropical Choked Coastal Lagoons
abstract: Abstract Coastal lagoons are highly dynamic transitional ecosystems in which benthic macroinvertebrate communities are shaped by spatial and temporal environmental filters. However, the relative importance of lagoon-specific conditions versus temporal variation remains poorly resolved, particularly in the tropics. Here, we investigated benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages in three neighboring choked coastal lagoons in southeastern Brazil over 23 consecutive months. title: Estimation of Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) over the Hiramandalam Reservoir Catchment Using GIS
abstract: Reliable estimation of the Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) and the resulting Probable Maximum Flood (PMF) is essential for fixing the design flood of high-hazard hydraulic structures such as spillways and flood-control dams. This paper presents a GIS-based estimation of one-day PMP and the corresponding PMF for the catchment of the Hiramandalam Reservoir, located in Hiramandalam mandal of Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh. title: Optimising renewable hydrogen hub locations: A GIS-based spatio-temporal integration framework
abstract: This paper presents a Geographic Information System (GIS)-integrated spatio-temporal optimisation framework for the design of renewable hydrogen hubs. This framework embeds high-resolution spatial datasets directly into an hourly Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation to co-optimise the siting, sizing, and hourly operation of system components, thereby minimising the Levelised Cost of Hydrogen (LCOH 2 ). title: Underwater hybrid ESD versus conventional ESD for colorectal laterally spreading tumors: a retrospective study
abstract: Background and aims Conventional endoscopic submucosal dissection (C-ESD) is standard for colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs) but is time-consuming. Underwater hybrid ESD (U-Hybrid ESD) is an emerging technique. We compared the efficacy and safety of U-Hybrid ESD versus C-ESD for colorectal LSTs. Methods This exploratory, single-center retrospective study included 300 patients with LSTs ≥20 mm (U-Hybrid ESD, n = 150; C-ESD, n = 150). title: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis for identifying optimal geothermal power plant sites: a case study of the Gulf of Suez, Egypt
abstract: Abstract The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. title: Field sampling guidelines for sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) research in lacustrine and coastal systems: from field collection to laboratory subsampling
abstract: Abstract Sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) has emerged as a powerful proxy for reconstructing past biodiversity and environmental change in lacustrine and coastal systems, yet standardized field guidance remains limited, particularly for researchers working in tropical and coastal depositional environments. Here, we present a practical sampling framework covering the key field protocols of sedaDNA research, from field collection to laboratory subsampling, with emphasis on contamination control at each step. title: Growth, physiological responses, and water quality in juvenile Malabar grouper reared in a low-salinity RAS: An 84-day operational trial
abstract: Recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) are expanding globally as a sustainable aquaculture technology. Although RAS enable intensive production of marine fish, their high capital and operating costs necessitate strategies that improve growth efficiency while maintaining stable water quality. Low-salinity seawater promotes growth in many marine fish species; however, concerns remain that reduced salinity may impair biofiltration. title: Artificial light at night causes unequal and species-specific shifts in infection risk by a generalist marine parasite
abstract: Abstract Light pollution, in the form of artificial light at night (ALAN), changes the normal physiology and behaviour of animals, leading to alterations in interspecific interactions. Parasitism is likely to be impacted, ranging from altered parasite proliferation and transmission to altered host exposure or susceptibility to infection. How these individual-level effects translate to higher level impacts remains poorly understood. title: Large-scale marine eDNA database reveals seasonal latitudinal diversity gradients in Japan driven by vagrant fish
abstract: Abstract The spatial and temporal patterns of marine diversity are essential for the sustainable use and management of marine ecosystems. Here, we investigated latitudinal and seasonal diversity gradients of fish genera in Japanese waters using environmental DNA (eDNA) data from 1,765 surveys conducted between 2017 to 2022. We found a negative relationship between genus richness and latitude, consistent with latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG). title: Analisis Kerawanan Longsor Berdasarkan Parameter Geologi dan Geospasial di Biluhu Timur, Kecamatan Batudaa Pantai, Gorontalo
abstract: Biluhu Timur Village and its surroundings, located in Batudaa Pantai District, Gorontalo Regency, have a topography ranging from hills to coastal plains and relatively high rainfall, which makes them prone to landslides. This study aims to analyze the geological and geomorphological conditions and to map landslide susceptibility zones in Biluhu Timur Village and its surroundings at a scale of 1:25,000. abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive durability comparison of a 100% cement-free ultra-high performance geopolymer concrete (GEO), based on ground granulated blast-furnace slag and silica fume, against a Portland cement-based ultra-high performance concrete reference of equivalent strength class (REF). A laboratory program assessed both mixes under sulfate attack, nitric acid, elevated temperature up to 900 °C, rapid chloride penetration (ASTM C1202), and electrical impedance monitoring over 365 days. title: Colombiains A–C, Three New Alkaloids From the Soft Coral‐Derived Fungus Cladosporium colombiae CSGL 10M10
abstract: Three new alkaloids, colombiains A-C (1-3), together with 8 known ones (4-11), were isolated from the soft coral-derived fungus Cladosporium colombiae CSGL 10M10. Their structures were elucidated by spectroscopic interpretation, electronic circular dichroism (ECD), and single-crystal X-ray crystallographic methods. Compounds 6 and 11 exhibited significant cardioprotective activity against oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-induced injury in H9c2 myocardial cell line at 10 µM. title: Spatial Assessment of Heat Health Risk in Brussels Through GIS and Local Climate Zone Analysis
abstract: Climate change and rapid urbanization are increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat events, posing significant risks to public health in cities. Although numerous studies have investigated urban heat islands and heat vulnerability, spatially explicit assessments integrating environmental, demographic, and urban morphological characteristics remain limited, particularly in European cities. title: Retención de residuos plásticos por vegetación ribereña: Reporte de caso y revisión sistemática
abstract: Poor plastic waste management has led to its widespread dispersion in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, causing significant impacts on biodiversity. While most studies focus on marine and coastal environments, continental ecosystems remain largely unexplored. In this report, we document for the first time the retention of plastic debris by riparian vegetation in the Sechura River in northern Peru. title: A community-informed, multilayered vegetative bioshield for climate-related coastal erosion on Sonadia Island, Bangladesh
abstract: Sonadia Island is an ecologically important barrier island on the southeastern coast of Bangladesh, where shoreline erosion, saline intrusion, cyclone exposure, and habitat degradation threaten both biodiversity and local livelihoods. This exploratory mixed-methods study assessed community perceptions of existing Jhaw plantations, documented selected dune and vegetation characteristics, and developed a site-specific conceptual bioshield for pilot testing. title: Flood susceptibility assessment using GIS and an analytical hierarchy process in Ilorin Metropolis, Kwara, Nigeria
abstract: Flooding remains a major environmental challenge in Ilorin Metropolis, Kwara State, Nigeria. In this study, flood susceptibility across the metropolis was assessed using geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and the analytical hierarchy process (AHP). abstract: Flood-risk studies in Malaysia have often concentrated on hydrological hazard, although the consequences of flooding also depend on where people and assets are located and how well communities can cope. This study develops a basin-wide flood-risk index for the Johor River Basin by integrating hazard, exposure and vulnerability within a geographic information system-based multi-criteria decision analysis. title: Open-Source GIS Applications for Flood and Landslide Assessment: Comparative Cases from Poland and Malaysia
abstract: Research on natural disasters requires analytical procedures that are rapid, reproducible, and based on sound scientific principles. Such procedures should also be accessible to institutions responsible for environmental monitoring, land-use planning, and disaster risk reduction. This study evaluated the practical use of publicly available geospatial data and open-source GIS tools for the preliminary assessment of two contrasting natural hazards: the September 2024 flood in Lower Silesia, Poland, with particular focus on the urban floodplain of Wrocław, and the December 2022 landslide in Batan

title: Georeferencing Historical Zoning Maps and Their Comparison with Current Zoning: GIS-Based Study of Japanese Regional Cities
abstract: Japan’s land-use zoning system, established with the 1919 City Building Act, has fundamentally shaped long-term urban spatial structures. This study clarifies the evolution of Japanese zoning by georeferencing historical maps and comparing them with contemporary GIS data for 11 regional cities. We introduced the Historical Zoning Consistency Index (HZCI) to quantify spatial continuity. title: Two Littoral Species of Dicranomyia (Idioglochina) (Diptera: Limoniidae) from Japan: a New Species and Transfer of D. monostromia with Notes on Ecology
abstract: The marine-associated crane fly subgenus Idioglochina Alexander, 1921 of the genus Dicranomyia Stephens, 1829 comprises coastal species whose immature stages are associated with shoreline habitats, but its diversity and ecology in Japan remain insufficiently documented. abstract: In recent years, simultaneous with the rapid growth of urbanization, the return of migrants from neighboring countries, and the development of urban infrastructure, including the repair and construction of several new roads in Kabul city, the pattern of physical expansion of the city and the distribution of land use have undergone significant changes. title: The Impact of Environmental Gradient (Climatic and Edaphic) on the Essential Oil Content of Rosemary (Rosmarinus officinalis) in Libya
abstract: This research investigates the quantitative and qualitative variations in essential oils (EOs) of Rosmarinus officinalis (Rosemary) across an environmental gradient in Libya, encompassing coastal, mountainous, and semi-arid desert regions. Rosemary is a key medicinal and aromatic plant in the Mediterranean basin, yet the influence of Libya’s unique ecological transitions on its secondary metabolites remains understudied. title: Graphene oxide nanointerfaces enable photothermally healable ion-conducting elastomers for wearable sensing and underwater communication
abstract: Ion-conducting elastomers combine large deformability with charge transport but often exhibit trade-offs among mechanical robustness, self-healing, conductivity, and environmental stability. Here, we develop a partially reduced graphene oxide (GO)-reinforced ion-conducting elastomer through thermally induced ring-opening polymerization of α -lipoic acid in the presence of dopamine methacrylamide. title: Project-based participation and the politics of adaptive water governance in coastal polders of Bangladesh
abstract: ABSTRACT In Coastal Bangladesh, community-based water management groups (WMGs) and water management associations (WMAs) have been central to participatory water governance, yet their postproject sustainability remains uncertain. This article examines how WMGs and WMAs shape participatory water governance and local adaptive capacity in two coastal polders after the withdrawal of project-based support. title: Thirsty clean energy: localized water stress and hydro-ecological tradeoffs in green hydrogen expansion
abstract: Green hydrogen is central to global decarbonization, yet its rapid expansion exposes a severe spatial contradiction: the regions possessing optimal renewable energy potential are overwhelmingly the planet’s most water-stressed and ecologically fragile landscapes. This review critically examines the localized hydro-ecological tradeoffs of mega-scale electrolysis across arid export corridors in Australia, Chile, and North Africa. abstract: This paper describes a dataset of drone-based optical 3D mesh models of geological outcrops across South Korea, developed by the Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources (KIGAM). The dataset includes 133 three-dimensional (3D) mesh models representing 80 outcrop groups in nine province-level administrative regions. These models were constructed from optical imagery acquired with various DJI drone platforms since October 2018. The outcrops cover a broad range of geological settings across the country. abstract: ABSTRACT Organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials for flexible and aquatic applications are limited by triplet exciton instability under deformation and environmental perturbation. Here, molecular π‐conjugation engineering is integrated with polymer‐matrix confinement to enable RTP in elastomeric systems. title: GIS-Based Modelling for Evaluating Soil Erosion Patterns in Ravine-Affected Regions of the Yamuna River, India
abstract: Soil erosion poses a significant environmental challenge, particularly in ravine-affected areas where high-intensity rainfall leads to substantial soil loss, resulting in declining soil fertility and the conversion of productive agricultural land into wasteland. The present study focuses on estimating the rate of soil erosion in one of the severely ravine-affected lands along the Yamuna River and examines changes in soil erosion rates over the years. The Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) Model was employed using various soil erosion estimation parameters in the ArcGIS 10.5 platform.

abstract: The co-occurrence of nanoplastics (NPs) and antibiotics in marine environments poses complex threats to primary producers, yet the multi-level mechanisms of their combined toxicity remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the physiological, biochemical, and transcriptomic responses of the marine cyanobacterium Synechococcus sp. abstract: Nigeria's mining sector was once a major driver of national economic growth during the 1960s and 1970s, but its prominence declined sharply following the rise of the crude oil industry, leaving it with a marginal GDP share of just 0.17% between 2018 and 2022. Reports from the Development Agenda for Western Nigeria Commission highlight that the country's Southwestern states possess rich mineral reserves such as gold, tin, zircon, rutile, feldspar, and quartz giving the region strong potential to emerge as a global mining hub. title: Comparative Screening of Marine-Derived Bacteria from Algae, Ascidians and Sediments for Biosurfactant Production and Crude Oil Bioremediation
abstract: Marine ecosystems harbor diverse microbial communities with considerable potential for the discovery of environmentally sustainable agents for hydrocarbon remediation. The present investigation compared bacteria isolated from three distinct marine ecological niches: marine algae, ascidians and oilcontaminated marine sediments, to identify efficient biosurfactant-producing strains and to evaluate their crude oil bioremediation potential. title: Spatial variability and multivariate analysis of natural radioactivity in monazite-bearing coastal soils of Odisha, India
abstract: Abstract This study investigates spatial variability in radionuclide distribution and radiological characteristics of coastal soils from Ganjam and Puri, Odisha, India. A total of 72 samples from 24 locations were analyzed using NaI(Tl) gamma-ray spectrometry for 238 U, 232 Th, and 40 K, together with in situ ambient gamma dose measurements. title: A Baseline Study of Historical Population Parameters and Recovery Projections for Southern Black Drum Pogonias courbina (Teleostei) After Fishery Collapse in Southern Brazil
abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐term fishery‐dependent datasets for threatened marine fishes are exceptionally rare, yet critical for reconstructing pre‐collapse population states. We analyzed an extensive archive of biological and fishery records for Pogonias courbina collected in southern Brazil during the 1970s–early 1980s, when the stock remained still abundant. title: Indicator-based assessment of coastal dune ecosystem degradation using historical land-cover change and UAV-LiDAR microtopography
abstract: Coastal sand dunes, which support numerous valuable plant species, are experiencing severe decline and degradation driven by development and coastal erosion. To facilitate the conservation and restoration of coastal dune vegetation, this study evaluated the spatial and temporal patterns of ecosystem degradation at the Kumihama dune using Juniperus conferta as an indicator species of the development-prone fixed zone. title: CO2 and CH4 fluxes from monomictic volcanic lakes in a remote oceanic island: Flores island case study (Azores)
abstract: Abstract Flores Island, situated in the Azores archipelago, is a volcanic island formed by overlapping stratovolcanoes. The island hosts several volcanic freshwater bodies, some of them present poor ecological state. title: Pollution duration drives divergent pathways of antibiotic and metal resistance gene dissemination in coastal mangrove sediments
abstract: Coastal mangrove sediments are critical reservoirs of antibiotic and heavy metal resistance genes (ARGs/HMRGs). Yet, how pollution history shapes their dissemination remains unclear. We elucidated this by comparing sedimentary resistomes across three distinct ecosystems: a pristine site (BH), a site under mid-term copper stress (BHCu), and a chronically multi-polluted site (FT). title: Associations between soil macroinvertebrate assemblages and physicochemical properties of tropical pasture soils in coastal Ecuador
abstract: Soil macroinvertebrates mediate key soil processes, but field evidence is scarce in coastal Neotropical pastures. This study evaluated how soil physicochemical properties covary with macroinvertebrate abundance and diversity in tropical pastures of Manabí, Ecuador. Thirty-five cattle farms, seven per locality, were sampled by convenience between April and July 2022. abstract: Accelerated sea level rise, combined with human-induced changes to hydrology and sediment transport, threatens the long-term persistence of coastal wetlands. Sediment addition is increasingly used to enhance wetland resilience to sea level rise, and incorporating biochar, a carbon-rich material produced through pyrolysis of organic matter, may enhance carbon storage, soil function, and vegetation recovery. abstract: Abstract Characterizing drivers of estuarine fish assemblages provides valuable insights into estuarine ecology and how each species may react to stressors such as climate change and anthropogenic disturbances. Although they are known to inhabit estuaries, gars are managed as freshwater species and little is known about their movements, reproduction, or other ecological requirements. abstract: Although coastal habitats play a vital ecological role in supporting migratory shorebirds, comprehensive reviews of shorebird populations in Malaysia are still lacking. Existing studies are primarily focused on single Important Bird Areas (IBAs) and typically cover a broad range of avifauna across various ecosystems, including terrestrial, wetland, and coastal zones, due to the diverse habitats often present within a single IBA. abstract: Rapid urbanization in Southeast Asia has intensified microplastic (MP) pollution in city water bodies, urban drainage systems, and coastal environments, posing significant threats to urban water quality and public health. This study employs a comparative policy analysis to evaluate how global, regional, and national legislative frameworks address MP pollution as a critical urban water management challenge, with emphasis on ASEAN member states and Malaysia’s cities. title: Relief Macro-Compartments and Morphostructures in the state of Paraná: a reinterpretation based on the Brazilian Landform Classification System (SBCR)
abstract: The Brazilian Landform Classification System (Sistema Brasileiro de Classificação de Relevo — SBCR) has organized a new geomorphological structure, placing macro-compartments at the first level and morphostructural domains and subdomains at the second. This study applies the two SBCR taxonomic levels to the territory of the state of Paraná and compares them with previous geomorphological representations. abstract: Groundwater resource protection is a worldwide issue because groundwater plays a crucial role in meeting water supply demands for both natural ecosystems and human activities. Effective groundwater management and protection therefore require appropriate approaches for assessing contamination risks and identifying areas that are particularly vulnerable to pollution. In this study, a GIS-based DRASTIC model was applied to assess groundwater vulnerability in Lai City, southern Chad. abstract: Plant communities are commonly used to assess ecological condition due to their sensitivity to local environmental factors and the practicality of conducting vegetation surveys. abstract: Poor environmental sanitation in coastal areas is closely associated with environmentally related diseases and malnutrition among under-five children, but participatory interventions are rarely evaluated at the household level. Therefore, this study aimed to implement and evaluate a family-centered adaptation of the Participatory Hygiene and Sanitation Transformation (PHAST) method in Medan Belawan District, Indonesia. abstract: Agglomeration is no longer confined to the economic sector but has also expanded into education, generating concentration effects around higher-education institutions. A similar phenomenon is evident around the campus of Universitas Sulawesi Barat in Majene Regency, where the rapid growth of rental housing risks triggering uncontrolled urban sprawl. abstract: Abstract Snow algae darken snow through biomass accumulation and pigmentation, yet nutrient controls on algal abundance and pigment composition in Antarctic snowfields remain poorly constrained. title: Biodiversity safeguards ecosystem services and functions worldwide
abstract: Abstract Biodiversity loss threatens ecosystem services on which humanity depends, yet the strength, form and context-dependency of biodiversity–ecosystem service and biodiversity–ecosystem function relationships remain poorly quantified. Here we synthesize 423 studies to determine how biodiversity affects ecosystem functioning and service delivery. abstract: This study aimed to analyzes population growth and land cover change in Palembang City from 2020 to 2024 using GIS, the overlay method, and correlation analysis between population data and time-series land cover maps. abstract: Flooding has become one of the most urgent climate-related threats to cities, especially in African coastal cities like eThekwini Municipality, South Africa. abstract: Drought constrains seedling establishment and ecological restoration in tropical coastal forests, where native pioneer species are needed to diversify vulnerable shelterbelt plantations. Mallotus paniculatus is a common pioneer tree with broad environmental adaptability, but its drought-response mechanisms remain poorly understood. abstract: Industrial expansion on the metropolitan fringe rarely follows a random geography. Firms respond to accessibility, land markets and the cumulative advantages of co-location, while inherited territorial structure constrains where new investment can be directed. title: Complementary Data Sources for Mapping Target Mediterranean Non-Native and Cryptogenic Species: The Role of Local Knowledge and Citizen Science
abstract: Citizen Science (CS) and especially Local Ecological Knowledge (LEK) play an increasingly crucial role in assessing the impacts of climate change on the biodiversity of Mediterranean shallow waters. We explored the use of multiple data sources - including CS, and particularly, LEK and social media - to assess the distribution of selected, especially non-native and cryptogenic thermophilic, marine species in the Mediterranean. This case study aims to test the complementarity and reliability of adequately validated participatory and informal knowledge systems in documenting species occurrences.

title: How Well Can the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) Satellite Mission Observe Irrigation Canals?
abstract: Abstract The capability of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite for observing irrigation canals has remained relatively unexplored. Here, we assess SWOT observability of irrigation canal networks across 22 Asian countries using a new confidence level (CL) metric. Validation against in situ gauge observations showed that higher CL corresponds to significantly lower water‐level retrieval error. Of approximately 795,110 km of canals analyzed, 37.5% (297,799 km) show high confidence, 46.9% (373,035 km) moderate confidence, and 15.6% (124,276 km) low confidence of observability.

title: GIS-based Quantitative Analysis Approach of Landslide Hazard Assessment: A case study of NH-513 from Pasighat to Mariyang, Arunachal Pradesh, India
abstract: Hill slope failure along the roadways is a major problem in hilly and mountainous areas. Landslide hazard zonation maps produced in GIS environment can be utilized for planning and tackle of disasters associated with landslides. The aim of the study is to create landslide susceptibility maps along National Highway 513 from Pasighat to Mariyang, Arunachal Pradesh, India using quantitative approaches such as frequency ratio and Shannon entropy technique. abstract: ABSTRACT The early evolutionary history of modern domestic horses ( Equus caballus / Equus ferus caballus ), known as the DOM2 lineage, is well documented due to numerous archaeological and ancient DNA (aDNA) studies. Although many uncertainties remain in the domestication timeline, current evidence suggests that the domestication of modern horses began in the Pontic‐Caspian steppe at least ~2700 bce , or even earlier. title: Study on the relationship between changes in benthic organisms in Dongting Lake over the past 20 years and water quality improvement
abstract: Benthic organisms have relatively limited mobility and long life cycles, enabling them to comprehensively reflect long-term changes in water quality, sediment conditions, and hydrological conditions. They are therefore important indicators for assessing the ecological health of lakes. This study integrates survey data on benthic animals in Dongting Lake from 2001 to 2025, with a particular focus on reviewing publicly available data from 2016 to 2025, and conducts stage-based visualization of three categories of indicators: phytoplankton, zooplankton, and benthic animals. title: Whole genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis of Photobacterium ganghwense CF1.2, the bacterial host of the lytic marine bacteriophage PhCF1.2: Insights into its mobilome and metabolic potential
abstract: Photobacterium species are abundant in marine ecosystems, where they help break down organic matter and serve as hosts of lytic bacteriophages that influence the dynamics of bacterial populations. Here, we report the draft genome sequence and comparative genome analysis of Photobacterium ganghwense strain CF1.2, isolated from Cochin Fisheries Harbour, Kochi, on the south-west coast of India, and identified as the host bacterium of the marine lytic phage PhCF1.2. title: Shortleaf Pine-Oak-Hickory-Bluestem: A Distinct Remnant Plant Community within the Longleaf Pine–Dominated North American Coastal Plain
abstract: Identifying a region's full range of remnant plant communities is necessary for conserving its biodiversity and associated ecosystem services. The eastern North American Coastal Plain, known for its historical dominance by longleaf pine-wiregrass (Pinus palustris-Aristida beyrichiana) communities, appears to have had embedded landscapes that supported shortleaf pine-oak-hickory-bluestem (Pinus echinata, Quercus spp., Carya spp., Schizachyrium scoparium) communities that preexist European colonization. title: Soil organic carbon dynamics and microbial responses to intercropping sweet corn with legumes under different row arrangements in coastal Odisha
abstract: Abstract Intercropping of cereals and legumes can improve resource-use efficiency and soil fertility compared with monocropping. A field experiment was conducted during rabi , 2023–24 at OUAT, Bhubaneswar, India to evaluate the effects of sweet corn ( Zea mays L.) intercropped with cowpea ( Vigna unguiculata ) and black gram ( Vigna mungo ) under different row arrangements on soil organic carbon (SOC), biological properties and soil fertility. title: Translocation of endangered black abalone (Haliotis cracherodii) as a population restoration tool
abstract: Introduction Conservation translocations are an essential tool for species restoration but come with inherent risks that require careful consideration. However, accelerating ecological change lends urgency to minimizing delays in restoring populations, biodiversity, and ecosystem function. The endangered black abalone ( Haliotis cracherodii ) is a large marine gastropod in eastern Pacific rocky intertidal ecosystems ranging from California, USA to Mexico that was decimated by disease in the 1980s-1990s. abstract: ABSTRACT Pocillopora is a widespread, dominant reef‐building coral genus in the Indo‐Pacific; many species within this group exhibit high morphological similarity and plasticity. Given this, genetic tools are needed to robustly identify Pocillopora individuals to the species level. Quick and accurate identification approaches for Pocillopora species are critical to estimating biodiversity patterns under current and future environmental challenges. title: High-throughput phenotyping reveals nutrient availability alters thermal performance in two Symbiodiniaceae species
abstract: Nutrient sharing between corals and Symbiodiniaceae is crucial to the survival of coral reefs. However, optimal nutrient conditions for different Symbiodiniaceae species remains unclear, partly due to a lack of high-throughput methods for phenotyping Symbiodiniaceae. We developed a high-throughput phenotyping method for Symbiodiniaceae to grow monocultures of Cladocopium proliferum and Durusdinium trenchii in 96-well plates. title: Nematode rapid adaptative response to the massive Deepwater Horizon oil spill
abstract: The Gulf ecosystem health was of great concern after the explosion of the Deepwater Horizon oil platform (April 2010). After the spill, a large volume of oil trapped in the deep-sea plumes was transported offshore and to deep-water sediments, causing detrimental effects on the benthic fauna. abstract: Diabetes Mellitus is a disease caused by decreased pancreatic function to produce insulin or insensitivity of insulin receptors. abstract: Ascetosporea is a group of parasitic protists within Endomyxa that primarily infect marine invertebrates and can cause serious damage to fishery resources such as oysters and prawns. Although approximately 50 species have been formally described, environmental DNA (eDNA) studies suggest that their diversity remains largely underestimated, with many lineages yet to be discovered. title: Dynamic evaluation of sugarcane drainage water as a sustainable low-salinity injection brine for enhanced oil recovery: integrated micromodel visualization and coreflooding study
abstract: Abstract The increasing scarcity of freshwater resources and the environmental challenges associated with agricultural wastewater disposal have intensified the search for alternative injection fluids for enhanced oil recovery (EOR). This study establishes a new dynamic framework for evaluating untreated sugarcane drainage water as a naturally occurring low-salinity injection brine for EOR, extending our previous compatibility-based work to direct pore- and core-scale displacement evaluation. title: Effects of Composite Reclamation Models of Sea Buckthorn, A Pioneer Species in Semi‐Arid Regions, on Soil Quality and Microbial Communities
abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐pit coal mining severely degrades soil and ecosystem functions, constraining regional sustainability. Vegetation‐based reclamation has therefore been widely adopted as an effective approach to promote soil recovery and ecosystem restoration. In this study, eight reclamation models were established at the Antaibao Open‐Pit Coal Mine, all dominated by sea buckthorn ( Hippophae rhamnoides L.) and combined with Chinese pine ( Pinus tabulaeformis Carr.), black locust ( Robinia pseudoacacia L.) and littleleaf peashrub ( Caragana microphylla Lam.). title: Comparative nasal and anal microbiomes in sympatric ringed and harbour seals: insights into host adaptation and niche differentiation
abstract: Abstract Understanding the microbiomes of marine mammals is essential to explore their health, ecological roles and responses to environmental change. We investigated the nasal and anal microbiota of two sympatric subarctic seals, the harbour seal (Phoca vitulina) and the ringed seal (Pusa hispida), using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. title: From sliding joints to shape change: A hierarchical kinematic framework for the ossicular body wall of the sea star Asterias rubens
abstract: Skeletal systems couple rigid elements with contractile and connective tissues to transmit forces and control movement. abstract: The article addresses air stability effects on whitecap coverage at sea. This is achieved by using the logarithmic mean wind speed profile including a stability function as well as adopting two sea surface roughness formulas. title: Bacterial Cytochrome C Orchestrates Larval Metamorphosis Through Bioelectrical Control of Extracellular Vesicles Biogenesis
abstract: Beyond the well-established roles in biomedical processes, extracellular vesicles (EVs) from Gram-negative bacteria are now identified as potent inducers of larval metamorphosis in marine invertebrates, a critical process for sustaining the health and function of global marine ecosystems. However, the specific inductive molecules within EVs remain largely unknown. title: Exact traveling wave and soliton solutions for an extended (2+1)-dimensional shallow water wave equation
abstract: This paper investigates a nonlinear partial differential equation that models shallow water waves in the ocean. By applying the extended Wang’s direct mapping method and the extended hyperbolic function method, a variety of soliton solutions are obtained, including both bright and dark solitons. title: Sex, genes and metabolism: exploring drivers of success through native and invasive populations of the European green crab.
abstract: ABSTRACT The European green crab ( Carcinus maenas ) is a keystone predator in its native range and one of the world’s most damaging invasive species. Although its invasion success has frequently been associated with exceptional physiological plasticity, comparatively few studies have simultaneously examined organismal energetics, biochemical regulation, physiological organization and mitochondrial genetic diversity across native and invasive populations. abstract: Introduction Land-based cultivation using alternative water resources, such as saline groundwater (brine), offers a promising strategy for the sustainable production of the green macroalga Ulva compressa . Because Ulva growth and morphogenesis depend strongly on associated bacteria, understanding microbiome dynamics during acclimatization to brine is essential for stable biomass production. title: Opportunistic Feeding and Parasite Assemblages in Sei Whales ( Balaenoptera borealis ) From Southern Chile Revealed by DNA Metabarcoding
abstract: ABSTRACT Balaenopterid whales are major consumers in pelagic ecosystems and play a fundamental role in marine food webs. The sei whale ( Balaenoptera borealis ) is a broadly generalist species that remains among the least studied baleen whales. In this study, we characterized diet composition and parasite assemblage in five stranded sei whales in southern Chile using DNA metabarcoding of stomach and intestinal contents. abstract: Abstract Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) remains a challenging malignancy with limited targeted therapies. Isorhamnetin (ISO), a natural flavonoid derived from sea buckthorn, exhibits promising antitumor activity. However, its molecular targets and underlying mechanisms in LUSC remain unclear. Concurrently, carbon dots (CDs) synthesized from herbal sources have emerged as promising nanoplatforms for cancer theranostics. abstract: This study develops a web-based digital marketing platform for tourism-sector micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Rua Village to improve access to business information, product promotion, ordering, and transaction management. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems across the northeast coastal Bay of Bengal are highly productive yet increasingly showing vulnerability to climate change. This study presents a comprehensive inventory of benthic foraminifera from the Indian Sundarbans mangrove and the Budhabalanga estuary along with surrounding mangroves by integrating published records with new observations. abstract: Abstract Developmental plasticity, where early-life environmental cues shape developmental trajectories with lasting impact into adulthood, may play an important role in determining how species respond to changing thermal environments. abstract: Urban landscapes can be defined as an area with high building and population density and functions where a very significant part of the world’s population lives. The character of urban landscapes is the combination of the features that differentiate a city both from its surroundings and others. Therefore, the concept of urban landscapes is critical to appreciation of their characters in the era of globalisation. abstract: Introduction Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose significant threats to aquatic ecosystems, fisheries, and public health worldwide. abstract: This study designed, implemented, and field-evaluated a low-cost Internet of Things (IoT)-based system for real-time water quality monitoring in integrated rice–black tiger shrimp farming at Xeo Dinh Hamlet, Tay Yen Commune, An Giang Province. abstract: Microplastic pollution in estuarine environments has attracted growing attention due to the persistence, widespread distribution, and potential ecological impacts of plastic particles. This study aimed to assess the abundance and characteristics of microplastics in water and sediment at the Opak River Estuary, Bantul Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia. abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms are recalcitrant to conventional antibiotic therapy due to their extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix, in which Psl polysaccharide serves as the primary structural scaffold. title: Role of Plant Biodiversity in Mitigating Natural Disasters and Enhancing Ecosystem Resilience
abstract: Plant biodiversity plays a pivotal role in buffering ecosystems and human societies against the impacts of natural disasters. Vegetation cover influences hydrological cycles, soil stability, fire regimes and atmospheric processes, thereby mitigating the frequency, magnitude and consequences of disasters such as floods, droughts, cyclones, landslides and wildfires. abstract: Invertebrate Systematics learning requires physical specimens, as digital media often fail to capture complete morphological traits. Addressing this limitation, this study aims to explore and characterize Bivalve and Gastropod shells from the Gadon coast to evaluate their feasibility as dry learning specimens. abstract: The self-excited oscillating water jet is widely used in ocean engineering. Its effectiveness stems from the impact of cavitation collapse driven by periodic pressure pulsations. abstract: Satisfaction with the urban environment is among the crucial elements of the quality of urban life. This study examines the results of the most recent wave of the Eurobarometer survey (year 2023), covering 83 European cities, to explore which city characteristics are associated with higher and lower perceived quality of different urban environment areas - air quality, noise levels, green spaces and city cleanliness. abstract: ABSTRACT Ecosystem response to forest management and disturbance is governed by many factors and their interactions. abstract: In this study, embryonic development in the gonad and glochidia development in the gill marsupium of Unio delicatus (Bivalvia: Unionidae) were examined using morphological, visual, and statistical analyses. title: Spatial and temporal variability of urban air quality across functional land-use zones in Eskişehir, Türkiye
abstract: Urban air quality is spatially heterogeneous because emission intensity, land-use function, daily activity, seasonal energy demand, and atmospheric dispersion vary across the urban fabric. This study quantified the short-term spatial and temporal variability of PM2.5, PM10, and CO2 across ten functionally contrasting locations in Eskişehir, Türkiye. Field observations were conducted during four weeks in February and four weeks in May, with measurements collected on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays during morning (08:30–10:30) and evening (17:00–19:00) periods. title: Early‐Stage Distribution of the Invasive Alga Rugulopteryx okamurae on the Catalan Coast: First Quantitative Baseline
abstract: ABSTRACT The non‐indigenous brown alga Rugulopteryx okamurae has rapidly expanded across the eastern Atlantic and the western Mediterranean Sea. The first record on the Catalan coast (NW Mediterranean) was in July 2024 in Llançà (Girona), followed by additional detections at nearby localities. We conducted targeted surveys in June–July 2025 across 13 sampling stations in four localities, combining visual inspections and transects. abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution and bacterial antimicrobial resistance are converging public health concerns. MPs provide persistent, mobile surfaces that can transport antibiotic-resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). abstract: In recent years, offshore wind energy systems (OWES) have risen to prominence as a compelling avenue for capitalizing on the unfailing and consistent wind resources of the open sea, chiefly to supply electricity to coastal regions. Even so, wind intermittency complicates OWES control, reducing energy extraction when generator control proves ineffective. title: Moored observations of the deep western boundary current east of the Gagua Ridge in the Northwestern Pacific
abstract: Abstract The deep western boundary current (DWBC) of the Pacific serves as a lower limb of the meridional overturning circulation that has been identified as a key component of the global climate system. Here, we report the results of observations from a set of full-depth subsurface moorings deployed in the Northwestern Pacific from August 2017 to May 2020. abstract: Peri-urban coastal areas such as Timbulsloko Village, Demak Regency, face increasing development pressure and chronic inundation as a slow-onset hazard that affects residents, public assets, and local micro-enterprises. abstract: Bogam Bay in West Kotawaringin Regency, Central Kalimantan Province is one of the bays that has dynamic potential influenced by local natural, social, economic, and environmental conditions. The Bogam Bay area faces ecological challenges in the form of coastal abrasion and ecosystem vulnerability due to uncertain climate change resulting in tidal waters in the coastal area. title: Improved ultrasonic tomographic imaging for reinforced concrete piles based on source-point ray tracing
abstract: The cross-hole sonic logging (CSL) method is a widely used nondestructive testing (NDT) technique for pile integrity assessment. However, conventional CSL methods are inadequate for precise defect identification due to low data utilization, limited testing efficiency and poor localization accuracy. To address these limitations, an improved ultrasonic tomography (UT) technique based on CSL and source-point ray tracing is proposed in this regard. abstract: Host-associated microbiomes play vital roles in species' ecology and evolution, yet little is known about their shift during the transition from aquatic to terrestrial habitats. We characterize the skin microbiomes of three combtooth blenny species (Blenniella paula, Praealticus labrovittatus, Alticus arnoldorum) that occupy distinct positions along the intertidal gradient-from fully subtidal to intertidal and supratidal environments. title: “The Guy(s) from California”: Race, the Tax Code, and the Relational Geographies of Rental Housing in Memphis
abstract: This article examines how high net worth, individual investors from coastal markets have reshaped the rental market in Memphis, Tennessee, and could be playing a growing role in housing markets across the United States. Drawing on interviews with local “turn-key” real estate companies and a computational analysis of property data across Memphis, I show how the historical trajectory of racial capitalism, coupled with the fallout of the 2008 financial crisis, has enabled local property managers to channel out-of-state investment from high-cost markets like California into Memphis neighborhoods.

abstract: Global trends illustrate unprecedented declines in biodiversity. The main threats driving these trends include climate change, land- and sea-use change, pollution, over-exploitation, and invasive species. Strategic allocation of conservation resources is critical to address the drivers of biodiversity loss and safeguard biodiversity and its benefits to people. abstract: This research develops and applies a comprehensive method for identifying landscape spatial units to support landscape character assessment in Latvia. abstract: Daily rainfall events have significant operational meaning in the port environment because rain can disrupt loading and unloading activities, reduce occupational safety, hinder ship movements, and affect scheduling efficiency. This study aims to improve the prediction of daily rainfall events at Tanjung Perak Port through an optimization that explicitly considers class imbalance within the existing SVM-RBF framework without adding new predictor variables. abstract: Climate change and anthropogenic stressors are degrading coastal biogenic habitats, disrupting the vital pathways fish use to shift from nearshore nurseries to offshore reef environments. Although fishes are critical for ecosystem health, spatial management rarely accounts for the interconnectedness of fish habitat needs across their life cycle. abstract: Carbon stock assessment is a critical component of climate change mitigation, particularly in coastal areas experiencing rapid land-use change. This study aims to estimate aboveground carbon stocks, potential CO₂ emissions, and the economic value of carbon across various land use and land cover (LULC) types in Sungai Kakap District, Kubu Raya Regency, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. abstract: ABSTRACT The large yellow croaker has experienced significant declines in wild stocks, while its populations have been replenished through diverse aquaculture systems, making it currently the most cultivated marine fish in China. The large yellow croaker farming industry has suffered greatly from bacterial and viral diseases. Given the economic importance of this species, extensive studies have been conducted on its genome and immune responses. abstract: Abstract Background Forensic DNA phenotyping (FDP) provides vital investigative leads by predicting externally visible characteristics (EVCs). abstract: Social values are increasingly acknowledged in land management and spatial planning, particularly amid urbanization and sustainable development. abstract: Abstract Understanding the mechanisms behind coastal plastic accumulation is crucial for more targeted clean-up actions and policy-making. We used a systematically collected dataset for plastic pollution along the Norwegian coast, added physical and socio-environmental response variables to it, and used linear regression to identify the most important factors that influence plastic accumulation. title: Rapid CFU-equivalent quantification of Enterococcus in environmental waters via a competitive lateral flow assay
abstract: Rapid and quantitative assessment of fecal contamination in environmental waters is essential for effective public health protection and timely water quality management. However, conventional monitoring based on membrane filtration requires 18–24 h incubation to enumerate culturable Enterococcus as colony-forming units (CFUs), resulting in delays between contamination events and management decisions. abstract: Behavioural endpoints offer a sensitive, non-invasive alternative to traditional mortality assays. Yet, they remain underutilized in regulatory frameworks due to a lack of standardised methodologies and baseline behavioural data. This study investigates the baseline locomotion of the marine amphipod Marinogammarus marinus to external light triggers to support standardised laboratory behavioural assays. title: Pemantauan Risiko Tabrakan dari Darat untuk Kendaraan Permukaan Otonom Menggunakan Penilaian Pertemuan CPA/TCPA
abstract: Autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) require reliable encounter assessment to support remote supervision in restricted and coastal waters. This paper proposes a shore-side collision-risk surveillance approach based on Closest Point of Approach (CPA) and Time to Closest Point of Approach (TCPA). The proposed framework combines own-ship telemetry, target-track data, relative-motion estimates, and communication status to produce a four-tier alert status for the monitoring operator. Evaluation used records from waypoint navigation, dynamic obstacle trials, web-based telemetry, and fail-safe testing.

title: Optimal duration of anticoagulation after successful catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: insights from recent randomized trials
abstract: The optimal duration of oral anticoagulation (OAC) after successful catheter ablation (CA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) remains controversial. Current guidelines recommend indefinite OAC based on stroke risk profiles, but long-term therapy adherence is suboptimal due to bleeding concerns. Recent randomized trials—ALONE-AF and OCEAN—provide critical insights into this debate. abstract: The marine pathogenic bacterium Vibrio vulnificus is linked to epizootics of a dermal ulcerative disease, causing high mortality in European and Japanese eels. American eels ( Anguilla rostrata ) experience a similar condition, commonly referred to as red sore disease (RSD). abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable estimates of abundance are fundamental to conservation assessments and measuring the success of conservation actions, especially where populations are in decline or recovery. Here we present an approach that improves statistical precision and biological value of estimates of population size by integrating multiple data sources in a marine system. abstract: Flood disasters have become increasingly frequent and severe in Nigeria, driven by a combination of climatic shifts and anthropogenic pressures. This research paper assesses flood risk vulnerability across the seven states of the Northwest geopolitical zone (Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Katsina, Kano, Jigawa, and Kaduna). title: Do salmon recipes work for cod? Environmental challenges and regulatory pathways in Norwegian aquaculture
abstract: Aquaculture governance in Norway has largely developed around the rapid expansion of Atlantic salmon farming, while repeated efforts to establish cod aquaculture have resulted in limited and discontinuous production. Recent improvements in breeding, biological performance, and market conditions have, however, renewed commercial interest in cod farming and raised a central policy question: to what extent can regulatory frameworks developed for salmon be transferred to cod aquaculture? abstract: Conventional agricultural practices face increasing scrutiny due to their environmental impact, including soil degradation, water pollution, and high reliance on synthetic inputs. abstract: A deeper understanding of the enzymatic machinery operating in the gastrointestinal tract of Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ) can aid nutritional research and the development of future aquafeeds. Current knowledge does not fully capture the diversity of digestive enzymes, their temporal and compartmental dynamics, and how the enzymatic repertoire is shaped by the feed. title: New traveling wave solutions for the extended (3+1)-dimensional KdV-Calogero-Bogoyavlenskii-Schiff and the fourth-order nonlinear Ablowitz-Kaup-Newell-Segur water wave equations using efficient techniques
abstract: This study develops novel solitary wave solutions for the recently introduced extended (3+1)-dimensional KdV-Calogero-Bogoyavlenskii-Schiff (KdV-CBS) equation and the fourth-order nonlinear Ablowitz-Kaup-Newell-Segur (AKNS) water wave equation with a perturbation parameter. We employ the improved generalized Riccati equation method on the KdV-CBS equation and the generalized Kudryashov method on the AKNS equation to derive fascinating and robust wave solutions, including hyperbolic, trigonometric, and rational exponential functions. title: Using spatio-temporal models to assist ecosystem-based fisheries management: a New Zealand case study
abstract: Tools to understand or predict ecosystem changes (e.g., fish community analyses) and the impacts of management measures on ecosystem components (e.g., ecosystem simulation models) are instrumental to the success of ecosystem-based fisheries management (EBFM). We developed a workflow using vector autoregressive spatio-temporal (VAST) models to assist EBFM in the Chatham Rise middle depth (CHAT MD) region, located in New Zealand waters. title: Mapping land-use/land-cover change and associated predictors in Cambodia from 2000 to 2020: Landsat-based SVM mapping and random forest analysis
abstract: Introduction Land-use/land-cover (LULC) change in Cambodia is relevant to forest conservation and land management in the Lower Mekong region. Methods This study describes mapped change between three national LULC snapshots (2000, 2010, and 2020) using Landsat TM/ETM+/OLI imagery, supervised support vector machine (SVM) classification, post-classification transition matrices, and random forest (RF) predictor-importance analysis. title: Population genetic structure and connectivity of Enhalus acoroides along the Southern Vietnamese coastline
abstract: Introduction Seagrass meadows have undergone substantial declines in Vietnam over recent decades owing to habitat loss, climate change, nutrient enrichment, and other anthropogenic disturbances. Enhalus acoroides , a dominant large tropical seagrass, has experienced marked reductions in distribution and abundance, yet information on its population genetic structure remains limited. title: Smartphone-based mapping of home ignition zone attributes for wildland–urban interface fire risk assessment
abstract: Background Assessing home ignition zone attributes is essential for reducing wildfire risk in wildland–urban interface (WUI) communities; however, traditional satellite imagery often lacks sufficient spatial resolution and timely updates to capture localized fuel conditions near structures. Aims This study develops and validates a smartphone-based framework for real-time detection, mapping and 3D visualization of building features and defensible space fuel to support wildfire risk assessment and mitigation in WUI environments. title: Complete mitochondrial genome of Arcuatula japonica (Mollusca: Mytilidae: Crenellinae) and its phylogenetic analysis
abstract: Arcuatula japonica (Dunker, 1857) (Mollusca: Mytilidae: Crenellinae) is a marine mussel distributed primarily in the northwestern Pacific. To clarify its evolutionary position and evaluate the taxonomic status of Crenellinae, we sequenced and characterized the complete mitochondrial genome of A. japonica. The mitogenome is 16,198 bp in length and contains 13 protein-coding genes (PCGs), 22 transfer RNA genes (tRNAs), 2 ribosomal RNA genes (rRNAs), and 1 non-coding control region (CR), with an A + T bias (68.7%). title: Station-Area Accessibility and Rail-Property Value Capture for Urban Regeneration in Yangon
abstract: Urban rail can support local economic development when station areas are accessible, connected and integrated with surrounding land uses. This study examines Ma Hlwa Gone Station on the East Wing of the Yangon Circular Railway as a case of railway-led urban regeneration. It applies an implementation-oriented TOCC framework combining TOD principles, compact urban form, Rail + Property mechanisms and institutional coordination. A mixed-methods approach was used, including GIS catchment analysis, field observation, land-use assessment, nine stakeholder interviews, policy review and STEEP evaluati

title: Industrial Development in Protected Zones: A Four-Gate Legal Assessment of the Tahura Ngurah Rai Factory Case in Bali
abstract: The reported construction-material factory linked to Russian investment near Bali's Tahura Ngurah Rai highlights a recurring difficulty in environmental governance: the coexistence of land certificates, business registrations, spatial restrictions and conservation boundaries. This article examines the legal consequences of that overlap through normative legal research using statutory, conceptual and documentary case approaches. journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS

title: An Integrated AHP–Entropy Weighted GOD model with K-Means Clustering for Groundwater Vulnerability Mapping in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater resources in the coastal sedimentary basins of sub-Saharan Africa face severe anthropogenic threats. Conventional groundwater vulnerability overlay models, such as the GOD index, are frequently constrained by subjective parameter weighting and arbitrary index thresholding, which can produce spatial over-smoothing and broad, homogeneous vulnerability classifications. To address these limitations, this study presents an integrated hydrogeophysical framework coupling Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) with unsupervised machine learning. title: RANCANG BANGUN SISTEM MONITORING KETINGGIAN AIR PADA BANJIR ROB MENGGUNAKAN TEKNOLOGI IOT BERBASIS WEBSITE
abstract: Wilayah pesisir Muara Angke, Jakarta Utara, sering mengalami banjir rob yang mengganggu aktivitas sosial dan ekonomi masyarakat, sementara informasi peringatan dini yang tersedia masih bersifat umum dan belum menggambarkan kondisi ketinggian air secara langsung di lokasi terdampak. title: Spatiotemporal analysis of land use change in the Eastern Slopes of the Jerusalem Area
abstract: Abstract Urban expansion is one of the main drivers of land use changes in the Central Palestinian Mountains. It influences the basic environmental components, including water, soil, and specifically vegetation cover. In the present study, the study area has experienced noticeable land use changes over the past three decades, resulting in many adverse impacts on the environment. This study aims to examine land use changes and identify the main drivers and consequences of these changes on vegetation cover during the period 1997 and 2022. Spatiotemporal analysis is used to quantify land use chan

title: SAFEBORDERS (DIGITAL CONVERSATIONAL AGENT): PREVENTION OF SMUGGLING OF CIGARETTES, DRUGS AND CONTROLLED GOODS AT MALAYSIAN BORDERS
abstract: This study presents the design, development, and usability evaluation of SafeBorders, an AI-powered bilingual digital conversational agent developed to support public advocacy and community engagement in preventing the smuggling of cigarettes, drugs, and controlled goods at Malaysian borders. Grounded in Mayer’s Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning, Social Agency Theory, and Conversational Design Principles, and guided by user-centered design, SafeBorders delivers general safety information, emergency guidance, and a structured incident reporting mechanism across web and mobile platforms in

title: Recurrence lacunarity of spatial data
abstract: Abstract Quantifying the structure and heterogeneity of complex spatial patterns remains a key challenge in spatial data analysis. Recurrence plots (RPs) offer a powerful method for visualizing the recurrent spatial patterns in such data. To quantify the structure of spatial recurrences, we extend the normalized recurrence lacunarity (nRL), a measure of the homogeneity of an RP, to the analysis of spatial RPs. title: Isolation and characterization of human skin-derived bacteriophages with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against coagulase-negative staphylococci
abstract: Abstract Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS), particularly Staphylococcus epidermidis and Staphylococcus capitis , are significant opportunistic pathogens associated with biofilm-related infections and antimicrobial resistance. Although bacteriophage therapy is a promising alternative to antibiotics, human skin-derived phages targeting clinically important CoNS remain poorly characterized. Four bacteriophages were isolated from facial skin swabs of healthy volunteers, and two (phages Se_20 and Se_42) were selected for detailed characterization. title: Archaeological micromorphology in Latin America: an overview
abstract: Micromorphology helps to reveal fundamental aspects of archaeological sites and landscapes that are invisible to the naked eye. Apart from discerning human contributions from patterns of natural sediment/soil formation, deposition, and alteration, this technique, coupled with others, has been able to showcase specific human activities hidden in the archaeological record. Over the last couple of decades, micromorphology has slowly entered the realm of archaeological techniques in Latin America and neighboring regions. title: The Evolutionary History of Early Ray‐Finned Fishes (Pan‐Actinopterygii)
abstract: One out of every two vertebrate species is a ray-finned fish (Actinopterygii). The ~380-million-year fossil record of ray-finned fishes provides a window into the evolutionary history of actinopterygian diversity in deep time. The actinopterygian fossil record shows that the ray-finned fish crown group (Actinopterygii) lived alongside speciose members of now extinct lineages, collectively referred to as early actinopterygians. title: Circulating in the oyster immune system: multi-compartment modeling reveals dynamic intercellular trafficking of biodegradable nanoplastics
abstract: Studies of the cellular fate of nanoplastics (NPs) in bivalves commonly overlook the dynamic trafficking of particles among immune cells. Here, we established a multi-compartment kinetic framework using time-resolved measurements of hemocyte populations for 2-h following a 1-h in vitro exposure to polylactic acid biodegradable nanoplastics (PLA-NPs). title: Building adaptive capacity of US Gulf Coast city practitioners to extreme weather events
abstract: Abstract Building city practitioners’ capacity to prepare for and respond to climate change-driven events can increase coastal cities’ resilience. We conducted a first-of-its-kind mixed methods research project from 2021 to 2023 with 46 US Gulf Coast small and midsize cities to measure the effectiveness of an adaptive capacity-building intervention: a stormwater planning tool called FloodWise Communities (FWC) deployed through the engagement between researchers and practitioners in each city. City practitioners were surveyed preintervention and postintervention between September 2021 and Decem

title: Rising Connectivity, Shifting Hubs: The Evolving Network and Governance Challenges of Global Wild‐Sourced Trade
abstract: ABSTRACT Global wild‐sourced wildlife trade is structured not only by the intensity and composition of traded species, but also by the routes, hubs, and redistribution pathways that connect countries/territories into an intricate network. Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of trade networks over time is essential for identifying emerging governance challenges and conservation priorities. title: A novel bacterial symbiont in the seaweed Gracilaria tenuistipitata and its promising anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative potential in relation to special secreted metabolites
abstract: Marine macroalgae host compositionally complex microbiomes that constitute an evolutionarily refined, yet largely unexplored source of structurally diverse natural products. Thus, the bioactivities of the algae may be related to those of their associated microorganisms. Here we describe the discovery of strain S.100, an endophytic bacterium isolated from the red alga Gracilaria tenuistipitata and displaying remarkable anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative activities, through a primary screening on ethyl acetate (EtAc), chloroform and n-hexane extracts of its culture. title: Biofilm-host immunometabolic crosstalk in Staphylococcus aureus orthopedic implant infection: mechanisms and translational constraints
abstract: Orthopedic implant biofilms are not only antibiotic-tolerant bacterial communities but metabolically active niches that reshape host immunity. Compared with planktonic infection, mature biofilms impose spatial and metabolic constraints that can uncouple leukocyte recruitment from sterilizing activity. Neutrophils can penetrate and phagocytose portions of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms, but clearance becomes incomplete as biofilms mature and may coexist with degranulation and neutrophil extracellular trap-associated tissue injury. institutions: Yunnan Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine

title: An Exploratory Quantitative Spatial Analysis of Early Saxon Discursive Identity (250-700 CE)
abstract: Traditional early medieval historiography frequently treats the early Saxons as a homogeneous, migrating ethnic entity. This paper explores this paradigm by conducting an exploratory quantitative textual and spatial analysis of early medieval identity construction, focusing on the maritime networks of the North Sea and the territorial river systems of the Rhine-Meuse delta in Northwest Europe. title: Chemical stress drives opposing bacterial biomass responses at the single-cell level
abstract: Abstract Microbial biomass is a central functional trait governing nutrient turnover and trophic transfer in aquatic ecosystems, yet how chemical stress reshapes biomass at the level of individual cells remains poorly resolved. Conventional toxicity assays primarily detect population-level growth inhibition and overlook sublethal physiological responses and heterogeneity within microbial populations. title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. title: Spatial Analysis of Atmospheric Pollutants in An-Najaf Governorate Based on Sentinel-5 Satellite Observations
abstract: Sentinel-5P satellite imagery, in combination with Geographic Information Systems (GIS), was utilized to analyze the spatial distribution of the atmospheric pollutant gases—ozone (O₃), sulfur dioxide (SO₂), and carbon monoxide (CO)—across An-Najaf Governorate in central Iraq. The study aimed to assess patterns of pollutant concentration and identify the anthropogenic and environmental factors influencing their distribution. title: Macroevolutionary dynamics and predictors of tropical rain forest plant diversity
abstract: Tropical rain forest is the most diverse terrestrial biome, yet the drivers of its diversification across space and time remain poorly understood. Although heterogeneous diversification rates, including both ancient and recent radiations, have been reported, these dynamics have rarely been examined within a single lineage across deep evolutionary timescales. Here, we reconstruct a dated phylogenomic tree of the pantropical plant family Annonaceae, sampling 2045 species (∼82% of its diversity) and spanning ∼100 million years of evolutionary history. title: Aplicación de fotogrametría para el análisis predial en áreas en riesgo de expropiación por proyectos de infraestructura en ventanilla, Lima 2025
abstract: This thesis sought to determine to what extent photogrammetry can reduce the time and resources required for property assessment when parcels are affected by expropriations linked to infrastructure projects taking the district of Ventanilla during 2025 as the case study. The work followed an applied approach with a quasi experimental design combining drone flights GIS based geoprocessing and document review. title: From preferences to narratives: regional preference and semantic structures in Weibo discussions of Beijing’s 5A attractions
abstract: Abstract Digital traces from social media increasingly shape how tourist preferences are observed and interpreted, yet attraction-related attention is often treated as a single aggregate indicator, with limited consideration of where this attention comes from and how attractions are discursively framed. title: From Content Coverage to Competence Development: Shifting Mechanics Education Toward Modeling and Reflection
abstract: ABSTRACT Many engineering courses are still organized according to a predominantly deductive and content‐oriented approach: theoretical foundations are introduced first, while authentic disciplinary activity is often postponed to later stages of the curriculum. This contribution argues that such an approach is insufficient for sustainable competence development in mechanics education. Instead, courses and problem statements should be designed from intended capabilities and observable learning outcomes. title: Antioxidant Activity of Unsaturated Fatty Acid Isolated From The Green Algae (Halimeda opuntia)
abstract: Halimeda is a genus of green macroalgae found in Indonesian waters, including the waters around Ternate Island. Coastal communities typically consume algae as a food source. However, over time, knowledge about algae has expanded, and people have become more aware of their nutritional content. This study aimed to determine the antioxidant activity and fatty acid composition of green algae from waters off Ternate Island. title: Standardized Ophthalmic Examination Protocol For Fish Developed During Assessment of 274 Eyes in Rockfish (Family Sebastidae)
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a practical, standardized ophthalmic examination protocol for teleost fish using captive rockfish (Family Sebastidae) as a pilot population. METHODS: One hundred twenty-seven captive rockfish housed at Hatfield Marine Science Center and 11 newly acquired rockfish at the Oregon Coast Aquarium, representing 9 Sebastes and 1 Sebastolobus species. title: Land Use/ Land Cover Dynamics and the Decline of Grazing Resources in Dauchi Grazing Reserve, Adamawa State, Nigeria
abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) change is a major driver of rangeland degradation, threatening grazing resources and pastoral livelihoods in the Guinea and Sudan savanna ecosystems of northeastern Nigeria. This study evaluates the impact of LULC change on grazing resources in Dauchi Grazing Reserve, Song LGA, Adamawa State, Nigeria, using multi-temporal satellite imagery covering forty years. Satellite data were processed and classified using supervised classification techniques within a Geographic Information System (GIS) and remote sensing framework. title: Diseño de una propuesta de gestión y preservación digital basada en tic para los proyectos académicos estudiantiles de la sede regional chrotega de la universidad nacional de costa rica
abstract: The primary objective of this article is to present the design of an Information and Communication Technology (ICT)-based web application for the management and preservation of academic projects created by students at the Chorotega Regional Campus of the National University of Costa Rica. The study employed a descriptive design to identify the characteristics of the phenomenon, subjects, and population under study, using a mixed-methods research approach that integrated both qualitative and quantitative perspectives. title: Aquavoltaics: Advancing the Water‐Food‐Energy Nexus Through Photovoltaic Integration for Sustainable Aquaculture Production—A Comprehensive Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Intensive aquaculture practices heavily reliant on conventional energy sources have contributed significantly to environmental degradation, primarily through greenhouse gas emissions. The sector faces ongoing challenges, including high energy consumption, land‐use conflicts, and unreliable electricity supply, all of which impede its sustainable development and pose broader risks to both human survival and long‐term ecological balance. title: The endless invasions: Spatiotemporal patterns of non-native insects in China
abstract: Biological invasions have been defined as one striking indicator of the Anthropocene epoch, with more species being translocated beyond their native range by human activities. The inventory of non-native species in a region provides basic information for further exploration of biological invasions. We compiled a checklist of non-native insects in China and then analyzed their diversity at species level and invasion patterns. title: Solar-driven brine evaporation with directional salt crystallization and passive removal
abstract: Hypersaline brines (salinity >10 wt%) generated by the water, energy, and agricultural sectors present a significant challenge for sustainable wastewater management. Although solar-driven interfacial evaporation offers an energy-efficient route for brine treatment and zero-liquid-discharge operation, persistent salt accumulation hinders long-term performance and operational stability. title: Targeting Flood Resilience Investments Through a Readiness Gaps Index: Evidence from Mississippi
abstract: Flooding is among the most costly and recurrent disasters globally, including in the United States. The Southeastern United States is vulnerable to billion-dollar climate disasters. In Mississippi, high flood exposure coincides with uneven institutional capacity and socioeconomic constraints, yet existing assessments largely emphasize hazard or social vulnerability in isolation while overlooking integrated readiness for resilience planning. Major limitations in resilience metrics include limited stakeholder engagement, transparency, sensitivity testing, validation, and multi-scalar assessment.
journal: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction

title: Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Assessment of Southern Offshore East Java Using Poisson and Gutenberg–Richter Models
abstract: The southern region of East Java is part of the Sunda Subduction Zone, which has high seismic activity due to the convergence of the Indo-Australian and Eurasian Plates. This study aims to analyze the probability of earthquake occurrences in the southern offshore of East Java using the Poisson distribution and the Gutenberg–Richter law. Earthquake catalog data from the International Seismological Centre (ISC) for the period 1996–2025 were used.
