title: Head-to-tail assembled borphyrins for solid-state lithium extraction
abstract: Abstract Lithium is a critical mineral for advancing greener technologies. Extraction of lithium ions (Li⁺) from sea salt, minerals, and waste is important, but has been hindered by the lack of extraction methods that offer both high selectivity and strong lithium affinity. Here, we report a dioxaborole-linked, head-to-tail assembled macrocycle – termed borphyrin – featuring a rigid cavity with a 16-crown-4-like configuration. title: Improving Housing Quality of the Bajo Tribe through a Self-Help Approach: A Case Study in Muna Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This study explains the living conditions of the coastal Bajo tribe in Muna Regency, Indonesia, and examines their potential for improving housing quality through a community-led self-help approach. Adopting a convergent parallel mixed-methods design, fieldwork was conducted across three purposively selected vulnerable settlements: Tapitapi, Lagasa, and Pasikuta villages (N = 259). Quantitative housing evaluation against PUPR/BPS standards reveals severe structural and environmental deprivation. title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of regional resilience in China: evidence from provincial panel data using Spearman-CRITIC and XGBoost-CatBoost-SHAP
abstract: Regional resilience is closely related to sustainable development because it reflects the capacity of a region to maintain stable economic, social, ecological, and infrastructural functions under long-term transformation. Based on provincial panel data for China from 2007 to 2024, this study constructs a regional resilience evaluation system covering economic resilience, social development resilience, ecological and environmental resilience, and infrastructure resilience. title: Nicotinium-based surface-active ionic liquids as antimicrobial surfactants: Micellization properties, antibiofilm activity, and biocompatibility
abstract: A new family of nicotinium-based surface-active ionic liquids (CₙNicBr, n = 10-16) was synthesized by N-alkylation of nicotine and characterized by NMR, MS and thermogravimetry (stable to 215 °C). Aqueous association, assessed by conductimetry, fluorescence, tensiometry and dynamic light scattering, gave critical micelle concentrations of 0.58-36 mM and a chain-length-independent apparent monomeric pKa of 5.6 ± 0.1 for the pyrrolidinium nitrogen. title: A new teleosauroid (Crocodylomorpha, Thalattosuchia) with a unique dentition from the Middle Jurassic of eastern Morocco
abstract: The Mesozoic and early Paleogene of Morocco provides a rich and extensive record of crocodylomorphs encompassing a wide range of skull, dental morphologies, and paleoecologies. Here we describe a new longirostrine teleosaurid thalattosuchian, Ctenosuchus tenuidens, gen. et sp. nov. with a needle-like dentition from a Middle Jurassic fluvio-lacustrine sequence of the Talsint–Anoual area of Figuig Province, southeastern Morocco. title: Bioactive potential of multi-species macroalgae: influence of extraction solvent on phytochemical composition, antioxidant, and antibacterial activities
abstract: The marine realm, which covers approximately 70% of Earth’s surface, harbours a vast diversity of untapped bioactive resources. In this study, the bioactive compounds in sixteen macroalgae were quantified using solvents of different polarities, such as petroleum ether, diethyl ether, ethanol, and water. Aqueous extracts showed significantly higher extraction yields than diethyl ether and ethanol extracts. title: Introgression Shapes Genetic Variation Associated With Humid Environments in Aedes aegypti Mosquitoes From Saudi Arabia
abstract: Introgression between genetically distinct populations generates variation that may promote adaptation to diverse environmental conditions. In the mosquito Aedes aegypti, the forest-associated subspecies Aedes aegypti formosus (Aaf) underwent a domestication process approximately 5000 years ago, giving rise to the globally invasive, human-associated arbovirus vector Aedes aegypti aegypti (Aaa). Despite extensive human-mediated transport, the two subspecies remain largely distinct, with admixture documented mainly in coastal Africa and Saudi Arabia. title: Where Menstrual Education and Environmental Justice Converge
abstract: When discussed together, menstrual and socioenvironmental health often focus on questions of hygiene and risk management, centering the materialities, distribution, and disposal of menstrual products. The toxicity of disposable menstrual products has long been a matter of concern, with growing public attention to endocrine disruptors (EDs) accompanying the expansion of a marketplace for “eco-friendly” options. title: Arbuscular Mycorrhizal fungi alleviate salinity stress in Avicennia marina through morphophysiological and biochemical modulation
abstract: Increasing salinity threatens coastal mangrove ecosystems worldwide by impairing plant growth, physiological function, and biochemical processes, ultimately reducing productivity and survival. The present study was conducted to examine the impact of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) on Avicennia marina under different salt concentrations (9, 14, and 19 dS/m). title: A case study on SWMM based evaluation of rain barrel and downspout disconnection scenarios for urban stormwater management
abstract: Colombo, the executive and judicial capital of Sri Lanka, is located on the southwestern coast of the country and has experienced rapid urbanization in recent years, driven by infrastructure development, land use changes, and the growing impacts of climate change. These factors have significantly increased the frequency and severity of urban flooding. Therefore, this study explores the stormwater management problems in the 686.3-hectare study catchment, adjacent to the Kelani River in suburban Colombo, and proposes effective stormwater management strategies to avoid flooding in the area. abstract: Kawasan pesisir utara Jawa menghadapi krisis sosial-ekologis akut berupa amblasan tanah, abrasi, dan banjir rob. abstract: This study examined the role of pre-boarding training in enhancing the mental health preparedness, safety awareness, and professional preparedness of Filipino seafarers who entered maritime service after March 2020. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was employed involving 390 purposively selected seafarers who had completed at least one sea contract and participated in a manning agency pre-boarding training program. title: Low-cost Efficient Wireless Intelligent Sensors (LEWIS) IoT-Based Rainfall Monitoring
abstract: Rainfall measurement with high spatial and temporal resolution is critical for flood forecasting, drought mitigation, and disaster preparedness. Rainfall patterns are highly variable, both geographically and over time. This variability presents a significant challenge for monitoring, as rain gauges can accurately capture temporal patterns only at a single location. Furthermore, the high cost of commercial instruments restricts their widespread deployment, and rain gauge networks often fail to adequately capture the spatial heterogeneity of precipitation patterns. title: Land-Use Change and Socio-Economic Impacts on Food Security in Aimas District, Sorong Regency
abstract: This study examines agricultural land-use change, socio-economic transformation, and food security implications in Aimas District, Sorong Regency, Indonesia. The study integrated GIS-based spatial analysis of land-cover data for 2014, 2019, and 2024 with a socio-economic survey of 210 households, complemented by direct field observation. abstract: The current study evaluated the genetic characterization and differentiation of oil families in the units of the Yamama, Nahr Umr, and Mishrif reservoirs of the Ratawi oil field, south of Iraq. abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of certification for Indonesian-flagged ships at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority and Harbor Master Office (KSOP Utama Tanjung Priok), identify the constraints encountered, examine its contribution to maritime safety and security, and formulate optimization efforts. The study employs a qualitative descriptive approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, direct observation, and documentation involving relevant parties in the certification process. title: Holistic Cyclone Preparedness in a River Nomadic Community: A Study on Manta Community, Bauphal Upazila, Bangladesh
abstract: Cyclones remain a serious threat to Bangladesh's coastal communities. However, their impacts are not felt equally across all geographical locations and sociodemographic groups. The community of Bauphal, Patuakhali, is especially vulnerable because its livelihoods are tied to rivers, boats, fishing, and seasonal mobility rather than fixed land-based settlement. abstract: Context and relevance. Modern trends in technology development are moving towards the transfer of computing from cloud platforms to embedded devices. In this regard, there is a growing need to determine the optimal stack of hardware and software technologies for solving computer vision problems. Goal. title: Beyond Basic ICT Access: Pedagogical Integration of Geospatial Technologies in Geography Teaching in Temeke Municipality, Tanzania
abstract: Digital technology is now central to competence-based Geography education, yet access and pedagogical use remain uneven in Tanzanian public schools. This study examined how ICT integration supports Geography teaching and learning in Temeke Municipality. Its main objective was to assess whether available technology was being converted into subject-specific, learner-centred practice. A mixed-methods approach and cross-sectional survey design were used. The sample comprised 120 participants: 100 students, 16 Geography teachers, and four Ward Education Officers. title: Towards an integrated approach to evaluating biodiversity‐ and water‐sensitive urban design: A review of popular software tools
abstract: Abstract Globally, cities are recognising a need to incorporate blue‐green infrastructure and ecosystem‐based approaches into urban design and development. With this recognition comes the need to design for biodiversity and water together—though current approaches typically consider these systems independently. The consequences of this are that relationships between biodiversity and water are overlooked, leading to a reduction in system resilience and functionality. title: Multi-Source Transfer Weighted Learning with Random Forest for Cross-Project Software Defect Prediction
abstract: Accurate software defect prediction is essential for identifying fault-prone modules early and reducing software testing and maintenance costs. However, Within-Project Defect Prediction (WPDP) models may perform poorly when the target project has limited labeled defect data. Cross-Project Defect Prediction (CPDP) addresses this limitation by transferring knowledge from other projects, but heterogeneous feature distributions, source–target mismatch, and negative transfer remain significant challenges. title: Fabrication of a citric acid-crosslinked β-cyclodextrin/silica composite and its selective adsorption of cholesterol from crude fish oil
abstract: A novel β-cyclodextrin-modified silica composite (β-CD-SiO 2 ) was prepared by in situ thermal esterification for selective elimination of cholesterol in tuna oil refining. Characterisations revealed the effective immobilisation of β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) onto mesoporous silica (mean pore size 24.40 nm). title: Improved estimation of lake storage variation via DEM reconstruction integrating elevation and morphological constraints
abstract: High-quality Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are essential for accurately estimating lake storage variations, but the high cost of in-situ measurements limits their large-scale application. Reconstructing DEMs from remote sensing-derived lake contours is a promising low-cost alternative. However, most existing methods primarily rely on elevation-matched contours and discard those without elevation data. title: Evaluating Carniolan honey bee (Apis mellifera carnica) lines under contrasting ecological zones
abstract: This study evaluates four breeding lines of the Carniolan honey bee, Apis mellifera carnica, across distinct ecological zones of Serbia and Montenegro. The objective was to assess phenotypic, morphometric, and isoenzyme polymorphism of local populations adapted to contrasting climatic and altitudinal conditions. Two Serbian lines (lowland Vršac and mountainous Vranje) and two Montenegrin lines (mountainous Bijelo Polje and coastal Sutomore) were examined. title: Integrating spatial econometrics and remote sensing for pixel-level wind energy corridor identification: evidence from West Bengal, India
abstract: This study integrates remote sensing and spatial econometric techniques to identify pixel-level wind energy corridors in West Bengal, India. Weibull scale (A) and shape (K) parameter rasters at 100 m resolution were combined with Dynamic World land-cover data to evaluate how landscape characteristics influence wind resource potential. District-level zonal statistics were analysed using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Spatial Autoregressive (SAR), Spatial Error Model (SEM), and Spatial Durbin Model (SDM). title: The Role of Geographical Indications in Sustainable Coffee Tourism in Forest Areas: Lessons from Lemukih Coffee
abstract: Geographical Indications (GIs) protect distinctive local products while supporting community development and sustainable tourism. However, their effectiveness depends on regional government capacity to integrate product protection, economic development, environmental conservation, and tourism. This study examines the potential of Lemukih Robusta Coffee as a regional flagship product, evaluates the effectiveness of the Buleleng Regency Government’s policies in managing and protecting its GI in areas adjacent to forests, and explores how GI protection can support sustainable coffee tourism. title: The Mediating Role of Spatial Skills in Learning Kinematic Graphics Assisted by Vector Animation Videos
abstract: Kinematic graph interpretation is a basic physics competency that often challenges students because of abstract vector representations and weak geometric transformation skills. This study analyzes the influence of vector animation videos on kinematic graph learning, with spatial skills as a mediating variable. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design was applied to 60 Grade X students of SMAS Ta’miriyah Surabaya. abstract: ABSTRACT Fifteen new actinomycin analogs were obtained from the marine‐derived Streptomyces polyantibioticus S4D258. abstract: ABSTRACT Pyrethroid insecticides are largely exploited in Italy to reduce Aedes albopictus nuisance and to discontinue autochthonous transmission of exotic arboviruses. V1016G mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene is strongly associated with resistance to pyrethroids in this species. abstract: Dental students often experience stress due to the curriculum’s theoretical and practical demands, whichcan negatively affect their well-being. Previous research suggests that room colors and images can reduceanxiety in certain populations. However, no studies have examined this effect among dental students. abstract: Abstract In this article, I examine how I embed algorithms in instrumental and electroacoustic compositional practices to organise numerical data drawn from extra-musical environmental and cosmological contexts within musical materials and structures. I explore such material-semiotic exchanges between music and surrounding environments to sonically reconfigure the matter of the life stories suggested by Ursula Le Guin, stories that challenge anthropocentric narratives. abstract: ABSTRACT Organizations face growing pressure to respond to environmental and social challenges, yet research has not sufficiently explained how organizational actors mobilise dynamic‐capability microfoundations across the development of sustainability‐oriented innovations. Drawing on 68 semistructured interviews conducted between March and November 2024 across 18 EU and UK marine firms, this qualitative study examines how innovation champions and related actors support sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring. title: Multiple introductions and spread of novel reassortant highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses via wild birds, South Korea, 2024–2025
abstract: Between 14 October 2024 and 24 March 2025, 43 cases of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) type A (H5N1) infections in wild birds and 1 case in a leopard cat were detected through the national HPAI surveillance program. title: Aramid inserts to reduce shear fracture in GFRP composite materials for aeronautical and naval use
abstract: Delamination is a critical failure mode in glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) laminates used in artisanal boatbuilding, particularly under dynamic loading associated with slamming phenomena. This study evaluates the effectiveness of interlaminar aramid fiber stitching as a reinforcement technique to improve the interlaminar shear strength and damage tolerance of GFRP laminates manufactured using traditional hand lay-up processes. title: Far-Red Turn-On Fluorogenic Probe for Versatile Detection of Inorganic Polyphosphates
abstract: Abstract Inorganic polyphosphate (polyP) is a ubiquitous phosphate biopolymer involved in diverse cellular processes. Despite its significance, selective detection of polyP remains challenging because of its simple and highly charged structure. title: Favorable habitats of endangered halophytes harbor unique soil properties and bacterial communities, with a dominant root-associated genus promoting host plant growth
abstract: Understanding how edaphic factors and root-associated bacterial communities interact to shape plant growth is essential for effective conservation of halophytic species in coastal ecosystems. We investigated relationships among bulk soil, rhizosphere, and root bacterial microbiota; soil physicochemical properties; and Salicornia europaea growth spanning three distinct areas (Lakeside Park, Ubaranai and Misaki) within a brackish lake in Japan. title: Integrative transcriptomic and lipidomic analysis of the effects of Eucommia ulmoides on growth performance and lipid metabolism in Larimichthys crocea
abstract: Introduction Larimichthys crocea is an economically important marine aquaculture species, and improving growth performance while maintaining lipid metabolic homeostasis is important for its sustainable production. This study investigated the effects of dietary Eucommia ulmoides supplementation on growth performance and lipid metabolism in L. crocea and explored the underlying molecular basis using integrated transcriptomic and lipidomic analyses. title: Youth and the future of labor- and knowledge-intensive small-scale farming in West Africa under climate change and political instability
abstract: Debates on the future of smallholder farming in sub-Saharan Africa often interpret rural youth mobility and non-farm work as withdrawal from agriculture. This article examines how rural youth in coastal Guinea-Bissau engage with labour- and knowledge-intensive, climate-vulnerable mangrove swamp rice farming, and the conditions under which agriculture remains part of their imagined futures. abstract: The Wazwaz–Kaur equation is a significant nonlinear partial differential equation. This equation is used to describe nonlinear wave propagation in fields including fluid dynamics, plasma physics, and other areas of mathematical physics. In this study, we investigate analytical solutions of the $(3+1)$-dimensional Wazwaz–Kaur Boussinesq Equation (WKBE). title: MerR-type regulator ZccR links zinc homeostasis to biofilm formation and interspecies competition in Streptococcus mutans
abstract: Objectives Zinc is widely present in the oral microenvironment and can influence the growth of oral bacteria. ZccR is a MerR-type transcriptional regulator that controls zinc efflux in Streptococcus mutans ( S. mutans ), but its role in biofilm virulence and interspecies competition with oral commensals remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of ZccR in the formation of single-species biofilms of S. mutans and dual-species biofilms with oral commensal streptococci, and its underlying regulatory mechanisms. abstract: Overtourism is increasingly understood as a multidimensional sustainability challenge, yet local decision-makers still lack replicable tools for assessing where tourism pressure may translate into territorial vulnerability. This paper develops a municipal impact-assessment framework for diagnosing overtourism vulnerability regimes. The analysis follows a two-step logic. title: Nature-based flood assessment for vulnerable educational infrastructure under tropical urban conditions
abstract: Worldwide, urban rainwater flooding is increasingly affecting small-scale public infrastructure in tropical cities. Consequently, drainage decisions are often made with limited hydrometric data. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate flood control alternatives using the Nature-based Solutions (NBS) approach through participatory assessment and modeling with the Stormwater Management Model (SWMM) at a vulnerable educational infrastructure (VEI) in Durán, Ecuador. abstract: Ti 6 Al 4 V components in aerospace and marine applications frequently suffer from coupled mechanical wear and corrosive degradation across severe temperature regimes. title: Empirically informed AHP-FR modeling for multi-hazard susceptibility mapping in a mountainous transport corridors
abstract: Abstract Mountainous transport corridors are increasingly exposed to interacting natural hazards that intensify infrastructure, socio-economic, and land-use risks. abstract: This study examines how Chinese high school students perceive and respond to online misinformation and how their responses are shaped by school, family, and wider social contexts. Four focus group discussions were conducted with 24 students aged 15-17 from two public high schools in a southeastern coastal city. abstract: This study examines the integration of concept mapping and authentic assessment in pre-service elementary science education using a four-phase professional development model. An embedded mixed-method design was employed, involving 82 seventh-semester students in a primary school teacher education program at a state university in Indonesia. title: Roblox-Based Immersive Learning for Environmental Literacy in Online Science Education
abstract: Environmental literacy requires learning environments that enable students to explore complex ecosystem interactions and evaluate the consequences of environmental decisions, yet conventional online science learning often provides limited opportunities for such experiences. This study developed and evaluated a Roblox-based immersive learning system designed to support environmental literacy, particularly in the context of peatland conservation. title: Phased ecological responses and effectiveness assessment of subtidal oyster reef restoration: a case study from Dashentang, Bohai Bay
abstract: Subtidal oyster reef restoration presents greater challenges for implementation and monitoring than intertidal restoration, and evaluations of relatively large-scale ecological restoration projects remain limited. This study evaluated the restoration project of Dashengtang using monitoring data from five field surveys collected from 2022 to 2026, and evaluated stage-specific ecological changes in oyster populations, aquatic environments, and macrobenthic communities. abstract: Mastigitae comprise 15 genera, of which seven are extinct, and species of two extant genera are also documented as fossils. abstract: This study aims to analyze the development, trends, and patterns of research related to the Halal Assurance System (SJH) in Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the Southeast Asian region using a bibliometric approach. abstract: This study presents an inaugural analysis of rock-forming mineral chemistry within andesites from the Polovinkinskaya Depression, situated at the junction of the Tynda and Nimnyr terranes in the central Aldan- Stanovoy Shield. abstract: This chapter surveys terrain visibility models, algorithms, and applications. abstract: Understanding the Earth’s deep interior remains challenging, as traditional geophysical methods face ambiguities in linking seismic observations to temperature, composition, or mass density variations. Atmospheric neutrinos, produced by the constant flux of cosmic rays colliding with the upper atmosphere, offer a complementary probe: with energies of a few GeV, they traverse the Earth and experience flavor oscillations influenced by the planet’s electron density distribution, which depends on both its mass density and composition. abstract: LiDAR return intensity provides complementary surface-response cues for robotic perception and state estimation, yet many simulation pipelines omit it or reproduce it using reconstruction methods that require real intensity supervision and per-scene optimization. abstract: Electroconvective (EC) instability near ion-selective surfaces plays a key role in electro-chemical transport beyond the diffusion-limited regime. abstract: Population cycles are important components of many natural systems. Most studied in short-lived and small-bodied species, cycles frequently appear to be driven by density-dependent feedbacks. abstract: Abstract Space weather events pose a growing threat to modern economies, yet their macroeconomic consequences remain underexplored. This study presents the first dedicated economic assessment of geomagnetic storm impacts on Aotearoa New Zealand, quantifying potential gross domestic product (GDP) losses across seven conservative disruption and mitigation scenarios due to an extreme coronal mass ejection (CME). title: SCRM: An Actionable Framework for Space Cyber Risk Management
abstract: Space infrastructures play critical roles in modern society, including satellite communications (SATCOM). Like the Internet, space infrastructures are vulnerable to cyber attacks, or space cyber attacks, highlighting the importance of managing cyber risks to space infrastructures, or space cyber risks. However, adequately managing space cyber risks is an open problem. abstract: Effective spatial organization of post-disaster shelter camps is essential for ensuring access to basic services while making efficient use of limited space and resources. In this paper, we propose a graph-theoretic framework for shelter-camp facility placement based on rainbow $k$-domination and Roman domination. abstract: Time-variable stellar heating may create new climate states, such as permanently hot or cold hemispheres, on asynchronous planets. title: Does a mortality schedule need a Makeham term? Calibrating the likelihood-ratio test
abstract: Whether a fitted mortality model needs a Makeham term, the non-negative constant representing background mortality, is commonly decided with a likelihood-ratio test. abstract: Richard Christopher Carrington carried out extensive sunspot observations from 1853 to 1861 and left numerous scientific legacies. However, despite his fame, consulting his original manuscripts, we have found Carrington's last sunspot drawing, which he never published. We date this drawing 23 Dec 1870, when Carrington was based at his Churt Observatory. abstract: Left-behind places are usually identified using economic, demographic and accessibility indicators, but these may not align with well-being and social cohesion. abstract: We investigate interacting spinless electrons on finite molecular networks described by a tight-binding Hubbard Hamiltonian. abstract: In real-world software development, code review typically involves iterative interactions between developers and reviewers to improve software quality, making the process costly and time-consuming. abstract: Small Island Developing States (SIDS) depend fundamentally on the ocean for their societies, economies and livelihoods, yet they are among the regions most exposed to ocean changes. abstract: The accuracy of FY-4B/AGRI sea surface temperature (SST) over the China Seas has not been systematically evaluated. abstract: Abstract This article examines the legal implications of autonomous fishing vessels ( AFV s) under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea ( LOSC ). abstract: With a growing global population and strict restrictions on traditional antibiotics, sustainable fish health management is crucial for aquaculture. abstract: Antarctic krill is a keystone species in the Southern Ocean ecosystem, in that it plays an essential role in healthy marine food webs and carbon sequestration. However, its survival is increasingly being threatened by a growing industrial fishery dominated by powerful corporations alongside habitat changes caused by climate change. abstract: This paper presents the results of research on fluxgate sensors, which are widely used in underwater navigation systems, magnetic anomaly detection, seabed magnetic surveying, as well as in tasks related to the detection of sunken objects and exploration of underwater mineral deposits. title: Harnessing macrogenomics to study changing marine ecosystems under global climate change
abstract: Climate change is reshaping marine ecosystems at an accelerating pace. Predicting its impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem functions is therefore crucial to developing effective conservation strategies. Integration of genomic tools, habitat modelling and simulations offers a transformative approach to forecast these impacts. Yet, current frameworks remain limited to single-species analyses. title: The power and potential of blue philanthropy
abstract: Abstract Blue philanthropy has quadrupled in the past 15 years, growing to over USD 2.2 billion annually. We spotlight areas in which it has resulted in significant impacts and is poised to generate more. Introducing a five-part research agenda, we describe the power, pitfalls and potential of blue philanthropy, and how scientists can contribute to shaping an increasingly impactful future for marine science and ocean conservation in concert with blue philanthropy.

abstract: Marine environments and seafood are potential reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance, but genome-level data linking antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and metal tolerance genes (MTGs) in these matrices remain fragmented. abstract: Instant seasoning manufacturing requires strict quality control to guarantee consumer safety and prevent biological, chemical, or physical contamination. title: MILITARY THREATS TO THE SECURITY OF UKRAINE'S MARITIME TRADE
abstract: The aggressive policy of the russian federation remains a source of threats to the security of Ukraine's maritime trade today. The main military threats to the security of Ukraine's maritime trade are: damage to port infrastructure; damage to merchant ships in ports and at sea passage to/from ports; mine hazard; cyber threats.

title: Effectiveness of Sea Employment Agreement (PKL) in Providing Legal Protection for Indonesian Crew Members (Case Study at the Tanjung Priok Main Harbormaster and Port Authority Office)
abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of the Sea Employment Agreement in providing legal protection for Indonesian crew members, with the Main Harbormaster and Port Authority Office (KSOP Utama) of Tanjung Priok as the case study. The research addresses three aspects: the implementation and effectiveness of Sea Employment Agreement, obstacles affecting its effectiveness, and efforts to strengthen its implementation. title: Next Generation Mining of Genebanks: Harnessing Sorghum ( Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench) Germplasm in the Uganda National Genebank Through Genomic Prediction
abstract: ABSTRACT Germplasm in genebanks is vital for crop improvement, yet it often lacks information on key traits of interest to users. Genomic prediction offers great potential to use genomic estimated breeding values as a proxy for phenotypic records. This minimizes the expensive and laborious large‐scale evaluation of large genebank collections. In this study, we assessed the use of genomic prediction to exploit the genetic diversity of 3333 sorghum accessions conserved by the Uganda National Genebank. title: A review of corrosion behavior of alloys in Arctic, Antarctic and cold regions: key factors, knowledge gaps, and the emerging role of metal additive manufacturing
abstract: The increasing strategic and economic importance of the Earth’s polar regions has created a growing need for metallic infrastructure that can withstand prolonged exposure to severe cold. Corrosion is an important factor affecting the reliability and service life of metallic components in these environments. title: Evaluations of Precipitation, Temperature, and Circulation Characteristics in Simulations of CMIP6 Models over the Arabian Peninsula
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the performance of 74 CMIP6 (including HighResMIP) models for the historical climate of the Arabian Peninsula (AP). The analysis examines whether models reproduce the mean climate, trends (accounting internal-variability), extremes, and key circulation/process diagnostics. Despite strengths, several limitations persist across key aspects. Precipitation biases include annual-mean wet-bias over the southern AP and dry-bias over the central AP, and models underestimate the frequency and intensity of heavy-precipitation-events. title: National Symbols and Identity in Hungary and the EU
abstract: The history of symbols is as old as humanity itself, and they continue to play a key role in expressing national identity today. The external function of symbols is to express sovereignty – as a representation of autonomy and independence – while their internal function is to express identity (emotional attachment to the community). This study examines the constitutional and criminal law protection of national symbols, their history and changes, presenting their role in expressing national identity. The study discusses the fundamental national symbols enshrined in the Fundamental Law of Hungar

title: Automated Indentation Geometry Detection for Hardness Measurement: A Vision-Based Nondestructive Evaluation Approach
abstract: Hardness testing is one of the most widely applied methods for evaluating the mechanical properties of metallic materials in manufacturing and quality control. Among standardized techniques, Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell are most commonly used, all relying on precise measurement of indentation geometry. However, conventional evaluation methods still depend on manual or semi-automated readings, which are prone to operator error and unsuitable for industrial automation. title: Levels and Health Risk Assessment of Heavy Metals in Selected Skin-Whitening Creams Marketed in Lafia Town
abstract: The rising popularity of skin-whitening creams in Nigeria raises alarms about potential exposure to harmful metals that may occur either as impurities or as intentionally added ingredients. This study assessed the levels of cadmium, chromium, copper, iron, and lead in various skin-whitening creams available in Lafia Town. Samples from different brands were randomly collected from shops in Lafia Modern Market, pre-treated through acid digestion, and analyzed using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS). title: The Legal and Socio-Economic Implications of Maritime Crimes in Nigeria: Challenges and the Way Forward
abstract: Maritime crimes constitute a significant threat to Nigeria’s national security, economic stability, and regional maritime governance. These crimes include piracy, armed robbery at sea, illegal oil bunkering, human trafficking, drug trafficking, illegal fishing, and environmental pollution. Despite various legal and institutional frameworks established to combat these offences, enforcement remains weak due to systemic corruption, inadequate maritime surveillance, jurisdictional challenges, and limited inter-agency coordination. title: Spatial heterogeneity, source contributions, and hazard mapping of potentially hazardous elements in irrigated soils of the Yellow River Basin, Northwest China
abstract: Introduction Potentially hazardous element (PHE) contamination threatens agroecosystem sustainability and food security, particularly in irrigated regions. The Yellow River Basin in Northwest China is a critical agricultural zone where intensive irrigation and fertilizer use may accelerate soil contamination. Methods A total of 487 topsoil samples were collected under a stratified random design. abstract: Background. Athletic performance genomics is dominated by studies conducted in European and African populations, leaving Southeast Asian (SEA) populations systematically underrepresented. title: Axenic and Gnotobiotic Aquatic Models: Methods, Husbandry, and Applications
abstract: Axenic and gnotobiotic aquatic animals provide direct experimental access to the causal roles of microorganisms in host physiology, nutrition, immunity and disease. Fish are particularly suitable vertebrate models because fertilization and embryogenesis commonly occur externally, allowing embryos to be disinfected before hatching and maintained under microbiologically controlled conditions. title: In the World of Aquatic Parasites, Microsporidia Matter!
abstract: Microsporidia are highly diverse, widespread parasites related to fungi and several groups of zoosporic protistan parasites. They infect a broad range of hosts, from protists to vertebrates, in many environments including most, if not all, aquatic habitats. Their genomes range from relatively conventional to highly reduced, yet they share key cellular structures and traits underlying infection and host association. abstract: Introduction Late sowing constrains grain yield formation in wheat by shortening the duration of post-anthesis assimilate accumulation and limiting the effective utilization of source-derived assimilates during grain filling. Optimizing nitrogen nutrition and growth regulation could help maintain physiological activity, sink development and grain productivity under late-sown conditions. title: Sustainable production of critical components for the oil and gas industry
abstract: This research addresses the need for sustainable manufacturing and quality assurance of high-load components in the oil and gas sector within the frameworks of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0. The primary objective was to optimize the finishing treatment of the functional internal surfaces of NB 32.02.102-04 cylinder liners for NB-32 drilling pumps by replacing conventional energy-intensive finishing processes with more resource-efficient alternatives. title: LDIAAD: A Lightweight Domain-Invariant Acoustic Anomaly Detector for Industrial Machine Condition Monitoring Under Operating Condition Shifts
abstract: Acoustic monitoring offered a low-cost, non-invasive approach to industrial predictive maintenance, but anomalous sound detection (ASD) models trained under one operating condition were shown in prior work to lose substantial accuracy when operating conditions shifted, and lightweight models suitable for edge deployment were rarely evaluated jointly for cross-domain generalization and computational efficiency. title: Building an ‘epigenetic clock’: utilizing whole genome DNA methylation patterns to predict age in haddock, Melanogrammus aeglefinus
abstract: Age-based population models are a gold standard approach to estimate stock size and sustainable catch recommendations for effective fisheries management. Traditional ageing by counting annuli on their ear stones (otoliths), is labor-intensive, lethal, and can be inaccurate for long-lived fishes. In this study, we present an accurate, non-lethal epigenetic clock method for predicting age in haddock, Melanogrammus aeglefinus , one of the most valuable commercial fisheries in the north Atlantic Ocean. title: Oil spill image recognition based on multiple-scale processing of brightness distribution histograms
abstract: The problem of detecting anomalies in processed images acquired from visual monitoring equipment becomes particularly relevant in the context of ecological monitoring of the world ocean's water areas, specifically when searching for the consequences of technogenic catastrophes caused by oil spills. In the present study, anomalies are understood as image fragments characterizing oil product spills. abstract: Fresh sweet flag ( Acorus calamus ) biochar (BC) was modified by impregnation pyrolysis, and the ability of the resulting Mn/N-BC material to activate peroxydisulfate (PDS) adsorption and degrade tetracycline (TC) was investigated alongside its reaction mechanism. abstract: Process safety is crucial for scaling up the hydrogen economy, particularly given the challenges posed by transportation-focused fuel cell applications. Thermal anomalies in Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCs) e,g, such as localized hotspots or rapid temperature excursions—severely impair electrochemical performance, accelerate material degradation (e.g., cracking of electrolytes, electrodes or sealing materials), and can lead to thermal runaway or catastrophic failures. title: Fully automatic trace gas plume detection
abstract: Abstract Future imaging spectrometers will expand contemporary data volumes by orders of magnitude, requiring automated methods to upscale labor-intensive detection of trace gas point sources. Here we present a fully-automated approach that achieves operational performance for plume detection and labelling without human participation. abstract: Introduction The organization of school time has been a focus of recent education reform, yet which school time reform practices appear in the official social media narratives of district education bureaus remains insufficiently understood. Methods Taking Qingdao, China, as a case study, this study employed directed content analysis. A deductive coding framework of 3 first-level and 9 second-level nodes was first constructed from the literature and policy documents. title: Zero-Shot Snow Depth Extraction from Time-Lapse Imagery Using Vision Foundation Models
abstract: Automated snow depth retrieval from time-lapse cameras is constrained by site-specific annotation and manual image quality screening, thus limiting scalability across deployments. We present a fully automated, zero-annotation pipeline that integrates text-prompted segmentation for snow pole detection with a vision language model for image quality control. title: Polymer-resolved ecological risk of microplastics in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta: a secondary-data assessment using pollution load and polymer hazard indices
abstract: Microplastics (MPs; plastic particles smaller than 5 mm) are widely reported in the surface water and sediment of the Vietnamese Mekong Delta, but their ecological hazard has not been synthesised across the Delta. Because polymer types differ by orders of magnitude in the toxicity of their constituent monomers and additives, particle abundance alone is an incomplete measure of hazard. title: Russia’s occupation of eastern Ukraine: the cultural infrastructure of rule
abstract: Focusing on areas of Ukraine’s Donetsk and Luhansk regions occupied by Russia since 2014, this article examines occupation as a cultural infrastructure assembled through heraldry, monuments, popular music, cinema, education policy, school materials, and literature. It shows how these media share a repertoire that stages conquest as “reunification” and dependence as local sovereignty, recasting violence as anti-fascist defence and historical restoration. abstract: ABSTRACT Motivation Modern sharks, rays and skates (Neoselachii) are a diverse, globally distributed and ecologically important group. They possess a rich, geologically extensive and well‐documented fossil record that provides a powerful basis for studying their macroevolution, paleoecology and biogeography. abstract: In the 2024 – 2025 growing season, a study was conducted at Selcuk University’s research station in Konya, Türkiye, to evaluate the effects of potassium silicate (K2SiO3) on bread wheat under water-limited field conditions with supplementary irrigation. title: Rainfall–Surface Temperature Coupling and Compound Dry-Hot Persistence Across Northwestern Bangladesh: A 25-Year Multi-Sensor Earth Observation Analysis
abstract: Understanding how rainfall variability regulates land-surface thermal conditions is essential for climate-sensitive regions where water availability, vegetation dynamics, and heat stress interact. title: Construction of Urban Functional Zones Identification Model Based on TF-IDF and Public Perception-Weighted Algorithms
abstract: Urban neighborhoods used to be fairly straightforward—residential here, commercial there. That is less and less true, and planners need ways to keep up. This paper tries to build one such tool, tested on Pudong New Area in Shanghai. We combine a TF-IDF weighting scheme with survey-based perception scores and feed both into a POI-based functional-zone classifier. TF-IDF handles the spatial-rarity side of the problem. abstract: The construction of the Landing Platform Dock (LPD) 163 M ship in the Warship Division of PT. XXX Indonesia is a project with a high level of complexity that requires effective project schedule control to minimize work delays. This study aims to analyze the construction scheduling of module I and module II using the Critical Path Method (CPM). abstract: Saudi Arabia’s industrial growth offers two key materials challenges: reducing the embodied carbon of construction and diverting mineral, glass, polymeric, metallurgical, and construction-and-demolition waste from disposal. This review analyzes how recycled materials and sustainable construction chemicals can be integrated as a unified low-carbon strategy, rather than as separate innovations. title: Estimating beam pointing of vertically pointing cloud radars using radiosonde measurements
abstract: Abstract. Accurate beam pointing is essential for vertically pointing cloud radars, as even small tilting off zenith introduces projections of horizontal wind into Doppler velocity measurements. These effects can bias the interpretation of vertical air motion and hydrometeor fall speeds, leading to systematic errors in cloud and precipitation retrievals. abstract: Abstract Fish-killing harmful algal blooms (HABs) continue to inflict severe economic losses on marine aquaculture worldwide, yet monitoring systems designed around microalgal cell counts frequently fail to anticipate acute mortality events. The dominant surveillance paradigm was inherited from shellfish-toxin monitoring, where a filter-feeding bivalve integrates exposure to intracellular phycotoxins and toxin burden in tissue triggers regulatory action. abstract: The Maritime Labour Convention (MLC, 2006) was designed to harmonise minimum standards of working and living conditions at sea across jurisdictions. Despite its near-universal ratification, significant disparities in labour conditions persist, indicating limited effectiveness in the implementation of the regulatory framework. This article aims to explain this paradox by analysing the MLC through the lens of institutional economics and multi-level governance. abstract: Toxic trace elements in edible oils pose public health risks because of their persistence, bioaccumulation, and, for some elements, carcinogenic potential. This study quantified Pb, Cd, Cr, As, Hg, Mn, Ni, and Cu in 21 commercially available soybean oil samples collected from Dhaka, Bangladesh. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly reported in foods, yet comparative data across commonly consumed dairy products remain limited in South Asia. abstract: This quantitative study examines the impact of waste on the Sri Lanka Navy's (SLN) technical seaworthiness processes and the mediating roles of organisational culture and corporate governance. Using Structural Equation Modelling on data from 391 SLN Marine and Electrical Engineering officers, the research identified nine waste types, including the unique category "Duties Other Than Prime Job." title: Guideline Adherence and Variability in AI‐Assisted Surgical Decision‐Making for Low Back Pain
abstract: BACKGROUND: Surgical decision-making in low back pain requires balancing diagnostic uncertainty, asymmetric risk and guideline adherence, particularly when distinguishing non-specific conditions from pathologies warranting timely surgical referral. As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered as decision-support tools, their reliability in guideline-concordant surgical triage requires systematic evaluation. abstract: Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from geothermal and oilfield brines is supported by many technology reviews, yet an operator holding a brine analysis still lacks a structured route to a defensible choice of technology. abstract: Satellite retrieval of chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) is central to monitoring eutrophication in inland reservoirs, yet the atmospheric-correction processors it depends on, trained on oceanic and large-lake conditions, are systematically biased over small water bodies. abstract: Access to safe and reliable water remains a persistent challenge for rural communities in Malaysia, where infrastructural limitations, spatial constraints, and governance fragmentation continue to undermine water security. title: Unlocking the mechanical, physical, and antimicrobial properties of gelatin-based films via chitosan nanoparticle reinforcement for active food packaging applications
abstract: The growing ecological concerns over plastic packaging have driven interest in biodegradable film materials. This study evaluates the mechanical, physical, and antimicrobial properties of chicken skin gelatin films reinforced with varying concentrations (0–8%) of chitosan nanoparticles (CNPs). title: Analysis of Multiple Tire Rubber-Derived Chemicals in Fish Bile and Plasma: Analytical Method and Field Assessment in Puget Sound, WA, USA
abstract: Abstract Tire rubber-derived chemicals (TRCs) are known to be highly toxic to fish, but understanding of their environmental levels and fate is still limited. This study presents a new method for the analysis of 18 TRCs, including phenylenediamines (TRC-PDs), their quinone derivatives (TRC-Qs), and rubber vulcanizing and curing-related chemicals (TRC-VCRs) in fish bile and plasma samples. abstract: This study evaluates the groundwater quality in the Landhi-Korangi areas of Karachi, Pakistan, using an integrated approach combining statistical analysis, hydro-geochemical analysis, and geospatial techniques. Groundwater samples shows higher concentrations of parameters (TDS, Cl-, and SO42−) in pre-monsoon samples and higher concentrations of parameters (Na2+, hardness, TDS, and SO42−) in post-monsoon samples, both exceeding the WHO drinking water limits. title: Assessment of Groundwater Quality from Tombia Community in Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State, Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater is the primary source of drinking water for rural communities in the Niger Delta, yet its quality is increasingly threatened by natural geochemical processes and anthropogenic activities. This study evaluated the quality of groundwater in Tombia community in Degema Local Government Area, Rivers State, Nigeria, with the aim of assessing its suitability for domestic consumption and identifying potential health risks. title: Underestimation of plastic pollution and implications for water quality assessments in urban lakes
abstract: Plastic pollution is increasingly recognized as a pervasive threat to water quality, yet most studies quantify only microplastics (<5 mm), potentially biasing estimates of environmental contamination. Here, we formally evaluated the underestimation bias associated with the intentional exclusion of plastics >5 mm from samples collected across a system of urban freshwater lakes (n = 20). title: Nutritional and Economic Potential of Needle Cuttlefish (Sepia aculeata): Unlocking an Underutilized Seafood Resource in Bangladesh
abstract: Needle cuttlefish ( Sepia aculeata ), an abundant yet underutilized cephalopod species in Bangladesh, remains a non-conventional seafood resource with limited nutritional information. This study evaluated the proximate composition, amino acid profile, fatty acid composition, micronutrients, and heavy metals of both edible and non-edible portions of S. aculeata , while recommended nutrient intake (RNI) contribution and economic efficiency were assessed using edible portions only. title: Quantifying spatially varying associations between water quality and sub-basin structural characteristics: a multiscale spatial approach
abstract: Abstract Water quality patterns reflect spatially heterogeneous associations among topography, drainage connectivity, land use configuration, and soil hydrologic structure, whereas concentration-based assessments and global models may obscure where these relationships emerge and at which spatial scales they operate. Using monitoring data from 2020 to 2024, this study examined six water quality indicators: total organic carbon (TOC), total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), dissolved oxygen (DO), pH, and electrical conductivity (EC) across 67 mid-basins in South Korea. title: Rare earth elements and yttrium in water sources of the Distrito Federal, Central Brazil: baseline data for water quality monitoring
abstract: Rare earth elements and yttrium (REY) were evaluated in water supply sources of the Distrito Federal, Central Brazil, to establish baseline data for water quality monitoring. Tap water was collected from the distribution system of two water sources: Lakes Paranoá and Descoberto, while groundwater samples were obtained from porous and fractured aquifers. title: Effects of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Supplementation on Growth, Survival and Fatty Acid Composition of Anadara tuberculosa Spat
abstract: ABSTRACT This research assessed the feasibility of using the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a complementary feed for the mangrove cockle Anadara tuberculosa spat. The nutritional impact of five mix diets was tested: (1) Tisochrysis lutea + Chaetoceros gracilis , (2) C. gracilis + S. cerevisiae , (3) S. cerevisiae , (4) T. lutea + S. cerevisiae and (5) T. lutea + C. gracilis + S. cerevisiae . title: Reconciling Competing Natural Resource Interests for Sustainable Development: The Role of Law in Balancing Oil Exploitation, Water Resource and Ecosystem Services in Nigeria
abstract: Oil exploitation remains important to the economy and development of Nigeria, but its interaction with the ecosystem and interconnected water resources create conflicts between competing forms of resource use. This paper examines whether Nigerian law provides a coherent and balanced framework for reconciling oil development with the continued impairment on water resources and associated ecosystems. title: Effect of storage time on release of microplastics (MPs) from different milk packaging
abstract: The growing detection of microplastics (MPs) in the human body has raised concerns about the potential entrance of MPs into the food chain and subsequently into humans. Due to wide consumption of milk by different age groups, investigating the MPs release into milk during storage time from different commercial milk packaging materials is crucial. MPs release in three common packaging types of ESL milk (bottles and packets) and sterilized milk (multi-layer carton) during storage periods (expiration date) was studied. title: Toxicological impacts of sulfamethoxazole on freshwater organisms – toxicity and oxidative stress
abstract: The continuous expansion of the pharmaceutical sector has intensified aquatic contamination, as persistent active compounds enter water bodies through urban, industrial, and agricultural runoff. Among these contaminants, sulfamethoxazole (SMX)—a widely used sulphonamide antibiotic—raises ecological concerns due to its persistence and potential for bioaccumulation. abstract: This study analyzed how valuation methods and spatial scale influence reported ecosystem service values. A systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines and the PICO approach screened 222 articles from the Scopus database (2016–2025); after applying rigorous inclusion criteria, 38 studies were selected. abstract: Abstract The global rise of harmful cyanobacterial blooms (HCBs) in freshwater systems is driven by anthropogenic pressure and climate change, yet limited information exists on how these factors shape HCBs and their phycosphere-associated bacterial communities (PBCs). title: Landscape spatial configuration determines seasonal nitrate transport rather than land-use proportions in mountainous rivers
abstract: Identifying seasonal nitrate (NO 3 − ) transport pathways remains a challenge in complex mountainous watersheds. This study integrated hydrogeochemistry, dual isotopes (δ 15 N-NO₃ − and δ 18 O-NO₃ − ), and the MixSIAR model with landscape metrics to investigate nitrate dynamics in the Chao River Basin. Spatial analysis categorized the watershed into upstream, midstream, and downstream zones. title: Method of meal delivery influences estimates of postprandial metabolism and alkaline tide in a benthic fish
abstract: Intragastric gavage is widely used in studies of digestive physiology to deliver standardised meals, yet it remains unclear whether it elicits postprandial metabolic and acid-base responses comparable to voluntary feeding. title: A cost-benefit analysis of small-holder floating-house fish farming in Chau Doc City, Vietnamese Mekong Delta
abstract: Smallholder floating-house aquaculture supports vital riverine livelihoods in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta but faces increasing environmental and hydrological pressures. This study conducts an empirical Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) to evaluate the economic viability, cost drivers, and adaptation strategies of smallholders in Chau Doc City in An Giang Province. Primary data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 35 fish farmers across three distinct river reaches. title: Humans and disasters: Examining the disaster mitigation knowledge of the Kaili tribe in Central Sulawesi
abstract: The natural disasters of earthquakes, liquefaction, and tsunamis marked the activation of the Palu Koro Fault on September 28, 2018, resulting in numerous casualties. However, the Kaili people, as the indigenous community, possess local knowledge of disaster mitigation, thereby minimizing risks. Therefore, this study was conducted to explore historical values and traditional knowledge related to disaster mitigation. abstract: Based on 112 water quality-related proceedings of the Hong Kong Legislative Council from 2014 to 2025, this study employed an analytical framework of policy tools, policy issues, and time evolution to investigate Hong Kong’s water-quality governance agenda. abstract: Microplastic (MP; MPs) and nanoplastic (NP; NPs) pollution poses a growing threat to global health. Their small size and large surface area facilitate ingestion, accumulation, and interactions with biological systems, leading to toxicity through oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cell death. abstract: This paper presents an AI-enabled predictive procurement model that integrates probabilistic demand forecasting, supplier lead-time prediction, and multi-echelon inventory optimization to secure target service levels while lowering working capital. The framework couples hierarchical time-series forecasting with gradient-boosted trees and lightweight sequence models, capturing seasonality, promotions, and regime shifts. title: Solid waste management practices in riparian communities are a key driver of microplastic concentrations in the Mekong River, Cambodia
abstract: Rivers are major conduits of plastic pollution, however the role of community level waste collection on riverine microplastic concentrations remains poorly understood. We investigated seasonal patterns and drivers of microplastic pollution along the Lower Mekong River, Cambodia, with a focus on riparian waste collection services. abstract: Abstract This study measured polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) contamination in ten commercially important fish species from the Al-Jubail industrial coastline, Arabian Gulf, Saudi Arabia. The plants were sprayed with three concentrations of the extract (0.0, 2.5, and 5) mL L⁻¹ at three growth stages. abstract: Abstract Emerging water pollutants such as pharmaceutical (PhACs) and microplastics (MPs) are progressively detected in aquatic environments, raising alarms about their mutual toxicological effects on non-target biota, particularly fish. abstract: Rock bolt–grout systems are critical load-transfer components in the subsea tunnel primary support, but its material deterioration and structural damage under aggressive groundwater remain insufficiently understood. In the article, the properties of rock bolt–grout specimens exposed to chloride, sulfate and chloride–sulfate environments were tested. abstract: This essay explores the environmental and spatial afterlives of plantation colonialism in the Seychelles through an ecofeminist auto-theoretical approach. Drawing on family archives and field philosophical research, the author reflects on her position as the granddaughter of a former plantation owner while tracing the material and spatial legacies of the Plantationocene. abstract: Abstract Sri Lankan cuisine is a layered ethnic food heritage shaped by tropical agriculture and by centuries of Arab, Portuguese, Dutch, and British contact atop a South Indian rice-and-curry foundation, and it is increasingly encountered by global audiences not at the destination but on digital platforms. abstract: Niche diplomacy is a notable characteristic of the foreign policy of middle powers - states that have the capacity to play a prominent role on the international stage, but are not powerful enough to impose their will on others. Therefore, middle powers need to rely on their ability to identify and fill in “niche spaces” through diplomatic methods and skills, that is, choosing a few specific issues, institutions or areas to specialize in and orient them as important foundations in its foreign policy. abstract: During embryonic development, cells undergo differentiation into highly specialized cell types. abstract: Abstract Trajectory tracking of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) remains difficult when hydrodynamic coupling, plant uncertainty, actuator constraints, and spatially varying flow disturbances act simultaneously. This study presents a simulation-based evaluation of an ADRC-GISMC strategy for an underactuated ROV under an engineering-oriented compound disturbance model combining background-current and local outfall-plume components. abstract: Oil plays a significant role in the Brazilian and global energy matrices. Brazilian oil production is predominantly offshore, particularly in pre-salt fields. abstract: This study evaluates the ability of accelerated laboratory testing to represent the field performance of four commercial multilayer protective coating systems. abstract: Abstract Seafood supply chains face increasing disruption from climate change, pandemics, and changing market conditions, creating challenges for maintaining both resilience and sustainability. Understanding the perspectives of people working in the industry and supply chain (i.e. stakeholders) are crucial to developing context-specific and practical pathways for supporting continued seafood supply, livelihoods and profitability. abstract: Ship recycling plays a central role in the circular economy of the maritime industry, yet significant disparities persist in safety, environmental performance, and regulatory compliance across global Ship Recycling Facilities (SRFs). This study analyzes 22 official inspection reports conducted by DNV for the European Commission under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation (EU SRR 1257/2013), comparing listed and non-listed facilities. abstract: This study developed and characterized a pectin (PEC) based coating incorporated with green tea spent extract (GTSE) and/or nisin. In response to the strategic transition from a focus on water quality standards to a broader focus on aquatic ecosystem health in the Yangtze River Basin, China implemented a pilot program for aquatic ecosystem monitoring and assessment. title: From supporting roles to leaders: women driving change in Odisha’s fisheries sector
abstract: Women are involved across all parts of the fisheries and aquaculture value chains; however, their access to productive assets, technical skills, capital, markets, and decision-making remains unequal. This study investigates changes in women's participation and enterprise performance among women self-help groups (WSHGs) engaged in fisheries and aquaculture in Balasore District, Odisha, India. abstract: Abstract. Snow algae are psychrophilic and psychrotolerant photosynthetic microorganisms found on every continent, predominantly in polar and alpine environments. Along with contributing to terrestrial carbon cycling and food webs, colourful snow algal blooms formed on snow surfaces can substantially reduce albedo and accelerate snowmelt. abstract: The quantity of water derivable from groundwater could be affected by overexploitation, which also promotes negative impact on the quality. This study investigated groundwater exploitation, treatment methods, and domestic water supply challenges in Yenagoa metropolis, Bayelsa State, Nigeria. abstract: This study analyzed the 2026 United States–Iran War and its impact on global LNG exports, using Qatar as a case study. title: Health Risk Assessment and Heavy Metal Contamination in Canned Tuna Fish from the Libyan Market
abstract: This study investigated the concentrations of selected heavy metals in canned tuna products commercially available in the Libyan market, given the widespread consumption of canned tuna as an affordable source of protein and the potential health risks associated with the bioaccumulation of chemical contaminants in fish tissues. We randomly obtained eight canned tuna samples from different brands and production batches from supermarkets and local markets in Tripoli, Libya. title: Integrated adaptations of muscle structure and mitochondrial function to locomotion demands in teleost fishes
abstract: Abstract Teleost fishes display diverse swimming modes supported by functional specialization of skeletal muscle. However, the ultrastructural adaptations and molecular mechanisms regulating mitochondrial homeostasis in relation to divergent locomotion remain unclear. We compared muscle fiber composition, mitochondrial ultrastructure, and regulatory pathways in two teleosts with contrasting swimming strategies: the sustained swimmer Pseudocaranx dentex and the burst swimmer Paralichthys olivaceus. title: Sexual dimorphism shapes the plasma metabolome of the endangered Iberian lynx
abstract: Sexual dimorphism is a key but still incompletely resolved determinant of mammalian systemic metabolism, particularly in endangered species where physiological organization remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrate untargeted plasma metabolomics to dissect hierarchical determinants of systemic metabolic organization in the Iberian lynx ( Lynx pardinus ), one of the world’s most endangered felids. title: Assessing the Socioeconomic Challenges Affecting Economic Development in Puntland
abstract: Puntland, a self-governing federal member state in north-eastern Somalia, occupies a distinctive position within one of the world's most fragile economies. Since declaring autonomy in 1998, Puntland has built functioning public institutions, a working seaport at Bosaso, and a livestock-led export economy, even as it has remained exposed to drought, clan-based insecurity, weak public revenue, and limited access to international finance. title: Evaluating the Courier and Delivery Services Company's Efficiency Using an EBM Model
abstract: The market for courier and delivery services is changing favorably as a result of the most recent and continuous technical developments in logistics. Thanks to real–time monitoring technology, which provides transparency and peace of mind, customers can now effortlessly keep a watch on their deliveries at every stage. This study aims to assess the efficiency of nine significant delivery and courier services. title: Microplastics at the ‘roof of the Americas’: widespread presence in snow on Mount Aconcagua, Central Andes, Argentina
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution has emerged as a pervasive contaminant in remote environments; however, its occurrence in high-altitude snow remains poorly constrained. Here, we provide baseline evidence of MP contamination in snow from four mountaineering camps on Mount Aconcagua (6,962 masl), the highest peak in the Americas and in the entire Western and Southern Hemispheres. Microplastics were identified using µFTIR-ATR spectroscopy. title: 16S rRNA amplicon profiling of Salvadora persica -associated rhizosphere bacterial communities under saline agricultural conditions
abstract: Salvadora persica (Arak) is a facultative halophyte adapted to arid and saline environments, yet its rhizosphere microbiome remains poorly characterised. We profiled bacterial communities associated with S. persica at Arak Farm, Rabigh, Saudi Arabia, using Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V3–V4 16S rRNA region and ASV-based analysis. Three rhizosphere composites and one adjacent bulk-soil composite were analysed. title: Beneficiation and metallurgical challenges of ilmenite-bearing heavy mineral sands: A comprehensive review
abstract: Ilmenite-bearing heavy mineral sand deposits constitute a primary source of titanium feedstock for pigment and metal production. Deposit evaluation and mineral processing flowsheet development are commonly based on total heavy mineral content and bulk titanium dioxide grade, parameters that do not capture the constraints imposed on downstream metallurgical processing. This review examines the physical beneficiation of ilmenite-bearing heavy mineral sands. abstract: ABSTRACT Global warming and environmental pollutants represent escalating threats to crustaceans, with serious implications for aquaculture sustainability and ecosystem stability. This review synthesises and advances current understanding by integrating physiological, biochemical, and molecular evidence on the effects of elevated temperature and diverse contaminants—including endocrine‐disrupting chemicals (EDCs), heavy metals (HMs), nanoparticles (NPs), pesticides, and microplastics—on crustacean reproduction and immunity. title: Bacteriological Quality and Physicochemical Properties of Drinking Water Sources in Slums of Lagos State, Southwest, Nigeria
abstract: Water is very essential and widely used by humans, animals and for the success of agricultural products. The inhabitants resort to use of borehole, sachet and bottle water for drinking and domestic use. There is paucity of information on bacterial contamination and phytochemical properties of drinking water sources in major slums of Lagos city. Such contaminants may be the cause of frequent febrile illnesses experienced amongst the inhabitants of these slums. abstract: This study aimed to identify Salmonella spp. and Escherichia coli contamination associated with foodborne diseases in fishery commodities from Bali, Indonesia. A total of 216 samples representing commercially important fish and shrimp species were collected from suppliers, fish processing units, micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), traditional markets, and modern markets across regencies in Bali. title: Mapping the Biodiversity, Climate, and Health Nexus: an Analysis of Horizon Europe research projects
abstract: Addressing the interconnected challenges of climate change, biodiversity loss, and human health requires a shift from fragmented governance toward integrated actions. This study applies an analytical framework combining Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modelling and network analysis to systematically map the Biodiversity, Climate, and Health (BCH) nexus within the Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe research portfolios. title: High diversity but limited expression of biosynthetic gene clusters in a peatland microbial community
abstract: The in situ relevance of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remains poorly understood. We apply meta-omics to characterize BGC diversity and activity along a peatland redox gradient. From seven metagenomes, we recover 9,694 BGCs, spanning diverse taxa, most lacking close relatives in reference databases, indicating extensive novelty. title: Multi-method non-parametric assessment of river water-quality trends and change-points in the Danshui River basin, metropolitan Taipei (2010–2026)
abstract: The Danshui River drains metropolitan Taipei, where two decades of expanding sewer connection and riparian constructed wetlands have targeted river pollution. title: Asynchronous Changes in Tempo‐Spatial Patterns of the Younger Dryas Hydroclimate in Northeastern China
abstract: Abstract The Younger Dryas (YD, 12,900–11,700 years before present) event offers a key opportunity to investigate climate system responses to abrupt perturbations, yet regional hydroclimate responses in northeastern China remain debated. Here we reconstruct the spatial fingerprint of YD hydroclimate variability using a comprehensive fossil pollen data set. Our results show regionally coherent cooling but strong spatial heterogeneity in precipitation. At YD onset, northern regions became drier, whereas southern areas experienced slight wetting. title: Fabrication and in vitro toxicity assessment of PET microplastic fibers with diameter and aspect ratio control
abstract: Microplastics (MP) are widespread anthropogenic pollutants present in the air we breathe, the food we eat and the water we drink. Their presence has been reported in almost all ecosystems and several human organs and tissues. Despite their pervasiveness, our knowledge regarding their effects remains in its infancy. Current understanding is largely limited to the assessment of a few specific particle types, even though MP exist in a variety of shapes, sizes, and materials. title: Overtime Drivers and Work–Rest Compliance among Indonesian Deck Seafarers: Implications for Maritime Traffic Safety
abstract: Work-rest compliance is an important component of maritime safety because deck seafarers are responsible for watchkeeping, lookout, vessel traffic monitoring, bridge communication, and navigational decision-making. Although international regulations emphasize adequate rest to reduce fatigue risk, overtime may still occur due to operational, technical, administrative, and regulatory demands. This study examines overtime drivers and work-rest compliance among Indonesian deck seafarers and discusses their implications for maritime traffic safety. title: Evolutionary game analysis of scientific research data sharing under the open science context
abstract: Scientific data sharing is central to open science, yet its development is constrained by fragmented data resources, heterogeneous stakeholder incentives, privacy risks, and limited regulatory capacity. This study develops a bounded-rationality, four-population evolutionary game framework involving data providers, data users, government agencies, and sharing platforms. title: Water retention strategies for drought-prone aquaculture ponds: Technologies, effectiveness, challenges, and future prospects
abstract: Water scarcity threatens earthen pond aquaculture's viability and profitability. Drought, variable rainfall, rising air and water temperatures, decreased groundwater availability, and inadequate pond soils deplete stored water through evaporation, seepage, and operating losses. This review synthesises drought-prone pond water retention solutions from engineering, hydrological, aquaculture, and climate-adaptation literature. title: Heavy Metal Contamination in Macrobrachium rosenbergii From the Khulna Division of Bangladesh: A Human Health Risk Assessment
abstract: This study aimed to determine the concentrations of heavy metals (As, Cr, Cd, Pb, and Hg) in Macrobrachium rosenbergii from prawn farms in Khulna division, Bangladesh, and to assess the associated human health risks. Twenty-four farms in different upazilas of Khulna division were selected for sampling, and heavy metal concentrations in prawns were determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). abstract: Abstract. Mount Qomolangma (MQ) serves as a natural laboratory for investigating aerosol–cloud–precipitation interactions over the Tibetan Plateau (TP). title: A harmonized dataset for dams and reservoirs in West Africa
abstract: Abstract. Most existing datasets that could support dam and reservoir management and assessments of their impacts in West Africa are limited by inaccurate georeferencing, inconsistent accessibility, heterogeneous data records, and a lack of validation against field observations. In this study, we review and assess existing datasets containing information on dams and reservoirs in West Africa and subsequently integrate them into a harmonized and consolidated regional dataset. abstract: Bioactive peptides (BPs), despite their multiple biological and nutritional effects, suffer from low bioavailability, instability, and high reactivity. Therefore, in this study, stabilization and preservation of the biological activities of poppy pollen peptides (PPPs) within coated Nanochitosomes (NCs) with different concentrations (0.1–0.5% w/v) of chitosan were evaluated. title: Injection-based microbially induced carbonate precipitation: soil improvement and restructuring of native microbial communities
abstract: Abstract Purpose Microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) is increasingly applied as an environmentally oriented soil-improvement technique; however, its ecological effects on native soil microbial communities remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated injection-based MICP for soil improvement and the associated restructuring of soil microbial communities. abstract: Maritime transport is subject to increasingly strict emission regulation. Ships operating in European waters must comply with the International Maritime Organization’s Carbon Intensity Indicator, the European Union Emissions Trading System, and the FuelEU Maritime regulation, raising regulatory and financial pressure on the existing fleet. To stay compliant, shipowners can adopt conventional energy-saving technologies, such as hull and propeller upgrades.
