title: New radiocarbon determinations for the late Pleistocene site of Badanj (Bosnia and Herzegovina): Implications for the Upper Palaeolithic sequence of the Adriatic basin
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the results of a new radiocarbon dating program for the Upper Palaeolithic site of Badanj, Bosnia and Herzegovina. After putting together older dates originating from the 1970s and 1980s with recent ones acquired as part of new fieldwork, we then combine the available radiocarbon record with the present understanding of the stratigraphy to create two alternative Bayesian models. title: Constitutive Behavior and Tangent Modulus Evaluation of Polyamide Multifilaments Under Post-Impact Conditions
abstract: This study investigates the constitutive behavior and tangent modulus of polyamide multifilaments in post-impact rupture. Polyamide is widely used in applications such as offshore mooring systems due to its excellent mechanical properties. However, its performance under dynamic conditions, especially after impact events, has not been extensively studied. title: Breeding on a Tropical Island Proves More Difficult Than Expected: The Ongoing Breeding Failure of Laysan Albatross on Clarion Island
abstract: ABSTRACT In the 1980s, the Laysan Albatross ( Phoebastria immutabilis ) expanded its breeding range into the eastern Pacific and established colonies on several islands off the coast of Mexico. Colony growth has varied widely among these islands, likely reflecting differences in immigration rates and local conditions, such as food availability and predation risk, which can influence breeding success and population dynamics. title: Bioaccessibility and health risk evaluation of heavy metals in commercial fruit juices of Pakistan using an in vitro simulated digestion model
abstract: In recent years, fruit juice consumption has increased worldwide due to its potential health benefits. However, there is concern regarding heavy metals (HMs) in commercial fruit juices, posing significant health risks to their consumers. The current research was carried out to assess the concentrations of HMs in commercially available packaged fruit juices in Pakistan and evaluate their potential health risks through an in vitro digestion model. title: Niche differentiation and functional complementarity between rare and abundant taxa sustain grassland soil bacterial diversity
abstract: Soil bacterial communities are central to grassland ecosystem functioning, yet how abundant and rare bacteria taxa differ in ecological strategies, community formation, and environmental responses remains unclear. Here we show, using 278 soil samples from grasslands across China, that these groups have contrasting but complementary ecological roles. Abundant taxa are mainly adapted to nutrient-poor conditions, tolerate a wider range of environments, and are shaped largely by random ecological processes. abstract: Using novel technology and dedicated algorithms, the FLuorescence EXplorer (FLEX) will yield information about the health of the world’s plants. The information gathered will be used to improve our understanding of how carbon moves between plants and the atmosphere and how photosynthesis affects the carbon and water cycles. The FLEX mission offers two high-level products for exploitation by end-users: the Level-1C (L1C) and Level-2 (L2). abstract: Soil biodiversity represents approximately 60% of all described species on Earth and plays a critical role in terrestrial ecosystem functioning. However, knowledge of tropical soil biota and their roles remains highly fragmentary, especially in hyperdiverse tropical regions that remain largely undersampled relative to their temperate counterparts. Recent non-invasive methods, such as environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, have enabled large-scale data collection across kingdoms of life and habitats, including understudied compartments such as soils. abstract: Spatial variation in the magnitude and pace of climate change impacts means some species will be more affected than others. This includes those occurring within global biodiversity hotspots, regions with exceptional concentrations of endemic species that have often been shaped by long-term climatic stability. title: High-resolution mangrove mapping in Guatemala using PlanetScope imagery and a SWIR-free moisture index
abstract: Mangrove forests are ecologically and socioeconomically important ecosystems that require accurate and timely monitoring. This study presents a high-resolution mangrove mapping approach along the Pacific coast of Guatemala using PlanetScope imagery integrated with a machine-learning framework. Sentinel-2 and Landsat data were used to derive the Modular Mangrove Recognition Index (MMRI), which depends on shortwave infrared (SWIR) bands. abstract: Remote ecosystems are often assumed to be insulated from chemical contamination; however, increasing human visitation may compromise this perception. We evaluated the occurrence, spatial distribution, and ecological implications of pharmaceutical active compounds (PhACs) in soils from the summit of Roraima-tepui, a high-elevation "sky island" in the Guiana Shield subjected to unregulated tourism and lacking sanitation infrastructure. title: Assessing the impact of climate change on wind energy potential in Brazil’s capitals: a long-term Weibull parameter analysis (1960–2020)
abstract: Abstract Brazil’s vast territory and favorable wind conditions have positioned it as a global leader in wind energy development. Accurate assessment of wind resources is essential for the feasibility of wind farms, particularly in the context of climate change. This study analyzes wind speed data from 27 Brazilian capitals (1960–2020) obtained from the CRUA database, using the two-parameter Weibull distribution to estimate the shape ( k ) and scale ( c ) parameters. abstract: Information about woody plant density and canopy cover is central to our definition of terrestrial ecosystem types and crucial for understanding ecosystem state, dynamics, biogeochemical processes, and biodiversity. The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) LiDAR on the International Space Station (ISS) samples 3-D structural information on woody vegetation structure, including an estimate of canopy cover in each 25 m diameter footprint. title: Assessment of Bacteriological and Physicochemical Quality of Drinking Water from Source to Household Storage in Dabat Town, Northwest Ethiopia
abstract: Microbial contamination of drinking water remains a major public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, particularly where water quality deteriorates between treatment and household consumption. This study assessed the bacteriological and physicochemical quality of drinking water along the supply chain and evaluated household water handling practices in Dabat Town, northwest Ethiopia. abstract: This study maps the global literature on drinking-water utility financing to examine the position of government capital participation (PMP), the instrument through which Indonesian regional governments inject equity into municipal water companies (PDAM). title: Fuel Heating for Reduce Emission of Diesel Engine
abstract: Diesel engines offer the highest efficiency compared to other internal combustion engines, and are therefore widely used in industry and transport. However, exhaust emissions from the combustion of diesel fuel pose a threat to the environment and human health. As a preventive measure, research has been conducted with the aim of modifying the fuel system or combustion system to reduce exhaust emissions. abstract: This research assessed the monitoring and evaluation (M&E) practices of the Brigada Eskwela Program across select public elementary schools in the District of Santa Fe, Division of Cebu Province, during School Year 2025–2026 to establish an empirical basis for program enhancement. title: Commercial Ambition and State Power of the British East India Company: The Rise of the "Company-State"
abstract: The British East India Company presents a typical case of the fusion between commercial expansion and state power in the history of the British Empire. The Company was initially established to secure a commercial monopoly, but its objectives were gradually converted to the de facto domination of South Asia. This paper examines the principal stages and mechanisms through which the EIC was transformed from a commercial enterprise into a "Company-State." abstract: The use of fish Liver as a histological bioindicators is an important environmental biomonitoring tool. abstract: The issue of water scarcity has become increasingly severe, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions like those in the Arab world, where water resources are limited. abstract: Neurodevelopmental impairments like cerebral palsy are prevalent infant developmental problems in clinical infant healthcare. Automated, large-scale screening tools remain scarce, and artificial intelligence offers a promising solution by identifying abnormal infant motion patterns. abstract: Automatic Identification System (AIS) data provide a large-scale record of maritime vessel movements, yet learning reusable port representations from these routes remains underexplored. This paper investigates whether unsupervised graph representation learning can produce meaningful and operationally useful embeddings for ports in a global maritime port network. abstract: Abstract Dendrocephalus brasiliensis Pesta, 1921 is an anostracan characteristic of temporary aquatic environments whose persistence depends on the viability of dormant cysts accumulated in the sediment. abstract: Expansive soils, characterised by significant volume instability due to seasonal moisture fluctuations, pose substantial risks to civil engineering infrastructure. abstract: Notopterygium incisum is not only a traditional Chinese medicine but also an endemic herb. Artificial domestication and large-scale cultivation are crucial for resolving the crisis of wild resources and the supply-demand imbalance of N. incisum, yet current techniques have failed to stably provide the herb medicine in good quality. abstract: Abstract Streams process and transport vast carbon quantities along the aquatic continuum. title: Defending synthetic DNA orders against intra-order splitting-based obfuscation
abstract: Biosecurity screening of synthetic DNA orders is a key defense against malicious actors and careless enthusiasts producing dangerous pathogens or toxins. It is important to evaluate biosecurity screening tools for potential vulnerabilities and to work responsibly with providers to ensure that vulnerabilities can be patched before being publicly disclosed. title: Future of edge AI in biodiversity monitoring
abstract: Abstract Many ecological decisions are slowed by the gap between collecting and analysing biodiversity information. Edge computing moves data processing closer to the sensor, with edge artificial intelligence (AI) using AI models for data processing and selective data transfer. edge AI extends the scope of biodiversity monitoring by complementing retrospective ecological analysis with real‐time sensing, enabling responsive and adaptive decision‐making. However, the adoption of edge AI systems in ecological research remains fragmented because deploying efficient and reliable systems is complex.

abstract: Urban impervious surfaces are major accumulation zones for microplastics, with deposited urban dust as a key carrier matrix facilitating their retention, redistribution, and transport from terrestrial to aquatic environments. However, processes governing microplastic build-up and the ability to predict its spatial distribution remain poorly understood. title: Localization in the internet of things based on game theory with applications in the healthcare
abstract: Accurate indoor localization is critical for healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) applications such as patient tracking and asset management. However, maintaining localization accuracy under node mobility, signal attenuation, and faulty or adversarial behaviors remains challenging. Existing schemes either assume benign environments or employ rigid filters that permanently exclude noisy nodes, causing unacceptable losses in patient monitoring coverage. title: MycorrhizaTracer: A bioinformatic pipeline for fungi and plant classification of Sanger DNA sequences
abstract: Processing Sanger DNA sequences remains a routine, yet technically demanding step in many biodiversity and ecological studies, particularly when barcoding large numbers of environmental samples. Manual inspection and editing of trace files, DNA sequence alignment and classification using taxonomic reference databases are time-consuming, inconsistent and prone to error, compromising workflow standardisation, traceability and reproducibility. title: Computational intelligence approaches for seismic data analysis: a comprehensive analysis of detection and prediction methods
abstract: The global imperative for early earthquake prediction is indisputable. As computational capabilities continually evolve alongside technological advancements, a profound opportunity emerges for researchers to confront the intricate challenges inherent in detecting and predicting precursory signals associated with earthquakes by developing innovative models using integrating statistical methods with emerging technologies. title: The investor gaze: recognition heuristic, social liability and legal disillusionment among foreign tourism entrepreneurs on Sri Lanka's southern coast
abstract: This study examines investment failures among foreign visitors and tourism entrepreneurs on Sri Lanka’s southern coast, exploring what can go wrong after tourism-related familiarity encourages investment. It introduces the “investor gaze” as the epistemic position emerging when tourists become resident investors, distinguishing it from familiarity-based confidence and “substitutional collapse,” a specific failure mechanism. journal: Journal of Business and Tourism Management (JBTM)

title: Engineering PET surface colonization with a synthetic bacterial consortium
abstract: Introduction Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a widely used synthetic polymer that persists in the environment because of its resistance to biological degradation. Although engineered PET hydrolases have shown improved catalytic performance, translating these advances into effective whole-cell degradation remains challenging because cells and enzymes must interact with an insoluble polymer surface. title: Field-SCADA measurement analysis of power-curve deviation and sector-dependent underperformance in an operating utility-scale wind turbine
abstract: Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) data can support transparent power-curve screening, but residual calculation, sector aggregation and wind-speed-bin median fitting are established tools rather than algorithmic innovations. This study analyzes 50,530 ten-minute records from a public 2018 single-turbine dataset containing active power, wind speed, wind direction and a source-supplied theoretical reference. title: Venice in the Jungle: An Archetype of the Urban Amazon
abstract: Résumé Partout en Amazonie, on trouve des villes et des zones urbaines comparées à Venise. Cet essai explore les origines de cette comparaison évocatrice, en se concentrant sur la ville brésilienne de Manaus pendant le boom du caoutchouc de la fin du xix e et du début du xx e siècle. En s’appuyant sur l’analyse des systèmes mondiaux et de l’écologie mondiale, il soutient que l’archétype de la « Venise de la jungle » peut mettre en lumière des schémas, mais aussi des divergences et des changements, dans les modes d’organisation de la nature à travers les espaces géographiques et au fil du temps

title: A comparison of consumer preferences for cell-based seafood across European countries
abstract: Global seafood consumption has been increasing and is expected to continue rising, driven by population growth and evolving dietary patterns. Cell-based seafood has the potential to complement capture fisheries and aquaculture in meeting this growing demand. However, the long-term viability of this emerging sector will depend largely on consumer acceptance. This study examines consumer preferences and acceptance of cell-based seafood in four European countries—Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Hungary. Using data from a stated preference experiment, we assess willingness to purchase cell-b

title: Technical–ethical–governance circuit–breaker framework for safe and sustainable AI governance
abstract: The growing use of large language models and autonomous AI systems in high-risk settings has created safety risks that cannot be addressed through technical safeguards alone. Existing approaches often treat technical failure control, ethical oversight, and institutional governance as separate domains, making coordinated intervention difficult when risks escalate across these boundaries. This study proposes the technical–ethical–governance (TEG) framework as an integrated circuit-breaker architecture for managing risks in high-risk AI systems. title: Not So Stories
abstract: Three short autobiographical stories introduce a host of characters (human and beyond), places, and objects that bridge worlds – worlds of fact and fiction, past and present, Africa and Europe. The three autobiographical reflections, How the Outside Got In, Of Migrants and Music, and New Transvaal Stories, serve as points of departure for diffractive engagements with relational ontologies, histories, and cultures. title: Crude Oil Theft and Environmental Degradation in Oil-Producing Communities of Rivers State, Nigeria: Evidence from Bodo And Rumuekpe
abstract: This study examines crude oil theft as a direct driver of environmental degradation in Bodo (Gokana LGA) and Rumuekpe (Emuoha LGA), two oil-producing communities in Rivers State, Nigeria, using a descriptive survey design anchored on Strain Theory, Resource Curse Theory, and Environmental Justice Theory. Two communities were purposively selected for their contrasting exposure profiles; within them, 200 respondents were drawn through stratified random sampling across six occupational categories. title: Sulfur Dioxide Point Sources Remain Important for Daytime Plume‐Scale New Particle Formation in the United States: Case Study for Gary, Indiana During the Summer 2023 AEROMMA Aircraft Campaign
abstract: Abstract Plumes from sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) point sources have been shown to be significant contributors to new particle formation (NPF), but SO 2 emissions in the United States (US) have decreased drastically by ∼10× since the early 2000s. We present observations of plume‐scale NPF from SO 2 point sources over the industrial hub in Gary, Indiana and assess the importance of SO 2 plumes to NPF using the P6 subgrid NPF parameterization and model the subsequent aerosol growth using the Statistical Oxidation Model‐TwO Moment Aerosol Sectional (SOM‐TOMAS) kinetic gas/aerosol model. title: Evaluation of Water Quality from Atmospheric Water Generators Deployed Across Multiple Indian Cities: A Comparative Study
abstract: Atmospheric Water Generators (AWGs) represent an emerging decentralized water solution that extracts moisture from ambient air to produce potable water without reliance on conventional freshwater sources. This study evaluates AWG-produced water quality at three Indian deployment sites — Pune (October 2025), Sringeri (November 2025), and Chennai (October 2025) — against IS 14543:2024, the Indian Standard for packaged drinking water, and benchmarks results against the WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality. title: Beyond cichlid diversification: environmental drivers of biodiversity across the Nicaraguan lake system
abstract: Abstract The Nicaraguan lake system, comprising two Great Lakes and several isolated crater lakes, is a natural laboratory for investigating how environmental heterogeneity and isolation shape biodiversity and a classic model for Midas cichlid diversification. We asked whether lake characteristics associated with cichlid diversification are also linked to prokaryotic and eukaryotic diversity patterns. title: Locking Down Science Gateways with Landlock and Seccomp
abstract: Abstract The most recent Linux kernels have a new feature for securing applications: Landlock. Like Seccomp before it, Landlock makes it possible for a running process to selectively relinquish access to certain system resources including network and filesystem access. Rather than being a proper successor to Seccomp, Landlock has different and somewhat complementary capabilities. title: SIRT2-mediated deacetylation of ANT3 at Lys96 promotes cell death
abstract: Abstract ANT3 is a key molecule that constitutes the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) and mediates cell death. Disruption or conformational changes in ANT3 protein homeostasis can trigger cell death. However, the molecular mechanism of ANT3 protein homeostasis regulation remains unclear. We found that prolonged starvation induces cell death by mediating ANT3 deacetylation-dependent pathways through the mitochondrial translocation of SIRT2, which in turn regulates ANT3 protein levels and conformational changes. title: Pathways to care in pinyon–juniper woodlands: Insights from Indigenous‐led monitoring and a public survey
abstract: Abstract Conservation decisions often require navigating tensions among ecological, cultural, economic and social priorities. While debates frequently centre on single‐species outcomes, less is known about how care for landscapes may contribute to co‐stewardship. Pinyon–juniper woodlands of California's Eastern Sierra Nevada provide a compelling case study. These culturally significant, climate‐stressed ecosystems are cared for by Tribes of the Eastern Sierra and Great Basin and managed by federal agencies, requiring coordination across knowledge systems and institutional mandates. title: Maintenance of bone health by osteoblasts in the absence of osteocytes: comparative analysis of gene expression in medaka and zebrafish vertebrae
abstract: Osteocytes are regarded as the strain-sensing bone cells; their capacity to sense and convert mechanical loads into biological signals underpins our current understanding of how bone is (re)modelled to normalise local strains. However, most extant fish are anosteocytic and lack osteocytes, yet their bone structure and (re)modelling abilities remain unimpeded, sitting uncomfortably with this paradigm. title: A validation framework for translating ethnomicrobiology into microbiome-enabled desert restoration
abstract: Microbiome-based dryland restoration is promising but weakly validated. We develop ethnomicrobiology, the study of how human communities manage microbial processes, as a discovery-and-validation framework. A structured evidence map of 42 systems shows food fermentation is most mature, whereas restoration practices lag. We propose a five-level evidence-maturity ladder, from traditional observation to governed field deployment, and apply it to waste-biomass valorization, converting traditional practices into mechanistically tested, ethically governed restoration interventions.

title: Recommendations for microbiological sampling in infected hard-to-heal wounds: an Italian association for cutaneous ulcers (AIUC) perspective
abstract: Chronic and hard-to-heal wounds represent a significant and growing healthcare burden, frequently complicated by infection and impaired healing. Despite the availability of international guidelines, microbiological assessment in clinical practice remains highly heterogeneous, with substantial variability in sampling techniques, timing, and interpretation of results. This variability occurs within a broader One Health context, where antimicrobial resistance and microbial ecology are shaped by interconnected human, environmental, and healthcare factors. abstract: This study asks whether an older, more granular epistemic resource within classical fiqh — the doctrine of ṭahārah–najāsah (ritual purity and impurity), with its finely graded taxonomy of contamination (najis mukhaffafah, mutawassiṭah, and mughallaẓah) — has likewise been mobilised. title: Analysis of Vessel Clearance in and Clearance Out Procedures at PT Eleanor Pradana Shipping
abstract: This study aims to analyze the procedures for ship clearance in and clearance out services at PT Eleanor Pradana Shipping, identify operational bottlenecks, and evaluate strategic efforts to optimize service efficiency. A descriptive qualitative method was employed, utilizing primary data gathered through field observation, semi-structured in-depth interviews with key personnel on General Manager, Head of Operations, and Operational Staff, and administrative documentation. title: ORGANIC-TAINTED MINERAL SOILS PART II: NEUTRALISATION-FIRST STABILISATION FROM LABORATORY TO FIELD
abstract: Organic-tainted mineral soils remain predominantly mineral and physically compactable, yet reactive organic matter can interfere with conventional lime- and cement-based treatment. Building on the mechanistic framework established in Part I, this companion paper translates neutralisation demand into a laboratory-to-field validation procedure. title: Marginalized Yet Enduring: Anglo-Indian Histories in Colonial and Post-Colonial Odisha
abstract: This article examines the overlooked history and present-day invisibility of the Anglo-Indian community in Odisha by spotlighting Dr. Josiah Dashwood Gillies and Captain Eric Tucker. Gillies, a colonial-era doctor, faced institutional prejudice that limited his professional recognition. Tucker, celebrated as a military hero after independence and Odisha’s first Ashok Chakra awardee, remains mostly unrecognized in regional history. abstract: High-resolution soil moisture (SM) information is essential for hydrological, agricultural and climate studies. This paper presents an NDMI–NDVI–LST-based downscaling technique, termed the NNL-SM model, to downscale SMAP SM from 9 to 1 km resolution. The model was validated in Varanasi, India, using ground SM measurements collected on fifteen dates and compared with the VMSMI and triangle optical-based models. title: Innovation in health tourism: a service innovation perspective and research agenda
abstract: Health tourism (HT) is an umbrella domain encompassing medical tourism and wellness tourism. While these subdomains have developed substantial research, service models increasingly connect hospitals, clinics, hotels, resorts, and wellness providers, creating overlaps between healthcare, hospitality, and travel. This study uses innovation to connect these subdomains and explain the development of HT and identify future directions. title: Spatial and Ecological Drivers of Diversification in the World's Southernmost Gecko
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the mechanisms driving genetic differentiation—and ultimately, speciation—is central to evolutionary biology, particularly in widespread species inhabiting environmentally complex landscapes. Homonota darwinii , a member of the H. whitii group, is the southernmost gecko in the world, distributed across the Patagonian Steppe—a vast, heterogeneous landscape with a complex geoclimatic history. title: A novel multivariate vine-copula–based drought index with application to high-elevation catchments
abstract: Abstract Drought is a complex, slowly evolving hazard governed by multiple interacting hydro-climatic factors, making it difficult to monitor, characterize, and predict. Conventional single-variable indices fail to capture the nonlinear, asymmetric dependence between precipitation and temperature—a limitation that is particularly critical in data-scarce, high-mountain catchments, where incomplete drought characterization undermines the reliability of early-warning systems. title: Identification of rainfall-activated multi-indicator pollution pulses and lagged responses in Erhai Lake based on continuous water quality monitoring
abstract: Rainfall runoff can activate non-point source pollution and generate short-term water-quality anomalies in plateau lake basins, but event-scale multi-indicator responses remain difficult to identify using conventional mean-based assessments. Here, water-quality records available between June 2021 and December 2024 from the Lake Center, Jiangwei, Xiaoguanyi, and Jinhe monitoring sections of Erhai Lake were combined with daily precipitation data to identify 127 rainfall events. title: Combination of instrumental and biomonitoring approaches elucidate the contributions of multiple and contrasted sources of atmospheric exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons
abstract: A combined approach was implemented to investigate the origins of elevated PAH concentrations in a complex urban environment where numerous emission sources coexist. This approach integrated one year of atmospheric measurements PM10 filters and continuous atmospheric monitoring), alongside lichen biomonitoring and soil analyses. title: Flow Tree: a model for navigator dynamics and environmental complexity
abstract: Navigation is a dynamic process, involving learning new environments and manoeuvring through them. Individuals differ widely in their abilities and strategies. Prior research often uses static measures, such as total distance travelled or location tallies, which overlook the variability and asymmetry in how trajectories unfold. title: SYSTEM FOR LAND-BASED EMISSIONS ESTIMATION IN KENYA(SLEEK) AND LAND-SECTOR CARBON ACCOUNTING IN KENYA: EVIDENCE FROM EMISSIONS AND REMOVALS ACCOUNTING, 1990-2015
abstract: Developing countries face persistent constraints in producing transparent, consistent and nationally owned greenhouse-gas inventories for the land sector. Kenya responded through the System for Land-based Emissions Estimation in Kenya (SLEEK), a national programme designed to integrate activity data, country-specific parameters, spatial modelling, reporting tools and institutional capacity. title: Two decades-long NDVI anomalies to understand Mediterranean forests ecosystem shifts
abstract: Abstract Mediterranean forest ecosystems are increasingly exposed to climate change, land-use transformations and altered disturbance regimes. Understanding vegetation shifts across these complex landscapes requires scalable, high-resolution tools. In this study, we analyzed a 24-year NDVI time series (2000–2023) from Landsat imagery over the Gargano National Park (Southern Italy) to identify anomalous vegetation dynamics and assess their potential drivers. title: IOT-driven multimodal deep visual analytics for air pollution forecasting in firework industrial regions
abstract: Abstract The increasing atmospheric burden associated with firework manufacturing requires intelligent environmental monitoring frameworks capable of integrating heterogeneous pollution indicators. This study presents an IoT-driven multimodal surveillance architecture designed for industrial air quality assessment in Sivakasi. The framework integrates environmental sensors with camera-based visual analytics to improve Air Quality Index forecasting under dynamic industrial conditions. title: A first, provisional, annotated checklist of the microlepidoptera of Albania (Insecta: Lepidoptera)
abstract: All available published data on the microlepidoptera fauna of Albania are collated and combined with the results of modern sampling to form the first known checklist of Albanian microlepidoptera. Published data are minimal as a consequence of the political history of the country; these historic reports are supplemented by active sampling during the present millennium. abstract: To explore the effects of compound microbial fertilizer (containing Lactobacillus acidophilus and Corynebacterium glutamicum ) combined with potassium fulvic acid on cotton growth and soil ecology in Xinjiang saline-alkali soil, a two-year field experiment with seven treatments was conducted in a randomized block design. title: Spatiotemporal wildfire occurrence, burn severity and early post-fire vegetation recovery in a tropical Andean landscape: Quilanga, southern Ecuador
abstract: Wildfires are recurrent environmental hazards in tropical Andean landscapes, where limited spatial records can constrain prevention, impact assessment, and post-fire management. This study presents an integrated assessment to characterize wildfire occurrence, burn severity, and early vegetation-greenness recovery in Quilanga, southern Ecuador. Official wildfire records from 2010-2025 were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Mann-Kendall tests, Sen’s slopes, and multiscale kernel density estimation. abstract: General Background Floating power station construction requires highly structured manufacturing workflows to deliver clean energy infrastructure reliably. Specific Background Barge Mounted Power Plant (BMPP) fabrication in shipyards operates under job shop environments with complex assembly sequences and extended production cycles. abstract: This research is based on forecasting the net demand for electricity by considering the previous trends. Considering the overall increase in demand for electricity year by year, predicting such a trend plays a crucial role in a country’s development, as it helps make an accurate prediction of future energy consumption and prepare accordingly. title: The Role of Simulation Technology in Enhancing Port Crane Operator Competence and Safety
abstract: Global maritime trade increasingly depends on efficient and safe port operations, where crane operators play a vital role in container handling. Although traditional training methods are effective, they require considerable time and may involve operational risks. Simulation-based training offers a risk-free, cost-effective, and performance-oriented alternative. This study evaluated the effectiveness of simulator training for ship-to-shore (STS) and rubber-tyred gantry (RTG) crane operators by examining error types, training periods, and changes in operator performance. title: Documented service-chain maturity and policy coordination capacity in climate services for tourism: A scoping review
abstract: Climate services for tourism (CST) face challenges in implementation and long-term continuity because policy coordination and governance mechanisms remain poorly documented. This study assessed whether the CST evidence base reflects a transition from climate-information products to mature service chains supported by policy coordination arrangements. We conducted a scoping review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). title: Simplifying Macroinvertebrate Biodiversity Assessment: A Standardised Metabarcoding Method for Invertebrate Samples With High Volumes of Debris
abstract: DNA metabarcoding of freshwater macroinvertebrate samples can provide rapid and accurate identification of species diversity. Processing samples where macroinvertebrates are not separated from net contents can substantially reduce time and cost. We devised and tested a standardised method for processing combined kick/sweep samples using DNA metabarcoding to provide accurate estimates of macroinvertebrate species diversity. title: Development Strategy for Snakehead Fish (Channa striata) Albumin Agroindustry in South Kalimantan: SWOT Analysis and IE Matrix
abstract: Snakehead fish albumin is a product based on South Kalimantan fishery resources that has the potential to be developed as a value-added agro-industrial product, but its development still faces various strategic obstacles. This study aims to formulate a strategy for developing snakehead fish albumin through an analysis of internal and external factors using the SWOT approach combined with the IFAS, EFAS, and IE matrices. abstract: Large dam vibrations will be assessed by using a sensor network as part of the proposed protocol. The other main components of the proposed protocol are dual-threshold selective reporting and structurally-based clustering methods which provide for nodes to report only vibration readings that have deviated from what is normal operationally; all vibration readings need not be reported. abstract: This study investigates the effect of incorporating 20 wt% ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS), ground waste bottle glass (GWBG) and metakaolin (MK) on the hydration behavior, mechanical and environmental performance of blended cements cured at 23 °C ± 2 °C for 7, 28, and 90 days. abstract: The growing demand for self-powered systems in distributed sensing, Internet-of-Things devices, and structural health monitoring has stimulated increasing interest in flow-induced piezoelectric energy harvesting. abstract: This research investigated the multi-sectoral readiness of Barcelona, Sorsogon, to implement the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) Smart and Sustainable Communities Program (SSCP). title: Techno-economic optimization of low-CAPEX/OPEX seafood valorization in SMEs using the TIDE framework
abstract: The valorization of seafood by-products is often framed as a technical opportunity, yet adoption in practice depends on whether small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) can embed new systems in their operational, economic, spatial, and regulatory realities. Drawing on survey-based evidence from Greek fisheries and seafood enterprises, the analysis identifies key operational and economic constraints and translates them into a configurational model of adoption credibility for blue SMEs. abstract: Hourly precipitation products are often assembled from station records with heterogeneous sub-hourly reporting cadences, yet users rarely know how much of the resulting difference in extreme diagnostics reflects temporal support, clock-hour alignment, the aggregation implementation, or the temporal structure of the rainfall. abstract: En la actualidad, los dilemas éticos y bioéticos existen en todos los ámbitos, especialmente en los laboratorios clínicos. abstract: Biomass-derived ashes (bioash) from energy production are increasingly promoted within circular bioeconomy frameworks as soil amendments that recycle nutrients and mitigate soil acidity. However, their impacts on rhizosphere bacterial communities in metal-contaminated soils (MCS) remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. abstract: This study estimates condominium rental price differentials from online listings across Thailand’s three major tourist cities, using Bangkok as the benchmark for Phuket and Pattaya while controlling for observable unit characteristics. abstract: ABSTRACT Topographic change detection is widely applied in fields such as geological hazard early warning, environmental monitoring, and geographic process analysis. abstract: Ixodes scapularis ticks transmit a number of pathogens important to human health, including Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto, the causative agent of Lyme disease. abstract: Industrial microbiology sits at the heart of food safety, fermentation technology, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance, and sustainable biotechnology, yet leadership in the field remains disproportionately male. abstract: Deoxynivalenol (DON) is a mycotoxin that contaminates approximately 60% of food worldwide and can impair reproduction. abstract: Auxotrophy, the inability of bacteria to synthesize one or multiple essential metabolites, is thought to be common among bacteria. abstract: This study examines the development of quality management in higher education institutions accredited under the Institutional Accreditation Program (IAP) of the Turkish Higher Education Quality Council (THEQC) through the conformity score method. abstract: This article examines the functioning of proper names from a sociolinguistic and political perspective, focusing on the name of the Republic of Belarus across languages. The aim of the study is to explain why the form Belarus (Byelarusʹ) is promoted by Belarusian authorities and communities, and why traditional exonyms continue to be used in other languages. abstract: ABSTRACT Microbial cultivation remains essential for understanding the physiology, ecology, and biotechnological potential of environmental microbes, yet conventional plate-based methods (CPM) recover only a minute fraction of the environmental microbiome. abstract: Solar power is a rapidly growing renewable energy source that converts sunlight into electricity using photovoltaic (PV) cells. abstract: Abstract Mallards ( Anas platyrhynchos ) have been domesticated and released in Europe and North America for centuries to supplement hunter harvest and in attempts to increase populations. abstract: ABSTRACT Floods remain among the most frequent and damaging natural hazards globally, with effective flood early warning messages (FEWMs) playing a critical role in reducing disaster risk and enhancing community preparedness. abstract: Clerodendrum infortunatum Linn (Family, Lamiaceae), extracts of acetone, methanol and aqueous evaluated against larvae of Culex quinquefasciatus Say, showed promising results. title: Morocco's grand strategy: Pillars and limitations
abstract: The Grand Strategy aims to align a state’s means and resources with its strategic priorities in pursuit of national interests, while taking into account internal and external constraints. For Morocco, the Grand Strategy provides a key framework for achieving national interests and redefining the country’s position within the international community. The New Development Model constitutes the backbone of this Grand Strategy and serves as the roadmap to be followed, although it is not the only component. The monarchy remains the primary driving force and impetus behind the Grand Strategy. This ar

title: Improving the reliability of ultrasonic welding: a hybrid FTA-DEMATEL-EC framework for cost and risk prioritization in mass production
abstract: Our research addresses the limited applicability of traditional reliability assessment methods by implementing a hybrid framework for the Branson 2000X AED ultrasonic welding system in mass production. We aimed to align the quantitative technical framework with the causality and financial impacts of identified failures. This approach created a tool that directly links failure frequency to its systemic causes and economic consequences. To do so, we developed a multi-dimensional hybrid model combining three analytical pillars: quantitative Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) to estimate failure probabilit
journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
institutions: Slovak University of Agriculture in Nitra

title: Molecular basis of sphingosine-1-phosphate transport by MFSD2B provides insights for selective inhibitor screening
abstract: Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) regulates immune cell trafficking, vascular homeostasis, and platelet function. Major facilitator superfamily domain-containing protein 2B (MFSD2B) maintains plasma levels of S1P by exporting it from erythrocytes and platelets, but how MFSD2B recognizes and transports S1P remains unclear. Here, we determined the structure of Sus scrofa MFSD2B by cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). title: Functional Profiles of Fish Gut Microbiota Associated With Feeding Habits in the Midstream of the Jialing River Under Cascade Channelization
abstract: ABSTRACT To examine the influence of diet on fish gut microbiota in channelized rivers, we characterized the gut microbial communities of fish with different feeding habits in the midstream of the Jialing River. The main findings are as follows: (1) 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing identified Firmicutes and Proteobacteria as the dominant phyla, with their relative abundances differing significantly among fish of distinct feeding habits. title: State Responsibility as Social Investment: Evaluating Indonesia’s 2026 Free Nutritious Meals Program for Students
abstract: The Free Nutritional Meals (MBG) program is one of the Indonesian government's largest post-2024 social interventions and positions schools as a crucial arena for fulfilling the right to food and developing human capital. This article evaluates the MBG program for students in its second year of implementation by developing an integrative framework linking state responsibility, the social investment paradigm, implementation theory, William Dunn's policy evaluation criteria, and the Context–Input–Process–Product (CIPP) model. The research uses qualitative policy analysis and structured evidence
journal: Best Journal of Administration and Management

title: Assessment of Microplastic Contamination in Surface Waters and Sediments of Pool Malebo, Congo River, Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract: Data on microplastics in Central African inland waters remain limited. This study assesses contamination in the surface waters and surficial sediments of four Pool Malebo sites: Maluku, Kinkole, Kingabwa-Baramoto, and Kinsuka, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Sampling was conducted in June 2024, with three independent replicates per site. Water samples were vacuum-filtered, and sediments underwent KOH digestion followed by vacuum filtration. Suspected particles were characterized by stereomicroscopy, and selected particles were identified by attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infr

title: N70 S/Y155H combined mutation of neuraminidase of avian influenza H9N2 virus confers oseltamivir and zanamivir resistance and pathogenicity to mice
abstract: Recently, H9N2 avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a significant threat to both the poultry industry and public health. Therefore, investigating the impact of its neuraminidase mutations on susceptibility to neuraminidase inhibitors (NAIs) is of great importance for clinically preventing potential cross-species transmission of H9N2. In this study, our results revealed that NAI resistance-related mutations of most H9N2 viruses isolated from China during 1998 to 2024 mainly occurred at positions N70S, E119A/D/G/V, Q133K, Q136A, D151E, Y155H, I222V, R224K, E276D, R292K, N294S, and R371K. title: Toxicogenomic signatures in zebrafish embryos provide a resource for mode-of-action-informed ecotoxic hazard screening
abstract: Depending on their application, chemicals may enter the environment and exert harmful effects on organisms, necessitating environmental hazard assessment (EHA) as part of most approval processes. However, the increasing number of chemicals and the substantial resources required for EHA - in terms of time, cost, and animal use - pose major challenges for legacy and future chemical management. Here, we employ toxicogenomic profiling in the 3R-compliant zebrafish embryo model to explore candidate molecular signatures that may support mode of action (MoA)-informed hazard screening. institutions: Fraunhofer Institute for Molecular Biology and Applied Ecology

title: A Preparedness Index for Cross-Border Railway Logistics Corridors: Integrating Situational Awareness, Cybersecurity, and Communication Redundancy
abstract: Technologically advanced defence infrastructure and railway information systems are achieving high levels of interoperability by creating a converged architecture that integrates airborne surveillance platforms, command-and-control networking principles, endpoint cybersecurity, and satellite communications. This paper proposes a consolidated approach that combines situational awareness principles (AWACS), a redundant satellite communications channel (Starlink) for telemetry and traffic coordination, and the implementation of proven security practices used in macOS (Secure Enclave, System Integ
journal: The Baltic Journal of Road and Bridge Engineering

title: AMBIENT PM2.5 IN EAST AFRICA: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF DRIVERS, IMPACTS, MONITORING AND POLICY DIRECTIONS
abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) has emerged as one of the most pressing environmental health challenges in East Africa, where rapid urbanization, industrial expansion, and reliance on biomass fuels converge to elevate exposure levels. Despite its recognized role in respiratory and cardiovascular morbidity, monitoring of PM₂.₅ across the region remains fragmented, with limited reference-grade stations and growing reliance on low-cost sensors and satellite-derived estimates. This review synthesizes evidence on PM₂.₅ monitoring approaches, key drivers, health and socio-economic impacts, a
journal: Magna Scientia Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Legacies of Past Climate Change Shape Future Resilience of Typha latifolia at Its Rear Edge in East Asia
abstract: Global warming poses a significant threat to rear-edge populations owing to their geographically marginal distributions. Understanding the historical dynamics and future trajectories of these populations is crucial for developing effective conservation strategies, yet they remain poorly understood. Here, we employed landscape genomic approaches on 153 samples from 24 Typha latifolia populations spanning its fragmented rear edge in East Asia, to explore demographic history, local adaptation, climate vulnerability and resilience potential. Our analyses reveal that repeated Pleistocene climatic c

title: CHARACTERIZATION OF MICROBIOME INCIDENCE AND ANTIBACTERIAL RESISTANCE PROFILES IN URINARY TRACT INFECTED PATIENTS
abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) represent one of the most common bacterial infections worldwide and are increasingly complicated by the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) uropathogens. The present cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the incidence, microbial diversity, and antimicrobial resistance profiles of uropathogens isolated from clinically diagnosed UTI patients belonging to different high-risk groups. A total of 385 clean-catch midstream urine samples were collected and processed using standard microbiological procedures. Samples were cultured on Mac Conkey agar and Blood aga

title: Ferroptosis Regulates the Biofilm Formation and Antifungal Drug Resistance of Candida albicans
abstract: Objectives Candida albicans ( C. albicans ) biofilm serves as a major cause of Candida-related infections. However, the available antifungal agents are limited in variety, and the emergence of drug resistance has complicated clinical treatment. Ferroptosis shows promise as a novel therapeutic strategy for combating fungal infections. This study aimed to investigate the effects of ferroptosis on the biofilm formation of C. albicans , as well as its susceptibility to antifungal agents. title: Disturbance-mediated invasion of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) in Zimbabwean freshwater ecosystems: distribution, ecological impacts and management challenges
abstract: Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) is one of the world’s most widely translocated freshwater fishes and remains central to aquaculture, food security and fisheries development across Africa. In Zimbabwe, however, the biological traits that favour production (rapid growth, early maturity, repeated spawning, parental care, trophic flexibility and broad environmental tolerance) also enhance the species’ ability to establish in open waters, particularly where repeated introductions coincide with environmental disturbance. This review therefore interprets the spread of O. niloticus as a disturb

title: Signal-Adapted Kernels and Lazy-Evaluation Gaussian Process Regression
abstract: Abstract Constant-bandwidth radial basis function (RBF) regression models are popular due to their simplicity, but they exhibit oscillatory patterns that resemble the Runge and Gibbs phenomenon on many real-world datasets. The Gaussian process regression (GPR) can be considered as an extension of RBF regression in that some RBFs can be posed as stationary kernels, but the GPR can also use non-stationary kernels. title: Quality analysis of hybrid and electric vehicle technology programs in Türkiye: A multi-criteria evaluation based on student and academic staff profiles
abstract: This study evaluated the development, student profile, academic staffing structure, and educational quality of HEVT programs in Türkiye between 2019 and 2025. Vehicle sales in Türkiye reached 1.37 million units in 2025, with hybrid and electric vehicles accounting for 27.2% and 17.7% of the market, respectively, continuing their upward market trend. Furthermore, the domestic production of these vehicles in Türkiye creates a demand for qualified technical personnel in after-sales service, maintenance, and repair sectors. To meet this demand, Hybrid and Electric Vehicle Technology (HEVT) program
journal: International Journal of Automotive Engineering and Technologies

title: Economic impacts of complex disasters affecting seaports and their associated supply chains
abstract: We develop a multi-regional computable general equilibrium (CGE) modeling approach to assess both direct and cascading supply-chain effects of complex seaport disruptions across U.S. regions and sectors. The analysis introduces a new, internally consistent method for estimating ship offloading congestion and the resilience effects of ship rerouting within the model’s production and trade structure. The model is illustrated by analyzing economic impacts of a complex seaport disruption involving a labor strike, wildfire-induced power outage, and terrorist attack at the twin ports of Los Angeles
institutions: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

title: Accurate and well-powered case–control analysis of spatial molecular data
abstract: As spatial molecular data grow in scope, there is a pressing need to identify disease-associated spatial structures. Current approaches typically make restrictive assumptions such as representing tissue regions by abundances of discrete cell types and samples by abundances of discrete niches; this risks overlooking important signals. Here we introduce variational inference-based microniche analysis (VIMA), a method combining deep learning with principled statistics to discover disease-associated spatial features with greater flexibility and precision. title: In with the old and out with the new: are old associations or new associations better for the biological control of Cactaceae?
abstract: Abstract Most biological control programmes against invasive alien plants (weeds) utilise agents collected from indigenous populations of the target weed that are thought to have a long coevolution history between the target weed and the agent. These biocontrol agents are referred to as old associations. There are, however, several examples of cactus weeds being successfully controlled by new associations, which are agents collected on other cactus species rather than the target weed itself and are thought to lack any significant coevolutionary history with the target weed. title: From the Soviet Invasion to the Rise of the Taliban: Political Transformation in Afghanistan
abstract: Afghanistan became one of the principal arenas in which great power rivalry, regional intervention, and internal political fragmentation intersected during the Cold War. This study analyses the political transformation of Afghanistan from the Soviet invasion of December 1979 to the Taliban’s capture of Kabul in September 1996 within its historical context. It aims to demonstrate how this transformation was shaped at the intersection of the international conjuncture, regional dynamics, and domestic political developments. title: Effect of thermo-sonication on the physicochemical properties, bioactive compounds, micronutrients, and antioxidant activity of cranberry juice
abstract: Fruits such as cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarponAiton), that contain several phenolic substances, are processed commercially as juices, requiring treatments to extend shelf-life. Thermo-sonication, the synergistic application of mild heat and ultrasound, is a promising non-thermal liquid foods processing technology. This study examined the kinetics of change of physicochemical properties, micronutrients, key bioactive compounds, and color attributes of thermo-sonicated cranberry juice at three varying temperatures 35 °C, 45 °C, and 55 °C, over varying treatment times of 1, 3, 5, and 7 min in co

title: Population genetic data for 23 STR loci of the Miskito ethnic group in Honduras
abstract: The Miskito constitute Honduras’s largest indigenous population (~ 80,000 individuals), yet population-specific genetic databases essential for accurate forensic analysis remain unavailable. Allele frequencies for 23 autosomal short tandem repeat loci were determined from 100 unrelated Miskito individuals (52 females, 48 males) from four settlements in Gracias a Dios department. DNA was amplified using the PowerPlex Fusion 6C System and analyzed by capillary electrophoresis. Statistical parameters were calculated using Arlequin v3.5.2.2 and Genepop v4.7.5. title: Atmospheric particle deposition and anthropogenic microparticles in tofu from plastic-waste-fueled small-scale industries in Sidoarjo, Indonesia
abstract: Plastic-waste combustion in small-scale food production may create particle-rich environments with potential for deposition onto exposed foods, yet paired environmental–food evidence remains limited. This cross-sectional study quantified atmospheric particle deposition and anthropogenic microparticles in tofu at 11 plastic-waste-fueled sites in Tropodo Village, Sidoarjo, Indonesia. Particles settling over 24 h were collected using passive dust-fall samplers, enumerated by stereomicroscopy, and classified as fibers, films, or fragments. title: An Interpretable Surrogate Model with an Enhanced Multivariance Product Representation Support and a Neural Residual: Dimension-Independent Accuracy on Product Structure and a Diagnostic for Real Data
abstract: High-dimensional model representation (HDMR) gives a surrogate that is interpretable by construction: with an orthonormal basis, its component functions translate directly into variance-based Sobol' sensitivity indices. The established HDMR surrogates, however, expand the response as a sum of low-order additive components, so a genuinely multiplicative (product or power law) response is reached only through a cascade of interaction terms whose count grows combinatorially with the dimension. title: Application of close‐kin mark–recapture to an American black bear population using harvest samples
abstract: Close-kin mark-recapture (CKMR) offers a promising alternative to traditional mark-recapture methods for estimating wildlife population parameters. CKMR estimates demographic parameters by identifying genetic relationships between individuals, effectively "recapturing" parental genotypes through their offspring's genetic profiles. One key advantage of CKMR over traditional methods is the ability to estimate abundance without recapture, facilitating the use of lethally collected biological samples. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: MST-former: multiparty shared representation enabled transformer for secure medical image analysis
abstract: Abstract Privacy-preserving collaborative medical image analysis across multiple healthcare institutions remains challenging due to data heterogeneity, patient privacy constraints, and incomplete cross-institutional record alignment. To address these limitations, this paper proposes MST-Former, a multiparty shared transformer framework that enables secure embedding fusion without sharing raw medical images. title: prepR4pcm: An R package for preparing data and trees for phylogenetic comparative methods
abstract: 1. Phylogenetic comparative methods require species names in a trait dataset to match tip labels in a phylogenetic tree. Yet this apparently simple prerequisite is often one of the most fragile steps in a comparative workflow. Names may differ because of, for example, formatting, taxonomic revisions, synonyms, or spelling errors. If these differences are resolved informally, species can be lost from analyses, and the reasons for their loss can be difficult to reconstruct. 2. title: Predictive modeling of lung cancer subtype with integration of clinical and thoracic imaging features to guide early brain metastasis management
abstract: PURPOSE: Optimal treatment for synchronous brain metastases at lung cancer diagnosis depends on subtype, but histologic/molecular profiling is often delayed. We developed machine-learning models using clinical and imaging data to classify lung cancer into three subtypes with distinct brain metastasis treatment implications: small cell lung cancer (SCLC), EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (EGFR+), and EGFR-wild-type non-small cell lung cancer (EGFR-). title: Soil and Water Contamination by Perfluoroalkyl Acids (PFAAs) at Fire Outbreak Sites in Ghana: Distribution and Screening-level Risk Assessment
abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants of concern because of their mobility, persistence, bioaccumulation potential, and possible adverse health effects. In this study, only two legacy perfluoroalkyl acids (PFAAs) that include perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) were quantified. title: Human–AI interaction in cybersecurity: An SOR model approach to users' intention to adopt AI-based authentication systems
abstract: Cyber-attack poses potential threats and challenges for both individuals and organizations. Although strong security systems can protect against the destructive outcomes of cybercrime victimization, this is comparatively feasible in the current era of Artificial Intelligence. Therefore, the current study aims to unlock users’ intention to adopt AI-based authentication systems (AAI), prioritizing the role of attitude toward AI (AT) as a key direct predictor, while investigating prior cybercrime victimization experience (CVE), perceived severity (PS), and fear of cybercrime victimization (FCV) a

title: Food Cold Chain Logistics and Social Sustainability: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Cold food chain logistics plays an important social role in maintaining the quality and safety of perishable products and ensuring the sustainability of supply chains. The purpose of the study is to identify the dynamics of development, thematic structure, and promising areas of scientific research in the field of logistics and management of the cold food chain. The research methodology is based on a systematic bibliographic, bibliometric, and substantive analysis of scientific publications. title: An Energy‐Efficient Multiparameter Clustering and Routing Framework for WSNs Using Adaptive Starfish Optimization Algorithm and Spider‐Tailed Horned Viper Optimization
abstract: ABSTRACT Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have become an essential component of environmental monitoring, military surveillance, industrial automation, and smart city applications. However, the limited energy capacity of sensor nodes and inefficient clustering and routing mechanisms significantly affect network lifetime, communication reliability, and quality of service (QoS). title: Association of Urban Greenness and Air Pollution on Asthma Visits Among Children and Adolescents in Industrial and Non-Industrial Cities in Taiwan
abstract: Background: Environmental factors such as air pollution and urban greenness are important in influencing pediatric asthma, yet their individual effects remain unclear across industrial and non-industrial settings. This study examined whether urban greenness modifies the link between air pollution and pediatric asthma in Kaohsiung (industrial) and Taipei (non-industrial), Taiwan, by highlighting differential environmental impacts on children’s health. Methods: Daily pediatric asthma clinic encounters across target age strata were tracked from 111 clinics in Taipei (January 1, 2019–May 31, 2023)

title: TSI-AsphaLab: an Open-source Software for Calibrating and Simulating the Thermo-Stiffness Integration (TSI) Model
abstract: Abstract This study presents TSI-AsphaLab , an open-source software developed to calibrate and simulate the Thermo-Stiffness Integration (TSI) model. Based on thermodynamics concepts and the time-temperature superposition principle, the TSI model accurately represents the stiffness modulus of asphalt mixtures along a wide range of loading conditions (i.e., frequency and temperature) without requiring shift factors. journal: International Journal of Pavement Research and Technology

title: LIKE, SHARES, AND TOURIST SUSTAINABLE BEHAVIOUR: THE POWER OF USER-GENERATED CONTENT IN GREEN TRAVEL
abstract: The emergence of new technologies has led to the rise of a new phase of social media with special interactivity features. Today, social media has become an important resource for individuals to gain information, communicate and create engage with others. User-generated content (UGC) is one of the methods of communication on social media platforms where users can interact with each other using various interactivity features provided by social media. title: Synergistic Polyherbal–Antibiotic Combinations: Emerging Trends, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Implications in Antimicrobial Research
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has become a pressing global health concern, threatening the efficacy of existing antibiotic therapies and complicating infection management. The indiscriminate and prolonged use of antimicrobial agents has accelerated the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella pneumoniae. title: The effect of compacted nylon particles and silica fume on mechanical properties and water absorption of lightweight concrete: experimental and theoretical study
abstract: Abstract In the last decade, the global demand for nylon and plastic products has surged markedly. Due to their slow decomposition, recycling and industrial application of these materials is vital. This process not only reduces the amount of plastic waste but also helps mitigate its environmental impact. In construction, these recycled materials offer a sustainable alternative to traditional aggregates in concrete. Moreover, the need to decrease building weight has gained increasing importance. title: Spatiotemporal Assessment of Climatic Water Scarcity in Nigeria Using an Integrated Standardized Precipitation Index–Temperature Anomaly Index (SPI–TAI) Framework
abstract: Climate change is increasing water scarcity in Nigeria through rising temperatures and declining rainfall, and most of the drought evaluations depend on precipitation only. The study examined the climate-induced water scarcity situation in Nigeria using the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and the Temperature Anomalies Index (TAI). Monthly precipitation and temperature data for 1901–2024 were extracted from the Climatic Research Unit Time Series (CRU TS v4.09) dataset through the Google Earth interface. title: FROM LUXURY TO RESPONSIBLE CONSUMPTION: NUTRITIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL PERSPECTIVES ON THE PRODUCTION OF SIBERIAN STURGEON CAVIAR (ACIPENSER BAERII, BRANDT, 1869)
abstract: Caviar is a fish-based food product of high gastronomic and economic value, traditionally associated with luxury cuisine, but increasingly examined in the context of sustainability and responsible aquaculture. This review paper summarizes current information on the consumption of caviar derived from the Siberian sturgeon (Acipenser baerii Brandt, 1869), from nutritional, technological, and ecological perspectives. title: Social Liability in Post-Regime-Change Afghanistan: The Taliban and Former Regime Supporters
abstract: Since the Taliban's return to power in August 2021, the movement has publicly maintained a blanket amnesty for members of the former Islamic Republic's government, armed forces, and civil service. In practice, United Nations, treaty-body, and non-governmental monitors have documented a persistent pattern of extrajudicial killing, enforced disappearance, arbitrary arrest, and torture directed at this population through 2025. title: Improved Constraints on the Surface of LHS 3844 b from its Mid-Infrared Spectrum
abstract: The thermal emission spectra of terrestrial exoplanets provide a window into their surface compositions and corresponding geological processes. Close-in, rocky planets orbiting M dwarfs are ideal targets for these studies, as observations have shown that most have little to no atmosphere. LHS 3844 b is an ultra-short period super-Earth orbiting a nearby M dwarf, and is the most favorable target that does not have a dayside magma ocean. title: Automated Sailboat Navigation using Controllabilty-Aware Nonlinear Model Predicitive Control under Stochastic Winds
abstract: This paper presents a systematic approach to plan and execute a time-efficient sailboat trajectory under the challenging stochastic wind conditions for automated sailboat. Unlike deterministic scenarios, stochastic wind disturbances introduce challenges such as gust unpredictability, directional shifts, and fluctuating apparent wind speeds. These characteristics render traditional planning methods, such as Line-of-Sight (LoS) and waypoint approaches, to be ineffective and not applicable, as they often rely on static or deterministic environmental models. title: What Do City Codes Say About Climate Risk?
abstract: Climate change is intensifying natural hazards, and preparing cities for them falls primarily to local governments. Yet what municipal codes say about hazards, and whether their requirements match each city's risk profile, has not been measured. I analyze 3.6 million sentences from 204 U.S. cities' municipal codes and compare each city's hazard text to its actual risk from FEMA's National Risk Index. I document four patterns. title: Pricing IoT Data Delivered via LEO Satellites
abstract: IoT terminals served by LEO satellite constellations transmit data to passing satellites in discrete uplink windows. That data is delivered to buyers only when the satellite reaches a ground station. This store-and-forward structure makes the achievable price a discontinuous function of the delivery completeness threshold (a phenomenon we call a pricing cliff) and creates a geographic pricing asymmetry between polar and equatorial terminals that depends on constellation size. abstract: The 1-ton prototype detector for Jinping neutrino experiment (JNE-1ton) has completed its hardware upgrade and has been successfully operated in both water and liquid-scintillator modes at CJPL-I, which is situated under a 2400-m rock overburden. During the upgrade, the detector's mechanical support structure and PMT layout were redesigned. The original Hamamatsu PMTs were replaced with 8-inch MCP-PMTs from North Night Vision, increasing the PMT count from 30 to 60. title: Memory Is a Derivation: The Distributed-Evidence Paradox in Long-Term Agents
abstract: Long-running LLM agents compress past interactions into persistent memories that may be reused as premises for later tasks. This creates a distinct derivation problem: whether the memory actually follows from what the interaction history supports. Relevant evidence may be scattered across earlier interactions, while compression can introduce relations or event status that the history never established. title: SkillGym: Training Skill-Use Agents with Automatic Verifiable Environment Generation
abstract: Skills equip LLM agents with professional knowledge and guidance to complete long-horizon and complex tasks. Although skills have been widely adopted in recent agent paradigms and harnesses, how to synthesize reliable training data and how to train agents for skill use remain underexplored. In this work, we propose SkillGym, an automatic pipeline to build verifiable environments, collect trajectories, and train skill-use agents. title: Drape-Compatible Tool-Tip Localization for Hand-Held Laparoscopic Instruments via UWB Carrier-Phase Ranging and Trocar-Constrained Geometry
abstract: A surgical robot policy needs to know where each instrument's working end sits relative to the camera and to the other instrument, yet a laparoscopic operation leaves only the endoscope video, and a draped instrument hides every optical path on itself. We estimate the tool tips from distances and an IMU alone. The distances are measured by ultra-wideband carrier phase between antenna nodes on the handle side of the instruments: one per hand-held instrument, one on the endoscope, all outside the sterile barrier. title: Measuring Mass Splittings in Baryon SU(2) Multiplets
abstract: The inclusion of isospin-breaking corrections arising from electromagnetic interactions and the up-down quark mass difference is becoming increasingly important in lattice QCD calculations, as the precision of observables is at or approaching the percent level. In this context, the RM123 method has been employed in recent years to take into account such isospin corrections. In this work, we study baryon mass splittings using the RM123 approach. title: DISCERN: Can AI Agents Work Like Scientists and Guide Discovery?
abstract: Reliable automated research requires agents to vet data, verify analyses, and generate hypotheses grounded in trustworthy evidence, potentially reducing routine scientific workload while allowing scientists to focus on interpretation and discovery. Existing benchmarks often only assess analytical task completion or hypothesis generation separately rather than testing whether reliable evidence supports valid and novel claims. title: Scanless quantum Fourier-transform mid-infrared spectroscopy for solids and surface analysis
abstract: Quantum infrared (IR) spectroscopy is a novel technique based on nonlinear interferometry and quantum sensing with undetected photons. abstract: Multiple-choice benchmarks are cheap to grade and are running out of room, and the standard remedy, writing harder items, is slow and repeated for every benchmark. title: Enabling global prediction of marsh vegetation survival during extreme storms
abstract: Flood protection by coastal vegetated systems depends on the persistence of vegetation structures, but it is currently impossible to predict vegetation survival during extreme storms. Using the largest artificially generated waves in the world, we here quantified the persistence of tidal marsh vegetation by measuring stem breakage of winter-state vegetation (3 species and mimics) during extreme storms with up to 2.0 m significant wave height, 4 m water level and 8 s peak period waves. title: A sensitivity analysis of data imputation in daily PM10 prediction
abstract: Reliable daily prediction of particulate matter (PM10) depends not only on model structure and predictor selection, but also on how missing data are treated during preprocessing. In air-quality applications, gaps are common in both ground-based monitoring records and satellite-derived predictors due to instrument downtime, quality screening, and cloud contamination. Despite this, data imputation is often treated as a purely technical step. abstract: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) has been widely applied in the fields of numerical optimization and UAV path planning, but it suffers from inherent limitations such as a tendency toward premature convergence, weak parameter adaptability, and insufficient population diversity. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel PSO variant algorithm (ACPSO) that integrates the Actor-Critic framework with genetic strategies. abstract: Rain-gauge network optimisation in complex terrain should consider more than station density or planar spacing. It should also assess whether the existing gauges adequately sample the elevation ranges and terrain settings that influence spatial rainfall variability. This study proposes a terrain-aware Composite Gap Coverage (COMP) strategy for augmenting an operational rain gauge network in the Wupper River catchment, western Germany. abstract: As the economy rapidly develops, people's livelihood has been improved. However, simultaneously, population growth, the air quality has deteriorated. Since the economic reforms of the 1980s, China has pursued economic growth at the expense of the environment, becoming the 2nd largest economy in the process. abstract: Engine performance in fishing vessel depends on the reliability and efficiency of diesel engine, in which the lubrication system plays a key role in reducing friction, controlling operating temperature, and minimizing component wear. abstract: Abstract Algal blooms pose significant environmental and economic challenges worldwide. As their impact increases, there is an urgent need to improve forecasting models that predict their occurrence, development, and trends. Understanding recent research developments in satellite-based monitoring of algal blooms in the African Great Lakes provides a vital foundation for creating effective early warning systems and improving both short- and long-term prediction accuracy. title: An historic fishery collapse driven by socioeconomic and environmental factors
abstract: Abstract In the Late Middle Ages, the western Baltic herring fishery played a central role in Europe. Salted herring was the basis for welfare and political power. We make use of a 450-year time series of Baltic herring catches (1200–1650), to identify which factors drove the herring catch dynamics during different phases of our time series. By the year 1570, the fishery suddenly collapsed, causing large-scale dislocations in trade, with major social and political consequences. abstract: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation in southern Alberta, Canada, preserves abundant plant fossils from the upper Campanian to upper Maastrichtian. abstract: Daily to seasonal weather information remains rare in Quaternary science, because proxy archives typically resolve only seasonal or annual means. Yet climate is felt at daily timescales, through frost, snowfall, wind and precipitation. Here a framework of Bayesian Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape is presented that anchors a modern day-of-year marginal climatology to a proxy-reconstructed seasonal mean, two millennia into the past. abstract: Anthropogenic land use and land cover changes alter watershed hydrological processes by modifying the partitioning of precipitation into evapotranspiration, infiltration, and surface runoff. abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable separation technologies has intensified interest in polymeric membranes due to their energy efficiency and versatility. However, many conventional membranes are fabricated from permanently crosslinked or non-degradable polymers, limiting their recyclability and contributing to environmental waste. abstract: Abstract In complex industrial environments, single monitoring signals, limited labeled data, and varying operating conditions often lead to low accuracy and poor generalization in cross-domain fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. To address these issues, a multi-channel information fusion with adaptive weighting network (MIFAWN) is proposed in this paper.
