abstract: Taking the debate over whether space exploration constitutes a necessity or a mere indulgence as its starting point, this essay adopts a philosophical and interdisciplinary perspective to re-examine the value of human space activities inspired by the Pale Blue Dot photograph. abstract: Abstract Climate change is reshaping drought patterns across Australia, increasing pressure on water-resource security and highlighting the need for more informed and adaptive river-basin management. abstract: Abstract The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG) underscores the need for eliminating hunger, improving nutrition, and promoting sustainable agriculture. For achieving SDG2, it is critical to address several factors such as agricultural production, groundwater depletion, and glacier decline under climate change. abstract: Biological porous materials exhibit complex architectures that are challenging to design using conventional modelling approaches. abstract: Architecture has long been regarded as a powerful medium through which societies express their values, priorities, and historical narratives. This study examined the architectural design of the Rivers State Government House, exploring how socio-economic and demographic factors influence its structure and symbolism. abstract: Many important plant diseases are caused by airborne spores. title: Coupling of VIIRS and Sentinel-2 observations to generate Landsat-scale TIR imagery for estimating landscape evapotranspiration using the Simplified Surface Energy Balance (SSEB) model
abstract: : Satellite thermal infrared (TIR) data are essential for remote sensing of energy exchange processes at the Earth-atmosphere interface. Current satellite sensors are subject to a trade-off between spatial resolution and temporal coverage. Daily TIR observations from MODIS and VIIRS are limited to coarse spatial resolutions of ∼400–1000 m, whereas higher-resolution Landsat TIRS observations (∼100 m) provide infrequent temporal coverage (∼8 days). Downscaling methods that correlate TIR imagery with higher-resolution multispectral data can improve the availability of fine-scale TIR observations.

abstract: Intact tropical forests store high amounts of carbon biomass, but this long-stored carbon has not been widely quantified at the regional scale. This study integrates multi-source remote sensing data and Random Forest (RF) to model above- and below-ground biomass carbon (AGBC and BGBC) in intact forests across Southeast Asia from 2000 to 2020. abstract: Abstract Applications of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) for positioning, navigation, and timing rely on precise orbit and satellite clock corrections provided by multiple Analysis Centers (ACs) of the International GNSS Service (IGS). abstract: Leaf length and width are key dimensions of tree leaf size and can influence leaf boundary-layer development and leaf-environment heat exchange. abstract: Rapid urban expansion has intensified regional human-land conflicts and ecological risks. abstract: The burgeoning market for heavy-cargo transportation poses an increasing challenge to the normal use of highway bridges. abstract: This research aimed to characterize soil morphological features and assess profile variability across sugarcane-dominated landscapes. abstract: Maintaining spatially adequate thermal and air-quality conditions is challenging in commercial multi-tier layer houses because environmental gradients can develop simultaneously across longitudinal regions and cage levels. abstract: Columba eversmanni, commonly known as the Yellow-eyed Pigeon, is a species with a limit-ed geographical distribution. It breeds in Central Asia and it moves toward South Asia during winters. The species faces significant threats from human activities and climate change. In this study, we used the MaxEnt model to assess the current and potential future distri-bution of the species based on climatic variables across its non-breeding range in the arid region of Rajasthan, India. title: An open-access workflow combining climate model projections with epidemiological frameworks to assess air quality mortality
abstract: Surface-level air pollution is a major source of human mortality worldwide, and future climate change is expected to alter concentrations of pollutants such as ozone and particulate matter. Estimating the health burden of these changes requires combining climate model projections with epidemiological frameworks, such as those developed in the Global Burden of Disease (GBD). However, significant barriers hinder this integration. Climate model outputs differ from health metrics in spatial resolution, temporal aggregation, and pollutant metrics. abstract: Geotechnical techniques are essential for subsurface geological investigations during the pre-feasibility phase of engineering projects.When the area under investigation is extensive, the density and consistency required for a conventional geotechnical reconnaissance program become both logistically complex and costly.The present study aims to estimate the main geotechnical parameters of the subsoil studied, namely water content (or moisture content), plasticity index, friction angle and cohesion from electrical resistivity data, through empirical equation calculations.The study area is locate

title: Technoeconomic and Life Cycle Analyses of the Co-production of Olefins, Aromatics, and Alkanes Using Microwave-Assisted Conversion of Polypropylene Plastic Waste
abstract: Abstract There is a growing interest in utilizing plastic waste to produce olefins and aromatics, which serve as essential building blocks for polyolefin production. In this paper, a novel microwave-assisted catalytic process is developed for converting polypropylene plastic waste into propylene, with simultaneous co-production of ethylene, aromatics, and alkanes, thereby closing the material loop by returning end-of-life plastic waste back into the petrochemical value chain as a high-value chemical feedstock, a key principle of the circular economy. title: Fish locomotor dynamics quantified using multiple inertial measurement units
abstract: Abstract Animals exhibit a diversity of locomotor behaviours that vary with body shape, ontogeny, motivation and environment. Documenting these behaviours often relies on recording videos of animals in controlled conditions displaying stereotyped behaviours. By contrast, animal-borne motion sensing data loggers can document diverse behaviours of animals in their natural environment. title: Beyond resilience: engineering antifragility and hazard mitigation in safety–critical systems using a stress–strain model
abstract: Abstract Traditional resilience engineering struggles with modern safety–critical systems operating under extreme uncertainty. Antifragility, the ability to gain from systemic stressors and near-misses, remains a philosophical ideal, lacking a rigorous, quantitative framework for engineering. The Systemic Stress–Strain Model (SSM) is a quantitative framework that operationalizes antifragility by analogy to material science. title: Comparing Remotely Sensed and Weather Station Measured Rainfall Data for Flood Prediction in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme rainfall events frequently trigger flash floods, which cause widespread damage to ecosystems, infrastructure, and livelihoods. Accurate rainfall estimation is therefore essential for flood modeling and early warning systems. This study assessed the performance of the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) and the Global Precipitation Measurement Integrated Multi‐Satellite Retrievals for GPM (GPM‐IMERG) against weather station rainfall observations collected across KwaZulu‐Natal, South Africa, between 2000 and 2022. title: Liberation-controlled beneficiation of Moroccan andalusite ore through particle size optimization and integrated gravity–magnetic separation
abstract: The beneficiation efficiency of andalusite ores is strongly governed by particle size because of its effect on mineral liberation and separation selectivity. In this study, the effect of particle size on the upgrading performance of an andalusite ore from the Moroccan Sidi Bou-Othmane deposit was investigated using shaking table gravity concentration followed by dry high-intensity magnetic separation. title: Bayesian Analysis of Seasonal and Periodic Time Series: Evidence from Nigerian Monthly Rainfall, 1981–2024
abstract: Monthly rainfall in Nigeria exhibits pronounced annual seasonality, season-dependent variability, and changes in temporal dependence that may not be adequately represented by a single fixed-parameter model. This study presents a Bayesian modelling framework for monthly rainfall records from 37 Nigerian Meteorological Agency stations spanning January 1981 to December 2024, a 44-year period comprising 528 monthly values per station. title: Improving the Quality of Chest X-rays Through Adaptive Image Enhancement Filters (ACEF)
abstract: Respiratory diseases are difficult to identify due to picture distortion, hence chest X-rays are commonly used to diagnose lung ailments, particularly in low-light settings. Raw radiographs frequently exhibit issues such as insufficient contrast, picture distortion, and poor tissue border definition, all of which can have a negative impact on radiographic accuracy, especially in low light. This paper describes the Adaptive Chest Enhancement Filter (ACEF), a three-stage preprocessing filter that combines image decongestion, lung-specific contrast enhancement, and tissue boundary preservation. title: Impact analysis of climate change on near future streamflow using CORDEX-SA datasets in a hilly watershed
abstract: The study analyses the impact of projected increase in temperature and rainfall on streamflow in the Barak Basin, Northeast India. The forest dominated rain-fed river basin up to Annapurna Ghat (Silchar) near the border of Bangladesh covers an area of 19004 Sq. Km. There has been an increasing occurrence of flood events in the basin due to decreasing forest cover. title: Findings on the efficacy of sonic debridement in chronic wound management – a case series
abstract: OBJECTIVES To evaluate the physiological rationale, mechanism of action, and emerging clinical evidence supporting sonic debridement as an adjunctive approach for wound hygiene and maintenance debridement in chronic wound management. METHODS A structured review of wound healing principles, biofilm biology, and current debridement modalities was performed alongside analysis of clinical observations and case series data using a sonic debridement device. title: Bauxite Residue (Red Mud) from the Bayer Process: A Critical Review of Management, Safe Storage, Valorization, Critical-Metal Recovery, and Industrial Integration
abstract: Bauxite residue (BR), commonly termed red mud, is the strongly alkaline, fine-grained solid generated during Bayer alumina refining. This critical review synthesizes a primary contemporary corpus of 145 publications from January 2020 to 23 September 2026, supplemented by a small set of pre-2020 foundational sources used only for historical and mechanistic context, and evaluates BR as an integrated management-and-resource system rather than an isolated waste stream. title: Reconstructing Ancient Copper Smelting Practices in the Eastern Part of the Srednogorie Metallogenic Zone (SE Bulgaria) Using Slag Mineralogy and Chemistry
abstract: This study reconstructs the smelting conditions of ancient copper production in the eastern Srednogorie metallogenic zone (SE Bulgaria) based on the mineralogical and chemical composition of archaeological slags. Slag samples from three ore fields were investigated: Rosen (Propadnala Voda, Korucheshme and Rosen deposits, and Atiya metallurgical centre), Zidarovo (Krushevets archaeological site) and St. Ilia (Boyadzhik archaeological site). title: A review of research on programmable airburst less-lethal munitions
abstract: As the demand for less-lethal response operations and their application in complex scenarios increases, the limitations of conventional less-lethal munitions in terms of strike accuracy, effective coverage, safety and controllability have become increasingly apparent. Programmable airburst less-lethal munitions have garnered attention due to their ability to detonate in a preset airspace and provide a controllable dispersal footprint. title: Simplified analysis of concentrically loaded reinforced concrete columns
abstract: Abstract Reinforced concrete columns subjected to concentric and eccentric compression loads are typically treated in an identical manner, taking into account both the imperfect shape, creep, and the second order effects, as described for example in fib Model Code 2020 and Eurocode 2. For concentrically loaded steel or timber columns and masonry walls simplified analyses are available, which are based on the cross‐sectional load bearing capacity reduced by a factor, which depends primarily on the slenderness. title: Physics-informed cross-domain image synthesis for microalgae growth phase classification in turbid media
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based classification of microalgae growth phases in Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME) requires representative training images. However, the available public data originate from a water medium with characteristics that differ from those of the POME. Existing methods apply uniform weighting to each channel and are inconsistent with light absorption in turbid media, leading to the collapse of the chromatic margin between the growth phases. Thus, these methods can only meet the global distribution (C1) but fail to simultaneously maintain inter-phase discriminability (C2).

title: Patterns, drivers, and consequences of narrow-ranged species loss for angiosperm functional diversity across East Eurasia
abstract: ABSTRACT Functional diversity links species traits to ecosystem functioning, yet its large-scale patterns and vulnerability to species loss remain poorly understood. Here, we assembled a comprehensive distribution and trait dataset of all angiosperms across East Eurasia and investigated geographic patterns of functional diversity represented by the richness (FR) and structure (standardized effect size of FR, sesFR) of functional traits, the environmental drivers underlying these patterns, and the potential consequences of losing narrow-ranged species. title: Exploring the gender wage gap in Indian agriculture—an interaction-based panel regression approach
abstract: This study investigates the gender wage disparities in Indian agriculture utilizing a pseudo-panel dataset and an interaction-based panel regression framework. The study seeks to examine the association of gender on agricultural wages over the years, especially in response to the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), which was enacted in 2005. title: Avaliação de modelos digitais de altura da vegetação derivados de dados LiDAR
abstract: Os Modelos Digitais de Altura (MDA) da vegetação são gerados pela subtração entre o Modelo Digital de Superfície (MDS) e o Modelo Digital de Terreno (MDT), que podem ser construídos pela interpolação das coordenadas tridimensionais obtidas por sistemas de perfilamento a laser (LiDAR). title: A Spectral–Semantic integration framework for hydrothermal alteration characterization using Landsat-8 OLI and AlphaEarth Foundations in the Eastern Tien Shan, China
abstract: Remote sensing-based hydrothermal alteration mapping plays an important role in regional mineral prospectivity analysis but remains challenging in structurally complex regions because of spectral mixing, weak peripheral anomalies, and fragmented spatial distributions. This study proposes an integrated spectral–semantic framework that combines Landsat-8 OLI multispectral imagery with AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) semantic embeddings for hydrothermal alteration characterization and prospectivity evaluation in the Tuwu copper belt, Eastern Tien Shan, China. title: Hybrid GA-DQN for opportunistic cluster head selection and routing in resource constraint Internet of Things networks
abstract: Abstract Energy efficiency and reliable data transmission are two important challenges in Internet of Things (IoT) networks because of the limited energy resources of sensor nodes and their dynamic nature. Accordingly, this research develops a Genetic Algorithm Deep Q-Network (GA-DQN) based hybrid framework for intelligent cluster head selection and adaptive IoT Network routing to counter these threats. title: Assessment of seismic velocity changes from ambient noise single-station cross-component analysis in Altamira, Brazil
abstract: Methods capable of monitoring groundwater systems are essential to support decisions and resource management. In recent years, techniques based on the analysis of ambient seismic noise have consolidated passive seismic methods as valuable monitoring tools. This work focuses on a single-station cross-component analysis based on Ambient Noise Seismic Interferometry and Coda Wave Interferometry to quantify seismic velocity variations ( δν/ν ) between 2014 and 2016 near the city of Altamira and the Belo Monte hydroelectric complex, located in the Xingu River Basin in Brazil. abstract: Determination of the ternary composition in a multicomponent distillation is critical for process control and system operation. However, monitoring saline-organic solutions (Water-NaCl-Ethanol) remains a challenge due to the non-linear interference between ionic conductivity and organic solvent concentration. abstract: Abstract The efficient synthesis of poly(ester amide)s (PEAs), which combine polyamide-like mechanical strength with polyester-like biodegradability, has remained a longstanding challenge. Herein, we introduce a unique coordination ring-opening transamidation copolymerization (CROTCP) mediated by a tetranuclear titanium catalyst. title: Projected climate extremes and demographic change provide a spatial context for linguistic vulnerability in Multilingual Yunnan
abstract: Abstract Climate change may reshape the demographic and socioeconomic conditions under which minority languages are maintained, although projected population change alone cannot demonstrate migration, language shift, or language loss. Focusing on multi-ethnic and multilingual Yunnan, China, this study integrates outputs from eight CMIP6 climate models with 1-km gridded demographic projection of resident population to examine changes in very-wet-day precipitation (R95p), warm-day frequency (TX90p), consecutive dry days (CDD), and resident population from 2020 to 2100 under the SSP5–8.5 scenario

abstract: Abstract This study investigates the suitability of sustainable, highly porous nanosponges, composed of TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibers (TOCNF) and branched polyethylenimine (bPEI, cross-linker), as scaffolds for PEDOT:PSS poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrenesulfonate dip coating to design piezoresistive pressure sensors. title: Hydrochemical Analysis and Associated Health Risk Assessment of Groundwater Quality of Hisar District of Haryana, India
abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater is a major drinking water resource supporting nearly half of the world's population but its quality is being compromised by various anthropogenic factors. This study provides an in‐depth analysis of groundwater quality in Hisar district, Haryana, India by integrating hydrogeochemical parameters and advanced analytical techniques. It evaluates the groundwater quality using samples collected from 76 locations (wells, tube wells, and hand pumps) in the pre‐monsoon season. title: AirComm: Your Smartphone Can “Smell” Fine Particles via Light
abstract: Fine-grained air quality monitoring is critical for assessing personal exposure to air pollution in indoor micro-environments; however, dedicated air quality sensors are costly and offer limited spatial coverage. In this work, we present AirComm , a smartphone-based air quality sensing system that requires no additional hardware. title: DOA estimation for autonomous vehicles by exploiting second-order statistics of Co-array domain of nested arrays by implementing Cuckoo Search Algorithm
abstract: Real-world situations require DSRC-based vehicular ad hoc networks that employ sensor fusion and perception systems. Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation is critical for sensor fusion as it helps track moving objects. This paper presents a new approach to DOA estimation for autonomous vehicles, using a nested sensor array and the Cuckoo Search (CS) Algorithm. abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of gross primary production (GPP), the mass of carbon fixed by plants through photosynthesis, and long‐term GPP trends is essential for monitoring ecosystems, analyzing the carbon cycle, and evaluating biosphere models. FluxSat (FS) is a global daily gridded GPP data set developed using machine learning with MODerate‐resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) satellite reflectances and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR), trained on eddy covariance (EC) flux tower data in the FLUXNET2015 and AmeriFlux networks. title: A life cycle-based Green Manufacturing framework for environmental decision-making: an application to heavy-duty vehicle chassis frame rail manufacturing
abstract: Abstract Heavy-duty vehicles (HDV) are essential to global transportation and logistics systems, yet environmental assessments have predominantly focused on the use phase, leaving the environmental impacts of the manufacturing stage comparatively underexplored. This study evaluates the cradle-to-gate environmental performance of steel chassis frame rail manufacturing using a process-level Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) based on primary industrial data collected directly from the shop floor. title: Which One Tastes Better? Testing Distinct Baits to Evaluate Fruit‐Feeding Butterfly Assemblages (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae) in a Subtropical Region
abstract: ABSTRACT Standardised sampling protocols are essential for improving biodiversity assessments, particularly for indicator groups such as fruit‐feeding butterflies. Although fermented banana is the most widely used bait in tropical regions, rotten fish is the best bait for catching fruit‐feeding butterflies in high‐altitude sites. Few studies have evaluated the effectiveness of alternative attractants in the subtropical region worldwide, where environmental conditions and resource availability differ markedly. abstract: Abstract. Evapotranspiration (ET) is the dominant hydrologic flux in wetlands, and partitioning into transpiration (T) and evaporation (E) is essential for understanding water and carbon dynamics, guiding sustainable water management practices, and predicting responses to climate change in these systems. However, the presence of moss layers in many wetlands challenges the assumptions of commonly used partitioning methods. title: Real-time heuristic evacuation pathfinding algorithm for flood avoidance
abstract: Floods rank among the world’s most devastating annual disasters in terms of casualties and economic losses, making evacuation route planning crucial for mitigating flood risks. This study proposes a Real-time Heuristic Flood Evacuation Path Planning Algorithm (RHEPFA) based on dynamic flood simulations using the ANUGA 2D model. abstract: Abstract Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation is a core technology in array signal processing, which is widely applied in radar, communications and sonar systems. Traditional subspace methods suffer from poor performance under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and limited snapshots, while Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) methods have high computational complexity. title: The impact of compound soil conditioner on the physicochemical properties of acidic farmland soil in Sichuan Province, China

abstract: Abstract Valve leakage in offshore pipelines threatens operational safety, while acoustic-emission (AE)-based identification remains difficult because leakage signals are non-stationary and sensitive to environmental interference. This study proposes BACNet, a lightweight auditory-inspired network for the closed-set identification of ten leaking valves and one no-leak condition. title: Spatial zoning of rural marginalization under environmental stress using geographic information systems and system dynamics
abstract: Abstract The persistence of regional development inequalities has highlighted the necessity of using dynamic models that encompass the multidimensional nature of rural isolation. Traditional spatial planning frameworks often overlook the synergistic impacts of service deprivation and geological hazards on the phenomenon of marginalization. title: The Promise and Perils of Private Enforcement under EU Law: The Digital Services Act in Context
abstract: Abstract This article offers a conceptual account of private enforcement under EU law, focusing on the DSA. It argues that the damages action under the DSA derives directly from Union law and cannot be reduced to a declaratory reference to national law. title: Eddy covariance station in a pine forest (Usmansky Bor, Central Forest-Steppe): results of monitoring ecosystem carbon exchange during the autumn-winter period
abstract: Continuous eddy covariance measurements of carbon fluxes remain unknown for pine forests in the forest-steppe zone of European Russia, limiting our understanding of the seasonal dynamics of ecosystem carbon exchange. This study aimed to assess net ecosystem carbon exchange between the atmosphere and an old-growth pine forest in Usmansky Bor during the autumn–winter period of 2025–2026. abstract: This study aims to compare the performance of the Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and Adaptive Momentum Backpropagation (AMBP) models for predicting monthly rainfall in West Nusa Tenggara Province. The data used consists of monthly rainfall from the NASA POWER dataset for the period from January 1981 to December 2025. title: Assessing forest ecological sustainability through wavelet decomposition and stationarity tests: a comparative analysis of major forest product producers
abstract: Introduction Forest ecosystems are central to environmental sustainability, yet the persistence of forest-specific ecological conditions remains insufficiently explored, particularly across different time horizons. Existing research has predominantly examined CO₂ emissions and aggregate ecological footprint indicators, while relatively limited attention has been devoted to the stochastic properties and frequency-dependent persistence of forest ecological balance (FEB). abstract: Abstract While it is crucial to address the pronounced nonlinearity, substantial time delays, and complex dynamics of post‐combustion carbon capture (PCC) systems using phase‐change solvents, most existing studies rely on idealized simulation data and thus have difficulty representing real industrial noise and long‐range temporal dependencies. title: Mechanisms of long-term degradation in plasticized PVDF pressure barriers under offshore service exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) is commonly used as a pressure sheath material in offshore flexible pipelines; however, there is limited experimental data from long-term service exposure. In this study, three PVDF layers recovered from a flexible riser after ten years of offshore operation were examined to understand the degradation mechanisms that occurred under field conditions. title: A novel multi-application heat recovery system with adsorption cooling and seasonal energy storage for liquid cooling data centers
abstract: Liquid-cooling data centers are emerging as the infrastructure for high-performance computing. They generate substantial heat, which is very promising for energy recovery. However, the seasonal mismatch between continuous waste-heat generation and winter-concentrated heating demand remains insufficiently addressed. This study proposes a novel multi-application heat recovery system that integrates waste-heat-driven cooling, cross-seasonal thermal storage, and winter heat supply to enable year-round energy recovery. title: Local geographies of housing inequality: Neighbourhood trajectories of housing purchasing (un)affordability across neighbourhoods in England and Wales (2010-2023)
abstract: In recent decades, housing purchasing prices have outpaced incomes, increasing spatial inequalities and creating a growing challenge to homeownership. Despite housing markets being highly localised with most residential moves made at local scales, analyses of housing affordability have typically focused on national- and regional-level trends. We draw on a novel housing price dataset, to present the first neighbourhood-level analysis of housing (un)affordability trajectories across England and Wales (2010 to 2023). title: Arboreal and Terrestrial Frugivore Vertebrate Assemblage Diversity and Composition Vary With Disturbance Histories in Guianan Forests
abstract: ABSTRACT Frugivorous vertebrates, as seed dispersers and predators, play critical roles in forest ecosystem dynamics. Understanding their responses to human disturbances is essential for assessing ecosystem functioning and guiding conservation programs. Using 60 camera traps at nutmeg trees ( Virola kwatae and V. michelii , Myristicaceae), we monitored terrestrial and arboreal frugivores across three forest sites in French Guiana submitted to various human disturbances: a protected mature forest (least disturbed), a formerly exploited forest (intermediately disturbed), and a forest near a road
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Bridging Albanian monitoring and Water Framework Directive oriented assessment: A surface water quality index
abstract: The implementation of the European Union Water Framework Directive (WFD) presents an important methodological challenge for countries whose established environmental monitoring systems are not yet fully harmonised with WFD compatible surface water body delineation and assessment structures.This situation is particularly relevant for EU candidate countries, where existing station-based monitoring programmes must increasingly support integrated river basin assessment and alignment with the environmental acquis.This study addresses this challenge by developing a composite surface water quality in

title: Passive acoustic monitoring reveals how urban vegetation supports acoustic refuges for avian communication in a subtropical megacity
abstract: Abstract Urbanisation fundamentally alters the sensory landscape, creating novel acoustic environments where anthropogenic noise acts as a rigorous filter on wildlife communities. While birds are known to adjust their songs to cope with noise, the limits of this plasticity and the role of fine‐scale habitat structure in buffering these constraints remain poorly understood, particularly in intensely urbanised megacities. title: Citizen Orb Photometry Pipeline (COPP): A Standardized Method for Computational Analysis of Anomalous Luminous Phenomena from Consumer Video Captures
abstract: We present the Citizen Orb Photometry Pipeline (COPP), a standardized ten-step computational method for quantitative analysis of anomalous luminous phenomena (ALP) captured in consumer video recordings. The pipeline extracts frame-by-frame photometric measurements including centroid position, apparent size, peak and integrated intensity, RGB spectral channel decomposition, and derived metrics including blue excess, pulsation periodicity, and position discontinuities. title: Good performance of low-cost fast-response carbon dioxide sensor based on intercomparison with the standard eddy-covariance system
abstract: Abstract. Flux measurements have started to play an important role outside academia in assessing carbon sinks of different ecosystems and land-use types. If natural carbon solutions are to be deployed and monetized in carbon markets, more low-powered and low-cost flux systems should be deployed. There is a growing need for low-cost sensors that still fulfil the requirements for scientific applications. title: Conservation genetics of the spotted bat: Insights from ancient, historical, and modern samples
abstract: Spotted bats (Euderma maculatum) are cryptic (nocturnal, volant, and roost solitarily) and thus their biology remains largely undescribed. Only 35 specimens were known to science before the mid-1960s. Hence, they are ideal candidates for genetic studies to uncover population genetic diversity and structure, and thereby inform conservation. title: Three-Dimensional Geostatistical Inverse Modeling of Coupled Heat and Salt Tracer Tests Based on Mildly and Highly Heterogeneous Synthetic Fields
abstract: Accurate characterization of subsurface heterogeneity is essential for understanding groundwater flow and contaminant transport. However, the value of integrating multiple data and how it relates to heterogeneity requires further investigation. This study systematically evaluates individual and joint inversion of head, temperature and concentration data using mildly heterogeneous (MH) and highly heterogeneous (HH) synthetic fields. title: A self-adaptive fuzzy pitch control method for suppressing vibration of large-scale wind turbines under combined wind-seismic loading
abstract: Abstract For large-scale wind turbines subjected to sudden seismic excitation during operation, a self-adaptive fuzzy pitch (SFP) control method is proposed to mitigate the structural seismic response. The displacement and velocity of tower-top fore-aft (TTFA) are used as input variables for the fuzzy controller, and a self-adaptive proportional factor is established through an exponential function. title: Assessing earthquake potential and fault activity from a newly estimated high-resolution geodetic velocity field in Hispaniola
abstract: Abstract The transpressive plate boundary between the Caribbean and North American plates in Hispaniola is a complex system of strike-slip faults, subduction zones, fold-and-thrust belts, and normal faulting. Tectonic deformation studies in this region have traditionally relied on sparse Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) networks. Here we present a new assessment of deformation in Hispaniola using a dense 3D velocity field generated by integrating existing GNSS observations with new Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) velocities. The University of Texas at Dallas

title: Geochemical Profiling and Health Risk Assessment of Heavy Metals in Yemeni Bottled Water: A Multivariate Statistical Approach
abstract: Objectives The quality and safety of bottled drinking water are of growing concern in Yemen due to increasing dependence on groundwater resources and potential contamination by trace metals. This study presents an integrated secondary analysis of previously published inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) data to evaluate the concentrations of seven heavy metals (Hg, Cd, Cr, Ni, Al, Co, and Cu) in 27 bottled water brands marketed in Yemen, combining health risk assessment with multivariate statistical analysis. title: Comparative analysis of rainfall erosivity estimation approaches and temporal resolution effects: A critical review supported by an observational case study
abstract: Accurate estimation of the rainfall erosivity factor (R-factor) is fundamental for soil erosion prediction and informed land conservation. This study provides a comprehensive review of the historical evolution and current status of R-factor estimation, ranging from simplified empirical equations to complex process-based models. Special emphasis is placed on data requirements, model assumptions, and method transferability. title: Unveiling the spatiotemporal patterns and predictive associations of human settlement quality in the Hunan-Jiangxi peripheral region
abstract: Abstract Peripheral regions remain underrepresented in analyses of between-county disparities in human settlements. Using 24 counties in the Hunan-Jiangxi peripheral region, this study integrates Spatial Markov Chains (SMC), Boosted Regression Trees (BRT), and the Optimal Parameters-based Geographical Detector (OPGD) to examine HSQ patterns and predictive spatial associations in 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2022. title: From resilience to potential transition risk: Exploring the spatial dynamics of species diversity across multiple regimes
abstract: Arid and semi-arid regions, as complex social-ecological systems, are not static states but a landscape in a condition of continuous “transition,” in which biodiversity is constantly reorganized through the nonlinear interaction between environmental constraints and human pressures. This study aimed to uncover the dynamic patterns of species diversity, social-ecological resilience, and regime transition risk in an arid basin of Kerman Province, Iran. title: Imagens Mentais na Terapia do Esquema: uma revisão de escopo
abstract: A Terapia do Esquema (TE) utiliza imagens mentais como um recurso central na mediação entre cognição e emoção, facilitando o acesso a memórias emocionais implícitas e a modificação de esquemas iniciais desadaptativos. O presente estudo teve como objetivo analisar a produção científica acerca do uso de técnicas de imagens mentais na TE, mapeando suas características metodológicas, efeitos terapêuticos e áreas cerebrais implicadas. title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF RADAR SYSTEMS IN REGIONAL AVIATION: A CASE STUDY OF DEBLIN AIRFIELD
abstract: This article presents the results of an experimental study on the registration performance of two radar-based systems - GCA-2000 and AVIA-W - using flight operations between the regional airfields of Deblin and Radom as a case study. GPS satellite navigation data were employed as a reference source to enable both quantitative and spatiotemporal comparisons of radar registration characteristics. journal: Scientific Journal of Silesian University of Technology Series Transport

title: Increasing exposure to potential flooding in high-mountain catchments
abstract: Abstract Exposure to flood hazards in high mountain catchments is expected to increase alongside natural hazards, driven by climate change, glacier retreat, and landscape evolution, yet temporally consistent, high-resolution exposure data remain scarce. Here we quantify changes in the exposure of buildings and people to flooding in Nepal and transboundary regions of India and China. Validation against a manually derived reference dataset revealed considerable differences in accuracy and completeness across five building footprint products. title: Integrated Assessment of Groundwater Quality and Suitability for Drinking and Irrigation in the Nineveh Plain, Iraq.
abstract: Groundwater is the principal source of domestic and agricultural water supply in the Nineveh Plain, northern Iraq, where population growth, agricultural expansion, climate variability, and declining surface-water availability have increased pressure on groundwater resources. A study of the groundwater hydrochemistry, irrigation suitability, trace metal occurrence, and microbiological quality was conducted in the Al-Qosh and Tel-Kif area of the Nineveh Plain during summer 2025. institutions: IHE Delft Institute for Water Education

title: Artifact-to-True Seepage Detection in RGB Images Using CLIP Representations
abstract: Red-Green-Blue (RGB) vision based supervised learning is demonstrated for the purpose of identifying subsurface groundwater seepage for low-cost and accurate inspection of dams and slope embankments using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Supervised learning is constrained by the scarcity of confirmed true seepage-positive images. Our study investigates artifact-to-true seepage detection at the earliest intervention point. journal: Journal of Infrastructure Intelligence and Resilience

title: Embracing Zero Waste as a Critical Tool for Addressing Climate Change: A Cross‐National Analysis of Mitigation Evidence
abstract: Global waste generation has become an increasing environmental pressure of the twenty‐first century, with humanity now producing between 2.1 and 2.3 billion tons of municipal solid waste annually. Without intervention, this figure is projected to reach 3.8 billion tons by 2050. 1 The World Bank reports waste generation reached 2.56 billion tons in 2022—years ahead of projections—and could reach 3.86 billion tons by 2050 if trends continue. 2 The crisis is most severe in Sub‐Saharan Africa and South Asia, where waste is rising fastest and collection infrastructure is weakest.

title: Reliability gated cross-modal attention with shear reparameterized directional reasoning for RGB-thermal salient object detection
abstract: Abstract RGB-Thermal (RGB-T) salient object detection localizes salient regions where appearance cues alone are insufficient, since thermal radiation stays informative under poor illumination. Two limitations persist. Cross-modal attention is applied at a strength fixed in advance, so a momentarily uninformative stream continues to contribute in full, and directional reasoning is confined to the two image axes, because diagonal coverage has required a dense affinity mask of quadratic cost. title: Life-cycle incremental cost-benefit model for passive buildings and a case study in Zhejiang Province, China
abstract: Passive buildings (PBs) offer substantial advantages in reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, making their promotion a strategic priority for China’s carbon goals. However, high upfront costs, unclear long-term benefits, and long payback periods hinder adoption. This study develops a Life-Cycle Incremental Cost-Benefit Model (LCICBM) covering design, construction, and operation. The model quantifies and monetizes economic, environmental, and social benefits. title: Provenance-Aware Physics-Guided Feasibility-Region Learning for Pre-layout Two-Stage CMOS Op-Amp Sizing: A Calibration-Ready Workflow
abstract: Analog operational-amplifier sizing is a costly multi-objective search problem: transistor dimensions and bias conditions jointly determine gain, bandwidth, stability, slew rate, rejection ratios, common-mode range, power, and offset. This paper presents a provenance-aware, physics-guided feasibility-region learning workflow for a two-stage CMOS operational amplifier. title: A Multi‐Scale Collaborative Framework for Transforming Cultural Power in Traditional Villages Through Ecological Resilience: Evidence From Zhejiang Province, China
abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional villages are heritage settlements whose continuity depends on interactions among cultural practice, ecological condition and governance capacity. This study examined how cultural power and governance networks are associated with ecological resilience in nine traditional villages in Zhejiang Province, China. A mixed‐methods design combined remote‐sensing analysis, spatial overlay, social network modelling, cultural inventories, interviews and institutional document review. title: Sub‑chronic PFOA exposure at human‑relevant increasing doses in male mice: Role of stress‑induced gut barrier disruption in shaping intestinal and hepatic responses under high-dose conditions
abstract: In humans, dietary intake is thought to be the main route of exposure to perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The gastrointestinal tract is the primary entry point for this highly persistent and bioaccumulative environmental pollutant; however, its fate and effects within the digestive system remain largely unknown. Combining biology-based approaches with mass-spectrometry chemical imaging, our study investigated the impact of 90-day oral exposure to PFOA at a dose relevant to highly exposed human populations on an intact versus stress-impaired gut barrier in adult male mice. title: Thermal Shifts Dominate Single‐Gene Responses to Transcription‐Targeting Antibiotics
abstract: ABSTRACT Combined exposure to thermal and antibiotic stresses is ubiquitous. How cells adapt to these concurrent cues at the single‐gene level remains unresolved. Here, we show that in Escherichia coli , both cold and heat shock responses dominate antibiotic stress responses across multiple levels of physiology. Using RNA‐seq, we demonstrate that combined exposure produces transcriptomes that are largely indistinguishable from those induced by thermal shifts alone. title: A prototype multi-hazard early warning system integrating flood and landslide forecasting: application in the upper Garonne River Basin
abstract: Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (MHEWS) are essential for disaster risk management, yet operational implementation remains limited by challenges in hazard integration, forecast uncertainty, and computational requirements. This study develops and evaluates a fast and lightweight prototype MHEWS integrating fluvial flooding and shallow landslide forecasting. The MHEWS couples snow-hydrological modeling (SNOW-17 and CREST) with a slope stability approach (infinite slope and Random Forest models) driven by bias-corrected Global Ensemble Forecast System (GEFS) meteorological forecasts. title: Patrón multivariado de la cobertura arbórea en un relicto de bosque seco tropical del CURDN, Armero-Guayabal (Colombia)
abstract: Esta investigación evalúa variables ambientales y dasométricas para identificar un patrón multivariado de la cobertura arbórea con diámetro normal ≥ 5 cm en un relicto ribereño de bosque seco tropical (bs-T), ubicado en el Centro Universitario Regional del Norte de la Universidad del Tolima (Colombia), sobre la quebrada La Zorra, afluente del río Sabandija. title: Extreme Rainfall Modeling Using the Generalized Extreme Value Distribution for r-Largest Order Statistics
abstract: Heavy rainfall is a major driver of floods, flash floods, and landslides, significantly impacting lives, property, and infrastructure. These risks are intensifying under climate change, which increases both the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall events. This study analyzed the characteristics and assessed the risk of maximum daily cumulative rainfall in Thailand using the Generalized Extreme Value for the r-largest order statistics (GEVr) model. title: Diversity and disparity in mammalian fossil assemblages of the John Day Formation, Oregon, USA
abstract: Abstract The John Day Formation offers a remarkably complete terrestrial record of Eocene-, Oligocene-, and Miocene-aged mammalian faunas in central Oregon. Sites in the John Day Formation have yielded numerous mammalian species spanning across many taxonomic orders, offering a unique opportunity to closely examine changes in mammalian diversity and disparity across a geographically constrained region. title: Average Temperature Trends and Rainfall patterns within Jere Local Government Area of Kaduna State, Northwest-Nigeria: A Case from 1989 to 2018
abstract: The Average Temperature Trends and rainfall patterns within Jere local government area of Kaduna State, Nigeria have been studied from 1989 to 2018. The results revealed a significant increase in annual rainfall from 1989 to 2018, with an annual trend of +143.26 mm/year. Rainfall ranged from 739.40 mm in 2008 to 1779.31 mm in 2018, with an average of 1267.61 mm, revealing the inter-annual variability nature within the study area. title: Detection of Personal Privacy Information in Social Data Taking Into Account Data Augmentation and Mask R‐ CNN
abstract: ABSTRACT Visual privacy‐sensitive objects in social images are often small, partially occluded, and unevenly represented in available training data, which limits the reliability of automatic privacy detection. This study develops a privacy‐sensitive object detection framework combining multi‐strategy image augmentation with SE‐Mask R‐CNN. title: Plateau–Rayleigh Instability–Driven Shell-First Growth of (Ge, Si1– x Ge x )–AlN Core–Shell Crystals Exhibiting Telecom E-Band Photoluminescence
abstract: Abstract Si and Ge are technologically important semiconductors for electronic, photovoltaic, and optoelectronic applications. Herein, we report mixed-source hydride vapor phase epitaxial growth of (Ge, Si1–xGex)–AlN core–shell crystals on Al-based nanoabsorbers. Nano-CT and microscopy resolve hollow, partially filled, and filled morphologies that together support a Plateau–Rayleigh-instability-mediated shell-first model in which an Al-derived shell-like structure precedes filling by Ge-containing or Si–Ge-containing material. title: Quantum collapse mutation-based Salp Swarm Algorithm (QCM-SSA) for spatial alliance of point clouds
abstract: The consistency of the metaphor approaches is crucial in attaining reliable and optimal solutions in multifaceted computational engineering and optimization processes. Although the Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) has earned recognition owing to its simplicity and efficiency, it often incurs from premature convergence in complicated and multi-modal settings. This constraint becomes especially crucial for tasks needing precision, such as 3D point cloud registration (PCR), where the confined minima may impede the fine spatial alignment of the point clouds. title: Future Extreme Climatic Events May Reshape Butterfly Distributions Across Biomes in Italy
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Extreme climatic events (ECEs) are increasingly recognized as major drivers of insect declines, yet remain rarely incorporated into biodiversity projections. Butterflies may be especially sensitive to prolonged ECEs because they are short‐lived ectotherms, while voltinism can influence their capacity to absorb climatic shocks. We assessed how the frequency of prolonged ECEs may reshape butterfly climatic suitability and richness patterns across Italy and whether responses vary among biomes and voltinism classes. title: Advancing wildlife image analysis: A Graph Attention Contrastive Learning approach for region‐specific mammal classification
abstract: Abstract Camera traps have become a cornerstone of wildlife ecology research, yet manually analysing the millions of images they generate requires substantial time and resources. Deep learning‐based automation has emerged as a promising solution. Existing global general‐purpose models, however, exhibit limitations in precisely recognizing local endemic species and adapting to unique local ecosystems. title: Conceptualizing a Building Passport: A Proposal regarding the Definition and Scope through a Delphi Study
abstract: The construction industry is among the most resource-intensive sectors, contributing substantially to global resource consumption. In light of the escalating scarcity of natural resources, the circular economy (CE) paradigm offers a promising avenue for the recovery and reuse of raw materials. In order to achieve this objective, it is essential to establish a reliable information base that encompasses both semantic and geometric building data throughout the entire life cycle of a building. title: Regeneración natural de plantas leñosas en el bosque mesófilo de montaña del volcán Nevado de Colima, México
abstract: La regeneración natural es fundamental en la dinámica de los ecosistemas forestales y su comprensión contribuye al diseño de prácticas de conservación, restauración y silvicultura. En 3 localidades del Parque Estatal Bosque Mesófilo del Nevado de Colima, México, se evaluaron la composición, diversidad y estructura de la regeneración natural de plantas leñosas con altura ≥ 10 cm y diámetro normal ≤ 2.5 cm, así como los factores ambientales que influyen en su distribución y abundancia. title: Global disaster risk assessment from Emergency Events Database (2013–2023)
abstract: Abstract. This paper defines an Accumulated Risk Index (ARI) to quantify regional risk levels in a global perspective utilizing Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT) from 2013 to 2023. Building on the World Risk Index (WRI) released from World Risk Report 2023, the ARI focuses more on major events caused by multiple natural hazards within 5°×5° latitude-longitude grids, and calculates their accumulative effects during the period. title: Spatial-Temporal Assessment of Air Pollutants and Environmental Quality in Nashik District: Evaluating the Influence of Electric Vehicle Adoption
abstract: Urban air pollution is a growing environmental concern in rapidly expanding cities due to increasing vehicular emissions, industrial activities and urbanization. The transition toward electric vehicles (EVs) has emerged as a promising strategy for reducing transportation-related emissions and improving urban environmental quality. This study evaluates environmental changes associated with EV adoption in Nashik city, Maharashtra, through the development of an Environmental Pollution Index (EPI) using the Analytic Hierarchy Process integrated with Geographic Information System techniques. title: Adaptive neuro-fuzzy risk index for safe and interpretable lane-change decisions in Level-3 autonomous driving
abstract: Introduction Highway lane-change maneuvers pose a safety challenge for SAE Level 3 autonomous driving because conventional threshold-based decisions and isolated surrogate safety measures may inadequately capture the coupling between longitudinal braking demand and evolving inter-vehicle gaps. This study develops an interpretable, risk-aware framework for continuous lane-change assessment during maneuver initiation and execution. title: Characterizing variability and change in European river basins using network-science metrics and nonlinear dynamical systems techniques
abstract: Abstract Hydrology and water resources demand robust, scalable analyses of river‐basin dynamics to inform policy. Network science offers a compact language for such systems—capturing inequality, connectivity, accessibility, and redundancy. In this study, we model European rivers as dynamic, flow-weighted graphs across 30 basins during 1992–2024. Beyond simple linear trends, we pair network metrics with nonlinear, data-driven windowing to uncover periodic structure and time-localized instabilities. title: Insights into life cycle assessment and rapid removal of malachite green by biochar derived from shrimp shell and sheep manure
abstract: Malachite green (MG) contamination of water resources poses significant ecological and human-health risks, while the environmental sustainability of its treatment strategies has rarely been evaluated. This study addresses this critical gap by integrating the synthesis of hybrid biochar from sheep manure and shrimp shells at a 2:1 ratio for MG removal with a comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA). title: Economic Losses Associated With Tropical Cyclones in Mexico: A Two-stage Model
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) are among the primary drivers of disaster declarations in Mexico, causing substantial economic losses. This study assesses reported TC-related economic losses in Mexican states from (Funk 1980 ) to 2023 and identifies the hazard and socioeconomic determinants of both the probability of loss occurrence and loss magnitude. title: Glacial lake outburst flood hazard and downstream impacts: lessons from Afghanistan examples
abstract: Abstract Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) pose a growing risk in high mountain regions as climate-driven glacier retreat accelerates lake expansion and new lake formation. In the Hindu Kush Himalaya, particularly in Afghanistan, triggering processes and GLOF propagation downstream are largely unstudied. This study evaluates two Afghanistan GLOFs (Peshghor 2018; Bam-Tanab 2021) using field observations and satellite imagery, and applies two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulation (BASEMENT-MD with BASEbreach) to the Kunj-Peshghor lake event to assess flood propagation, dam-breach dynamics, and

title: Study on Students' Exercise Load Monitoring in PE Classroom Based on the Fusion of FedAvg and Grey Relationship Analysis
abstract: Real time observation of students' exercise load is very important for scientific sports teaching and injury prevention. However, the traditional centralized monitoring paradigm faces significant privacy challenges when it processes highly sensitive physiological and biological characteristics. At the same time, existing federated learning algorithms often degrade global model performance due to "client drift" arising from Non-IID data caused by individual differences among students. title: NeuPlume: generative inversion of atmospheric point-source emissions from sparse observations
abstract: Abstract. Inverting point-source emissions from sparse atmospheric observations is difficult because emission rate, release height, wind speed, turbulence, and plume morphology can compensate for one another. We present NeuPlume, a neural-physical probabilistic inversion framework that returns an ensemble of data-compatible plume fields rather than a single point estimate. title: Assessment of compressive characteristics of coir fiber-reinforced concrete modified with wheat straw ash using predictive modeling
abstract: The growing demand for environmentally responsible construction materials requires reliable tools to predict the compressive strength of concrete incorporating agricultural waste and natural fibers. This study investigates the prediction of compressive strength of sustainable concrete incorporating wheat straw ash (WSA) and coir fiber (CF) using explainable ensemble machine learning. A database of 361 concrete mixtures was compiled from published experimental studies, considering cement, WSA, fine aggregate, coarse aggregate, water, superplasticizer, CF, and curing age as input variables. title: Forward self-similar solutions to the MHD-Boussinesq system with Newtonian gravitational field
abstract: This paper is concerned with the existence of forward self-similar solutions to the three-dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic-Boussinesq (MHD-Boussinesq) system with a Newtonian gravitational field. By employing a blow-up argument and the Leray-Schauder theorem, we construct a forward self-similar solution to this system without imposing any smallness assumptions on the self-similar initial value.

title: Unsupervised learning for detection of defects during machining of additively manufactured components
abstract: Detection of defects such as porosities is important in additive manufacturing to ensure the desired material properties. Most additively manufactured components require finish machining to achieve the desired surface finish and geometric tolerances. This paper presents an unsupervised machine learning approach using an autoencoder to detect defects during the machining of additively manufactured components. This work reports a sustainable strategy for the development of highly efficient copper-based nanoparticles supported on lignosulfonate and magnetite or maghemite cores. The degassing process observed here is widely recognized as the surface manifestation of the interaction between mantle-derived CO 2 and a complex shallow fracture network. The hazardous conditions surrounding the main emission vents limit conventional ground-based geophysical surveys, making an accurate reconstruction of the geometry and spatial distribution of the local fracture system particularly challenging. abstract: The Stoniness of Molloy’s Anxiety: An Attempted Petrification in Samuel Beckett’s Molloy. abstract: A hierarchical nonlinear control benchmark is presented for gust load alleviation (GLA) and maneuver load alleviation (MLA) in a highly flexible winged UAV. abstract: Abstract. Great Britain’s variable maritime climate has until relatively recently limited the utility of seasonal hydrological forecasts. The latest generations of seasonal atmospheric forecasting systems have created new opportunities to improve flow forecasting across Great Britain, such as for the UK Hydrological Outlook. abstract: Human populations across Eurasia have long been connected through the steppe corridor and Silk Road, yet their paternal genetic history remains poorly understood. abstract: Cryptography is essential in many digital fields to provide information security and confidentiality. abstract: Mountain ecosystems are functionally diverse and have concentrated environmental gradients. Exploring the changing characteristics and trade-offs of ecosystem services (ESs) under different environmental gradients is beneficial to the conservation and sustainable use of mountain resources. This study evaluated the spatial-temporal changes of habitat quality (HQ), soil conservation (SC), water yield (WY), water purification (N output load) and net primary productivity (NPP) in the Qilian Mountains from 2000 to 2018, and analyzed their responses to environmental gradients. title: Forest loss is increasingly driven by international consumption
abstract: Deforestation remains one of the greatest obstacles to limiting global warming, yet the economic mechanisms linking global supply chains to final consumers are poorly understood. Fine-scale satellite monitoring tracks where forests are lost, but rarely reveals who ultimately drives this loss through consumption. We further apply machine learning techniques to identify key socioeconomic drivers behind consumption-induced forest loss. abstract: Abstract Bedload transport widely occurs in natural environments and encompasses flow regimes from saltation to sheet‐flow, with markedly different fluid‐particle interaction characteristics. abstract: Plastics are widely used as food contact materials, which have the potential to release microplastics (MPs), nanoplastics (NPs), and plastic-associated organic and inorganic chemicals into foodstuffs, thereby posing a potential risk to human health. abstract: Capsicum, often known as sweet pepper (Capsicum annuum var. grossum L.), is becoming more and more popular in Bangladesh as a vegetable. abstract: Abstract In response to the insufficient conformability, limited grasping stability, and low force threshold of existing magnetically driven grippers for highly curved and fragile workpieces, this study proposes a magnetically actuated adaptive gripper that integrates spring-based energy storage and magnetorheological particle blocking. abstract: Satellite image classification plays an important role in various applications like monitoring, surveillance, land cover planning, etc. Deep learning models with many learnable parameters face overfitting as model depth increases and have struggled to extract both fine details and broader patterns simultaneously. abstract: This study presents a Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) of a turbulent, globally rich, premixed NH 3 /H 2 /N 2 –air slot flame at 25 bar, representative of partially cracked ammonia combustion. title: A modular framework for quantifying the impact of multi-domain modelling assumptions on urban building energy demand
abstract: Urban Building Energy Modelling (UBEM) is an established approach for evaluating urban energy demand and informing infrastructure planning and policy. However, UBEM workflows often rely on simplified modelling assumptions and input representations that overlook evolving urban and climate conditions. This study presents a modular multi-domain framework that quantifies the impact of three urban factors on energy demand: urban context, climate variability (including site-specific monitored weather and future weather projections), and electric vehicle (EV) adoption. abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) systems are among the most promising renewable energy sources, yet their efficiency is critically compromised under partial shading conditions (PSC). abstract: Abstract Understanding how fire activity reorganizes across space is key to interpreting long-term interactions among climate variability, land-use change, and integrated fire management in Brazil. abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the performance of an open fan operating in the high subsonic flight regime, with emphasis on the interaction between the blades and the nacelle and its impact on thrust, drag and overall efficiency. Strong spatial gradients in static pressure induced by the curved geometry of the nacelle can locally accelerate or diffuse the flow over rotor and stator blades. abstract: Clean electricity production has become a major focus in recent years due to the rise in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions annually. abstract: This study examines the impacts of climate change on blue water flow (BWF), green water storage (GWS), and green water flow (GWF) components of water resources in the Tekeze Atbara watershed of the Nile basin. abstract: Stone crushing and mining activities in the Brahmani-Dwarka interfluve have significantly contributed to environmental degradation, emphasising the need to assess their impact on environmental quality. abstract: Photodetectors (PDs), which are core components of modern optoelectronic systems, are widely used in medical diagnostics and biosensing. abstract: This study addresses a critical need in regional development planning by combining aspatial biclustering with spatial autocorrelation analysis to examine European industrial competitiveness. abstract: Rapid growth in satellite deployments has transformed Earth orbit from a sparse operational environment into a continuously negotiated shared domain. Space situational awareness (SSA) is therefore indispensable but incomplete: it provides probabilistic knowledge of orbital conditions but does not yet constitute a traffic management regime capable of ensuring consistent, system-level predictability. abstract: Introduction Remote maritime operations increasingly depend on complex, distributed socio-technical systems in which safe and effective performance relies on team cognition rather than on individual decision-making alone. Despite its importance, the conceptualisation and measurement of team cognition in this domain remain fragmented and underdeveloped. title: Pathways for carbon management in the cement industry in a carbon neutral energy system with focus on Baden-Württemberg
abstract: Reducing CO 2 emissions from the cement industry is challenging because a large share of the emissions arises from core chemical processes, and the further handling of the CO 2 depends highly on regional CO 2 storage availability. We provide the first quantitative, system-wide comparison of oxygen-from-electrolysis, CO₂ grid, and flexible grinding for cement decarbonisation, based on an endogenous linear optimisation model quantifying the system-cost and technology-mix implications. title: Agrivoltaic systems can improve agricultural yield by mitigating extreme plant temperatures
abstract: Agriculture suffers from more intense, prolonged, and frequent extreme temperature events such as heat waves, droughts, and frosts. Agrivoltaic systems offer an opportunity to mitigate such events by deploying photovoltaic (PV) panels above crops. In this study, measurements of plant, air, and soil temperatures, along with solar and infrared radiation, wind speed, and soil moisture demonstrate that plants benefit from cooler microclimates beneath PV panels during extreme heat events, and conversely from warmer microclimates during cold nights. abstract: Food-hydrocolloid performance depends on polymer architecture and processing history rather than ingredient name alone. This critical narrative review evaluates CAZyme-guided modification of cactus-derived pectic materials and related regional polysaccharides for food hydrocolloid applications. Opuntia mucilage and pectic fractions are the focal substrates; non-cactus pectins provide the closest mechanistic evidence, and arabinoxylan is retained only as a bounded comparison for substitution and oxidative crosslinking. title: Signatures of photospheric convection throughout the solar atmosphere: the EVE Sun-as-a-star mHz continuum
abstract: Abstract Convectively driven motions in the solar photosphere can generate broadband Doppler variability across the chromosphere, transition region and corona. Here we investigate this variability using “Sun-as-a-Star” observations from the Extreme Ultraviolet Variability Experiment (EVE) aboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory, constructing high signal-to-noise Doppler power spectra by incoherently averaging spectra from 3-hour sequences of the centroid wavelengths of emission lines that span wavelengths 35–104 nm. title: Risk-aware hierarchical reinforcement learning for investment and operations in cross-border energy supply chains under the belt and road initiative
abstract: Abstract Cross-border energy supply chains under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) face unprecedented challenges, including geopolitical instability, macroeconomic volatility, and operational disruptions. Traditional optimization or flat reinforcement learning (RL) methods often struggle to address the scale, uncertainty, and multi-stakeholder complexity inherent in such environments. title: Path deviation control for multi-UAV cooperative task execution based on laser vision guidance and trajectory prediction
abstract: This paper proposes a path deviation control method that integrates laser vision guidance and trajectory prediction to address deviations caused by limited environmental perception in multi-drone cooperative tasks. title: GeoCaseRec: a knowledge graph semantics-driven framework for sustainable urban renewal recommendation
abstract: As urbanisation shifts from outward expansion to the regeneration of existing built environments, sustainable urban renewal increasingly depends on the effective reuse of historical cases. However, this remains constrained by fragmented multi-source geo-referenced data, semantic heterogeneity, and limited case evaluation. title: Can the digital economy enhance urban ecological environment resilience?
abstract: Based on city-level panel data of China from 2006 to 2022, this study develops comprehensive indicator system for urban ecological environment resilience, and derives the composite development index of urban ecological environment resilience via the entropy method. title: A global base temperature dataset for residential building energy demand modelling
abstract: Abstract. Accurate building energy demand modeling is critical to decarbonizing regional energy systems. The cooling and heating degree-day models are widely used due to their simplicity and low data requirements; however, the lack of accurate base temperature data limits their performance. In particular, the scarcity of high temporal resolution building energy demand data constrains regional-scale base temperature estimation through conventional methods such as the energy signature method and the performance line method. title: Additive manufacturing of superelastic NiTi braided metamaterials: an innovative strategy for engineering minimally invasive vascular medical devices
abstract: Additive manufacturing of superelastic Nitinol (NiTi) braided metamaterials is demonstrated in this study, enabling the creation of a wide variety of concepts for personalized vascular medical devices. Engineering contributions include the algorithmic design of lattices and woven structures, which can be adjusted to anatomical surfaces and whose mechanical properties can be controlled by design, enabling functional gradients of stiffness and transitions between lattices and wovens, as well as the creation of fully-connected braided structures achieved in a single printing step. title: Predicting cultivation probability to target monitoring in smallholder landscapes: Proof of concept from dispersed medicinal plant cultivation in Taihe County, China
abstract: Dispersed medicinal plant cultivation by smallholder farmers presents a monitoring challenge that differs fundamentally from conventional agricultural monitoring: fragmented fields, mixed spectra, and canopy occlusion make direct detection difficult, while exhaustive field surveys are prohibitively costly. title: Staged digital transformation and firms’ total factor productivity: evidence from Chinese cultural firms
abstract: This study explores the effects of digital transformation (DT) on firms’ total factor productivity (TFP) across the digital technology application (DTA) stage and digital business model innovation (DBMI) stage. Using a sample of 245 Chinese listed cultural firms from 2011 to 2022, we examine how DT impacts TFP differently across these stages. abstract: ABSTRACT Fuel cells represent the core components of next‐generation high‐efficiency electrochemical energy conversion technologies. The performance of the cathode oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalyst determines battery efficiency and lifespan. title: Wind gusts prediction using multivariate time series classification
abstract: Wind speed intermittency is a key challenge for integrating wind energy into the energy mix. Accurate wind power forecasting in wind farms is crucial for mitigating this issue. A major source of uncertainty in nowcasting and short-term wind power prediction arises from wind gusts. At very short timescales (seconds), gusts impact turbine stability and loads, while at longer scales (hours), they significantly affect wind speed and power prediction accuracy. title: Indicators from fish habitat time series for climate change and environmental flows assessment
abstract: Mediterranean rivers are exposed to climate-driven hydrological change, yet environmental-flow assessment relies on static habitat metrics that poorly represent fish habitat variability over time. We developed a time-explicit framework that converts monthly weighted usable area (WUA) series into indicators of the magnitude, variability, duration, frequency and persistence of limiting physical habitat conditions. abstract: The pursuit of socioeconomic development, food security, and ecological sustainability has driven the multifunctional evolution of cultivated land. Under the constraint of limited cultivated land resources, achieving synergy among the economic, food security, and ecological functions of cultivated land has become a major challenge for agricultural modernization in Sichuan Province. abstract: Introduction Climate policy uncertainty can affect long-term investment decisions in agriculture, yet its influence on agricultural digital-intelligent transformation remains insufficiently understood. This study examines how lagged climate policy uncertainty affects agricultural digital-intelligent transformation and whether rural finance and agricultural service policies can moderate this relationship. abstract: Low nitrogen use efficiency of prilled urea contributes to substantial economic loss and environmental pollution through leaching, denitrification, and ammonia volatilization. This study evaluated urea-loaded nanoclay biopolymer composites (NCBPCs), synthesized from clay-acrylic acid + aczrylamide-based polymer composite grafted with maize flour (NCBPC-M) and mango kernel flour (NCBPC-MK), integrated with phosphorus- and zinc-solubilizing bacteria ( Lactococcus lactis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ), as a sustainable alternative nitrogen source in a maize–wheat cropping system. title: Cloud computing and global satellite products for potential groundwater recharge estimation: application to the Basin of Mexico
abstract: Groundwater recharge (GWr) estimation is fundamental for assessing aquifer storage changes, ensuring groundwater sustainability, and supporting effective water management. However, regional groundwater recharge assessment remains challenging because it requires integrating large geospatial datasets, computational resources, and hydrogeological information that are often unavailable in data-limited regions. abstract: The transition of urban energy systems toward sustainability and smartness depends on effective policy design. Despite significant scholarly attention, research remains fragmented across policy instruments, system components, and analytical perspectives. To address these limitations, this study presents an integrated framework that combines a PRISMA-guided systematic review, artificial intelligence-assisted topic modeling (BERTopic), and Multi-Level Perspective (MLP) transition theory. title: Molecular detection and characterization of flea-associated bacteria: genetic diversity and co-occurrence patterns involving Bartonella, Rickettsia, and Wolbachia in Ctenocephalides felis felis from an Atlantic Forest region of Brazil
abstract: Ctenocephalides felis felis is a widespread ectoparasite of dogs and cats and has been associated with transmission of several microorganisms of veterinary and public health relevance. This study investigated the molecular occurrence, genetic diversity, and co-occurrence patterns of Bartonella spp., Rickettsia spp., and Wolbachia spp. in fleas collected from dogs and cats in an Atlantic Forest area encompassing the Ilhéus and Itabuna microregions, Bahia State, northeastern Brazil. abstract: BACKGROUND: Prenatal cannabis exposure is associated with adverse offspring outcomes including altered neurodevelopment. This contrasts with the widespread multi-nutrient limitations of highly weathered soils, which may restrict the effectiveness of N-only fertilization. abstract: Abstract. Ocean waves erode the waterline of Antarctic ice-shelf fronts and carve a thermo-erosional notch. abstract: Color enhancement of 4K images must meet a quality target under a tight compute budget. Three-dimensional lookup tables (3D LUTs) dominate real-time enhancement because they decide at low resolution and apply a per-pixel lookup at full resolution. abstract: In atmospheric neutrino analyses, the usable zenith-angle range is generally restricted to upward-going events to suppress the cosmic-ray muon background. Together with the known ill-posedness results for $0\leqα<1$, this establishes the sharp dissipation threshold for large-data global well-posedness in the corresponding solution framework. abstract: We report the measurement of the $^{39}$Ar specific activity of atmospheric argon using DArT, a low-background single-phase liquid-argon detector read out by cryogenic silicon photomultipliers, at the Canfranc Underground Laboratory (LSC) in Spain. DArT was first filled with atmospheric argon and then with a sample of underground argon of known radioactivity from the DarkSide-50 experiment. abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents face critical privacy risks when acting as delegates in human-agent-human communication. title: The TIB Terminology Service and Its Terminology Collection for the Earth System Sciences
abstract: Advancing Earth System Sciences (ESS) depends on our ability to integrate highly diverse data from a range of disciplines, including geographical information sciences, palaeontology, marine science, biodiversity research, atmospheric sciences and biology. A major scientific obstacle to this integration is semantic heterogeneity: different disciplines use different methods and terms to describe data, resulting in fragmented vocabularies. abstract: Sustained, high-resolution ocean observation is essential for understanding how marine ecosystems respond to climate variability, human pressure, and conservation action. abstract: Coral reef ecosystems face cumulative pressures from ocean warming, ocean acidification and diverse coastal human disturbances. abstract: This study assessed fisherfolk perceptions of coastal resource importance, the perceived condition of resources in Mati’s coastal barangays, differences in views across demographic profiles, existing management practices, and implications for the Coastal Resource Management Program (CRMP).
