abstract: Southeast Asia is a hotspot for azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus yet remains underrepresented in global surveillance. We outline a One Health attribution framework linking selection pressures, environmental reservoirs, exposure pathways, and clinical resistance signals to prioritise surveillance, target interventions, and allocate resources where they will have greatest impact.

abstract: Boreal forests account for 11.5% of the Earth's land area, and, unlike oceanic and mediterranean forests, their cold winters typically represent the harshest season for earthworms. In Fennoscandia, these forests are subject to substantial global changes, notably climate change and land use intensification, which might impact earthworm populations. At the same time, they are also exhibiting a unique, post‐glacial recolonisation of earthworms, as the last glaciation maximum resulted in a tabula rasa of earthworm species. title: E. coli and total coliform presence in private drinking water wells on Maryland farms: Determination of the impact of well properties, geographic, and precipitation factors
abstract: Over 43 million individuals in the United States use private wells for drinking water, but these wells are not regulated by the Safe Drinking Water Act. Unmaintained private wells on farms could become contaminated from pathogens from various potential sources including on-farm animal waste. Microbial contaminants in private wells could increase infectious disease risks among well users, therefore it is important to conduct well water testing and keep a well maintained system. title: Making living infrastructure legible: Patricia Johanson’s legacy for water-centered nature-based solutions
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NBS) are increasingly advanced as responses to climate change, urban flooding, water pollution, biodiversity loss, and declining ecosystem resilience. Yet their evaluation often gives less attention to the cultural, educational, and experiential conditions through which ecological functions become publicly understood and maintained. title: How to address challenges in the life cycle assessment of innovative cropping systems: Insights from a comparative study of a pesticide-free and a conventional system
abstract: CONTEXT Understanding environmental impacts of innovative cropping systems is integral to their development process. The most common method used for this purpose is life cycle assessment (LCA). However, several methodological challenges complicate the reliable application of LCA to such systems. OBJECTIVE This study critically reflects on six methodological challenges in the LCA of innovative cropping systems. title: Accelerated weathering of limestone for CO 2 capture and storage: a critical review of unbuffered, buffered, and modified pathways
abstract: Accelerated weathering of limestone (AWL) converts CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate by reacting calcium carbonate and water, an alternative to geological storage. This review examines AWL as a branching family spanning the unbuffered concept, buffered AWL (BAWL), and modified routes (potable-water, construction-grade waste limestone, promoter-assisted, utilization-based, ship-based, and electrochemical AWL), grouped into six classes covering reactor configuration, feedstock, dissolution promotion, effluent conditioning, downstream utilization, and electrochemically driven alkalinity generation.

title: Right on time: evaluating accuracy and timing of burn-severity assessments to support post-fire management
abstract: Abstract Effective post-fire management – including flood mitigation, revegetation, and salvage logging – depends on timely and reliable burn-severity assessments that characterize impacts to vegetation and soils. These assessments are typically derived from satellite-based change detection but can be delayed or degraded by aerosols (i.e., dust or smoke), clouds, and snow. abstract: Purpose: This study evaluated five publicly available large language model-based systems using a multidimensional, expert-based assessment of consensus-based clinical questions on bone stress injuries. Methods: Ten standardised questions derived from a 2025 international Delphi consensus on bone stress injuries were submitted to ChatGPT-5, Perplexity AI, Claude 4, Google Gemini 2.5 and Microsoft Copilot. title: Occurrence and human health implications of organochlorine pesticides in Nile tilapia from Al Massira Reservoir (Morocco) across consumer groups

title: Experimental data integration with fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making framework for matrix material selection of 2XXX series aluminium alloys
abstract: Matrix material selection for engineering purposes presents difficulties because specific requirements in economic, physical, mechanical, and thermal terms are not always compatible in the face of uncertainty in decision-making. While prior studies have employed Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) models for material selection, most studies are concerned with reinforcement selection, achieving composite optimization, or knowing the rank of a certain material. title: TRENDS IN DIVERSITY, SIZE, AND COMPLEXITY OF TRIASSIC FORAMINIFERA
abstract: Trends in the diversity, size, and complexity of Triassic foraminifera were studied. Diversity was calculated as the number of species and as standing diversity. Maximum linear dimensions were taken as approximations of size. As per complexity, foraminifera were graded based on test architecture and wall features. Foraminiferal diversity continually increased through the Triassic, but at a slower pace after the middle Anisian. The lower size limit of foraminifera does not change. title: Eleven tenets for the integrated, evolving and sustainable management of European Research Infrastructure Consortia
abstract: Research Infrastructures are increasingly central to scientific discovery, innovation and evidence-informed policy, but their management requires the integration of many dimensions that are often treated separately. This paper proposes an eleven-tenet framework for the integrated, evolving and sustainable management of European Research Infrastructure Consortia, extending existing tenet-based approaches by adding the explicit dimension of enabling scientific excellence. title: Novel Occurrence of Breeding Second-Year Gyrfalcons Suggests Elevated Mortality in Alaska
abstract: La presencia de individuos sub-adultos en una población reproductora de rapaces por lo demás estable suele considerarse un posible indicador de cambios en la demografía poblacional o de declive de la población. Como parte de un proyecto de monitoreo e investigación en curso en el oeste de Alaska, realizamos censos aéreos de rapaces que nidifican en paredes rocosas entre 2005–2025 en 550–850 sitios por año, e instalamos cámaras activadas por movimiento en 92 territorios ocupados por Falco rusticolus entre 2014 y 2025. abstract: Abstract Detecting sand beds in laboratory sediment experiments is challenging, especially when artificial vegetation or other structures are present. RGB‐D cameras offer fast, high‐resolution, and low‐cost sand bed reconstruction. However, the commonly applied Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM)‐based approaches for RGB‐D data often fail on the flat and textureless sand surfaces with artificial structures, due to difficulties in RGB‐D‐based camera pose optimization. abstract: The role of Cabinet in the implementation of fisheries legislation and the promulgation of regulations relating to fishery-related offences remains under-studied. This is a global phenomenon and entails instances where the relevant Minister promulgates regulations for the outlawing of fishery-related activities that are not sanctioned by law. abstract: Introduction: This paper explores the intersection of ecopreneurship and sustainable business practices through the lens of Northeast Indian literature. Northeast Indian literature skillfully intertwines themes of ecopreneurship and sustainable business practices, showcasing the area's vibrant cultural heritage and profound relationship with nature. abstract: Abstrak: Artikel bertujuan menganalisis bagaimana Detik.com mengonstruksi resistensi masyarakat dan negosiasi keadilan ekologis dalam pemberitaan penolakan tambang pasir di Desa Bababinanga, Kabupaten Pinrang, Sulawesi Selatan. title: To release or not to release? Understanding sawfish release behavior in a global south complex fishery
abstract: Abstract What socio‐economic, cultural, subjective, or institutional factors might motivate a socially marginalized, economically constrained fisher to voluntarily release a highly valuable catch such as a sawfish? This study looked at fishers' attitudes (ability, willingness, and challenges) toward the live release of Critically Endangered sawfish in Bangladesh. The study findings revealed that while goodwill and cultural beliefs were found to encourage live release, the most frequently mentioned challenges were financial loss, fear of injury, and unintentional gear entanglement among others.

abstract: Sustainable local economic development at the village level requires a balance between community welfare, environmental protection, and effective local governance. In Madura, the utilization of natural resources remains insufficiently aligned with environmental carrying capacity, creating challenges for achieving sustainable village development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). abstract: Sathurukondan wetland in the Batticaloa District contains valuable mangrove resources, yet baseline ecological information remains rather scarce. This study assessed mangrove vegetation from May to October 2023, focusing on species distribution, abundance, and diversity. A total of 59 line transects and 99 quadrats were established to compile a species checklist and evaluate community structure using diversity indices such as the Shannon–Wiener index, Pielou’s evenness, and Margalef richness. title: Biodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Development in the Niger Delta: Community Participation, Environmental Governance, and the Road to Achieving the SDGs 2030
abstract: The Niger Delta region of Nigeria represents one of the most ecologically significant yet environmentally vulnerable ecosystems globally. Since the onset of oil and gas exploration in the 1950s, the region has experienced severe environmental degradation manifested through oil spills, gas flaring, deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and declining fish populations. These anthropogenic activities have led to biodiversity loss, compromised ecosystem services, and heightened socio-economic vulnerabilities among local communities. abstract: Baleen whale strandings are rare in the southern Gulf of Mexico and can provide valuable molecular information where species are infrequently documented. We analyzed tissue from a highly decomposed whale stranded on the central coast of Veracruz, Mexico, by amplifying and bidirectionally sequencing the mitochondrial DNA control region. abstract: This desk-review article examines the ecological damage and lost investment opportunities associated with the prevailing economic paradigm. It proposes Return on Environment (RoEn) as a complement to Return on Investment (ROI) for evaluating and encouraging regenerative, nature-positive investment. The global economy has transgressed seven of nine planetary boundaries, while more than half of global gross domestic product depends moderately or highly on nature. title: Place-based climate adaptation: How Atlantic Canadian communities translate local knowledge into action
abstract: This study examines how communities in Atlantic Canada recognize, value, and integrate local knowledge into climate change adaptation, focusing on the enabling and constraining roles of funding, governance, and institutional structures. Guided by the Socio-Ecological Systems (SES) framework, the research forms part of a larger transdisciplinary project on collaborative governance in financing climate adaptation and mitigation. title: The limits of Antarctic conservation governance
abstract: Abstract The Antarctic region exerts a profound influence on the Earth system, making its conservation fundamental to sustaining planetary health and human wellbeing. The Antarctic Treaty System (ATS) holds near-exclusive authority for environmental protection across the region, yet questions remain regarding its capacity to address a growing range of conservation threats. title: How does climate risk affect fisheries? New evidence from the operating cash flows of Chinese listed firms
abstract: Listed fisheries companies depend heavily on natural conditions, leaving their operations particularly exposed to climate change. Using Chinese listed fisheries companies as the research sample, this study examines the effect of regional climate risk on operating cash flow and investigates potential mitigating mechanisms. abstract: Saudi Arabia is moving away from having tourism based on a number of individual flagship destinations towards establishing a development system that is linked across territories, in which issues relating to mobility, utilities, heritage, ecosystems, communities and investment have to be coordinated on a regional basis. This study presents an integrated framework for regional tourism development planning aimed at achieving sustainable infrastructure and destination growth in line with Vision 2030. abstract: An estimated one billion children live at extremely high risk of adverse effects from climate change. Even when children are not exposed to direct physical impacts, the existential threat of climate change can have a psychological impact by creating a stressor that exacerbates underlying mental health disorders or contributes to the development of new disorders. abstract: Abstract Quick and cheap water quality monitoring is an increasingly important tool to make the best use of an increasingly valuable resource. Fluid conductivity is an important parameter and can be measured contactless using inductive or capacitive coupling while maintaining low cost. Only the inductively coupled sensors are completely free of electrode polarization effects due to the absence of electrodes. abstract: La informalidad laboral en México representa un obstáculo estructural para el ejercicio pleno del derecho a la seguridad social y para la sostenibilidad del sistema de protección social. abstract: Today European ports have moved beyond their traditional role as logistical gateways to become strategic infrastructure for energy, supply-chain resilience and urban development. In this context, port competitiveness can no longer be understood only in terms of logistical performance but must be assessed within a governance model capable of integrating environmental sustainability and territorial resilience. abstract: Geoscience in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) operates amid persistent variability that challenges the continuity, credibil-ity, and public value of scientific work. This paper analyzes the resilience of the geoscience enterprise in the region—how science is designed, conducted, synthesized, and shared to serve public mandates—under shifting political, institutional, economic, environ-mental, and social conditions. abstract: Abstract Background Land-use intensification has enhanced impacts on water quality of South American rivers. A long-term database was compiled from public monitoring data to evaluate the temporal variation in water quality in the mid-lower Uruguay River from 1987 to 2019. Forty-two parameters (physicochemical, nutrients, metals, microbiological, pesticides, persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic substances and hydrological) in three sites across 440 km of the river were selected. title: Strategic Pathways for Magnesium–Aluminum‐Layered Double Hydroxides: Multidimensional Footprints of Production Routes
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium–aluminum‐layered double hydroxides (MgAl‐LDHs) are used in flame retardants, remediation, and catalysis. Sustainability comparisons of industrial routes are insufficient. This study couples techno‐economic analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA) to evaluate two routes (hydrothermal synthesis and modification) at 1000 t/a using industrial data. In the unglaciated Kenai Peninsula Lowlands (KPL), Alaska, groundwater originates from shallow hillslope groundwater (HGW) or deeper aquifer‐outcrop groundwater (AOGW) sources. abstract: ABSTRACT Sorption‐based atmospheric water harvesting (SAWH) offers a promising route for decentralized freshwater production, but practical water output is often limited by slow sorption kinetics in salt‐loaded hydrogel sorbents. Here, a biomimetic multi‐layer heterogeneous hygroscopic (MHH) membrane is developed to decouple vapor capture from bulk liquid storage. abstract: Abstract The Songliao River Basin, a critical hub for China's food security and renewable energy development, is increasingly vulnerable to extreme temperatures, yet raw Earth System Models (ESMs) exhibit substantial uncertainties in projecting future regional climate extremes. abstract: Knowledge plays an important role in Disaster Risk Management (DRM). However, although processes of organization, representation, classification, retrieval, and sharing are widely mobilized in this field, their relationship with Knowledge Organization (KO) remains insufficiently explicit and is frequently addressed from the perspectives of Knowledge Management (KM), Information Management (IM), and technological solutions. title: Predation on American Common Eiders in Eastern Nova Scotia, Canada
abstract: Somateria mollissima dresseri (American Common Eider) numbers are declining in parts of their historic breeding range in eastern North America. We conducted nesting surveys on 16 islands in 2013 to investigate eider breeding phenology and breeding effort, and whether predation pressure on eiders nesting in the Eastern Shore Islands Wildlife Management Area could be contributing to observed declines in eider numbers in Nova Scotia, Canada. abstract: The German sector of the North Alpine Foreland Basin contains more than 50 oil and gas fields. To determine the origin of the oils, Lower Oligocene source rocks—the only significant source rock for which no modern data is available—were examined and compared with recently published data from the Jurassic Posidonia Shale and from Permo-Carboniferous rocks. abstract: Abstract Urban flooding severely disrupts emergency services. Equitable mitigation requires identifying if socially vulnerable neighborhoods face disproportionate travel delays. Previous research overlooks estimation biases, where underestimating risks for vulnerable populations can skew assessments, ultimately hindering effective efforts to reduce risk inequities. abstract: This paper presents a communication-constrained coordinated path planning method for heterogeneous unmanned surface vehicle (USV)-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems operating in maritime environments. The path planning problem is formulated as a multi-objective optimization problem that simultaneously considers propulsion energy consumption, obstacle avoidance, communication maintenance, and trajectory smoothness. abstract: Abstract Accurate noise modeling is essential for realistic uncertainty assessment of GNSS coordinate time series. abstract: Abstract Environmental sciences and policy have long been framed on the premise that environmental harm is an expression of human nature rather than a product of specific historical and political arrangements. This framing has shaped a generation of interventions designed to constrain human behaviour rather than enable human capacity. title: Sustainable Freight Transportation via Inland Waterways: Challenges and Strategic Solutions in Bangladesh
abstract: Inland water transport (IWT) is crucial for socio-economic development, facilitating rural connectivity, trade logistics, energy provision and tourism. Nevertheless, it is neglected due to historical underinvestment, inadequate infrastructure and regulatory inefficiencies in Bangladesh. This study evaluates the current state of freight movement via inland waterways, identifies key challenges and proposes strategies to improve sustainability. abstract: GIScience is crucial for spatial understanding, analysis, and decision-making across multiple sectors. As GIScience demonstrates its continual impact in addressing critical societal and environmental challenges, growing concerns regarding its responsible use rise accordingly. The integration of vast and intricate datasets and the application of translucent algorithms hold the potential to infringe on privacy, perpetuate biases, exacerbate societal inequities, or undermine reliability. title: Between restrictions and rewards: Understanding community perceptions of protected area governance and outcomes
abstract: Protected areas (PAs) play a critical role in conserving biodiversity and maintaining ecosystem functions, yet their effectiveness is closely associated with how local communities perceive conservation outcomes and governance practices. This study examined community perceptions of ecological benefits, conservation costs and PA benefits, and governance practices associated with the Magamba Nature Forest Reserve (MNFR), Tanzania. title: Strategic ambitions and discursive divergences: China’s belt and road initiative in official and academic narratives
abstract: The present article seeks to analyse and interpret the discursive construction and strategic orientation of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). It aims to elucidate how the initiativeis framed within geopolitical, economic, sociocultural, technological, environmental, and institutional contexts, while critically assessing the coherence and divergences between China’s official narratives and academic discourses. title: Uncharted links from mining to fed animal systems: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract Animal-source foods are an increasingly large part of human diets worldwide, with feed production representing the primary driver of environmental impacts in farmed animal systems. While much attention has focused on agricultural and fisheries-based feed ingredients, the role of mineral supplements - a critical feed component - remains largely overlooked in sustainability assessments. title: Maximizing Tourism Potentials in Rivers State
abstract: Tourism is a pivotal driver of economic growth, cultural preservation, and social cohesion. However, in Nigeria, and particularly in Rivers State, the tourism sector remains largely underutilized despite the state's vast natural resources, vibrant cultural heritage, and strategic location in the Niger Delta region. This study explores the untapped potential of tourism in Rivers State; this paper explores the various tourism potentials of Rivers State, examining its cultural, ecological, recreational, educational, and industrial attractions. title: Quantifying ecosystem degradation via energetic deficits
abstract: Abstract Ecosystem degradation is accelerating, posing critical threats to both biodiversity and human economies. A central challenge is to quantify degradation relative to a reference baseline in a way that supports restoration planning and resource allocation. title: Reconstruction of an Ecosystem-Based Law Enforcement Model: Transformation of the Principle of Utility for the Restoration of Protected Forests
abstract: Indonesia, as a megabiodiverse country, faces serious challenges from the degradation of protected forests caused by land conversion into illegal agricultural areas. This study aims to analyze current law enforcement efforts against forest land conversion and formulate an environmental restoration-based law enforcement model grounded in the principle of legal utility. title: Spatial variation shapes gut microbiome composition and functional potential in an Afrotropical fish
abstract: Abstract Host-associated microbiomes are shaped by environmental heterogeneity across spatial gradients. However, the extent to which site-level variation structures gut microbial communities in Afrotropical fishes remains poorly resolved. In this study, we employed high-throughput 16S rRNA gene sequencing to characterize the gut microbiome of the African forktail catfish ( Chrysichthys nigrodigitatus ) encompassing two contrasting habitat types, with the aim of assessing spatial patterns in microbial composition and predicted functional potential. title: Environmental Jurisprudence in Anthropocene: Evaluation of Law in Addressing Impact of Environment Degradation on Economically Disadvantaged Communities
abstract: The Anthropocene represents a period in which human activities have become a major force influencing the Earth’s ecological systems. Environmental degradation arising from climate change, pollution, deforestation, biodiversity loss and resource depletion does not affect all sections of society equally. Economically disadvantaged communities, including rural, tribal, forest-dependent, agricultural and fishing communities, often experience greater environmental burdens because of their dependence on natural resources and their limited capacity to adapt or to obtain effective remedies. abstract: Background and research aims: To reconcile biodiversity protection with the livelihoods of communities living near national parks, Tanzania’s conservation policy puts a strong emphasis on participatory initiatives. However, the effectiveness of these approaches remains unclear to local communities. This study assessed (1) local stakeholders’ perceptions of their participation in protected area management and (2) how these perceptions influence perceived management effectiveness in Mikumi and Saadani National Parks. abstract: With the tremendous growth of cloud computing, cyber threat intelligence systems, and compressed big-data storage, efficient and secure compressed pattern-matching techniques are in high demand. Traditional compressed pattern-matching methods mainly focus on computational efficiency and do not consider privacy preservation or pattern search over encrypted patterns. abstract: The Act East Policy of India, launched in 2014 as the successor to the Look East Policy, has been envisioned to enhance India's economic, strategic, and diplomatic relations with ASEAN in the changing context of the Indo-Pacific region. The progress achieved in bilateral relations raises the question of whether the Act East Policy generated any real economic benefits and enhanced India's influence in the region compared to China that continues to build its economic position. title: How port governance shapes living labs for energy transitions
abstract: Ports are increasingly central to decarbonisation, energy-system integration, and resilience, yet less is known about how port governance shapes experimentation and whether learning becomes embedded in organisational practice. Living Labs (LLs)—organised forms of multi-actor experimentation in real-life settings—offer a promising approach, but are often treated as governance-neutral. abstract: Background: Scabies is a neglected tropical disease with at least 200 million people affected worldwide at any one time and a disproportionate burden in resource-limited settings. Although World Health Organization (WHO) prioritization has increased attention to scabies control, the evolution, geographic distribution, collaboration patterns, and policy alignment of the global research landscape remain incompletely characterized. abstract: The article addresses the complex relationship between the cultural adaptation of migrants and their perception of local traditions. title: Sacred forests in space and time: Intangible Cultural Heritage and naturebased solutions
abstract: Sacred forests have a long history of protection and many of them are old-growth forests with centuries old trees important for conservation. Some of these forests can be traced back to lands and territories inhabited for millennia by Indigenous peoples. These sites are considered important in the development of religion and spirituality in our distant ancestors and today their Intangible Cultural Heritage demonstrates a special relationship between people and nature. abstract: This article examines how coexistence in the Gerbang Mas Perkasa transmigration area, Sambas Regency, West Kalimantan, can be understood through Charles Taylor's politics of recognition. The area is a border transmigration zone in which transmigrant and local communities live within a plural society marked by historical memory, economic vulnerability, ecological pressure, and uneven public services. title: The Spatial Morphology of Future History
abstract: Big History characterizes cosmic evolution as a sequence of thresholds where ordered systems—from stars to civilizations—harvest energy to maintain rising complexity. However, standard historical narratives typically terminate at the present, treating the future as a domain of pure uncertainty. This study proposes that while specific events are unpredictable, the morphological structure of civilization follows a trajectory shaped by the time-invariant constraints of its generalized environment. abstract: Wearable activity-recognition models may lose reliability when transferred across participants, sensor placements, sampling rates, acquisition protocols, and activity definitions. This study evaluates a compact unsupervised target-aware feature-selection strategy for cross-dataset wearable activity monitoring under a pre-specified MHEALTH→PAMAP2 transfer protocol. title: Beyond the Seat at the Table: Structural Justice, Academic Agency, and the Reality of "Africa Rising"
abstract: Africa is central to the world's future. The continent holds immense human potential, vast natural wealth, and a very young population. Yet, historical trauma from colonialism and ongoing neocolonial practices still hold African nations back. Unfair global financial rules, high borrowing costs, and severe climate impacts create deep systemic barriers. Africa contributes barely 4% of global carbon emissions, yet suffers massive economic losses from climate change. The concept of "Africa Rising" must move beyond simple economic metrics. abstract: The leopard tortoise (Stigmochelys pardalis) is the only large tortoise in southern Africa and is the most widespread of any sub-Saharan testudinid. However, the population trend of this species is unknown, and it has become increasingly rare outside fenced areas and farmland. Little is known about their behavioural ecology in response to environmental stimuli. abstract: This paper discusses the pressing need for a transboundary approach to tackle climate change through STEM education, which is currently limited by traditional education methods. It introduces the Climate-Smart Transnational STEM Framework, encompassing seven dimensions: Cross-border Collaboration, Localised Climate Context, Innovation for Mitigation and Adaptation, Measurement and Data, Awareness and Action, Teacher Capacity, and Equity and Access. abstract: Outdoor athletes in equatorial regions are exposed to high levels of ultraviolet (UV) radiation year-round, increasing the risk of cumulative photodamage. abstract: Soil salinization and sodicity are accelerating worldwide, reducing crop productivity across more than 160 million hectares of farmland and causing production losses approaching USD 27 billion annually. Despite decades of research documenting these impacts, the extent of salt-affected soils continues to expand. abstract: Introduction The present study is part of the PRIMA Fish-PhotoCAT project, which aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a smart purification system for improving water quality, fish production, and environmental sustainability in aquaculture. title: Direct 3D extreme rainfall risk mapping from urban aerial LiDAR point clouds
abstract: Flooding is one of the most frequent and damaging natural hazards, increasingly intensified by rapid urbanization and extreme precipitation events. Accurate modelling of water accumulation and runoff in dense urban environments remains challenging due to complex geometries and the limitations of conventional surface-based representations. abstract: Abstract This article examines how investor–state dispute settlement (ISDS) tribunals engage with the precautionary principle (PP) when environmental measures are challenged in the face of scientific uncertainty over ecological harm. An analysis of awards identifies three recurrent treatments: (i) strong risk prevention, (ii) flexible risk management, and (iii) nominal acknowledgement. abstract: Watermelon seeds are nutrient-dense, phytochemical-rich by-products often discarded by the food industry. The present study aimed to develop effervescent granules from defatted watermelon seed flour and to evaluate their physicochemical characteristics. Watermelon seeds were processed and defatted using n-hexane solvent extraction. abstract: Abstract Microbial ammonia oxidation, the first and rate-limiting step of nitrification, plays a central role in soil nitrogen cycling. It is most relevant in agricultural soils as nitrifiers compete with crops for ammonia-based fertilizers. Therefore, synthetic nitrification inhibitors are widely used alongside fertilizers to reduce the activities of dominant drivers of this process, i.e., ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) and bacteria (AOB). abstract: As global urbanization accelerates cities increasingly face ecological challenges, most notably the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. This study investigates the formation and spatial distribution of UHI’s in the cities of Mingachevir, Shirvan and Yevlakh, located in the central region of the Republic of Azerbaijan. abstract: Rapidly expanding metropolitan areas across Sub-Saharan Africa face systemic risk from hazard-induced disruptions, exacerbated by infrastructure deficits and socioeconomic vulnerabilities. title: Digital Colonialism and the Reproduction of Hegemony in Africa: A Postcolonial Approach
abstract: This article presents a critical analysis of contemporary manifestations of digital colonialism in Africa, focusing on how global technology powers reproduce traditional patterns of domination through modern digital infrastructures and platforms. abstract: The Niger Delta presents a uniquely challenging emergency logistics environment characterized by extensive creek systems, seasonal inundation of road networks, and dispersed communities accessible only by water or air, yet emergency response operations in the region rely predominantly on road transport, with minimal integration of inland waterway and aviation modalities. abstract: Water resource management in Nigeria is a complex issue shaped by its diverse geography, climate variability, and rapid population growth. Despite substantial water resources, the country faces significant challenges in ensuring reliable access to clean and safe water. abstract: This paper undertakes a comparative examination of two geographically distant but conceptually convergent traditions of vernacular building: the timber architecture of the Dong ethnic minority in Guizhou, China — epitomised by the drum tower (gulou) and wind-and-rain bridge — and the earthen and painted vernacular forms of sub-Saharan Africa, exemplified by Dogon settlement architecture in Mali and Ndebele mural-house traditions in southern Africa. title: Rarefaction is better than robust Aitchison PCA and other compositional data analysis methods at controlling for uneven sequencing effort
abstract: Amplicon sequencing typically results in a wide distribution in the number of sequences obtained from each sample. How best to account for this variation has been a persistent problem in the microbial ecology literature. Historically, rarefaction has been used in ecology and this practice was adopted by microbial ecologists. However, rarefaction has been strongly criticized, leading to the development of compositional data analysis and normalization methods. Therefore, I reassessed the benchmarking data that were generated by the developers of one such method, robust Aitchison PCA. I found num

title: Innovation for Climate Change Adaptation: A Meta‐Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Evidence on climate adaptation innovations remains fragmented, limiting evidence‐informed policy. This meta‐analysis of 418 studies (2010–2023), stratified by outcome and design with publication‐bias adjustment, synthesizes effectiveness, equity, and scalability. Hybrid approaches showed a 39% advantage over single‐domain innovations ( g = 1.24), although bias correction reduced this by 18%. Outcomes varied across domains. Equity improved when women's participation exceeded 40%, yet 73% of technological interventions showed elite capture. Portfolio approaches are recommended, supporte

title: Contract enforcement and foreign direct investment in Nigeria: A critical review of legal predictability and investor confidence
abstract: This paper critically examines the relationship between contract enforcement and foreign direct investment (FDI) in Nigeria, highlighting the legal, institutional, and economic factors that shape investor behaviour. Employing a structured review methodology, the study synthesises evidence from peer-reviewed literature, policy analyses, and legal scholarship to identify trends, challenges, and gaps in Nigeria’s commercial legal environment. The review integrates theoretical perspectives from Transaction Cost Economics, Institutional Theory, and Property Rights Theory to explain how judicial eff
journal: International Journal of Law Justice and Jurisprudence

title: Biodiversity footprints and handprints in agricultural life cycle assessment a review of methods and field-based evidence
abstract: Abstract Biodiversity loss is a critical component of the current planetary crisis, yet it remains insufficiently represented in life cycle assessment (LCA) and in related sustainability metrics. This paper presents a narrative literature review of how biodiversity is currently incorporated into agricultural LCA, with particular attention to the extent to which field-based biodiversity monitoring data have been used to evaluate modelled indicators, and to whether environmental footprints are complemented by biodiversity handprints, that is, by positive-impact accounting. The literature was map

title: Rates of Evolution Differ Between Cell Types Identified by Single‐Cell RNAseq in Threespine Stickleback
abstract: ABSTRACT Rates of evolutionary change vary by gene. While some broad gene categories are highly conserved with little divergence over time, others undergo continuous selection pressure and are highly divergent among populations or species. But such comparative evolutionary studies rely on gene ontology categories that are rarely validated in the study's focal species. An alternative is to determine species‐specific gene functions using single‐cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) that identifies cell types and the characteristic genes that each expresses. institutions: Center for Marine Sciences and Technology

title: How the historical structure of local gazetteers conditioned modern science: Machinery in China, 1840–1949
abstract: Abstract This study asks why certain Western materials and practices came to be understood as modern science in China. By examining a corpus of Chinese local gazetteers ( difangzhi 地方志) representing roughly 52% of all collated titles within this genre, it argues that the gazetteer actively mediated an emerging technological reality between 1840 and 1949, thereby shaping a Chinese scientific modernity through material, geospatial and epistemic paths. title: Sharing the benefits and costs of conservation: public preferences for transboundary lynx policy
abstract: Transnational conservation is becoming ever-more important, yet reaching consensus on international conservation agreements remains challenging when decision-makers prioritise national benefits. Whether such approaches align with public preferences, however, remains unclear. We conduct a Discrete Choice Experiment to understand preferences for Iberian lynx conservation in Spain and Portugal, with a focus on the distribution of costs and benefits across countries. Results indicate that respondents favour an equal sharing of conservation costs and benefits over alternative allocation schemes. We

title: Network diagnosis and governance-coupled optimization in seaport–dry port multimodal transport corridors under the Maritime Silk Road
abstract: Research into seaport–dry port corridors has tended to focus on the design of the physical network on the one hand and the coordination of governance on the other. It is hard to maintain this separation in well-established Maritime Silk Road corridors. A corridor might have routes, inland nodes and digital platforms, and still not function smoothly at the rail/dry-port interface. This article therefore tackles corridor optimization as a problem of diagnosis and governance. title: The Ethical Risks of a Future-Saddling, Present-Sparing World Climate Bank
abstract: Abstract John Broome and Duncan Foley argue that future generations should shoulder the full burden of climate mitigation. To achieve this, they propose that economists design a new institution they dub “the World Climate Bank.” Their argument appeals primarily to self-interest and to the idea of making a Pareto improvement that delivers “efficiency without sacrifice.” This article argues against their strategy on both ethical and pragmatic grounds. title: Automatic Radiance Level Data Quality and Signal-to-Noise Assessment for Hyperspectral Imaging
abstract: Raw hyperspectral imaging (HSI) data require multiple processing steps before physically meaningful reflectance products can be derived. Quality issues at the radiance level – e.g., detector artifacts, low-signal regions, or excessive noise – can propagate through the processing chain and compromise subsequent analyses. HSI workflows typically focus on calibration and correction but often lack standardized integrity checks prior to atmospheric compensation. To address this gap, we developed an automated Data Quality Assessment (DQA) toolbox within the EU Horizon m4mining project. The toolbox i

title: Divergent narratives: community perceptions of illegal bushmeat hunting dynamics in the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem
abstract: Conservation outreach programs (COPs) aim to reduce illegal bushmeat hunting by providing communities with tangible benefits and fostering positive attitudes toward wildlife, but their influence is difficult to separate from law enforcement and wider social change. We compared how COPs beneficiary and non-beneficiary communities perceived and explained illegal bushmeat hunting dynamics in the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem across 2018-2024. Using a comparative mixed-methods design, we surveyed 360 households (180 per category), conducted 12 focus group discussions, and interviewed 24 key informants
institutions: Nelson Mandela African Institution of Science and Technology

title: Gut microbial metabolism of peanuts generates immunoregulatory metabolites
abstract: Background. Complementary feeding practices and timing are thought to significantly influence early life immune development, with the early introduction of allergenic foods being especially important for prevention of food allergy. We hypothesized that allergen-containing foods such as peanut, tree nuts and sesame may indirectly influence the immune system via their effects on gut microbiota composition and metabolism. Methods. title: Para-doxa: historicidad poética, contemporaneidad y sentido de lo eterno
abstract: This article theorizes a singular form of temporal and historical immanence—or poetic historicity—manifest in the Church of St. Dimitrios Loumbardiaris, designed by Dimitris Pikionis (1887–1968) as part of the landscape setting of the Acropolis and Philopappou Hill in Athens (1951–1957). The study develops a theoretical framework followed by an on-site, place-based experiential narrative, informed by phenomenological and hermeneutic practices. title: Prediction of Potentially Suitable Areas of Hazelnut (Corylus avellana L.) in Romania Based on Bioclimatic Variables
abstract: The hazelnut (Corylus avellana L.) is widespread throughout Europe, except in the northeastern parts. Due to its exceptional nutritional profile and associated health benefits, it’s recognised as a premier nut crop, ranking fifth among nut crops, based on total harvested area. The objectives of this study were: to identify the bioclimatic variables that influence the distribution of hazelnut in Europe, to predict its current and future habitat suitability in Romania and to evaluate the range dynamics. institutions: National Institute for Research and Development in Forestry "Marin Drăcea"

title: Collateralization of the Body in the Central Sahara: On Forms and Effects
abstract: ABSTRACT This article tracks a transporter along the route linking Tripoli to the Saharan town of Ghadames in post‐2011 Libya, asking what secures an obligation when the institutions that normally underwrite it (offices, courts, recognized names) have receded. I distinguish the debt, the sum owed, from the security pledged to answer for it: what may be taken if the owing fails. To collateralize is to fix that security beforehand, and I follow this act along a road where enforcement is personal. title: Suppression of Multimodal Vibrations in Plates With Distributed Dynamic Vibration Absorbers
abstract: ABSTRACT Due to the low damping characteristics of thin plate structures, harmful vibrations can easily occur under external excitation, potentially leading to fatigue failure and a reduced service life. A single dynamic vibration absorber (DVA) is often insufficient to effectively suppress the multimodal vibrations of the plate. Moreover, over time, factors such as fastener loosening and rubber aging can cause shifts in the resonant frequency of a single absorber, significantly affecting its vibration suppression performance. journal: ZAMM ‐ Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics / Zeitschrift für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik

title: Wastewater irrigation effects on contaminant fate soil quality nutritional traits and human health risks in rice agroecosystems with emphasis on microplastics
abstract: Freshwater scarcity, rapid urbanization, and rising agricultural demand have increased interest in wastewater irrigation, especially in water-intensive rice systems. Wastewater reuse can support crop production through nutrient recycling and reduced fertilizer dependence, yet it also introduces a persistent mixture of contaminants into soil–plant systems. title: THE MANUSCRIPT COLLECTION OF LEIMONOS MONASTERY HISTORICAL VALUE PRESERVATION AND DIGITAL PROMOTION
abstract: This article examines the manuscript collection of the Holy Monastery of Leimonos on Lesbos as a complex body of material evidence preserving aspects of Byzantine and post-Byzantine literature, Orthodox worship, education and local history. It considers the historical formation of the collection, its religious, palaeographical, codicological and artistic significance, and the contribution of digitisation to research and protection. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationship between preservation, scholarly access and sustainable cultural tourism. The article argues that the collection sh

title: Decolonizing Digital Ecosystems: Translating Tamil Bhakti Socio-Philosophical Frameworks into Sustainable Sociotechnical Systems for SDG 13 & 15
abstract: The dominant frame for current Information System research on environmental sustainability (usually termed as "Green IS") is still based on Western, anthropocentric, techno-bureaucratic which mirrors in corporate metrics, carbon footprint accounting, and compliance-driven enterprise architectures. Such top-down design slogans have little immediate scope for entering into an organic, bottom-up behavioural change paradigm of community groups, especially outside the Western dominions. title: A major monastic centre? Rethinking Lismore’s place in the ecclesiastical landscapes of early medieval Britain
abstract: Until recent decades, the monastery of Lios Mòr (Lismore) in Argyll, Scotland, established by Saint Mo Luóc in the sixth century, was attested only via historical references and local traditions. Community-led investigations have now revealed an early medieval cemetery, sophisticated craftworking of international importance and early structures around the island’s parish church. title: Oil and Gas Governance in the Nigerian Petroleum Industry: Imbibing the Good Governance Concept
abstract: This study appraised the governance structure in Nigeria petroleum industry, and as contained in the recent enacted PIA 2021 which is now the principal legal instrument as far as Nigeria’s petroleum industry is concerned. The challenges faced by regulators of the petroleum industry, being integral part of the system, are highlighted. It is observed that in seeking to proffer solution to tackle the problems facing Nigeria’s ailing petroleum industry the Norwegian model was resorted to. journal: JOURNAL OF LAW AND GLOBAL POLICY

title: Social context information and acoustic convergence in elephant vocal choruses
abstract: Abstract Elephants use low-frequency rumbles to communicate among individuals. Rumbles occur in several patterns: as discrete, non-overlapping calls, in antiphonal sequences where individuals alternate vocalizations, and in choruses where multiple individuals produce overlapping calls. Despite the wide availability of bioacoustics tools, most studies focus on non-overlapping signals rather than on choruses. title: Reservoir-computing-based chaos synchronization and its application to medical image encryption
abstract: Abstract Chaos synchronization provides a physically interpretable route for generating common dynamical states at spatially separated terminals, but most existing schemes require an accurate model and explicitly injected actuation. This paper develops a data-driven synchronization framework based on reservoir computing (RC) that learns nonlinear state couplings directly from observed trajectories. title: Quantifying spatial perception in the adaptive reuse of cultural-creative industrial heritage using user-generated text in Chongqing
abstract: Abstract Adaptive reuse of industrial heritage requires operational-stage evidence on public spatial perception, yet scalable and reproducible assessment remains limited. We developed a user-generated content (UGC)-based text-mining framework and applied it to eight cultural-creative industrial heritage sites in central Chongqing, China. title: Spatial Prioritization of Habitats and Conceptual Framework for Impact Assessment and Mitigation Planning for Protected Wetlands
abstract: Reconciling development and biodiversity conservation remains a critical challenge in contemporary conservation planning. Our study is based on a case study for the assessment of the Harike wetland, a Ramsar site and a Protected Area, a human-made reservoir, for understanding the impacts of proposed desilting operations and mitigation planning. A multi-taxa biodiversity assessment was undertaken to generate baseline ecological information for spatial prioritization, mitigation, and monitoring. title: Sustainability and Willingness to Pay: A Review of Approaches in Urban Mobility and Climate Change Resilience
abstract: Willingness to pay (WTP) is widely used to inform sustainability-related policy and investment decisions, yet its application remains fragmented across research domains. In urban mobility, WTP is typically employed to value service quality improvements, technological adoption, and efficiency gains, while climate change resilience research primarily frames WTP around risk reduction, loss avoidance, and adaptation measures. title: A phosphoproteome atlas of human cell lines reveals the landscape of kinase activity
abstract: Protein phosphorylation orchestrates cellular signaling and controls most biological processes, with its dysregulation driving diseases, notably cancer. Comprehensive, high-throughput phosphoproteomics remains limited by detection sensitivity, data completeness and computational bottlenecks, especially in low-input settings. Here we present a comprehensive empirical human phosphoproteome resource, regrouping over 200,000 class I phosphosites across 33 diverse human cell lines. We demonstrate that this spectral library dramatically improves single-shot phosphoproteomics with 30-fold faster data

title: Spatiotemporal modelling of post-COVID recreation reveals persistent and emerging pressures on freshwater ecosystems
abstract: Restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic pushed large numbers of recreationists towards freshwater ecosystems, but whether this shift was temporary or lasting has remained unclear. Using 129045 freshwater-related Wikiloc records (2016–2024), we modelled how recreation changed in time and space along the entire river network of the Catalan River Basin District (NE Spain), separating the pandemic effect from the platform's own growth. journal: Journal of Outdoor Recreation and Tourism

title: Between Revelation and Digitality: A Gadamerian Qur’anic Hermeneutics of Prophet Jonah and the #KaburAjaDulu Phenomenon
abstract: The emergence of the hashtag #KaburAjaDulu on various social media platforms represents a manifestation of psychosocial distress, structural criticism and the younger generation’s urge to escape the economic pressures and public policies perceived as failing to prioritise their interests. This qualitative, literature-based study aims to contextualise the Qur’anic narrative of the story of Prophet Jonah in Surah al-Anbiya’, verse 37, using Hans-Georg Gadamer’s hermeneutic framework. title: The evolution of Pakistan and China’s engagement with Afghanistan since 9/1
abstract: This study examines how Pakistan’s and China’s interests toward Afghanistan have evolved since 9/11 in pursuit of their security and political and economic objectives. Existing scholarship tends to treat Pakistan–Afghanistan and China–Afghanistan relations separately and rarely trace continuity and change across the whole post-9/11 period. title: Lightweight visual detection approach for apple ripeness perception in intelligent orchard harvesting scenarios
abstract: Apple ripeness detection in complex orchard scenarios is plagued by fruit occlusion, overlapping, intense illumination interference, and subtle maturity feature differences among similar fruits. Conventional lightweight detection models also suffer from low accuracy and severe feature loss in field environments. To address these problems, this paper proposes a real-time lightweight method for apple ripeness detection with optimized multi-dimensional network structures, which balances lightweight deployment and feature perception capability for complex orchard backgrounds. title: Household and community drivers of Aedes aegypti infestation in tropical cities: Guiding community-led interventions
abstract: Disadvantaged communities characterised by poor sanitation conditions, overcrowding, and limited vector control are highly susceptible to Aedes aegypti proliferation and arboviral disease transmission. Effective mosquito vector control requires a detailed understanding of Ae. aegypti oviposition preferences and spatial distribution within such urban environments. title: Curating the Polycrisis: Affective Assemblages, the Interactive Synopticon, and Trans-Corporeal Narratives in the Anthropocene
abstract: Humanity currently navigates an era defined by the Anthropocene and the “polycrisis”—a complex, destabilizing web of interconnected ecological, social, and political emergencies. Concurrently, our primary mode of processing, debating, and governing these existential threats is mediated through the algorithmic infrastructure of digital platforms. This said, this paper synthesizes five distinct but deeply interconnected domains of contemporary scholarship to propose a novel theoretical framework: Digital Anthropocene Studies. title: Infrastructure and Inclusiveness in Election Administration: Insights from India’s General Elections
abstract: The Lok Sabha (Lower House of Parliament) elections of India, represent the world’s largest democratic exercise, requiring an extraordinary scale of logistics, manpower and infrastructural readiness. This paper analyses the operational magnitude of Lok Sabha elections by assessing candidates, electors, polling stations, mobility assets, observers, surveillance teams, home-voting facilities, etc. The findings suggest that India's electoral process is characterised by a strong emphasis on inclusiveness and involves substantial human and material resources and elector-friendly polling stations. title: Governing urban floods in an emerging capital region: a social-ecological-technological systems policy analysis of Samarinda City, Indonesia
abstract: Urban flood governance in Samarinda is entering a new regional context. The establishment of Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN) and the emerging IKN–Samarinda–Balikpapan urban ecosystem are accelerating spatial, infrastructural, and institutional interdependence across East Kalimantan. This transition increases the importance of ensuring that Samarinda's flood policies are not only technically effective but also socially inclusive and ecologically grounded. title: Teacher Professional Reasoning for AI-Mediated Language Teaching Under Multi-Level AI Governance: An Embedded Multiple-Case Study
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is reshaping teaching, learning, assessment, and professional practice in English as a Foreign Language. However, little is known about how university teachers exercise professional reasoning within emerging AI governance environments. This embedded qualitative multiple-case study explored how university teachers of English as a Foreign Language in Vietnam reasoned professionally about generative artificial intelligence. journal: International Journal of Learning Teaching and Educational Research

title: Nature-based solutions in built environment education for developing sustainability competencies through bibliometric and systematic analysis
abstract: Abstract Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are increasingly recognized for their potential to address complex urban sustainability challenges; however, their integration into higher education curricula within built environment disciplines remains fragmented. This study examines how NbS contribute to the development of professional sustainability competencies and identifies pedagogical strategies most effective for embedding NbS in built environment education. title: Global Harmonization of Life Cycle Assessments for Small- and Medium-Scale Wastewater Treatment
abstract: Abstract Wastewater management (WWM) is vital for protecting human health and the environment, yet conventional centralized systems are resource-intensive and unsuited to growing urban pressure. Small and medium WWMs offer a potentially more sustainable alternative, but the lack of standardized life cycle assessment (LCA) approaches limits robust comparison and informed decision-making. In this study, we conduct a global harmonization of life cycle assessments of small- and medium-scale systems across 96 LCAs and 9 treatment technologies. title: Governance, dependency, and performance in nuclear megaprojects: A strategic analysis of the Akkuyu NPP
abstract: This study examines the Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) as a strategic governance system within Türkiye’s long-term energy transition. While existing research has primarily focused on the technical, environmental, and economic aspects of nuclear energy, limited attention has been given to the governance mechanisms that shape high-risk megaprojects. title: An Ecocritical Perspective on the Poems “Darg‘a” and “Tabiat Xato Ketdi” by the Uzbek Poet Tursunoy Sodiqova
abstract: The relationship between human beings and nature has been interpreted in various ways throughout history, and the meanings attributed to the natural environment have evolved in response to social, cultural, and economic transformations. Literature, as a reflection of human experiences and perceptions, has consistently incorporated natural elements and, particularly in the modern era, has developed new perspectives in response to growing environmental concerns. title: BIOSECURITY IN THE INDO-PACIFIC: BIOLOGICAL RISKS, REGIONAL COOPERATION, AND STRATEGIC COMPETITION
abstract: The Indo-Pacific is a major centre of global population, trade, and strategic competition, but it also faces growing biological risks from disease outbreaks, animal diseases, laboratory accidents, and the deliberate misuse of biological agents. This study examines how biological risks interact with regional cooperation and strategic competition in the Indo-Pacific. It addresses the problem of uneven regional cooperation, particularly in sensitive areas such as laboratory oversight, information sharing, and biosecurity governance. title: Nepalese Calamity of 2026: Manmade or Climate Driven
abstract: The flash floods of August 26, 2026, along the Nepal-Tibet border are one of the most devastating Himalayan disasters since the 2015 earthquake. Some believe that the event was driven by anthropogenic activities. Others attribute it to climate change. To have greater clarity of the primary cause and to draw lessons for the future, this paper examines the catalysts behind the disaster. Although the primary geological event may have been rooted in climate change, the catastrophic scale of downstream destruction seems to have been greatly amplified by manmade vulnerabilities. title: First evidence of Tahyna virus in Central Italy and seasonal dynamics of its putative vector, Aedes caspius
abstract: Tahyna virus (TAHV) is a neglected mosquito-borne Orthobunyavirus pathogenic to humans. In Italy, TAHV was first recorded in Friuli Venezia-Giulia and then repeatedly in Emilia Romagna Region (Northern Italy). This study was set up to verify the presence of TAHV in Central Italy and to identify its potential vectors. Mosquito surveillance was conducted from April to November 2025, using 78 CDC-CO₂ traps across Latium and Tuscany Regions. title: Integrating Local Wisdom into Business Strategy: Chinese Ethnic Entrepreneurs in Madura and the Relevance of Islamic Economic Values
abstract: Purpose – The integration of local wisdom by the Chinese ethnic group in Madura serves as an effective business strategy. It determines a venture’s success, particularly within a complex cultural context like Madura. An effective business strategy is a key determinant of enterprise success, particularly within complex cultural contexts such as Madura. title: Public perspectives on water quality communication and interest in participatory monitoring approaches in Jalisco, Mexico
abstract: Surface water governance depends not only on monitoring capacity but also on whether residents can access relevant information, navigate institutional responsibilities, and recognize opportunities to participate. This study examined these dimensions in Jalisco, Mexico, through a statewide, face-to-face household survey assessing exposure to and perceptions of surface water quality communication, information-seeking practices, awareness of inquiry and feedback mechanisms, and interest in public hearings and participatory monitoring, including perceived motivations and barriers. title: Access and Benefit Sharing in India: Reconciling Biodiversity Conservation, Sustainable Development and Community Rights
abstract: International environmental law has historically centered on the control and ownership of natural and biogenetic resources. Numerous environmental conventions have addressed this question, prioritizing benefit-sharing mechanisms. Among these, Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) emerged as a key solution, aiming to balance the interests of developed and developing nations while conserving biodiversity. title: Public knowledge, perceptions and support for climate and health action in Nairobi: a cross-sectional survey with an embedded conjoint experiment
abstract: Background Public support is important for the adoption, implementation, and sustainability of effective climate action. Evidence suggests that policy instrument characteristics, individual characteristics, and the way in which climate messages are framed can influence public support. Evidence on the effectiveness of different climate message framing, however, is largely limited to high-income countries, with limited research conducted in Sub-Saharan Africa, where the impacts of climate change are particularly severe. title: Ancient Indian Knowledge Traditions and Modern Scientific Thought: A Critical Review of Hindu Philosophical and Scientific Texts
abstract: Ancient Indian philosophical literature, including the Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, Mahabharata, Ramayana, and classical scientific treatises such as the Vaisheshika Sutra, Sushruta Samhita, Charaka Samhita, and Aryabhatiya, contains numerous discussions concerning cosmology, mathematics, medicine, astronomy, causality, and the nature of matter. title: Nature and interbeing: an ecocritical-postcolonial reading of Thich Nhat Hanh's poetry
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this research article is to explore nature and interbeing in the poetic works of Thich Nhat Hanh within the context of ecocritical-postcolonial theories. Design/methodology/approach This research article is designed to discuss two key dimensions: nature as a witness to war and colonization, and interbeing as ecology's resistance to colonial violence. title: Using matrix analysis to understand competition in food webs and antimicrobial resistance networks
abstract: Abstract Indirect competition is a fundamental mechanism shaping the structure of biological systems, from food webs to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) networks. Translating directed interaction data into a quantitative measure of competition remains a modelling challenge. This paper develops a spectral framework that maps directed bipartite networks into symmetric, positive semidefinite (PSD) competition matrices via the shared-target principle (C=AA⊤). title: Remote estimation of plastic distribution in California agriculture using Sentinel-2 imagery: a case study
abstract: Global application of agricultural plastic mulch is increasing. While these films offer benefits for crop production, they also are a large source of plastic waste and pollution in both terrestrial and aquatic systems. The current scale of global mulch application and its deleterious impacts are unclear. Current estimates of agricultural plastic use remain limited by field-specific growing patterns and data limitations. abstract: Abstract This study quantifies the lagged association between grass pollen exposure and the onset of allergic rhinitis (AR) symptoms, including differences between asthmatic and non‐asthmatic subgroups. title: A lightweight model for steel surface defect detection based on EDGI-YOLO
abstract: To address the limitations of YOLOv8n in steel surface defect detection–namely, its large parameter count and computational cost, insufficient multi-scale feature modeling capability, and poor scale adaptability of the detection head– we propose a lightweight improved model named EDGI-YOLO. abstract: ABSTRACT Recently, the integrated satellite‐terrestrial network (ISTN) system offers a promising solution for extending wireless communication services to remote and underserved areas. To effectively provide a variety of services, it is essential to cache the corresponding services on satellites while dynamically allocating the satellite bandwidth. title: Sustainable Risk Management of the Porang Supply Chain as an Agro-Industrial Commodity in Madiun Regency
abstract: Porang is a key agro-industrial commodity in Madiun Regency, Indonesia. Its supply chain currently faces numerous challenges, particularly in terms of risk management and sustainability issues. Various risks continue to affect the stability and performance of supply chains, posing a threat to their long-term viability. Additionally, stakeholder involvement remains fragmented, with limited collaboration across supply chain networks in the industry. This study aimed to identify and analyze supply chain risks and develop relevant risk mitigation strategies from the perspective of sustainability.

Studying which microorganisms have been long-term residents of the human gut and may have co-evolved with humans2,7,8 could provide insights into how microbial biodiversity loss affects human health. abstract: Efficient data dissemination in large-scale internet of things (IoT) networks remain challenging due to energy constraints, congestion, and delay under dynamic network traffic. This paper introduces a joint routing and medium access control (MAC)-layer scheduling framework (JRSM), incorporating priority-aware clustering to enhance energy efficiency and reduce latency in the IoT data acquisition layer. title: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights’ Advisory Opinion on the Climate Emergency: Implications for Canada
abstract: Abstract This article analyzes the Inter-American Court of Human Rights’ 2025 advisory opinion on the climate emergency from the perspective of its implications for Canada. The authors identify key legal developments: “climate emergency” as a decisive interpretive element; the peremptory ( jus cogens ) obligation not to generate irreversible harm to the common planetary ecosystem; a new right to a healthy climate; and states’ “enhanced” due diligence obligation. We propose EvoPatch-IoT, an evolution-aware retrieval framework whose novelty lies not in another standalone encoder, but in coupling target-local geometric localization, architecture-normalized anonymous multi-view evidence, and a version-causal historical prototype memory for reference-guided retrieval. abstract: Amid rising global demand for sustainable energy, agricultural and forestry residues (AFRs) emerge as a key yet underutilized resource in energy transition. abstract: This article presents the evolution of financial reporting regulations and practices regarding decommissioning liabilities with a focus on the managerial approach to value creation processes in mining companies. abstract: Abstract American chestnut ( Castanea dentata ) was once a dominant tree species spanning the eastern temperate forests of the United States until the introduction of chestnut blight in the early twentieth century resulted in its functional extinction. Recent advances in the development of blight‐resistant American chestnut could support widespread restoration, but optimal locations for restoration plantings remain uncertain. abstract: Namibia is emerging as a pioneer in Africa's green transition, leveraging its abundant renewable resources to pursue a development pathway that integrates green economy management, sustainable development, and technological transformation. title: Reframing antimicrobial resistance as a land-system challenge through environmental pathways and climate interactions
abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a planetary health challenge, yet land-system change remains overlooked. This review examines how agriculture, urbanisation, waste management, deforestation, aquaculture and climate-driven transitions shape resistance through altered input intensity, habitat reorganisation and enhanced connectivity. abstract: Autonomous ecological monitoring requires robotic systems capable of efficiently exploring large natural environments while minimizing redundant traversal under limited communication and partial environmental knowledge. I argue that scientific leadership is less about exercising authority than about cultivating the trust, diversity, interactions and intellectual freedom from which scientific excellence can emerge.

abstract: The increasing adoption of digital communication technologies has enhanced States' ability to monitor communications for national security, crime prevention, and law enforcement. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents an existential One Health threat. abstract: Prosocial behavior, the tendency to act for others' benefit, is essential for mental health. title: Censorship or Accident? Distinguishing Natural and Intentional Geometric Errors on Cold War City Plans Published in the Eastern Bloc
abstract: During the Cold War, maps published in Eastern Bloc countries were subject to strict censorship. title: That’s not what a uterus looks like: representations of female reproductive anatomy produced by Adobe Stock creators and the generative AI tools they use
abstract: The production of medical illustrations has traditionally required professional skills in illustration, knowledge of human anatomy, and access to reference material such as cadavers, specimens, or surgical photos. The ability of generative AI tools to rapidly produce visually compelling illustrations introduces new issues in trustworthiness of medical illustrations. We collected representations of the female reproductive system on the Adobe Stock platform that had been created with generative AI. title: A framework for unit-level biodiversity credit integrity and market-level governance
abstract: Biodiversity credits (BCs) are one innovative financing scheme that the Global Biodiversity Framework proposes to mobilise private capital and narrow the biodiversity financing gap. BCs and the voluntary biodiversity markets (VBMs) around them are nascent, offering an opportunity to learn from shortcomings of the adjacent voluntary carbon markets and design them for both ecological and social integrity from the outset. title: Traditional versus Next-Generation Probiotics for the Control of Multidrug-Resistant Enterococci: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives
abstract: Abstract: Multidrug-resistant enterococci, particularly vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE), represent an important clinical challenge because of their antimicrobial resistance, intestinal persistence, and potential for transmission and infection. The limited effectiveness of conventional antimicrobial approaches in preventing intestinal colonization has increased interest in microbiome-based strategies, including traditional probiotics and next-generation probiotics (NGPs). Traditional probiotics may inhibit enterococci through competitive exclusion, bacteriocin and organic acid production

title: Tribal Culture, Lifestyle, and Sustainable Development: A Path of Harmony with Nature
abstract: Introduction: This paper explores the sustainable lifestyle practices of tribal communities in Andhra Pradesh, focusing on their deep-rooted connection with nature. The history of human evolution is a story of adaptation, survival and transformation, and while some early groups chose permanent settlements, tribes continued a mobile existence deeply connected to the natural world. title: Dilemmas of engagement: local government officials’ perspectives on roles and responsibilities in climate change adaptation in rural and remote Nordic municipalities
abstract: As climate change impacts intensify across the Nordic countries, calls for deeper and more sustained citizen engagement in adaptation efforts have become increasingly prominent in both national and local policy agendas. This shift has spurred growing scholarly interest in how citizen responsibilisation is reshaping the roles and responsibilities of local government officials. While existing research has predominantly focused on urban contexts, this article examines local government officials in remote rural municipalities in Denmark and Norway. title: Comparative genomic analysis of established and emerging anti-tubercular drug targets reveals evolutionary conservation and antimicrobial resistance patterns in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Indonesia
abstract: Background Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) remains a major public health threat in Indonesia, which ranks second globally in tuberculosis burden. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) studies of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Indonesia have so far been analyzed largely in isolation, and no previous study has systematically compared the evolutionary conservation of classical, clinically validated resistance-associated genes with newly proposed metabolic drug targets within a single, geographically diverse Indonesian isolate collection. title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza as a systemic risk - implications for control and preparedness
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has evolved from episodic outbreaks into a globally entrenched, multi-host panzootic, with recurrent spillover into mammals. The expanding host range and increasing wildlife–livestock interfaces challenge traditional control strategies, increase opportunities for viral adaptation, and thereby elevate zoonotic risk. We therefore propose that HPAI should be reframed as a long-term systemic risk requiring resilience-based governance, and strengthened One Health control and preparedness.

title: Carbon credits as market-based mechanisms for climate mitigation: Opportunities, challenges and future perspectives
abstract: Carbon credits are a promising market-based tool for combating climate change, biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation, three of the most pressing environmental problems currently facing the global environment. Carbon credit schemes have stimulated investments in renewable energy, forestry, sustainable agriculture, soil carbon management and decreased emissions by putting a monetary value on greater carbon sequestration and reduced emissions. abstract: Abstract LiDAR-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems suffer from environment-induced degeneracy in geometrically self-similar scenes such as tunnels and cylindrical structures, where the point cloud registration problem becomes ill-conditioned. Existing degeneracy detection methods predominantly rely on eigenvalue analysis of the Hessian matrix, which assesses geometric conditioning at a fixed linearization point. abstract: As batteries are widely used in port operation vehicles, cargo handling equipment, and fixed energy storage systems, ports need to establish reliable mechanisms for battery recycling and disposal. This study develops a Stackelberg model led by a battery system integrator, with an authorized recovery service provider and a representative green-port operator. abstract: Abstract The audit expectation gap exists and persists due to changing “…social, economic, and political developments of the time.” (Sikka, et al., 1998) Like stakeholders’ demands for and the profession’s response to fraud detection in the 2000s, investors are increasingly interested in C-suite employees’ and entity’s illegal acts, finding them both relevant and material (Cline, Walkling & Yore, 2018).
