abstract: This article examines the evolving ecosystem of climate solution evidence tools and distinguishes the different functions they serve, including evidence aggregation, assessment of evidence strength, comparison of solution options, spatial targeting, policy benchmarking, and adaptive management. Drawing from research on evidence-informed policymaking and climate decision science, the authors identify persistent barriers to evidence use, including misalignment with decision needs, deep uncertainty, institutional incentives, and limited capacity for collective sensemaking. abstract: Purpose - This study maps the spatial structure of Italy’s tourism economy across the 20 regional capitals. It identifies central hubs, peripheral nodes and territorial disparities, and considers how the resulting network evidence can inform more coordinated tourism development. title: Urban Accessibility, Housing Prices and Socio-Economic Status: A Spatial Analysis of Istanbul Neighbourhoods
abstract: Multidimensional accessibility shapes both housing markets and the socio-economic composition of neighbourhoods, yet fine-grained evidence from rapidly urbanising contexts remains limited. This study examines how pedestrian accessibility to 88 urban services relates to listed housing prices and socio-economic status across 816 Istanbul neighbourhoods with at least 1,000 residents. abstract: ABSTRACT Sand mining is widely recognized as one of the most significant threats to river health in the Lower Mekong Basin, where intensive extraction interacts with sediment starvation, hydropower development, climate variability, and delta subsidence to produce complex, transboundary environmental impacts. title: Localizing water and climate SDGs: comparative insights from Ecuador and Switzerland’s governance contexts
abstract: Abstract Localizing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is critical for achieving global sustainability, yet translating international commitments into actionable local policies remains challenging, not least because interdependent goals require coherent implementation. This article examines how external pressure, local capacity, and local demand condition coherent SDG localization at the level of discourse, norms, and institutions. abstract: Near-synonymy in the Qur’an challenges translators because related lexical items can differ in intensity, scope, expressive force, and contextual function. This exploratory qualitative study compares selected English expressions by Arberry and Irving with excerpts reported as GPT-4 outputs. abstract: Biological degradation provides a sustainable approach for managing the organic impurities accumulating in Bayer liquor. However, the limited functional understanding of microbial communities in hypersaline, haloalkaline bioreactors constrains process optimisation. abstract: This article investigates the activation and transformation of Nordic identity during a critical political juncture in the early 1990s with respect to EU membership discussions in the Finnish Parliament. Triggered by Sweden’s pursuit of EC membership in 1990 and the post-Cold War context, the discourse surrounding Nordicness gained significance as Finland, Sweden, and Norway prepared for the 1994 membership referenda. title: Mapping the exposome of Zimbabwean preschool-aged children using a novel peptide microarray approach
abstract: Immune responses vary substantially between individuals and populations, reflecting differences in genetics, environment, and cumulative antigenic exposures. Characterizing these exposures, or the immunological exposome, is essential for understanding population-specific immune development, susceptibility to infection, and responses to interventions. abstract: Abstract: The zebrafish is a widely utilized model organism in medical research because of its high reproductive capacity, rapid development, transparent embryos, genetic tractability, and similarity to humans in skeletal development. abstract: Many of the most challenging decisions facing natural resource managers today can be understood as time dependent. The concept of time-dependent decisions is useful when considering natural resource management decisions that are characterized by nonstationarity in the underlying ecological system, uncertainty surrounding key ecological relationships, efficacy of management interventions, and difficult trade-offs between the present and the future. title: Service Innovation and Venture Sustainability of Three-Star Hotels in South-South, Nigeria
abstract: The study investigated the relationship between service innovation and the economic, social and environmental sustainability of three-star hotels in South-South Nigeria. The research was conducted with a positivist philosophy and correlational survey design, based on the Resource Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Sustainability Theory. abstract: The increasing proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), wireless sensor networks (WSN), wearable electronics, and smart sensing platforms have intensified the demand for sustainable and maintenance-free power sources. Energy harvesting has emerged as a promising solution to replace or complement traditional batteries by converting ambient energy into usable electrical power. title: From Reactivity to Proactivity: The Use of Behavioural Data in Life and Health Insurance
abstract: Abstract Traditional life and health insurance compensates after the fact, acting reactively in response to adverse events. Today, the rise of digital technologies enables insurers to intervene proactively, monitoring policyholders’ behaviour and incentivizing lifestyle changes intended to reduce risks before they materialize. abstract: Planetary Health Knowledge (PHK) refers to knowledge about global conditions and interrelations between the health of the planet, human health, and human civilization. In times of various humanitarian and environmental crises, knowledge about and awareness of these problems become increasingly important. abstract: Rapid urbanisation in arid regions intensifies heat exposure, vegetation loss, and particulate pollution, yet medium-sized desert cities remain underrepresented in integrated environmental assessments. We quantified spatiotemporal changes in environmental quality in Jodhpur, India, from 2001 to 2021 using a novel grid-based Environmental Quality Index (EQI). abstract: BACKGROUND: Medication adherence is a persistent challenge in the treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and HIV. abstract: This study presents a comprehensive national-scale assessment of biomethane potential from organic waste streams in Qatar, evaluating its impact on two strategic climate mitigation pathways: (1) sustainable energy in water supply and agriculture, and (2) potential natural-gas substitution in Qatar’s gas-to-liquids (GTL) industry. abstract: This article mobilises generation as a lens for theorising and examining the contingent and permuting character of settler colonial formations, with a specific focus on Gaza. Generation, we argue, calls attention to settler colonial rule as situated and embodied, and temporalities of survival and resistance as layered and heterogenous. abstract: Blockchain technology is revolutionising UK supply chain management by improving security and transparency. This study examines how blockchain mitigates fraud, improves traceability, and optimises operational efficiency through Everledger, IBM Food Trust, Maersk TradeLens, and Walmart UK case studies. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a sliding variable‐based optimal control (SVBOC) framework for canonical nonlinear systems with unknown control direction. abstract: The use of near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy for material classification in recycling facilities has become increasingly prominent due to its rapid, accurate and non-destructive capabilities. abstract: How do the legacies of colonisation, cultures of exploitation and marginalisation undermine the needs of historically marginalised populations across geographies? abstract: Introduction The World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Agreement, adopted in May 2025, represents a major step toward strengthening global pandemic governance after COVID-19. abstract: This study presents the design, fabrication, and preliminary experimental evaluation of a locally manufactured vest-type Personal Flotation Device (PFD) for adults weighing 75–80 kg under controlled calm-water conditions. abstract: Background Feedlot nutrition is formulated to maximize growth rate and feed efficiency for high-quality meat production; however, high-grain diets can disrupt rumen function and cause digestive disorders, the inclusion of non-nutritive feed additives helps counter these effects, thereby enhancing growth performance and overall feed efficiency. abstract: Urban Woody Vegetation Cover (UWVC) near schools shapes the thermal and psychological conditions of students' daily environments, yet canopy cover surrounding schools remains poorly documented. abstract: This study investigated the impact of funding constraints on rural development project implementation in Owo Local Government Council, Ondo State, Nigeria. abstract: Deciphering the molecular mechanisms underlying complex biological interactions requires comprehensive approaches that capture these interactions across multiple regulatory and functional levels. Here, we present a protocol applied to the host-pathogen-environment interactions underlying Pacific oyster mortality syndrome (POMS) in Magallana gigas . abstract: This paper explores Instagram as a platform for visual and emotional narratives of disaster across the response and recovery phases. Focusing on the extreme flooding that affected western Germany in July 2021, the study analyzes approximately 2,700 Instagram posts collected over a three-year period. title: A Systematic Investigation of Bias in Large Language Models for Advertising Relevance
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to judge how well an advertisement matches a query, but the fairness of these judgments has received limited attention. We conduct a systematic study of fairness in relevance judgments made by LLMs for queries and advertisements. abstract: Very-high-resolution Earth-observation satellites acquire more data than they can store and downlink, while in maritime surveillance the vessels cover a tiny fraction of each scene. abstract: We investigate the structure of the pion in a magnetized nuclear medium at finite temperature by analyzing the in-medium modifications of its parton distribution functions (PDFs) and electromagnetic form factors (EMFFs). abstract: The five Regional Internet Registries (RIRs) provide the critical function of IP address resource delegation and registration. The accuracy of registration data directly impacts Internet operation, management, security, and optimization. In addition, the scarcity of IP addresses has brought into focus conflicts between RIR policy and IP registration ownership and use. abstract: We introduce GeoOutageBench, a benchmark for assessing LLM-based geospatiotemporal KGQA for multimodal outage and resilience analysis. title: Debug2Fix: Can Interactive Debugging Help Coding Agents Fix More Bugs?
abstract: While significant progress has been made in automating various aspects of software development through coding agents, there is still significant room for improvement in their bug fixing capabilities. Debugging and investigation of runtime behavior remains largely a manual, developer-driven process. abstract: Multi-party interaction is a central setting for human communication and a necessary target for human-agent interaction systems that must participate in group conversation. Yet available corpora often focus on meetings, task-oriented interaction, text-based interaction, or acted scenarios, and fewer resources support cross-linguistic comparison of spontaneous face-to-face triadic discussion. abstract: Codon optimization is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem with important applications in synthetic biology, protein expression, and biotechnology. While quantum annealing has previously been explored for this problem, the application of gate-based quantum algorithms remains largely unexplored. abstract: Programs that compute with physical quantities often need to convert between units of measurement, and as the Mars Climate Orbiter showed, these conversions can be a rich source of errors. abstract: Industry applications often demand low-latency classification, yet current large language model (LLM) approaches remain poorly suited for latency-critical applications. Existing prompting and constrained decoding produce verbose, multi-token outputs that require expensive token-by-token generation, while encoder-based models achieve faster inference but sacrifice task flexibility. abstract: Hybrid underwater robotic vehicles integrate features typically found in separate classes of vehicles: autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), amphibious robots, and cross-medium robotic vehicles. abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in marine environments must navigate rugged bathymetry, ocean-current disturbances, sudden obstacles, and limited perception. abstract: The article examines the design and operating principle Launch and Recovery Systems (LARS) for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) based on unmanned boats (UBs) of various purposes. abstract: The hydrodynamic interaction between closely spaced autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) in formation produces strongly nonlinear drag responses. abstract: Abstract Surface riblets have emerged as a highly efficient passive drag-reduction strategy for enhancing the endurance of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). abstract: The paper proposes a cost-effective solution for simultaneously determining the coordinates for a group of inexpensive autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). abstract: Diving accidents remain frequently fatal, and most stem from preventable human factors: panic, failed buoyancy control, and disorientation. Underwater human–robot interaction research has focused on observing the diver and offers little help when a diver must be pulled to safety. In addition to bulk nitrogen isotope analysis, compound-specific nitrogen isotope analysis of amino acids (CSIA-AA) further enables the separation of biogeochemical processes from the trophic effects. abstract: Abstract On 08 October 2023, a series of submarine earthquakes that took place in the Izu-Ogasawara Islands, Japan, excited at least 14 hydroacoustic signals (i.e., T -waves or H -waves) over a period of three hours. These signals were detected by the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) International Monitoring System (IMS) hydrophone station HA11 at Wake Island. title: Kellia porculus Pilsbry, 1904 (Bivalvia: Lasaeidae), a new record in the Russian molluscan fauna, with taxonomic notes on allied species
abstract: Kellia porculus Pilsbry, 1904, is recorded for the first time in the Russian waters of the Sea of Japan along the coast of Primorye (Valentin, Olga, Rynda bays and Tatarsky Strait). An updated description, photographs, synonymy, data on biology and distribution are provided. Taxonomic comments on seven other north-western Pacific species of Kellia Turton, 1822 are given, along with illustrations of type material, for K. japonica Pilsbry, 1895, K. laperousii (Deshayes, 1839), K. subrotunda (Dunker, 1882), K. comandorica Scarlato, 1981, and K. grebnitzskii (Dall, 1916). title: Meio- and macrofauna as indicators in the ecological monitoring program: Do they behave similarly?
abstract: Bivalve aquaculture and land-based pollution increasingly affect benthic ecosystems in Jiaozhou Bay along the southern Yellow Sea coast of China. Meiofauna and macrofauna are key components of benthic communities and are widely used as indicators of ecosystem health, yet their responses to aquaculture impacts and environmental gradients remain poorly understood. abstract: Fluctuations in the level of the Caspian Sea played a decisive role in the development of the settlement complexes’ infrastructure in the Volga River delta during the Holocene. In turn, the transgressive-regressive cycle had a significant impact on the restructuring of the hydrographic network and sedimentation conditions in the Volga River delta. During periods of transgression, part of the delta was flooded, leading to the development of extensive bays in which a distinctive complex of sediments and malacofaunal assemblages formed. title: THE FORGOTTEN WORKERS OF KISH: IRAQI ARCHAEOLOGICAL LABOUR IN EARLY 20 TH -CENTURY HILLAH
abstract: In this article I explore the experience of excavation for Iraqi archaeological workers in the first decades of the twentieth century, using the site of Kish as a case study. I draw upon published and archival sources from the brief French-funded work at Kish in 1912 and the Oxford-Field Museum Expedition of 1923–33, situating them within an increasingly rich historiography of late Ottoman and Mandate Iraq. title: Booty into Property: The View from the Desert
abstract: Lauren Benton’s paper invites a comparison between deserts and oceans, camels and ships. This is a comparison that I have always resisted, partly because it is somewhat trite; partly because it directs attention away from the desert—the Sahara, in this case—not merely as a space to be crossed, but as a space of life in its own right. abstract: This study reports findings from preliminary commercial trials conducted in India’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) to explore the commercial potential of mesopelagic resources in the south-eastern Arabian Sea along the Karnataka coast. Two modified commercial multiday trawl vessels equipped with navigation and fish detection systems conducted 15 midwater trawl hauls at depths of 300-800 m, during night time over a three-month period (January, April, and May 2025). Fuel debris detection system using in-situ measurements of gamma rays and neutrons for investigation of fuel debris distribution
abstract: This paper presents a compact, integrated system for in-situ detection of fuel debris via simultaneous gamma-ray and neutron measurements, developed for application within the primary containment vessel (PCV) of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 1. The system combines a miniaturized CdTe detector with 100-ns signal processing for gamma-ray spectroscopy and a compact B-10 proportional counter structually designed to suppress its gamma-ray response, both enclosed in a shielded container weighing less than 8 kg. title: Tracking palaeoenvironmental changes across the Eocene-Oligocene boundary using diagnostic PAH ratios and DWAF assemblages
abstract: This study investigates the distribution and sources of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAH) across the Eocene-Oligocene Transition (EOT) in the Caltavuturo Formation at Portella Colla (northern Sicily, Italy). The EOT represents a critical shift from greenhouse to icehouse conditions, and this research evaluates the utility of PAHs as geochemical proxies for paleoenvironmental and paleoclimatic changes. title: Major and Rapid Morphodynamic Changes to an Unvegetated Cay Under Typical Weather Conditions: Taylor Cay, Central Great Barrier Reef, Australia
abstract: ABSTRACT Cays are low‐lying accumulations of carbonate sediment, formed and modified by hydrodynamic processes acting over coral reef platforms. More than 230 cays occur within the Great Barrier Reef (GBR), supporting valuable ecosystem and cultural functions. Although unvegetated cays are generally small, they comprise 55% of all GBR cays. Despite their prevalence, the morphodynamic behaviour of unvegetated cays on the GBR has rarely been documented. title: Testing of Multi-Section Deep Well Sampler and Fluid Sampling from Borehole 5G at Vostok Station, Antarctica
abstract: Testing of the Multi-section Deep Well Sampler (MDWS) was conducted during the 70th Russian Antarctic Expedition at Vostok Station in 2024/25. The MDWS is a non-circulating piston sampler designed to collect borehole fluid samples from multiple depths in a single round trip. Surface tests verified the operational integrity of the electromechanical system and identified optimal performance parameters. title: In-flight cosmic radiation doses along the current alternative routes between Tokyo and Frankfurt
abstract: Background Calculation-based dose assessment for aircraft crew is required worldwide by authorities, as cosmic radiation dose rates at aviation altitudes are substantially higher than at sea level. The accuracy of the calculated in-flight dose onboard aircraft (“route dose” hereafter) should be confirmed periodically, particularly when the flight route is significantly changed. title: Maternal Intertextuality, Diasporic Identity, and Narrative Hybridity in Amit Chaudhuri’s Odysseus Abroad
abstract: Amit Chaudhuri’s Odysseus Abroad is a subtle expedition of identity, belonging, and meaning in the globalised era. The novel’s explorative narrative structure interweaves genres, blending themes of diasporic experience, cultural hybridity, and existential introspection. Through its non-linear narrative, stream-of-consciousness narration, and intertextuality with Homer’s Odyssey, Chaudhuri both reinstates essentialist notions of identity and celebrates its temporal, conditional nature. title: Exploring Spitsbergen’s Potential for Sustainable Development and Geopark Creation
abstract: There is growing evidence of environmental degradation in the Arctic, reflected in rising temperatures, ice melt, and more frequent extreme weather events. In this context, tourism development in Spitsbergen must be balanced with nature conservation. This study aims to examine experiences of tourism and opinions on sustainable activities, as well as to explore the potential for establishing a geopark on Svalbard. title: Global length–weight relationships of deep‐pelagic fishes: Coverage, biases and variability
abstract: Length-weight relationships (LWRs) are morphometric tools that allow body mass to be estimated from fish length, providing input for fisheries, ecological and biodiversity studies. For deep-pelagic fishes, however, LWR data remain fragmented and unavailable for most species. Here, we present a global synthesis of LWRs for deep-pelagic fishes, consolidating available data into a single harmonised dataset and mapping taxonomic and geographic gaps. We provide the first LWR estimates for seven species and provide additional morphometric information, including extensions of previously reported size

title: Divination and Danger in the Festival of Indra’s Banner
abstract: Abstract This article centers on an analysis of the structure of the medieval Hindu festive ritual of “Indra’s Banner” ( indradhvaja ), using the canonical account of the sixth-century astrologer-astronomer Varāhamihira ( Bṛhatsaṃhitā 42). After situating the ritual within the broader calendar of royal ceremonial, as the inauguration of the autumnal war season, it argues for an interpretation centering on two outstanding and related themes: warfare and divination. title: MEDIEVAL GLASS OBJECTS FROM THE LOWER SYR DARYA: COMPOSITION, TECHNOLOGY, AND ARCHAEOLOGICAL SIGNIFICANCE
abstract: The article presents the preliminary results of a study of the chemical composition of glass artifacts discovered at medieval archaeological sites located along the ancient Zhanadarya riverbed in the lower reaches of the Syr Darya in the Eastern Aral Sea region. The study focuses on materials from the Zhankala (Zhent) and Mortyk settlements, the Kumkala fortress, and other archaeological sites in the region. title: Club Antarctica? Why a community approach matters for public engagement in gateway cities
abstract: Abstract With Antarctica facing many urgent environmental challenges, it is becoming increasingly important to ensure that members of the public are supported to understand, care about and protect the southern polar region. Research to date has taken a variety of approaches to Antarctic public engagement, framing it as a challenge for science communication, the media, education and/or the arts. In this paper, we take a social approach by examining public engagement with Antarctica’s communities, applying theories of place attachment, social capital and structuration. title: A reliability analysis method for Christmas tree in operating conditions based on FEMCA, FTA and numerical simulation
abstract: The installation and recovery process of Christmas tree is complex and technically difficult, and it bears high internal and external loads during production and has extremely high requirements for operation reliability. To ensure the safe operation of China's first domestically produced deepwater subsea Christmas tree installation and production conditions, a reliability analysis method for Christmas tree in operating conditions based on FEMCA, FTA and numerical simulation is established. title: Supersonic jets and strong shock waves generated by electrical explosions of V-shaped foils in water and gelatin
abstract: Abstract Building on prior work demonstrating that underwater microsecond timescale electrical explosions of semi-cylindrical wire arrays produce radially converging strong shock waves and blade-shaped supersonic jets reaching 1.6 km/s [ Experiments in Fluids 67, 25 (2026)], this study presents experimental investigations and two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations aimed at optimizing jets generation from tamped, V-shaped electrically exploded foils. title: INVENTORY OF THE INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE OF THE KAZAKHS OF THE AKTOBE REGION: SELECTED TRADITIONS OFNATIONAL CUISINE
abstract: Based on materials from a comprehensive ethnographic expedition, this article examines the preservation of generational continuity through the systematic collection of the intangible cultural heritage of the Aktobe region Kazakhs. The study aims to identify the contemporary significance and generational continuity of the intangible cultural heritage of the Kazakhs of the Aktobe region through its comprehensive inventory, scientific analysis, and systematization. title: Colonial Environmental Governance in Maluku (1652–1799): Historical Insights from Hongi Tochten
abstract: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) maintained its clove monopoly in the Maluku Islands through Hongi Tochten, a series of naval expeditions traditionally interpreted as instruments of military coercion and commercial control. However, their role as mechanisms of environmental governance has received limited scholarly attention. This study examines how Hongi Tochten unctioned as a system of colonial environmental governance and analyses its implications for indigenous social–ecological systems in Maluku between 1652 and 1799. title: Tropical Bastions: It’s Time for a Pacific Bastion Strategy in the First Island Chain
abstract: This article proposes an operational approach to the use of naval forces in the first island chain of the Pacific vis-à-vis the threat of the People’s Liberation Army Navy of China and its attempts to enforce the nine-dash line. It argues that geography, deception, and mobility, particularly in the Philippine Archipelago, offer policy makers and military planners opportunity for the employment of naval forces in natural inland sea bastions. title: Pharmakos and Sacrificial Womanhood: The Politics of Social Order in Euripides’ Iphigenia at Aulis and Idegu’s the Legendary Inikpi
abstract: Communal survival, gender, tragedy and sacrifice are recurring subject matter in Greek and Igala cultural and literary traditions. This study compares Euripides’ Iphigenia at Aulis and Idegu's The Legendary Inikpi to examine how sacrificial womanhood is constructed and used to sustain social order within two distinct cultural logics. title: Accounting and Maritime Accounting: Differences and Relationships
abstract: Background: The global and Indonesian maritime sector requires accounting systems capable of addressing distinctive transaction characteristics, operational risks, and sustainability demands. Maritime accounting refers to accounting practices adapted to shipping, port, marine, and fisheries industries. However, its conceptual boundaries and scope remain insufficiently defined in the literature. title: PRESERVING REGIONAL HISTORY THROUGH CULTURAL TOURISM: A CASE STUDY OF THE SAVITSKY MUSEUM AND ITS GLOBAL AUDIENCE
abstract: This paper examines the pivotal role of cultural tourism in safeguarding regional history and ethnic identity, focusing on the I.V. Savitsky State Museum of Arts in Nukus, Uzbekistan. Known globally as the "Louvre of the Desert," the museum holds a unique dual repository consisting of the world's second-largest collection of Soviet avant-garde art and an extensive archive of traditional Karakalpak applied arts alongside ancient Khorezm archaeological antiquities. title: Morphology and Morphometrics of Macrophthalmidae (Brachyura) in Manado Bay, North Sulawesi, Indonesia
abstract: The objective of this research was to examine the morphological and descriptive morphometric characteristics of two sand crab species of the genus Macrophthalmus found in the rocky intertidal zone in Manado Bay, North Sulawesi. Three individuals of Macrophthalmus (Mareotis) purpureocheir were collected during the new moon phase, while one individual of Macrophthalmus (Mareotis) crinitus was collected during the first quarter moon phase. title: From the Indo-Pacific to Mexico: establishment of the Longfin Batfish, Platax teira (Forsskål, 1775) (Acanthuriformes, Ephippidae), in the Tropical Eastern Pacific
abstract: We report 100 individuals of the Longfin Batfish, Platax teira (Forsskål, 1775), from the Mexican Pacific. Records include first reports from the Revillagigedo Islands and Michoacán, as well as additional sightings from Baja California Sur, Jalisco, Colima, Guerrero, and Oaxaca. Individuals included juveniles, subadults, and adults documented through diving, snorkeling, and one incidental fishery capture. abstract: A new species of the ostracod genus Polycopsis G. W. Müller, 1894 (Myodocopa: Halocyprida: Polycopidae), P. higejii sp. nov., is described from the interstitial habitat of a sandy beach in Miura City, central Japan. This is the first record of the genus from a sandy beach interstitial environment. The new species is characterized by a broadly suboval carapace with approximately 20 serrations along the anterior margin, 16 plumose setae on the branchial plate of the fifth limb, and a straight sword-like ejaculatory duct on the male copulatory organ. title: Operational management of Nile water intakes: assessing safe submergence against ship and wind-induced vortexing
abstract: Water intakes in navigable rivers like the Nile face significant risks of air-entraining vortices due to ship- and wind-induced surface fluctuations, which conventional static submergence criteria fail to address. This study evaluates these dynamic effects and develops an integrated framework for determining Safe Minimum Submergence Depth (SMSD) in the Aswan-Esna reach (158 cross-sections). title: Latent Gestures: Autobiographical Perception and Queer Recognition in the South East Archive of Seaside Photography
abstract: This practice-based paper examines how embodied, queer and neurodivergent modes of perception shape the interpretation of photographic archives. Focusing on Latent: A Hidden History, a project developed through the South East Archive of Seaside Photography (SEAS), it explores how mid-twentieth-century seaside photographs, produced under the social and legal constraints of male homosexuality, can be reengaged through sustained acts of photographic looking. title: Methane oxidation in African lakes increases with phytoplankton and outweighs photosynthesis-driven oxic methane production
abstract: Lakes are large natural sources of methane (CH4), a potent greenhouse gas, resulting from the net balance of inputs from anaerobic and oxic methane production (OMP) and removal by methane oxidation (MOX). Here we investigate spatial patterns and causes of MOX variability in 79 African lakes. MOX is highest in the most productive lakes presumably due to methanotrophs attached to phytoplankton, as well as in lakes draining the wetlands of the Congo basin presumably due to inputs of methanotrophs from flooded forest soils. title: High-Altitude Exposure: Effects on Cognitive Performance, Neurovascular Mechanisms, and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: Abstract Travel to and work at high altitudes expose individuals to hypobaric hypoxia; however, its effects on neural activity and function remain insufficiently understood. Here, we present findings from a longitudinal panel study incorporating oxygen supplementation tests in individuals who traveled from low altitude (Beijing, ∼50 meters above sea level (m.a.s.l.)) to high altitude (Xizang, 3600–5000 m.a.s.l.) and subsequently returned to low altitude. title: The Intertidal Hydroids of Mount Desert Rock, Maine
abstract: We examined the intertidal hydroids of Mount Desert Rock, ME, a remote island in the Gulf of Maine. Our study was conducted concurrently with a long-term ecological survey. We collected 20 specimens of hydroids in June through August 2023 and identified these specimens using a combination of morphological keys and DNA barcoding with the 16S rRNA gene. We recorded 13 species representing 6 families and 12 genera. Our investigation reveals a diverse group of species not reflected in modern ecological surveys and represents the first inventory of hydroid species for this island.

title: Conservation Messages as Catalysts of Post-Visit Action: Insights from Zoo and Aquarium Visitors
abstract: Zoos and aquariums face an urgent challenge to convey conservation messages that motivate visitors to change their environmental behavior. This study explores the reflections of 768 visitors to one of twelve zoos and aquariums in Australia, USA, and Canada regarding the features of conservation messaging that prompted their post-visit involvement in specific environmental behaviors. Thematic analysis uncovered eight features of conservation messaging that visitors felt prompted them to adopt new behaviors or increase their engagement in existing environmental actions. abstract: Dear Readers, Welcome to this year's third issue of the International Maritime Health Magazine. Every medical specialty has a history, but not every history is preserved. Hyperbaric medicine in Latin America did not emerge from a single institution or a single pioneering individual. Rather, it evolved through diverse national experiences that were shaped by geography, maritime traditions, military and civilian medicine, engineering, scientific curiosity, and the dedication of countless, often silent, professionals. title: Estimating biomass density in land-based cultivation of Ulva spp. using a low cost RGB imaging system
abstract: Abstract Seaweed cultivation faces scalability challenges due to labor-intensive biomass monitoring. Here, we demonstrate a low cost RGB imaging system for Ulva spp. biomass estimation (0.5–5.0 g L − 1 ) in land-based raceways. title: Acoustic emission monitoring of infrastructure using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) techniques - possibilities, limitations, and optimization
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) testing is an established method for structural health monitoring and damage detection in engineering structures. Conventional AE systems are based on piezoelectric sensors that are applied at discrete locations, requiring extensive cabling and offering limited spatial coverage. Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) provides an alternative approach as a fiber-optic measurement technique, in which a single optical fiber cable serves as a continuous, spatially distributed sensor. abstract: Abstract The “Collaborative Gas Hydrate R&D Project in Alaska,” led by the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC), the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and the U.S. Geological Survey, aims to examine and assess gas hydrate reservoir systems, their production behavior, potential environmental impacts, and extraction methodologies. They were also compared with the genus descriptions and with their respective species complexes available in the literature. title: Impacts of the 2026 US-Iran War on Environmental Security in the Middle East
abstract: Modern warfare does not merely inflict human casualties; it also degrades the environmental systems vital for daily life. The 2026 US-Iran conflict poses a severe threat to regional ecosystems, as belligerents deliberately target critical infrastructure and weaponize natural resources to secure military advantages or compel concessions. Oil and gas tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, alongside refineries and energy installations throughout Iran and the Arab Gulf states, have emerged as primary targets. title: A Methodological Case Study for Integrating Virtual Reality and 3D Photogrammetry: A Pilot Digital Platform for Exploring Mangrove Environments
abstract: Mangroves are ecologically vital ecosystems that present unique logistical challenges for field-based environmental education and research due to seasonal tidal fluctuations, difficult muddy terrain, and visitor safety considerations. Balancing sustainable conservation with accessible site exploration requires innovative approaches. To address these constraints, we developed a pilot multimodal platform to demonstrate the technical feasibility of integrating virtual reality (VR) and 3D photogrammetry as core methodological components for environmental representation. abstract: The siphonostomatoid copepod Dirivultus spinigulatus Humes, 1999 (Dirivultidae) was originally described as an associate of the siboglinid tubeworm Paraescarpia echinospica Southward, Schulze, and Tunnicliffe, 2002 from the Edison Seamount hydrothermal vent in Papua New Guinea. Here, we report a new record and range extension of this copepod from the Off Toi cold seep in Suruga Bay, Japan where it was also found on P. echinospica. title: Carbon intensity compliance of a crude oil tanker: A five-year voyage-level analysis
abstract: The Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) of ships is evaluated annually; however, this aggregated calculation may conceal substantial variation in carbon intensity across different voyage types. abstract: This paper examines the civilizational role of the Arabian Gulf islands as depicted in classical sources from the 4th century BCE to the 4th century CE. Classical Greek and Roman historians and geographers produced a wealth of significant scholarly works that serve as authoritative references for the history of regions within their sphere of interest and influence, most notably the Ancient Near East, the Arabian Peninsula, and the Arabian Gulf region in particular. title: The anatomy and taxonomy of selected Neogastropoda (Gastropoda) of phylogenetic importance
abstract: Recently the phylogeny of the order Neogastropoda based on exon-capture [Fedosov et al., 2026], has confirmed the monophyly of the group and achieved high resolution for many deep nodes. Thorough examination of the sequenced species frequently revealed novel and distinctive morphological characters, and in several cases highlighted unresolved taxonomic issues. Some sequenced species proved to be new to science, while others required reassessment of their generic or familial placement in light of the phylogenetic results. The anatomy of the anterior foregut of Enigmavasidae is described herein

title: On the edge: habitat patchiness and island isolation fracture the distribution of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat
abstract: We integrate demography, morphology and genetics to assess the biology and population structure of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat (Zyzomys woodwardi), a habitat specialist of the monsoonal tropics. The species is confined to the extreme north-west of the continent and 16 adjacent islands that were part of the mainland during the last Pleistocene glaciation. Islands became isolated from ~6500 years before present (BP), with their current populations being considered relictual. abstract: The Koli and Agri communities have occupied a visibly glaring space in the landscape of Mumbai since time immemorial.They have made their presence felt not only demographically, but also culturally and politically.However, despite being the city's age-old inhabitants and landowners, both communities have been pushed to the margins for various reasons.From facing a serious bout of identity crisis to being introduced to other religions, the Koli and Agri communities are plagued with a whole host of problems.As a permanent solution to these problems and also for a sense of security, the two commu

title: Dorsal-Fin Musculoskeletal System of Oarfishes (Regalecidae): Fin Rays as Rotating Elements in an Undulatory System
abstract: In addition to lateral undulation, oarfishes (Regalecus spp.) swim by passing unidirectional or counter-propagating waves along the elongated dorsal fin. Such ribbon-finned swimming evolved independently in several groups of teleosts, such as the gymnotiform knifefishes, which have an elongated anal fin. Studies of ribbon-finned swimming in knifefishes led to an interest in the biomimetic potential of this type of propulsion. title: Fletcheria gen. nov. (Ralfsiales, Phaeophyceae): A new crustose brown algal genus clarifying evolutionary relationships of Ralfsia pacifica
abstract: The genus Ralfsia was historically broadly circumscribed but has recently undergone significant taxonomic revision. Based on molecular data, a restricted Ralfsia sensu stricto was delineated that had many species reassigned to new genera and families. The current work builds on that work by resolving the phylogenetic position, defining the morphological features, and establishing the biogeographic distribution of Ralfsia pacifica-a crustose brown alga widely distributed along the eastern Pacific coastline. Ship Safety Analysis in Indonesia: Determining Crew Competence, Port Digitalization and Ship Technology Innovation
abstract: This study aims to analyze the determinants of ship safety in Indonesia by integrating three key constructs: crew competence, port digitalization, and ship technology innovation. The high risk of domestic maritime accidents underscores the urgent need for a holistic evaluation of the maritime ecosystem. The study employs a descriptive qualitative approach based on a Systematic Literature Review (SLR). title: Multistage Evolution and Inheritance in a Magma‐Poor Conjugate Margin: Insights From Serpentinized Peridotites of the Newfoundland Margin (ODP Hole 1277A)
abstract: Abstract The nature of mantle sections exhumed at magma‐poor rifted margins remains poorly constrained, largely because direct sampling of mantle in modern passive margins is exceptionally rare. The Iberia–Newfoundland system is unique in providing drilled mantle rocks on both conjugate margins, offering an unprecedented glimpse into mantle heterogeneity across an entire rift system. Here we present new in situ major and trace element data from highly serpentinized peridotites recovered at ODP Hole 1277A (Newfoundland margin). title: Pollution Prevention by Design for Wing-in-Ground Craft: A Technical Design Review Based on IMO Environmental Requirements
abstract: The increasing development of Wing-in-Ground (WIG) craft as an energy-efficient maritime transportation system has highlighted the importance of integrating environmental protection into the early stages of vessel design. Although WIG craft offer advantages in fuel efficiency and reduced operational resistance through the ground effect phenomenon, their unique operational characteristics introduce environmental risks associated with fuel leakage, solid waste, sewage discharge, and atmospheric emissions. journal: International Journal of Marine Engineering Innovation and Research

title: Heliox versus trimix in closed‐circuit rebreather diving: A comparative study of pulmonary and decompression stress in male divers
abstract: Abstract Closed‐circuit rebreather (CCR) and helium‐based breathing mixtures are widely used in technical diving. This study compared the effects of Heliox and Trimix on pulmonary function and decompression stress during CCR dives. Nineteen divers performed a standardized dive (50 ± 3 msw, 147 ± 10 min) using Heliox (16% O 2 /84% He; n = 9) or Trimix (16% O 2 /32% He/52% N 2 ; n = 10). institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

title: Heavy metals in raw cow, goat and sheep milk: Associated dietary exposure and human health risk assessment in eastern Algeria
abstract: In recent years, the presence of heavy metals in milk has emerged as an important public health issue, owing to their potential detrimental effects on milk quality.The present study aimed to assess the occurrence and levels of heavy metals in raw cow, goat, and sheep milk obtained from eastern Algeria.Sixty milk samples were analysed for Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni and Fe using atomic absorption spectrometry.Results demonstrated that Fe (5.49 ± 21.93) was the dominant metal in cow milk, followed by Cu (0.86 ± 0.02) and Cr (0.56 ± 0.05).In goat milk, Fe (9.77 ± 0.69) and Cu (2.79 ± 0.04) were highest, while

title: Challenges of the assessment of nature conservation value of aquatic habitats using microalgae
abstract: Abstract The increasing focus on ecosystem restoration in European environmental policy highlights the need for reliable methods to quantify the nature conservation value (NCV) of aquatic habitats. Current Water Framework Directive (WFD) metrics assess ecological quality mainly through the phytoplankton community composition and abundance. However, these approaches do not reflect properly the real conservation value of the habitats, because they overlook the contribution of rare and unique algal species. Currently, the method proposed by Coesel is the only microalgae-based framework explicitly

title: Research on the Green Development of Port Mechanical and Electrical Equipment under the "Dual Carbon" Strategy
abstract: After the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality were put forward, the pressure of emission reduction in the shipping industry has been accelerated to transmit to ports, and the green and low-carbon transformation of mechanical and electrical equipment has thus become an important starting point for the implementation of emission reduction. This paper reviews the carbon reduction practices of typical ports at home and abroad, and examines the application effects and bottlenecks of core technologies from four directions: new energy power machinery, braking energy recovery, multi-energy c

title: Science as added value? Tourists’ perceptions of science-tourism practices in Antarctic deep-field tourism and implications for ambassadorship
abstract: This paper investigates the role of science-tourism practices in shaping tourists’ perceptions and ethical positioning within Antarctic deep-field tourism. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork in East Antarctica and semi-structured interviews, the study examines how operators’ support for science influences tourists’ pre-trip decision-making, perceptions of legitimacy, and environmental responsibility. The findings reveal that support for scientific research contributes to both operational and moral legitimacy, enhancing trust in tour operators by signalling competence and reliability, while also

title: Relocating Large Hollow‐Bearing Tree Trunk Sections to Restore Forest Owl Breeding Habitat: When Is It Warranted?
abstract: ABSTRACT Relocating large hollows to minimise the potential impacts of development on threatened species is generally considered too difficult and/or too costly. Small and medium‐sized hollows are commonly relocated, recreated by carving into a living surrogate tree, or replaced with nest boxes; however, larger hollows, which take much longer to form naturally, are far less represented in the landscape, are preferred over nest boxes by large forest owls, are being destroyed during vegetation clearing and are not being replaced. title: Formation of the sclerites in Solenogastres and Caudofoveata (Mollusca, Aplacophora)
abstract: Solenogastres and Caudofoveata are vermiform, shell-less molluscs, with the mantle covered by calcareous scales or spines (sclerites) embedded in a cuticle secreted by the mantle epithelium. Molecular studies recover them as a single clade (Aplacophora), sister of Polyplacophora, and together, they form the sister group to all other molluscs. Within this phylogenetic framework, sclerites emerge as potentially informative characters for reconstructing early molluscan evolution. However, the cellular mechanisms underlying sclerite formation in Aplacophora remain poorly resolved. Previous work ha

title: Modular ESP Teaching Design of Maritime English Based on STCW Requirements for Higher Vocational Seafarer Majors
abstract: The Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping for Seafarers (STCW) Convention establishes statutory requirements for seafarers’ practical proficiency in maritime English, which is directly related to navigation safety and international shipping operations. However, current maritime English instruction in higher vocational colleges focuses more on theoretical knowledge, such as vocabulary and grammar, while neglecting practical onboard applications, leading to a disconnect between students’ examination performance and actual job requirements. title: Study on the application of U-shape anti-roll tank for a water hyacinth processing machine
abstract: This study focuses on developing a stabilization system suitable for the actual operating conditions of a water hyacinth shredding machine on inland rivers and canals, with the aim of maintaining roll stability throughout operation. The paper proposes the application of a U-shaped anti-roll tank, or U-tank, to the water hyacinth shredding machine. Based on a survey of the vessel’s operating conditions, a two-degree-of-freedom mathematical model was developed to describe the interaction between the vessel’s roll motion and liquid oscillation inside the U-tank. journal: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology

title: Foodborne Illnesses, Food Poisoning, Environmental Contaminants and Food Safety in the World: A Comprehensive Mini Review
abstract: Food safety remains an absolute cornerstone of global public health and socioeconomic stability. Unsafe food causes an estimated 866 million illnesses and 1.52 million deaths globally each year, resulting in an annual economic loss of US$ 310 billion across the globe. The main objective of this mini-review is to synthesize current knowledge on foodborne pathogens, food additives, heavy metals, microplastics, emerging anthropogenic hazards, and advances in diagnostic methods. A total of 1,500 research articles retrieved from Google Scholar, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, ResearchGate, and PubMe

title: Dynamic Influence Based Fitness Shaping For Cooperative Coevolution
abstract: Multiagent settings are naturally characterized by coevolutionary dynamics, where agents must adapt and learn in the context of their teammates. A key challenge in such domains is determining how to credit an agent for its individual contribution to team performance. Fitness shaping approaches partially address this by identifying and isolating an agent's direct contribution to team success. However, when an agent's contribution is indirect, such as influencing other teammates to succeed, existing methods fail to capture its impact on the team. journal: ACM Transactions on Evolutionary Learning and Optimization

title: First confirmed record of Centrophorus uyato (Rafinesque, 1810) in Irish waters: integration of morphological traits and DNA barcoding
abstract: Abstract We report the occurrence of a mature male Centrophorus uyato (Squaliformes: Centrophoridae) from the Porcupine Bank off western Ireland. A single specimen with a total length of 853 mm was caught by bottom trawl in 2023 at a depth of 660 m. The specimen was identified morphologically and confirmed by molecular taxonomy using DNA barcoding. The morphometric data obtained are consistent with previous descriptions of the species. abstract: Indian knowledge system associated with the traditional methodology aesthetic philosophy and cultural heritage.And this study explores sustainable art practices within the Indian art field through a practicebased research methodology.The primary objective is to examine art projects, case study and the creative processes, as well as their ecological and social impacts on society.It is imperative to acknowledge the environmental crisis of the current century and to adapt our ecological framework to safeguard the future.This research focuses on the work of artists engaged in sustainable art pract

title: Results of two-year observations of snow evaporation and sublimation in the area of the “Ice Base Cape Baranova” Research Station (Severnaya Zemlya archipelago)
abstract: Instrumental data on sublimation from the snow cover surface in the high-latitude Arctic remain scarce. Existing estimates indicate a wide range of sublimation losses, varying from 10 to 90 % of the total cold-season precipitation depending on local climatic and landscape conditions. The paper presents the results of two-year (2024–2025) instrumental observations of sublimation from the snow cover in the high-latitude Arctic, specifically in the area of the research station “Ice Base Cape Baranova” (Severnaya Zemlya archipelago). abstract: Out of all raw natural resources, groundwater is among the most exploited by humans.We have entered an era of global water bankruptcy, with many regions consuming water resources beyond their capacity for natural renewal.As groundwater extraction escalates, we are not only depleting the vastest global unfrozen freshwater reservoir but also compromising the integrity of groundwater (and groundwater-dependent) ecosystems and aggravating climate change-related effects such as salinization and desertification.Aiming to widen our understanding on the role of groundwaters within the global water cyc

title: Spatial variation in aquatic arthropod biodiversity in floating photovoltaic host waterbodies
abstract: Abstract Floating photovoltaic (FPV) solar energy is a rapidly expanding renewable energy technology in which photovoltaic panels are deployed on floating structures atop waterbodies. While FPVs may alleviate pressure on terrestrial biodiversity, relatively little is known about aquatic biodiversity within FPV host waterbodies. Most FPV studies have focused on abiotic environmental changes, with comparatively few examining wildlife responses. title: A high-throughput method for quantifying degradation in maritime PEM fuel cells using a multichannel potentiostat
abstract: The durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells under maritime conditions is influenced by the vessel's operational profile, for example idling and intermittent shutdowns. To investigate this, we introduce a high-throughput accelerated stress test (AST) methodology using a multichannel potentiostat to simultaneously analyze up to eight membrane electrode assemblies. title: Taxonomic and ecological assessment of an Antarctic Eocene Folivora (Mammalia) metacarpal using three‐dimensional geometric morphometrics
abstract: Here, we reassess the taxonomic affinities and functional morphology of TMM 44190-1, an isolated metacarpal II from the Eocene La Meseta Formation, Marambio (Seymour) Island, Antarctic Peninsula, previously referred to an indeterminate xenarthran. We evaluated its morphological similarities using three-dimensional geometric morphometrics. title: Design of Technological Infrastructures in Health and Wellness Tourism and their Effects on Hotel Hospitality: The Case of the Municipality of Lamia
abstract: Health and well-being are increasingly pursued through prevention rather than treatment, creating demand for new tourism products and services. This paper examines how technological infrastructures can support health and wellness tourism and how they affect hotel hospitality, using the Municipality of Lamia, Central Greece, as a case study. title: Regulatory Intermediation and Energy Transition Readiness at the Port of Keelung, Taiwan
abstract: International maritime environmental regulation is changing port sustainability from a predominantly local environmental-management task into a cross-organisational challenge involving vessels, energy systems, terminal operations, logistics customers, public authorities, and port-city communities. This article examines how the International Maritime Organization’s greenhouse-gas framework and the European Union’s FuelEU Maritime regime transmit strategic pressure to the non-EU Port of Keelung in Taiwan. title: A Love Made of Stones: Contemporary Anishinaabe Lyric and Asiniig Sovereignty
abstract: This article delves into the literary motif of the stone (asiniig) in contemporary Anishinaabe poetry as an ontological assertion of Indigenous sovereignty. By synthesising Michelle Raheja’s “visual sovereignty” (2007) and Kenneth White’s “geopoetics” (1979; 2004), I trace how poets Kimberly Blaeser, Louise Erdrich, and Denise Sweet deploy an Indigenous geopoetics that challenges settler-colonial cartographies. title: A tengeralattjárók fejlődésének története
abstract: A tengeralattjárók fejlődése a haditechnika egyik legizgalmasabb és legdinamikusabb területe, amely a kezdeti, egyszerű víz alatti járművektől a modern, nukleáris meghajtású, nagy hatótávolságú tengeralattjárókig terjed. A cikk – nagy vonalakban - áttekinti a technológiai innovációk és a stratégiai alkalmazások fejlődését, valamint a tengeralattjárók szerepét a hadviselés és a tengerészeti biztonság területén.

title: Pérez de Ribas’ Historia (1645) and the Protohistoric Period in Sonora and Southern Arizona
abstract: The protohistoric period along the Arizona-Sonora borderlands is an important yet poorly understood period. Historical sources, particularly Perez de Ribas’ Historia (1645), are discussed along with archaeological data that point to a late prehistoric expansion of the Opata into O'odham lands. Evidence of warfare and invasion is presented that may help explain the appearance of forts and defensive retreats, Sobaipuri origins, and Eudeve/Teguima linguistics.

title: Water Bodies and Colonization of the Niger Delta, 1800 to 1900
abstract: It is a truism that water bodies provided the gateway for the colonization of the Niger Delta. The work argues that the explorers, missionaries and traders promoted European political and economic interests in the Niger Delta hence, the Lander Brothers through their exploration opened up the Delta for commerce and used the waterway to explore the interior while providing information of their findings to Britain. title: Full‐Waveform Seismic Tomography of the Upper Mantle Beneath the Arabia‐Eurasia Collision Zone
abstract: Abstract Despite being one of the most recent major orogenic events, the timing of the Arabia‐Eurasia collision is still debated. Much of the discrepancy arises due to uncertainties over the amount of continental subduction of the Arabian passive margin and the timing of a hard collision of cratonic Arabian lithosphere with Eurasia. Subducted continental lithosphere and underthrusted cratons can be imaged using high resolution seismic tomography, which can be used to improve understanding of the tectonic history of the region. title: Strategy and Contradiction: Towards a Theory of Strategic Judgement
abstract: Strategy is commonly concerned with relating political purposes to the means available for their achievement. This article asks a prior question: what conditions make strategic judgement necessary in the first place? It argues that strategic problems arise from the contradictory character of political life, in which competing purposes cannot be permanently reconciled, and every decision alters the circumstances confronting those that follow. Strategy therefore requires practical judgement rather than the application of predetermined solutions. Drawing upon Clausewitz and examining deterrence,

title: Outpacing: A Grand Strategy for Avoiding the Carthaginian Error
abstract: This article warns Western democracies against committing the Carthaginian error, that is, not taking a strategic rival seriously. It argues strategic rivals should be dealt with through a grand strategy of Outpacing, the aim of which is to establish a lead over them severe enough to cause their political and economic collapse, or their forfeiture of the competition.

title: The Fortified Disposition, Part I: Strategic Complexes, Historical Attenuation, and the Return of the Guarded City
abstract: Fortification is better understood as a movement-slowing strategic complex than as a wall that either holds or fails. This paper traces the long attenuation of that disposition in the West, then shows how scarce manpower, costly platforms and persistent surveillance are bringing it back—first of all in the guarded, closable city assembled through dual-use fabric, regulation and urban air defence.

title: The Golden Dome, Missile Defenses and Deterrence
abstract: This article examines the Trump administration proposal for a Golden Dome missile defense system in terms of its implications for technology, strategy and U.S. national security policy. It also considers whether the proposed missile defense system, once having been deployed, will support deterrence as we now understand it, or require a rethinking of past assumptions about nuclear-strategic stability.

title: Research on Tourism Environmental Economy of Hainan Free Trade Port: Evolution Context, Hotspot Review and Frontier Prospect
abstract: As the highest form of opening-up in the global contemporary economy, the free trade port undertakes the strategic function of promoting institutional reform and high-quality regional development through opening-up. As the core experimental field of China’s open economic system with Chinese characteristics, Hainan Free Trade Port (Hainan FTP) deeply integrates tourism, ecological environment and economic development in its construction process, forming a unique research field of tourism environmental economy. title: Updating thermal head of RECoverable Autonomous Sonde (RECAS) for better drilling performance in Qilin Subglacial Lake exploration
abstract: Abstract. There are numerous subglacial lakes in Antarctica, typically covered by thick ice sheets. Qilin subglacial lake is one of the largest subglacial lakes in Antarctica, lying beneath approximately 3600 m of ice. The exploration of this unique environment is of considerable scientific importance. Recoverable Autonomous Sonde (RECAS) has been proposed for exploring Qilin subglacial lake. However, drilling into the lakes with such probe may be impeded by volcanic ash or small rock clasts within the ice sheet. abstract: The article analyzes the current state and prospects of implementing fiber-optic technologies in unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) as an effective response to the challenges of modern electronic warfare. Their potential applications are considered both in the field of intelligence gathering and for the delivery of explosives to designated targets.The classification features of drones are systematized, their main functional purposes are defined, and the advantages and limitations of traditional radio-controlled systems are examined. title: Heteroptera (Insecta, Hemiptera) fauna of Eritrea
abstract: The suborder Heteroptera, commonly known as “true bugs,” represents the largest group within hemi-metabolous insects, comprising over 45,000 species. Eritrea, characterised by a Hot Semi-Arid to Hot Desert Climate, is notable for its four regional centres of vegetation endemism and approximately 430 woody plant species. This study aims to review and update the list of Heteroptera fauna recorded in Eritrea, based on existing historical literature. title: Trigonometrical Juridism in British India: Unificatory Images and Jurisdictional Rationality
abstract: Abstract This article engages with two aspects of how cartography enabled law and jurisdictional ordering in a specific historical context. First, by interrogating the ways in which the great trigonometrical surveys of the British colonial enterprise and the Atlas of India entrenched “India” as a distinct, coherent, and contiguous geographical entity, this article will demonstrate how an epistemology rooted in a civilising impulse produced the perception of India as a thoroughly refined British legal territory. title: Opegaster plateen n. sp. (Digenea: Opecoelidae) from the giant mudskipper Periophthalmus schlosseri (Pallas, 1770) (Perciformes: Gobiidae) from Thailand
abstract: Abstract Mudskippers (Oxudercinae) are amphibious gobioid fishes inhabiting intertidal and mangrove ecosystems throughout the Indo–West Pacific region. Despite their ecological importance, information on their helminth fauna remains scarce. During a survey of parasites infecting the giant mudskipper, Periophthalmodon schlosseri (Pallas, 1770), in Chumphon Province, Thailand, specimens of an undescribed species of Opegaster Ozaki, 1925 (Opecoelidae) were recovered from the intestine. title: Systemic risks for Greece’s economy and the need for its national strategy of new industrialization. Lessons for Ukraine
abstract: The research paper focuses on the structural imbalances in the Greek economy, which pose systemic risks to its development amid geopolitical turbulence, global trade wars and a slowdown in economic growth in EU countries – its main trading partners. The structural imbalances in the Greek economy are categorised into four interrelated groups, and the paper examines their causes and consequences. We analysed the core factors of the protracted and deep Greek financial and economic crisis, which entered its active phase in 2010 and lasted for almost ten years. abstract: Overtourism is an increasing concern for destinations seeking to accommodate visitor growth while protecting residents’ quality of life and long-term sustainability. Yet, how overtourism is represented through user-generated social media content remains underexplored. Drawing on destination image theory, this study analyses 600 Instagram posts tagged #overtourism to examine the visual themes, attraction types, sentiment, and thematic framing associated with overtourism. title: Archipelagic memories at Lau King Howe Hospital Memorial Museum
abstract: Colonial pasts, geopolitical differences, and plural social constructions of Malaya/post-independence Malaysia contributed to and were reflected in hospital design. Sarawak in East Malaysia, on Borneo Island, saw developments that paralleled those in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur. How did the multi-ethnic complexity of the patient demographic impact post-independence medical institutions? title: Influence Without Alliances: China, Pakistan, and Indirect Military Engagement in the Persian Gulf
abstract: This article examines how China expands security influence in the Persian Gulf without alliances, bases, or direct intervention. It introduces indirect military engagement to explain influence through technology diffusion, defence-industrial cooperation, intermediary partnerships, and partner adaptation. Focusing on Pakistan, it argues that Chinese systems gain regional relevance through Pakistani absorption, localisation, training, maintenance, and demonstration. title: Modern Air Operations and Wylie’s Cumulative and Sequential Operational Patterns
abstract: Strategist Joseph Caldwell Wylie argued that strategies were implemented through two general types of operational patterns: sequential and cumulative. This article discusses the conceptualisations of these two patterns and then applies them to three modern air war cases to bring out their subtleties and nuances. Wylie’s simple typology has a surprising depth that makes it useful to air strategists when considering future air operations whether in peace of war.

abstract: Swedish botanist Kåre Bremer (b.1948) reshaped modern botany across three interconnected domains: the systematics of Compositae, the theory and practice of cladistics, and the phylogenetic classification of flowering plants. title: Violating the Sacred Order: Sin, Punishment, and Ecological Consciousness in Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
abstract: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner by Samuel Taylor Coleridge explores themes of sin, guilt, retribution, and salvation. According to the research, the Mariner’s killing of the Albatross violates the sacred bond among humans, nature, and the divine and is a moral transgression. The study examines how Coleridge portrays punishment as a psychological and spiritual process rather than a consequence, drawing on the poem’s symbolism, supernatural imagery, and religious themes. title: Etymologies of Australian reptiles
abstract: Australia, covering almost 7.7 million km2 (3 million mi2), is a mega-biodiverse region with 19 recognised families, 164 genera, six subgenera, 1152 species, and 60 subspecies of reptiles. This study resolves the etymologies of their scientific names (nomina). Most generic and subgeneric names (69%) are derived from Greek, while half (50%) of species and subspecies originate from Latin. Greek-derived names are more often composites than Latin-derived ones. abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate the environmental, economic and social sustainability of next-generation commercial supersonic transport and develops the Supersonic Sustainability Transition Assessment Model (SSTAM) to distinguish near-term actionable pathways from options dependent on wider socio-technical readiness. Design/methodology/approach SSTAM integrates ISO 14040/44-aligned life-cycle assessment, triple bottom line indicators, multi-criteria decision analysis, scenario and Monte Carlo uncertainty testing and socio-technical systems/multi-level perspective interpretation. title: The impact of behavioural activity on the EEG power spectrum, its source localisation, and global functional connectivity in rats
abstract: The behavioural activity of freely moving animals is a confounding factor that affects the recording, analysis, and final results of animal EEG experiments. Along with the lack of standardisation in animal in vivo electrophysiology experiments, this could lead to significant inconsistencies, especially in the analysis of centrally acting drugs. abstract: To address the Haeckelian deficit in Apobaetis, a genus in which the adult stage remains unknown for most species, with imagos currently described for only six of the 22 valid species, we provide new descriptions of the adult stages of A. jacobusi (male and female), A. pasternakae, A. nisiae and A. biancae (females). abstract: Background: Teaching in maritime higher education places simultaneous demands on instruction, assessment, student support, and administrative work. Objective: The study described stress management and perceived professional efficacy among instructors at a Philippine maritime college, and compared rank patterns across program-size groups. title: Cosmo-currere: Conventional to circumspective
abstract: Through autobiographical study, I explore the relations of my lived experiences with my academic interests. Conversations are complicated not only by the singularity of the individual, but also by the world, conceived here as historical and biospheric. Engagements with the worlds of within and without and study through and on the method of currere (Pinar, 1975) structure the research. abstract: Loktak Lake in Manipur is more than an ecological resource — it is a deeply storied landscape embedded with material, cultural, and spiritual significance. Central to its ecological uniqueness is the phumdi , a floating biomass that supports both human habitation and rich biodiversity. abstract: This study examines the spatial and seasonal variability of water quality in glacier-fed river systems within the Karatal River basin, located in the north-western sector of the Zhetysu Alatau (Kazakhstan). The investigation focused on the Kora and Shyzhy rivers, which play a key role in forming the hydrological regime of the Karatal River. abstract: This study develops a mission energy-based framework to assess the performance and technical feasibility of retrofitting an existing commuter aircraft with battery-electric propulsion. abstract: Libya, one of the largest countries in North Africa, is characterized by a Mediterranean climate along its northern coast and an extensive hot desert climate across much of its territory. These environmental conditions provide suitable habitats for a diverse assemblage of scorpion species adapted to arid ecosystems. title: Shaped by humans but increasingly threatened: pathways for the conservation of Palaearctic grasslands
abstract: Palaearctic grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems of the Northern Hemisphere, but their conservation depends on continued management that must be reconciled with agricultural production, rural livelihoods and other socio-economic demands. Introducing a special issue that brings together 18 contributions from across Eurasia, we synthesize the interacting pressures shaping these grasslands and identify pathways towards their effective conservation. abstract: Heavy-duty trucks account for a disproportionate share of road-transport emissions, yet the eco-driving coaches deployed in commercial fleets typically deliver generic and opaque feedback. This paper reports an industrial case study, conducted with Volvo Group, of an end-to-end conversational AI coach for heavy-duty eco-driving. abstract: The Siege of Szigetvar in 1566 was the closing move of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent's 46-year reign and one of the peak points of the Ottoman Empire's military strategies towards Western Europe in the 16th century. Historians examine the military, logistical, socio-economic, and political dimensions of the campaign with an interdisciplinary approach. title: Chinese Expansionist Philosophy’s Historical Bacground
abstract: This article examines the historical foundations and contemporary manifestations of ideas commonly associated with Chinese expansionism. It asks how classical concepts such as Tianxia, Confucian moral authority, Legalist state capacity, and tributary relations are reinterpreted in present-day foreign policy. title: Work Stress, Coping Strategies, and Job Satisfaction Among Food Service Workers in Bohol: A Descriptive-Correlational Study
abstract: Work stress is a significant occupational concern in the food service industry, with documented links to burnout, emotional labor, reduced service quality, and turnover intentions. This study examined the relationships among perceived work stress, coping strategies, and job satisfaction among food service workers in Bohol, Philippines, and explored which stressor domains – particularly social support – are more salient in this context. abstract: This study presents the results of bryological surveys conducted in 2003 and 2012 on Mount Muruk Mio and Bukit Rimau in Sipitang, Sabah, Malaysian Borneo, with a focus on assessing species richness and composition of mosses. abstract: Travel serves as a doorway to other worlds and a tool for self-discovery, allowing travellers to transcend preconceptions and gain a more profound comprehension of individuals and locations. This paper explores how firsthand interactions with foreign cultures, environments, and social realities alter perception. abstract: One specimen of Otodus auriculatus and three specimens of O. megalodon are added to the catalogue of skeletal material from megatooth sharks. The development of BTMS has been a crucial part of the commercialization of electric vehicles. The efficiency of the BTMS has become a bottleneck to increasing the battery's charging and discharging rates. title: When heritage becomes a burden: an evidence-based reference class of tourism stress in historic cities
abstract: Overtourism and carrying-capacity models have traditionally explained heritage-city stress through visitor volume and density. However, these approaches provide limited explanation of why comparable tourism pressures produce different forms and levels of stress across historic cities. This study addresses this gap by examining heritage stress as a perception-driven, context-dependent process shaped by interactions among spatial, social, infrastructural, cultural, and governance conditions. Embryo and root infections caused especially by soil-borne pathogens reduce yield by negatively affecting plant growth and tillering. title: First Observation of Wild Double‐Flowered Rhododendron nivale With Stamen Petaloidy and Possible Parallel Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Parallel evolution of similar phenotypes under similar selective pressures is often viewed as evidence for natural selection. However, how often such parallel variation occurs in floral traits, and its underlying mechanisms, remain poorly understood—especially in alpine plants. abstract: Mesozoic volcanic rocks of the Argentine Islands Formation (AIF) are the most common stratigraphic unit in the area of Ukrainian Antarctic Station. title: From Difficult Heritage to Difficult Temporality: The Political Life of History in Cities With Scarce Heritage
abstract: This article examines the challenges in self-narration faced by cities with short, sparse, and monotonous histories. Moving beyond the concept of “difficult heritage,” which focuses on problematic historical content (e.g., legacies of forced labor), the authors introduce “difficult temporality” to describe a structural scarcity of historical events. Drawing on emotional geography and the right to the city, this study challenges the assumption that resistance is a direct response to tourism pressures. abstract: Summary A new species of Guadua (Poaceae, Bambusoideae) from the Amazon Basin is described and illustrated. Guadua londonoae is easily distinguished from other species in the genus by a unique combination of primarily vegetative morphological characters. The most prominent diagnostic feature is the size of the auricles on the foliage leaves, which are on average four times longer than the maximum length previously recorded for any Guadua species. abstract: This research article presents a comparative analysis of economic development efforts in four West Michigan communities: Grand Haven, Holland, Hudsonville, and Zeeland. abstract: Dystopian fiction usually warns us about the future, but its most critical force often lies in what it erases from the past. abstract: Redefining Liminality in the Reading of Icelandic Sagas. abstract: The Seventh-day Adventist Church, a Christian denomination with a global presence, articulates its theology through a formal statement of 28 Fundamental Beliefs. abstract: Return mobilities are often conceptualised as an economic necessity or a failed migration outcome. Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from geothermal brines is of particular interest because co-location with closed-loop geothermal operations avoids the large land footprint of evaporitic ponds and the carbon intensity of hard-rock mining.
