title: First Documented Macroscopic Regression of Fibropapillomatosis in a Recaptured Green Sea Turtle (Chelonia mydas): A Case Study from Curaçao
abstract: Fibropapillomatosis (FP) is a neoplastic disease affecting sea turtles worldwide and is particularly prevalent in green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas). Although spontaneous regression of FP has been documented in some populations, observations remain uncommon, and the mechanisms underlying regression are poorly understood. This study documents the first known case of macroscopic FP regression in a free-ranging green sea turtle from Curaçao. title: Distinction between seismic tsunamis and meteotsunamis recorded in Greece from antiquity up to the present
abstract: Abstract Tsunami generation from earthquakes is well-known in Greece from antiquity up to the present. Tsunami studies also include cases of tsunami-like sea disturbances that possibly were meteotsunamis because of their doubtful association with earthquakes. Descriptive information and tide-gauge records were examined for a set of ten cases, three of them occurring in historical times and seven during the instrumental period after 1900. abstract: Background/Objective: Sea buckthorn contains an exceptionally rich profile of bioactive nutrients and metabolites, with established systemic therapeutic benefits across diverse pathological models. However, comprehensive data bridging these systemic outcomes with specific tissue responses are still lacking. This descriptive transcriptomic study establishes a predictive framework to guide the future application of sea buckthorn and its isolated derivatives in targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies. title: The Sino-Soviet Alliance, the Korean War, and the Predicament of the CCP’s Attack Plans for Taiwan, 1949–50
abstract: Abstract Drawing on archival materials from the Republic of China (Taiwan), the People’s Republic of China (PRC), the United States, and the former Soviet Union, this article discusses why the PRC’s 1949–50 strike plans for Taiwan went unfulfilled. What prevented the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) from “liberating” Taiwan was the fact that it lacked sufficient naval and air power to overwhelm the comparatively better equipped Kuomintang (KMT). abstract: Water and energy are interdependent resources essential for economic development and societal well-being. Consequently, increasing water demand has intensified water scarcity in many regions, a problem exacerbated by climate change. In such contexts, seawater desalination can provide a reliable and climate-independent source of freshwater, reducing pressure on conventional water resources through reverse osmosis. title: Lake eutrophication increases unprotected organic carbon pools in sediments
abstract: Abstract Reactive iron oxide-bound organic carbon (Fe–OC) is a key pathway for long-term carbon burial, but its effectiveness under increasingly widespread eutrophication remains uncertain. abstract: Abstract This article explores moral order through two cultural beliefs of usinga and limbwata as they operated in the coastal Tanga’s sisal plantations in north-eastern Tanzania, between the 1920s and the 1960s. abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Oceanic islands host exceptional biodiversity and endemism but are highly vulnerable to biological invasions. abstract: The ongoing debate regarding the spatial pattern of precipitation and effective moisture changes in monsoonal eastern China during the Marine Isotope Stage 2 (MIS 2) centers on the hydroclimatic evolution of the middle and lower Yangtze River Valley. abstract: Short-chain chlorinated paraffins (SCCPs) are persistent, bioaccumulative industrial chemicals whose environmental fate remains poorly constrained. abstract: Plastic pellets (2-5 mm industrial feedstock granules) are an increasingly important component of plastic pollution in aquatic environments. abstract: While existing scholarship extensively documents the dominance of Indian migrants in coastal and urban hubs of Kenya, the localised rural role of the diaspora in Western Kenya remains critically underexplored. The study traces the history of migration and early settlement of Indians in Kakamega Municipality, Kenya, between 1901 and 1920. abstract: Abstract The little tunny ( Euthynnus alletteratus, Scombridae) have great economic importance with a large volume of catches. Recently, both the south-eastern and northern stocks were found to be at high and moderate risk of overfishing, respectively. Here we investigated the stock structure of E. alletteratus and the phylogenetic relationships through a combination of genetic, genomic and growth analysis. Genetic data consisted of mtDNA CR sequences that defined 263 haplotypes amongst 633 individuals from nine locations. The genomic data consisted of 37,888 SNPs obtained by sequencing 89 ind

title: Macrofungi Diversity in a Community Forest, Tha Mai District, Chanthaburi Province, Thailand
abstract: This study aimed to survey macrofungi diversity in a community forest in Tha Mai District, Chanthaburi Province, Thailand, and to evaluate their trophic mode and edibility; the knowledge gained from this study will help to establish a macrofungi database as part of a biodiversity learning center for the community. Macrofungi sampling was performed in the area, with identification being done by morphological analysis and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) sequencing. title: Genetic analysis of bone morphometry and ivory vertebrae in threespine stickleback
abstract: Previous genetic studies of skeletal variation in threespine stickleback fish (Gasterosteus aculeatus) have focused primarily on striking morphological differences. Here, we examine the largely unexplored genetic architecture of internal bone microstructural variation between marine and freshwater stickleback. Micro-computed tomography X-ray analysis revealed differences in the porosity, bone thickness, and bone volume fraction within armor plates and vertebrae from a marine and freshwater stickleback. title: Review of reintroduction as a conservation tool for Pacific salmon in western North America
abstract: Abstract Objective Reintroduction of Pacific salmon Oncorhynchus spp. into historically occupied habitat is a widely used management strategy in western North America. Since the last major review, new information on donor populations, fish passage, dam removal, ecological interactions, monitoring, and cultural and societal considerations has emerged. We conducted a comprehensive review to synthesize these advances and inform best practices. Methods Co-authors representing federal, state, tribal, academic, and private organizations with expertise in Pacific salmon reintroductions convened to sy

title: Performance Analysis of Floating Solar Photovoltaic System for Humid and Saline Conditions
abstract: Floating solar photovoltaic (FSPV) systems have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional land-based photovoltaic (LSPV) systems by reducing land-use constraints and improving electrical performance through the natural cooling effect of water bodies. However, long-term deployment in humid and saline coastal environments may accelerate moisture ingress, salt deposition, and corrosion, reducing system reliability and energy generation. title: The role of host resource dynamics in shaping life-history evolution of pine processionary moths
abstract: Synchronization between larval development and peak resource quality drives life-history evolution in forest defoliators from cold-temperate regions but is less considered in other ecosystems, such as those in the Mediterranean region. Studies on Thaumetopoea pityocampa , the main Mediterranean pine defoliator, which typically develops during winter (winter population [WP]), have mostly focused on climate. title: Eukaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes recovered from deep metagenomic sequencing of the seagrass, Zostera marina, include a novel chytrid in the order Lobulomycetales
abstract: Fungi play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystems as decomposers, pathogens and endophytes, yet their significance in marine environments is often understudied. Seagrasses, as globally distributed marine flowering plants, have critical ecological functions but knowledge about their associated fungal communities remains relatively limited. Previous amplicon surveys of the fungal community associated with the seagrass, Zostera marina, have revealed an abundance of potentially novel chytrids. title: Evaluation of 18 S rRNA as an endogenous control in OpenArray® plasma RNA qPCR workflows
abstract: Abstract Background Reliable qPCR analysis depends on stable endogenous controls, particularly in high-throughput pre-amplification workflows where technical bias may arise. The suitability of highly abundant 18 S rRNA as a reference gene in multiplex OpenArray ® platforms remains debated. This study evaluated the stability of 18 S rRNA, its impact on co-amplified targets, and comparability between archived and newly manufactured primer pools. title: Potential of cloud and aerosol retrievals using highly accurate hyperspectral satellite imagery
abstract: Abstract Reducing uncertainty in anthropogenic climate forcing requires improved observational constraints on aerosol and cloud properties. This study demonstrates how hyperspectral observations with exceptionally low radiometric uncertainty, exemplified by the proposed Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial and Helio Studies (TRUTHS)-like configuration, can strengthen these constraints relative to PACE Ocean Color Instrument (OCI)-like configuration. title: Market Access and Adoption of Climate Smart Agriculture: A Systematic Review
abstract: Market access is an important determinant influencing farmers’ adoption decisions by affecting prospective profitability, access to modern inputs, availability of information and extension services, and exposure to production and price risks. This systematic review is a synthesis of the evidence on the relationship between market access and CSA adoption in various agroecological settings. According to the PRISMA guidelines, five databases were used in the search: USDA Agricola, Semantic Scholar, DOAJ, EBSCOhost, and Google Scholar from which a total of 55 peer-reviewed studies were retrieved f

title: Late Quaternary glacial history of Zangser Kangri in the central Tibetan Plateau based on initial results from cosmogenic 10Be and optically stimulated luminescence dating
abstract: Few glacial chronological studies have been conducted in the extremely cold and arid interior of the Tibetan Plateau, limiting a plateau-wide understanding of Quaternary glacial spatiotemporal patterns. This study presents an initial late Quaternary glacial chronology for six moraine ridges on the southwestern slope of Zangser Kangri using cosmogenic 10 Be and single-grain K-feldspar optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating. title: Natural compounds in products of plant and animal origin
abstract: Natural compounds of animal and plant origin play a key role in maintaining human health and preventing diseases. Camel milk and sea buckthorn Hippophae rhamnoides are traditional food products and medicinal remedies with a unique composition and therapeutic properties. The aim of this work was a comprehensive study of the natural compounds in camel milk from Bactrian and Dromedary camels in the village of Nura (Ili District), as well as a comparative analysis of the biochemical composition of large-fruited and dessert varieties of sea buckthorn from the highland region of the village of Naryn

title: Aterian Lithic Technology and Functional Studies in North Africa: A Review of Current Evidence and Perspectives
abstract: Abstract In North Africa, the Middle Stone Age (MSA) has been associated with the emergence and evolution of Homo sapiens and is considered a pivotal period in the development of behavioral complexity. Recent archaeological discoveries have yielded a range of technological innovations, which are likely connected with ecological adaptations as well as new social and symbolic practices. title: Temporal heterogeneity in the animal fossil record driven by proliferation of microbial collagenases
abstract: The animal fossil record is a non-uniform archive of evolutionary history in which exceptional preservation diminishes toward the present, 1 , 2 , 3 with biomineralized skeletal elements constituting the majority of the fossil record. title: Presence and characterization of microplastics in pet blood (dogs and cats): evidence of environmental contamination
abstract: Increasing evidence identifies microplastics (MPs) as ubiquitous environmental contaminants, across marine, terrestrial, and atmospheric ecosystems. Their size and physicochemical properties facilitate widespread distribution and bioavailability, raising increasing concerns regarding their potential impact on animal and human health. Their presence in aquatic organisms (e.g., fish, mussels), marine mammals, and birds is demonstrated but evidence related to dogs and cats are relatively few. title: Effects of Krill-Based Product Supplementation on the Growth Performance and Immunity of Pacific White Shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei): A Literature Review
abstract: The increasing scarcity and price volatility of fish meal (FM), largely driven by overexploitation of marine fisheries, have intensified the search for sustainable and functional alternatives in shrimp aquaculture. This review synthesizes current evidence published between 2016 and 2026 to evaluate the nutritional and immunological effects of Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba)-based products on the growth performance and health of Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei). title: Chronological Analysis of Occupation on Providence Island, Liberia, by Luminescence Dating
abstract: In 1822, the American Colonization Society established a settlement on Providence Island, at the mouth of the Mesurado River in present-day Liberia. This settlement, which later became part of Monrovia, marked the beginning of Liberia as a colony for free Black Americans, some of whom were formerly enslaved. Oral histories and limited archival sources suggest that, prior to 1822, Indigenous peoples inhabited the area long before the arrival of these settlers. title: Moving Toward Risk: A County-Level Analysis of Climate Hazards on Post-Covid Domestic Migration in the United States
abstract: Although COVID-19 raised public awareness of climate-driven migration, existing research often overlooks socioeconomic and natural amenity factors that typically influence domestic migration. Controlling for these variables, we analyzed U.S. county-level migration between 2019-2024 against climate risks. We found that areas with greater risk of coastal flooding, drought, and tornadoes were negatively correlated with domestic migration, indicating possible displacement or avoidance. Counterintuitively, hurricane and heat risks exhibited positive correlations with in-migration. Our findings high

title: Residential proximity to oil and gas development and socioeconomic conditions: A comparative analysis of 33 countries
abstract: Abstract Fossil fuels continue to dominate the global energy supply. As emerging technologies drive up global energy consumption (e.g., cryptocurrency mining, data centers), identifying which populations are exposed to oil and gas extraction will become increasingly important. Yet, no prior study has done so internationally. We combine the Oil and Gas Infrastructure Mapping database with the Global Human Settlement Layer to estimate population exposure to oil and gas wells through residential proximity across 33 countries in 2024. title: Landed estates and cottage provision in rural England: The Manvers Estate, Nottinghamshire in the 19 th and early 20 th century
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates changing housing provision in rural Nottinghamshire during the 19 th and early 20th centuries using archival material and historical census data. The Manvers estate archives contain valuable information to reconstruct the role of landed estates, land agents and tenant farmers in shaping housing provision and conditions. The role of structural circumstances, such as the agricultural crisis, the poor law regime and the open-closed settlement model, discourses around cottage sanitary conditions and the development of governmental regulations are considered. Azheekkal, Kollam, Kerala, supports a diverse molluscan fauna, but historical records of its gastropod assemblage remain limited. Objectives: This study documents the gastropod assemblage recorded at Azheekkal during August–November 2017 and provides a historical reference dataset for future biodiversity assessments. abstract: Introduction Characterizing Critical Zone processes requires high-frequency, spatially distributed environmental data. Environmental wireless sensing networks (WSNs) can meet this need, but few researchers currently implement this infrastructure themselves, instead relying on legacy data loggers that require manual data retrieval or commercial telemetry systems that are too often hindered by financial and logistical constraints, e.g., sensor lock in, proprietary data models, recurring cellular fees, and lack of programmatic data access (e.g., APIs). title: CLIMATE-RELATED DISASTERS AND PROVINCIAL CONTINGENCY BUDGET ADAPTATION IN INDONESIA
abstract: This study examines whether Indonesian regional contingency budgets adapt to realised climate-related disaster experience, treating budget responsiveness as one dimension of fiscal resilience. A balanced province-year panel covering 32 provinces is estimated using fixed effects with standard errors clustered by province. The dependent variable is the budgeted share of contingency expenditure (Belanja Tidak Terduga/BTT) in total regional expenditure. journal: Proceeding of The International Seminar on Business Economics Social Science and Technology (ISBEST)

title: Culturally Responsive Digital Learning in Social Studies: An Integrative Review and the MOSAIC Model for Integrating Local Diversity into Classroom Innovation
abstract: Digital technology can widen access to information and multimodal expression, but it can also reproduce cultural exclusion when classroom innovation ignores learners' languages, identities, places, and community knowledge. This integrative review examined how culturally responsive digital learning can incorporate local diversity into social studies education. The review followed five stages: problem identification, literature search, data evaluation, thematic analysis, and synthesis. title: Low cost photogrammetry as a tool to enhance and preserve fossil collections: an example applied to Pleistocene molluscs from Gravina in Puglia (MurGEopark - Southern Italy)
abstract: High-resolution photogrammetry has become a pivotal tool in palaeontology for scientific documentation, morphometric analysis, and virtual heritage preservation. This study details the photogrammetric workflow implemented to digitise Pleistocene fossil molluscs sampled near Gravina in Puglia (Southern Italy). A significant portion of these specimens corresponds to the fossil fauna originally investigated by Arcangelo Scacchi (1810–1893), who in 1835 described 16 new species from this area, most of which remain valid taxa. abstract: Ichthyoelephas humeralis (bocachico) is a native fish species of high ecological and socioeconomic importance in Ecuador. This study integrates a systematic review and a spatial analysis to synthesize its distribution, biology, ecological requirements, economic importance, threats, and conservation strategies. Under the PRISMA 2020 protocol, 29 available studies on the species were analyzed, primarily addressing biological, ecological, and use aspects. title: In-situ tracer percolation experiments to quantify the influence of near-surface melting on Svalbard snow signatures
abstract: Abstract. The Arctic is at the forefront of global warming. More frequent and intense rain-on-snow events during winter are altering the annual snowpack with its environmental proxy records, so that Svalbard glaciers are not only rapidly losing mass but are endangered as climate archives. In this study, we aim to visualise and better constrain the influence of near-surface melt caused by small-scale rain-on-snow events on stable water isotope signatures in seasonal snow in the vicinity of Ny-Ålesund in Svalbard. title: Umbrella Desalinator
abstract: Saltwater and industrial contamination is gradually rendering groundwater in coastal India undrinkable, and the impact is most severely felt by the populations who lack access to centralised water treatment facilities. This paper details the design, construction, and initial performance assessment of the Umbrella Desalinator, a portable passive solar still intended to serve precisely these households. title: An open reproducible framework for CNN-based cetacean vocalization detection in passive acoustic monitoring
abstract: Background Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) combined with deep learning is increasingly used to detect cetacean vocalizations. The workflow from raw audio to a trained detector — annotation, segmentation, spectrogram parameterization, image processing, and model evaluation — is seldom accompanied by the complete set of configuration parameters, code, and data needed for independent reproduction, limiting methodological comparability and systematic benchmarking. title: The Emergence of Iron Shipbuilding on the River Tyne: A Study of Entrepreneurial Agency
abstract: Abstract From the 1840s, Tyneside emerged as a key center for iron shipbuilding, rivaling Britain’s established hubs. This industrial shift was driven initially not by legacy firms but by migrant entrepreneurs from Aberdeen—John Coutts, Charles Mitchell, and Andrew Leslie. This article investigates the divergent trajectories of these entrepreneurs, asking why two succeeded in establishing sustainable enterprises while the other failed. abstract: Functional profiling of meta-omics is essential for understanding microbial communities, yet support for custom genome-resolved reference databases is limited. We introduce Leviathan for integrated taxonomic and functional profiling at both genome and pangenome resolution. Leviathan combines Sylph for ultrafast alignment-free taxonomic profiling with Salmon for pseudo-alignment-based read quantification in DNA space against (pan)genome-resolved gene catalogs, producing dual metrics per (pan)genome: pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage. title: Palaeoclimatic Development and Stratigraphy of the Walsdorfer Maar (West Eifel Volcanic Field, Germany) During the Latter Half of the Saalian Glacial Period (MIS 7/6)
abstract: We investigated the lithology and tephra of the 87-metre-long drill core (WD1) from the Walsdorfer maar (Eifel, Germany) in order to reconstruct the sequence of volcanic activity and its integration into palaeoclimatic developments between Marine Isotope Stage (MIS) 7 and MIS 6. title: Más allá del snacking: microinteracciones informativas de comunicadores en formación
abstract: This study examines the factors associated with the frequency of news consumption and small acts of engagement (liking, sharing, commenting, reading in full, and archiving). Drawing on a survey (N=730) of communication students at Jesuit universities in Mexico, the findings show that proactive political practices in the digital sphere catalyze all five micro-interactions, followed by the consumption of both hard and soft news topics, particularly those related to crime and court news. abstract: This study presents a predictive framework for the ultimate compressive strength (UCS) of initially deflected plates subjected to longitudinal axial compression under simply supported (SS) and clamped (CL) boundary conditions. title: Mediaciones, medialidades y testimonios: entre cinedocumental, arte y memoria. Un análisis de Lemebel, Cicatrices en la tierra y Este arte que abraza
abstract: This article examines how documentary cinema establishes relationships between art and memory in three documentaries: Lemebel, Cicatrices en la tierra, and Este arte que abraza. The analysis identifies three distinct forms of mediation, mediality, and testimonial practice. Lemebel is an authorial and didactic documentary centered on the recovery of the artist’s archive and the reconstruction of his life and work. title: A new Caribbean species of the giant isopod genus Bathynomus (Crustacea, Isopoda, Cirolanidae) with notes on its evolutionary history
abstract: Abstract The new species Bathynomus tuebingoborikensis sp. nov., discovered in an historic museum collection, is described. We provide preliminary phylogenetic analyses of the genus, including extant and fossil species, using morphological characters. We reconstruct the evolutionary origin of the genus in the Caribbean, and suggest ten different migration waves all over the world oceans, including multiple recolonizations of the Americas. title: Review of Salmonid Alphavirus: Focus on Viral Survival, Shedding, Detection and Effects of Vaccination
abstract: This review of salmonid alphavirus provides a collection of the most recent knowledge on the factors relevant for the transmission and control of the virus including updates on SAV survival, viral shedding, detection, and effects of vaccination as reported in peer-reviewed literature, presentations, theses, and annual reports. SAV can survive in all water types, being the longest in colder marine waters without organic loading. The biophysical properties of SAV indicate a moderate to high robustness. abstract: Environmental degradation requires broader forms of social accountability that extend beyond formal regulations. abstract: Abstract This study presents the digital documentation of traditional Fijian architectural heritage through an in-depth investigation of the bure , Fiji’s indigenous house, focusing on three distinct bure types in Navala village. abstract: India's maritime diplomacy has undergone a decisive transformation over the past decade, evolving from a continental-focused posture toward a proactive, maritime-centric vision for the Indo-Pacific. This article examines that evolution and assesses the operational relevance of minilateral architectures in advancing India's strategic objectives. title: From Bandung to Brezhnev: Indonesia-Soviet Diplomacy
abstract: This article describes how, in the wider context of the Cold War, Indonesian-Soviet diplomatic relations developed from the Bandung Conference of 1955 through to the commencement of the L. This research employs comparative historiographical methodology with Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) to account for Soviet political and media discourse framing Indonesia as a postcolonial model of independence and a vanguard leader of the Non-Aligned Movement. title: On the distribution of Jordanita (Roccia) hector (Jordan, 1907) (Lepidoptera: Zygaenidae, Procridinae, Procridini)
abstract: The species Jordanita (Roccia) hector (Jordan, 1907) is known only from the Levant (a subregion of West Asia situated along the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea), an area characterized by high level of endemism. Recently, this species has been reported from Azerbaijan (Buntebarth et al. 2024). abstract: In the mid-1980s, scientific studies first highlighted the role of anthropogenic methane in global warming and emissions from cows as an important source. abstract: This study examines the changes in village names from the Rejang language to Indonesian in Kepahiang Regency, Bengkulu, focusing on referential meanings, community perceptions, and the impact on local cultural identity. abstract: Nuclear melt glass provides a valuable archive of information about the nature of the nuclear detonation. abstract: The risk of thyroid dysfunction (TD) persists in the Chinese population. However, large-scale epidemiological studies investigating TD prevalence and its geographic disparities are limited. abstract: Abstract Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a progressive ocular complication of diabetes and is commonly graded into five severity levels, ranging from no DR to proliferative DR. Automated severity grading is challenging because the classes are imbalanced and misclassification between severity levels may have different implications depending on the distance between the true and predicted grades. abstract: Abstract In this assessment, we reviewed existing literature to assess the ecological risks, benefits, and uncertainties associated with reintroducing Chinook salmon ( Oncorhynchus tshawytcha ) into the McCloud River, a tributary of the Sacramento River, California. abstract: Although the Ottoman Empire experienced a chronological delay in transitioning to permanent diplomacy, it established an embassy in Madrid, as it did in various other European cities, to improve its relations with European states and to closely monitor continental politics. title: Illusions of peace: eurocentrism, endemic violence and the burden of the Postcolony in the Central African Republic
abstract: This paper interrogates how Eurocentrism structures what counts as violence and, by extension, what counts as peace. abstract: Ògún, Ọba and Ọ̀ràmfẹ̀ festivals are the most elaborately celebrated festivals in Oǹdó Kingdom, for their spiritual and social significance. title: No critical slowing down in the Atlantic Overturning Circulation in historical CMIP6 simulations
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a key component of the Earth’s climate system, and has been suggested to have multiple stable states. abstract: Mussel reefs have been depleted globally by overfishing and habitat degradation, but the advent of reef restoration has produced promising results in terms of adult mussel survival and biodiversity enhancement. However, an absence of juvenile recruitment into restored mussel reefs is regularly cited as jeopardising their persistence and expansion. title: Petrophysical Dataset of Representative Volcanic Rocks from Dokdo, South Korea
abstract: Dokdo, a volcanic island in the East Sea, comprises alkaline volcanic and pyroclastic rocks formed during multiple stages of Cenozoic volcanism. This study presents a petrophysical dataset for 61 rock specimens collected from Dongdo and Seodo, Dokdo, to support the interpretation of geological and geophysical data. The specimens comprise trachyte, trachyandesite I, II, and III, lapilli tuff, and ash tuff. abstract: Was the desiccation of Lake Urmia a natural disaster or a manmade collapse? This paper reverts climatic factors from foregrounds to background but brings forth a range of hidden drivers and diagnostic techniques to unravel the decisive role of the trigger cause: infrastructural encroachments, planning omissions, and governance failures. abstract: Cross-modal vector retrieval is widely used in multimodal systems, such as search engines and vector databases. It typically operates in out-of-distribution (OOD) settings, where query vectors follow a distribution that differs from that of the vectors stored in the database. abstract: The icy dwarf planets in the outer solar system are among the most enigmatic bodies known, showing activity ranging from atmospheric resurfacing to possible cryovolcanism. Yet the study of their interiors remains largely theoretical, with few empirical measurements to guide our understanding. abstract: A growing number of countries are adopting policies to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, a process expected to reshape production systems and labour markets by altering relative prices and changing production and demand patterns across sectors. abstract: Small, trade-dependent economies often exhibit limited maritime connectivity, yet empirical evidence on the structural configuration of their container systems remains limited. This study analyzes route concentration and node distributions in Mauritania’s maritime container system during 2019–2022 using shipment-level data measured in forty-foot equivalent units (FFE). abstract: Landing a multirotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) on a moving platform is challenging because a UAV is underactuated and the desired landing state is generally a non-equilibrium state. title: The Persistence of a Phantom: A Geospatial and Multi-temporal Investigation of Mayda Island (1367–1914)
abstract: Since the dawn of cartography, mapmakers have experienced the need to give myths and legends a real space by locating them within maps. The Great Ocean, which comprised the known world until the end of the Middle Ages, and the remote lands at the edge of the world, were the best places to locate imaginary places. Mayda island is not the most famous, but it is the oldest with about 500 years of history. This paper aims to investigate the position of Mayda through a geospatial and multitemporal analysis. title: Incorporating multiple bands and land cover improves cross-sensor normalization
abstract: The Landsat archive and the Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) 2.0 virtual constellations enable monitoring of long-term and rapid environmental change with optical imagery, but differences in sensor design and atmospheric correction algorithms require cross-sensor normalization to ensure consistent observations. This study evaluates methods for such normalization using two global datasets: Landsat ETM+/OLI and HLS 2.0. title: Personalized drug discovery from rare diseases to cancer
abstract: Precision medicine selects individual treatments from a small toolbox of therapies already available. Personalized drug discovery (PDD) brings this concept one step ahead, developing drugs for individual patient's diseases. Currently, PDD is being developed for rare disorders, where conventional drug discovery paradigms are non-applicable due to small patient sizes, but also for cancer. As a new frontier in precision medicine, PDD should be upscaled in rare and non-rare diseases.

abstract: Construction remains a high-risk project-based industry, especially where formal safety systems, contractor controls, inspection capacity, and worker training are still developing. This article presents a Liberia-focused mixed-methods empirical analysis of safety management and organizational safety practices in construction projects. abstract: Domoic acid (DA) produced by toxigenic species of the diatom genus Pseudo-nitzschia during harmful algal blooms (HABs) bioaccumulates in filter feeders, bait fish, and commercial seafood products, posing a threat to marine organisms and public health. Copepodamides, a group of polar lipids exuded by copepods, are known to induce DA production in multiple species of Pseudo-nitzschia . abstract: Abstract From small molecules and systemic administration to biologics and targeted drug–carrier complexes, the drug delivery field’s “toolbox” of therapeutic materials has skyrocketed in scope and sophistication over the past decade alone. The tunable properties, modularity, and structural control afforded by such materials as lipids, synthetic polymers, peptides, and polysaccharides are highly favorable not only to the design of novel drugs but also drug carriers which help guide and deliver them. title: The Joint Expeditionary Force in the European Security System: Institutional Evolution and Prospects for Partnership with Ukraine
abstract: This article examines the opportunities and limitations of the Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) as a regional defense cooperation framework and assesses prospects for partnership with Ukraine. It uses a qualitative case study design and documentary analysis of official materials and research publications, covering 2014 to 1 September 2026. abstract: The miniaturization of patterns to sub-20 nm dimensions remains challenging, owing to the fundamental constraints of optical patterning and the increasing complexity and cost of advanced lithographic technologies such as extreme-ultraviolet lithography. Here, we introduce an electrochemical etching strategy that effectively decouples the final feature size from the optical diffraction limit by leveraging voltage-gated solubility switching in electro-responsive polymers. title: The furnace of crisis: assessing the European Union’s trajectory toward strategic independence and global actor in the shadow of the Russo-Ukrainian war
abstract: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has removed the assumptions on which the post-Cold War European security order rested and has increased pressure on the European Union to act as a provider of hard security rather than primarily as a regulatory and geo-economic power. This article examines whether that pressure is producing meaningful strategic autonomy and a more consequential global role. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines drug cartels as creative, innovation‐driven organizations rather than solely violent criminal enterprises. Building on creativity research applied to terrorist groups, we use a qualitative case study approach—drawing from news reports, official documents, open‐source materials, and academic work—to analyze 10 cases of cartel innovation across tactical, strategic, and organizational domains. title: The System Hallucination Scale (SHS): A Human-Centered Instrument for Assessing Perceived Reliability of Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models routinely produce factually incorrect or misleading outputs, yet conventional automated benchmarks overlook how users perceive reliability during interaction. We introduce the System Hallucination Scale (SHS), a lightweight instrument modeling the famous System Usability Scale (SUS) and System Causability Scales (SCS). title: Development and Validation of Girth‐, Volume‐, and Mass‐Based Body Condition Indices for Free‐Swimming Dugongs, via Drone Photogrammetry
abstract: ABSTRACT Drone photogrammetry provides a minimally invasive morphometric tool to assess growth and energy reserve in marine mammals. Converting drone‐derived measurements (e.g., body width) into body condition indices (BCIs, residuals from expected body girth, volume, or mass) requires prior knowledge of normative body shape. title: Distribution and Abundance of the Bioeroding Sponge Cliona sp. in Oyster Populations of Ostrea chilensis Across New Zealand
abstract: Bioeroding sponges are recognised pests in shellfish fisheries, as their boring activity can reduce market value, contribute to oyster mortality and cause economic losses. In New Zealand, bioeroding sponges in the shell‐burrowing alpha form are frequently observed in shells of the flat oyster Ostrea chilensis , a historically and culturally important species supporting several fisheries, including those in Foveaux Strait. A basic prerequisite for systematically minimizing and addressing losses and damages is reliable quantification in the aftermath of a disaster. abstract: In the twenty-first century, international politics unfolds within a battlespace where narratives, imagery, and algorithmic influence operate alongside conventional instruments of power. As reality itself becomes a strategic target, state and nonstate actors weaponize information to shape perception, legitimacy, and decision-making. abstract: Background: The growth of digital technologies has expanded opportunities for online freelance work among youth. Online freelance portals enable access to global employment and income opportunities, but adoption may be constrained by digital literacy, technology access, payment concerns, and job security. Purpose: The purpose of the study is to identify the factors influencing the intention to adapt and use online freelance portals among the youths of the Kathmandu Valley. title: AccES: A Framework for Predicting Building‐Level Loss of Accessibility to Essential Services Post‐Disasters Based on Publicly Available Information
abstract: Natural hazards significantly disrupt access to essential services, affecting individuals' capacity to withstand and recover from such events. However, existing hazard resilience models often fail to account for the interdependencies among essential services and lack the spatial resolution needed to assess accessibility loss at the building level. abstract: Background: Employee retention is increasingly challenging as Generation Z enters the corporate workforce with distinct expectations regarding career growth, compensation, supervisory support, organizational culture, and work–life balance. Understanding these factors is essential for organizations seeking to retain young employees and strengthen workforce stability. abstract: Background: International student mobility has become an increasingly important component of higher education, with students seeking educational opportunities abroad for academic, personal, cultural, and economic reasons. The decision to study abroad is shaped by a combination of factors originating from students’ home environment and perceived advantages of destination countries. abstract: Background Out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) finances 43.4% of total health expenditure in India, and emergency trauma—unforeseeable, unpostponable and costly—is among the sharpest tests of whether a health-financing mechanism protects households from catastrophic spending. abstract: Malaysia, recognized as one of the world’s mega-diverse hotspots, is currently facing a decline of many endangered and rare species due to natural and anthropogenic factors. Amid these species, Rafflesia kerrii, the largest iconic parasitic flower, is facing threats from ecological changes, habitat disturbance, and human activity. abstract: Herbivory can significantly limit seagrass restoration success, leading practitioners to explore the use of exclusion devices to reduce grazing pressure during transplant establishment. To evaluate the performance and practical application of these devices, we combined a quantitative meta-analysis of published studies across the wider Caribbean and tropical Atlantic with a survey of restoration practitioners implementing herbivore exclusion in Florida. abstract: Far-red light (FRL) cyanobacteria occupy spectrally filtered habitats where visible wavelengths are depleted but far-red radiation persists. title: Resilient Civil Infrastructure Design against Earthquake and Flood Risks Under Climate Change
abstract: The civil infrastructure is becoming more and more prone to earthquake and flood hazards whereas climate change is adding another level of uncertainty for infrastructure designs, structural performance, and sustainability. This research work attempts to explore resilient civil infrastructure designs under earthquake and flood hazards and changing climatic conditions, which include topics related to structural vulnerability, multi-hazard assessment, climate adaptation, and sustainable engineering practices. abstract: Abstract Fe‐Mg carbonates on Mars preserve key evidence of past aqueous chemistry and climate, yet their formation conditions remain poorly constrained. The engine room is one of the most critical areas on board, functioning as the operational center for the main propulsion system and auxiliary machinery. Due to its nature, the engine room presents various hazards, including fire, explosion, fuel leakage, heat exposure, excessive noise, and other occupational accidents. title: Trophic reorganization may contribute to shifts in nitrogen transformations following alleviation of saline alkaline stress
abstract: Soil salinization is a widespread form of land degradation, yet how saline-alkaline stress is linked to belowground micro-food webs and shapes nitrogen transformations remains poorly understood. Here we compare natural saline–sodic and reclaimed farmland soils in northeastern China using microscopy and genetic sequencing. Farmland has higher nematode and prokaryote abundances and greater nematode, protist and prokaryote richness, whereas fungal richness is higher in solonetz soils. Nitrogen mineralization rates and nitrification potential are 118.2% and 72.3% higher in farmland, respectively.

abstract: One emerging technology is the use of conveyor-based trash collection boats. This study aims to design and analyze the electrical system of a paddle conveyor—based on a DC motor and a linear actuator—on a trash collection boat as a means of improving the effectiveness of trash collection from the water’s surface. abstract: ABSTRACT Global change is reshaping biological communities, leading to shifts in community composition, species distributions and species realized niches. These processes are especially relevant in freshwater ecosystems, where vertebrate declines are particularly severe and dispersal is naturally constrained by drainage basins. title: Intermittent cyanobacterial accumulation reshapes water column sulfur cycling and favors sulfur-oxidizing denitrifiers in freshwater lake mesocosms
abstract: Recent studies have established that cyanobacterial bloom biomass (CBB) decomposition critically drives sulfur cycling in the water column of shallow lakes. While CBB can accumulate via single pulses or intermittent inputs depending on hydroclimatic conditions, how these distinct patterns affect sulfur cycling remains poorly understood. abstract: Excitation–emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectroscopy is widely used to investigate the properties, composition, and sources of chromophores in atmospheric water-soluble organic matter (WSOM). However, the fluorescence characteristics of WSOM under different environmental conditions and their implications for atmospheric processing remain unclear. abstract: Introduction Phenotypic plasticity enables organisms to adjust their traits in response to environmental conditions, yet studies of animal coloration, particularly in cephalopods, have largely focused on rapid neural control while overlooking slower changes in the cellular substrate underlying color change. Here, we investigated whether morphological color change contributes to phenotypic plasticity in the bigfin reef squid ( Sepioteuthis lessoniana ). abstract: Pisciculture has been established as a strategic activity in the Amazon, with emphasis on the cultivation of tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum) and its hybrids. abstract: Abstract Introduction Arctic Grayling Thymallus arcticus were extirpated from Michigan in 1936. abstract: Timely and accurate projections of when global warming will exceed the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 °C threshold are essential for effective climate policy. abstract: Spatial clusters of animal nests can be driven by mating behaviors, social benefits, and landscape heterogeneity. abstract: ABSTRACT In aquaculture, omega‐3 fatty acids (FAs) are essential for fish health and growth during early development, making them important indicators of egg quality. Using Illumina MiSeq and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS), we investigated how tree species (pine vs. liquidambar) and forest composition (pure vs. mixed) shape rhizosphere microbial communities and root metabolites in subtropical forests. abstract: Ferredoxins are central to cellular metabolism by mediating electron flow in energy conversion reactions. abstract: Abstract Strong sky background radiation and motion-induced signal smearing are the key factors limiting the effective detection of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites during daytime. To improve the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and detection capability of optical systems, this paper proposes an optimization method for the observation direction of LEO satellite optical detection systems under strong background radiation. abstract: ABSTRACT The Pinerolo‐Sanfront Unit (PSU), the structurally lowest tectonic unit of the Dora‐Maira Massif (Western Alps), has been regarded as a monocyclic unit composed of Permo‐Carboniferous sediments and Permian granitoids that were metamorphosed during the Alpine orogeny. abstract: This research evaluated the occupational safety, health (OSH) conditions, operational performance, and workplace hurdles experienced by field engineers across the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Bohol First, Second, and Third District Engineering Offices (DEO). abstract: This study presents a synthetic proof-of-concept surrogate-assisted simulation–optimisation framework for identifying potentially mineralised locations using groundwater copper-isotope observations. Understanding the response of yeast is crucial if measures are to be developed that allow adaptation under multifactorial stress conditions. title: From Mexico to Argentina: Predicting the distribution of the invasive weed Tithonia tubaeformis beyond its native range using niche modelling
abstract: 1. Biological invasions are a major driver of global change, affecting biodiversity, ecosystem functioning and agricultural productivity. Tithonia tubaeformis (Asteraceae) is a weed native to Mexico that has become invasive in several regions worldwide, including Argentina, where it threatens crop systems. abstract: Abstract Underground gas storage (UGS) operations can perturb reservoir conditions and modulate local seismicity, but the temporal evolution of this response under cyclic injection–withdrawal remains poorly constrained. abstract: We report additional records of the recently described, supposedly rare species of wolf snake, Lycodon irwini Naveen et al., 2025, known only from Great Nicobar Island, India. abstract: Wetland plants must supply oxygen to their rhizomes and roots to maintain aerobic respiration despite soil anoxia. Excess oxygen can diffuse into the environment, strongly affecting rhizosphere biogeochemistry. This radial oxygen loss (ROL) has often been observed to increase in the daytime, perhaps supported by photosynthetic oxygen production and stomatal opening. abstract: Defects are increasingly recognized as powerful modulators of the chemistry and photophysics of fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs), enabling tunable optical responses toward exogenously introduced analytes. abstract: Abstract During mate choice, both males and females can exhibit choosiness when selecting a partner. The expression and measurement of preferences is typically constrained by the traits presented during mate-choice trials, which generally represent a subset of the phenotypic trait space and thus may not capture the full range of potential preferences. abstract: An experiment was conducted to assess effects of aeration on water quality and yield of carps at farmer‘s pond of Kathar, Chitwan, Nepal for 225 days from 25 May 2018 to 10 January 2019. abstract: Abstract Indoor molds damage building materials and can compromise occupant health. Correction of the moisture source and physical removal of contaminated material remain central to remediation, but inactivation of residual viable growth may be useful as an adjunct where heat or liquid biocides are unsuitable. abstract: Abstract Introduction Ecological restoration projects often rely on nurseries (NU) to provide plants to restore ecological communities. abstract: The El Gigante Metamorphic Complex, in the homonymous range (Sierras Pampeanas, Argentina), consists of three lithostratigraphic units that, from bottom to top, are: Quebrada Grande (Mesoproterozoic protoliths), Loma Cortada (Ediacaran-early Cambrian sedimentary protoliths), and Los Morteritos (middle to late Cambrian protoliths), all reworked by the Famatinian orogeny. abstract: Abstract The extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix serves as a structural scaffold for biofilm organization, contributing to structural integrity and antimicrobial tolerance by modulating the penetration and distribution of antimicrobial agents. However, whether this EPS matrix can also potentiate antimicrobial localization and activity remains poorly understood. abstract: Ecosystem services (ES) are fundamental to achieving human well-being. The research addresses the growing need for efficient flood risk mapping in urban settings by providing a simplified, yet effective, method for identifying high-risk zones. abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into software development workflows, their trustworthiness has become a critical concern. abstract: This paper introduces a simulation-based methodological and conceptual study addressing a critical gap in tourism research: the fragmented treatment of spatial, sequential and temporal dimensions of visual attention. title: Carbohydrate‐binding modules: powerful tools in the research and development of carbohydrates – a review
abstract: Carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) are independent domains generally appended in carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) with carbohydrate-binding functions. abstract: This study was conducted to assess phenotypic variation in traditional cashew populations from Nachingwea and Newala districts in Tanzania. title: From ward to wastewater: optimising near-source surveillance for microbial targets in hospitals
abstract: ABSTRACT Hospitals generate wastewater enriched with human-derived microbes, making them strong sites for focused, near-source surveillance of pathogens. We compared in-sewer 24-h composite and passive sampling at two hospital discharge locations and influent sampling at a municipal wastewater treatment plant (WWTP). We also evaluated three extraction workflows to determine how sampling and extraction methods influence detection sensitivity across faecal indicators (HF183, crAssphage) and clinically relevant pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, human adenovirus, Campylobacter jejuni). title: Assessing biogenic carbon dioxide resource for synthetic e-fuel production to decarbonise shipping
abstract: A high-level assessment of the production potential and costs of three synthetic e-fuels, methane, methanol and Fischer–Tropsch diesel, derived from renewable hydrogen and biogenic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) was conducted for maritime transport in the EU and Ireland for 2050. Biogenic CO 2 sources included by-products from biomethane production and ethanol fermentation (priced at €30/tonne), and emissions from biomass combustion (€80/tonne). title: Repurposing the Insecticide Flufenerim, the Only Anti- Cryptococcus Compound Identified in the MMV Global Health Priority Box, as a Candidate for the Environmental Control of the Cryptococcosis Agents
abstract: Abstract Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are environmental fungi that cause cryptococcosis, a severe, life-threatening infection, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. Current treatments are limited by toxicity, restricted availability, and the emergence of resistance, highlighting the need for novel antifungal agents. Here, 240 compounds from the Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV) Global Health Priority Box were screened for activity against these two species. Flufenerim, originally developed as an insecticide, was the only compound that exhibited inhibitory activity

title: Automated fledgling call detection links adult songbird abundance to reproductive success in restored habitat
abstract: Many wildlife monitoring programs assume that adult abundance reflects habitat quality and, by extension, reproductive success, despite the possibility of these parameters decoupling. Abundance may be more likely to decouple with reproduction in human-modified landscapes such as those created through habitat restoration. However, the extent to which this occurs remains unclear due to extensive manual effort required for monitoring reproduction, especially at scale. Passive-acoustic monitoring (PAM) has recently shown promise for detecting fledgling begging calls to infer reproductive success.

title: Recent Progress in Skin Bioelectronics for Electrophysiological Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT The acquisition of high‐quality electrophysiological signals can provide comprehensive information in disease diagnosis, athletic training, human‐computer interaction, and human healthcare, which plays an important role in improving the quality of life, boosting the development of wearable bioelectronics. This review addresses recent progress in skin bioelectronics for electrophysiological signal monitoring and its applications. title: Morphological, genetic, and phenolic characterization of Baccharis glutinosa and Baccharis salicifolia and their application in the biogenic synthesis of silver nanoparticles
abstract: The genus Baccharis exhibits high taxonomic diversity and marked morphological plasticity, which complicates the species-level delimitation of closely related taxa. In this study, an integrated characterization of Baccharis glutinosa and Baccharis salicifolia collected in the La Libertad region, Peru, was conducted by combining morphological, molecular, and phytochemical evidence, together with their biotechnological application in the biogenic synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs). title: CRISPR-enhanced microalgae for carbon sequestration and carotenoid production: opportunities and fundamental constraints
abstract: Microalgae represent a promising biological platform for CO2 sequestration and the sustainable production of high-value metabolites, particularly carotenoids such as lutein and astaxanthin. However, industrial performance remains constrained by low carbon conversion efficiency, reduced photosynthetic performance, and competing metabolic fluxes that limit product yield. The emergence of CRISPR/Cas-based genome engineering has enabled precise and multiplexed modulation of microalgal metabolic networks, offering new opportunities to overcome these limitations. title: Shedding darkness.
abstract: This article reflects on the critical inquiry that shapes the Darkness Reframed issue and, from a decolonial perspective, problematizes the possible assumptions attached to the category of darkness. Unpacking coloniality not only as a historical legacy but as a living force that continues to shape ways of thinking, the reflection points to the plurality of futures to be reframed in order to embrace a multilayered understanding of darkness(es). title: Development and Physico-Mechanical Characterization of Epoxy Matrix Biocomposite Reinforced with Multi-Short Cynara Scolymus Fibers
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the development and physico-mechanical evaluation of an epoxy matrix biocomposite reinforced with multi-short Cynara Scolymus fibers of lengths 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 cm, in a bid to bridge the gap in studies conducted in the millimeter scale and to statistically validate the results obtained. Fabrication of biocomposites was performed by the hand-lay-up gravity casting method, and the biocomposites were characterized by tensile tests (ASTM D638), three-point bending tests (ASTM D790), Charpy impact tests (ASTM D6110) and optical microscopy, SEM, EDX, and sta

title: Spatial and genetic dynamics of Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein2 in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: BACKGROUND: Malaria rapid diagnosis tests (mRDTs) detecting Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (Pfhrp2) are the most widely adopted diagnostic tool in malaria-endemic areas. However, extensive polymorphisms in Pfhrp2 could modify Pfhrp2 epitopes, rendering it undetectable by Pfhrp2-based mRDTs. This study investigates the spatial distribution and population dynamics of Pfhrp2 in sub-Saharan Africa (sSA). title: Habitat-use flexibility may promote the spread of Asian weatherloaches in Europe
abstract: Asian weatherloaches have expanded their range across Europe, potentially increasing competitive pressure on the conservation-dependent native European weatherfish Misgurnus fossilis . Because interspecific interactions are potentially mediated by benthic habitat use, we quantified substrate choice of native European and invasive Asian weatherloaches in a replicated laboratory two-way choice experiment. title: BaTiO3/ZnO nanocomposite photocatalysts for enhanced degradation of mixed antibiotics and dyes
abstract: Abstract Composite photocatalysts were developed from hydrothermally synthesized barium titanate (BaTiO 3 , BTO) and zinc oxide (ZnO), combined by ultrasonic mixing in ethanol followed by calcination, and applied to remove a quaternary mixture of persistent pollutants in wastewater (ciprofloxacin (CIP), tetracycline (TC), methylene blue (MB), and methyl orange (MO)) in a heterogeneous photocatalysis process. title: Sex-specific intestinal transcriptional responses to oral polyvinyl chloride microplastic exposure in Wistar rats, with an in-vitro validation in a human gut model
abstract: The widespread presence of microplastics in the environment has raised concerns about potential health effects following oral exposure in humans, particularly in individuals with impaired intestinal barrier function. This study investigated the effects of dietary polyvinyl chloride (PVC) microplastics fragments (<25 μm) in healthy and dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis Wistar rats, with a complementary assessment in a human 3D intestinal microtissue model. title: Body size, season, and host taxon predict patterns of monogenean gill parasite infection in two assemblages of darters (Percidae: Etheostomatini) in Tennessee
abstract: Parasites are an important component of freshwater ecosystems due to the ways they regulate energy flow and shape community structure. The goal of this study was to analyze infection patterns of monogenean gill parasites (genus Aethycteron) that have specialized on darters (genus Etheostoma), freshwater fishes native to North America. We sampled hosts from two stream sites in Tennessee and evaluated whether prevalence and intensity of infection varied in the hosts by site, season, body size, sex, or host taxon. Month, standard length, and host clade were strong predictors of infection patterns

title: Quantum‐Engineered Magnesium Phthalocyanine for Multifunctional Optoelectronics: Charge Transfer Dynamics, Topological Features, and Device‐Level Integration
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium phthalocyanine (MgPc) is investigated as an organic semiconductor through a combined theoretical and experimental approach. Density functional theory (DFT) and time‐dependent DFT calculations reveal a moderate HOMO‐LUMO gap (2.16 eV), pronounced π→π* and intramolecular charge‐transfer transitions, and a low exciton binding energy (0.345 eV), indicating favorable charge separation. title: N-LAS-IAM: Climate change in a balance-of-payments framework
abstract: Climate change is becoming a macro-financial development problem for peripheral economies, yet integrated assessment models remain poorly equipped to analyse climate vulnerability in externally constrained developing countries. Existing heterodox models are mostly closed or global, while balance-of-payments-constrained growth models treat climate in reduced form and incompletely formalise the financial channel. title: Genetic diversity and conservation of a rare Miconia species (Melastomataceae) from the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
abstract: Biodiversity is undergoing an unprecedented global decline, and genetic diversity plays a fundamental role in ensuring species persistence. Miconia ulei, an endemic species from the eastern Atlantic Forest in Santa Catarina, southern Brazil, is rare and has few known populations. We investigated genetic diversity and population structure using microsatellite markers and assessed its conservation status following IUCN guidelines and by incorporating genetic parameters in the evaluation. title: The cool façade paradox: Balancing urban climate regulation and outdoor thermal stress – A systematized review
abstract: Cool façades — building walls with high solar reflectance and high thermal emittance — are promoted as a passive urban cooling strategy. However, their effects on outdoor thermal strain remain insufficiently understood. This systematized review synthesizes evidence from 77 studies to quantify the effects of increased façade solar reflectance on air temperature and outdoor thermal stress in urban environments. abstract: Через одну добу після введення отрути Leiurus macroctenus у легенях щурів спостерігаються виражені гістологічні зміни мікроциркуляторного русла, що характеризувалися порушенням кровонаповнення та ремоделюванням судинних стінок. title: Dietary 5-hydroxytryptophan supplementation improves growth and metabolism of large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) in association with microbiota-gut-brain axis-related changes
abstract: The microbiota–gut–brain (MGB) axis and it’s the role in physiology and behaviors of the host with serotonin as a key signaling molecule have received much attention in recent years. 5-Hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP), an effective serotonin precursor, has regulatory effects on the MGB axis, but little is known about these effects in fish. title: When psychedelic discourse meets local narrative: Selective uptake of psychedelic meanings surrounding mad honey in Nepal
abstract: AIMS: 'Mad honey' is produced when bees collect nectar from Rhododendron species containing grayanotoxins, naturally occurring diterpenoid toxins that can produce dose-dependent intoxication. It has long been embedded in Nepalese medicinal and ritual practices but has recently become part of global psychedelic discourse. This study examined how globally circulating discourse and local narrative practices interact in shaping meanings of intoxication, using mad honey as a case. title: Two new sulfur-containing pyridine alkaloids from the co-culture of Diaporthe fungi
abstract: The untapped metabolome of filamentous fungi represents a profound reservoir for therapeutic lead discovery. Although genomic mining confirms an abundance of cryptic biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), axenic laboratory culture frequently lacks the ecological stimuli required to trigger their expression, inevitably leading to the redundant isolation of known metabolites. title: Global grassland productivity and carbon storage benefit from functional diversity under climate change
abstract: Functional diversity plays an important role for ecosystem services of managed grasslands such as their gross primary productivity (GPP) and soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. Yet vegetation models assessing functional diversity have been limited to small spatial scales. We used the Lund-Potsdam-Jena managed land (LPJmL) competitor stress-tolerant ruderal (CSR) model to assess the role of functional diversity for managed grassland GPP and SOC under climate change at the global scale. title: The Evolution and Assessment of Intelligence Architectures in Nigerian Security: A Historical Analysis
abstract: This paper has discussed the development and evaluation of intelligence structures in Nigeria, and how these structures are effective in dealing with the modern internal security issues. The study follows the historical evolution of intelligence systems in Nigeria, which started with indigenous security establishments in the pre-colonial period and colonial surveillance systems, through the centralization of the systems in the post-independent era, expansions of the systems in the military era, and the reform in the democratic era. title: Bio-ecology of the harmful leafhopper Zyginidia sohrab Zachvatkin, 1947 (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) in maize fields of the Central Anatolia Region
abstract: Leafhoppers damage plants by piercing and sucking leaf tissues. Among the leafhopper species occurring in Central Anatolia, Zyginidia sohrab (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) is the most widespread and abundant species. This study was conducted under natural field conditions during the 2021 and 2022 growing seasons to investigate the bioecology of Z. sohrab in maize production areas. Z. sohrab overwinters as an adult and begins to emerge from overwintering sites in the last week of April as temperatures increase. abstract: Introduction Many methods for evaluating enthesis rugosity are qualitative or fail to capture the entire entheseal surface. title: Disrupting antimicrobial resistance in food systems from a One Health perspective: a complex systems analysis in Canada, Senegal and the Netherlands
abstract: BACKGROUND: Food systems are a key contributor to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Given the multi-sectoral nature of AMR, a One Health perspective has been advocated. Recent research situates AMR as an emerging property of a complex system, a perspective which can help identify root drivers of AMR and theorise the impacts of proposed solutions. This study aims to combine systems modelling and a One Health perspective to identify system-level dynamics and priority actions for addressing AMR in food systems. title: Antimicrobial resistance in the monotreme microbiome
abstract: Context Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global health crisis requiring a One Health approach that recognises the interconnectedness of people, animals and the environment. Since wide adoption of the One Health framework, wildlife species have been identified as important potential reservoirs and vectors of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria. title: Native-range origin predicts genomic contribution in an experimental Mimulus guttatus invasion
abstract: Biological invasions and range expansions act as natural experiments for understanding evolutionary processes at and beyond a species' range margin. However, unlike manipulative experiments, invasions and range expansions are less genetically tractable and often involve genotypes of uncertain origin that are subject to complex evolutionary pressures. Here, we replay the earliest stages of the colonisation of the widespread North American plant species Mimulus guttatus (synonym Erythranthe guttata) in the United Kingdom. title: In the beginning was the name: naming and framing sustainable cultural tourism destinations in peripheral areas
abstract: Early-stage tourism development in peripheral areas often takes place under ‘below-zero’ conditions, where tourism is weakly established, place identities fragmented, and conventional branding strategies premature. In such contexts, the name of a place and its associated communicative framings become a first vital connector between potential visitors, local stakeholders, and the area itself. This article examines how naming and framing processes operate under these conditions and how they can be diagnosed and engaged to support sustainable cultural tourism development. abstract: Abstract Modal blending maps high-dimensional sensor and actuator arrays onto low-dimensional virtual inputs and outputs for targeted modal control. title: Development of a browser–based computational tool for preliminary estimation of vertical-axis wind turbine power output
abstract: Rapid estimation of vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) power output is essential for preliminary assessment. However, existing approaches using spreadsheets, software, or simulations are resource-intensive and require a tedious process. This study presents a lightweight browser-based computational framework developed using JavaScript for rapid preliminary estimation of VAWT power output. The framework provides an interactive web interface that automatically estimates swept area, available wind power, mechanical power, and electrical power from user-defined parameters. title: Political Advantage, Political Risk: The Nascent Stage of Statoil’s International Expansion, 1978–1999
abstract: This article analyses how the dynamics between the Norwegian national oil company Statoil and its government owner gradually changed during the 1980s and 1990s, as Statoil invested in politically risky business environments outside its domicile. Yet, despite this seemingly profit-maximizing behaviour, the NOC was closely intertwined with its government owner and this owner’s pursuit of a value-based foreign policy with emphasis on support for poverty reduction, democracy, human rights and peace building. title: Adsorption–crosslinking immobilization of SHSL on NKA macroporous resin: Operational stability and molecular dynamics at the enzyme–resin interface
abstract: Lipase immobilization can improve operational stability, while enzyme–support interactions may alter conformational behavior near the catalytic region. How local support association relates to catalytic-region dynamics remains unclear. Here, SHSL was immobilized on NKA macroporous resin by hydrophobic adsorption followed by glutaraldehyde post-treatment. title: A revised early Jurassic to Albian chronology for dinosaur evolution in tropical Asia
abstract: The Mesozoic deposits of the Khorat Plateau in Thailand have yielded a rich but chronologically unclear record of dinosaur evolution. Here, we use detrital zircon U-Pb dating to establish precise ages for these deposits. The Nam Phong Formation, once thought to include some of the oldest sauropodomorphs, is now dated to the Pliensbachian stage of the Early Jurassic (ca. 190 Ma), at least 20 million years younger than previously assumed. title: Shadow Pricing Ecosystem Services in Boreal Forests
abstract: Abstract Boreal forests jointly produce marketed goods and non-market ecosystem services, generating unavoidable trade-offs. We estimate shadow prices with the directional distance function (R. G. Chambers et al. 1996), endogenizing the directional vector and correcting for sampling variation via bootstrap methods. Using a county-by-year panel of Swedish forests, we find that shadow prices vary spatially and temporally yet remain generally low, implying modest opportunity costs for improving biodiversity and carbon sequestration relative to timber. abstract: Introduction Soil salinization and alkalization increasingly threaten global ecosystem stability, necessitating a clearer understanding of how dominant halophytes respond to complex salt stresses. Methods This study examined the differential effects of neutral and alkaline salt stresses on seed germination and early seedling growth of Suaeda salsa , a dominant halophyte in the Yellow River Delta. title: Design Parameter Justification of Loosening Tine for Layer-by-Layer Treatment of Saline Soils
abstract: In the arid regions of Kazakhstan, agricultural crops are grown on low-productivity saline-alkali soils with varying properties across different horizons. Soil tillage is performed using non-plow implements that generate high traction resistance and turn over large clods of soil with a low degree of fragmentation. The aim of this study is to provide technical support for primary tillage to maximize soil moisture accumulation and humus conservation. title: Disturbance‐Associated Plant Communities in Africa's Largest Alpine Ecosystem: Evidence for Long‐Term Anthropogenic Influence
abstract: ABSTRACT Questions Africa's largest alpine ecosystem is perceived as relatively pristine; nonetheless, it contains numerous pastoral settlements and some of the world's oldest evidence of human presence in an alpine ecosystem. This study aims to address (i) demarcation of settlement vegetation and boundary delineation, (ii) investigation of settlement indicator plants, (iii) species composition of settlement vegetation, and (iv) since when the time of human footprint amplified by pastoralism. title: The Effect of i-PUBERS Implementation on Subsidized Fertilizer Distribution Effectiveness
abstract: The implementation of digital systems in public administration has become increasingly important in improving the effectiveness, transparency, and accountability of public service delivery. In the agricultural sector, digitalization is expected to support more accurate and efficient distribution of subsidized fertilizers to eligible farmers. abstract: A systematic combinatorial study of anodic oxidation on Ti-Yb alloys was conducted along a compositional range of 7–27 at.% Yb. For this purpose, a thin-film library was produced by co-sputtering in a self-developed vacuum system. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy were employed to investigate the compositional spread and surface structure of the thin film alloys. title: Hatching failure and embryo mortality in endangered populations of Eurasian Curlew ( Numenius arquata )
abstract: Hatching failure represents a significant and growing barrier to reproductive success in threatened birds and yet is often poorly understood. Populations of the Eurasian Curlew Numenius arquata in the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland have experienced significant declines over recent decades, and low breeding productivity is a major barrier to conservation efforts. However, data on hatching failure, infertility and embryo mortality rates are currently lacking. title: Synchrony of floral volatile emission with diurnal pollinators of possible decomposition mimic Asarum savatieri (Aristolochiaceae)
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Floral scent is crucial for mediating plant-pollinator interactions, a primary driver of angiosperm diversity. The dynamic nature of olfactory cues means they can be fine-tuned to suit pollinator activity, making them an effective method of adaptation to local pollinator niches. Asarum sect. Heterotropa is one of the most species-rich lineages in Japan with remarkable variation in floral scents. title: Repurposed lives: shipping containers as contested sites of urban citizenship in Accra
abstract: This study investigates how shipping containers are repurposed as architecture in Accra, Ghana. The study reveals the spatial factors shaping the emergence of these adaptive structures. Rather than being randomly situated, containers cluster in strategic locations enabling access to livelihoods while also avoiding eviction threats. Their positioning highlights contradictions between top-down urban planning favouring elite interests and the needs of marginalised residents. title: The plasma protease inhibitor ITIH4 forms oligomeric complexes and senses broader proteolytic activity

abstract: A microwave‐assisted tandem synthesis of pyrazolo[3,4‐ h ][1,6]naphthyridines bearing substituents with diverse stereoelectronic character (i.e., alkyl, aryl, CN, and MeO) is reported. Products were obtained in good yields by reacting 5‐aroyl‐pyrazolo[3,4‐ b ]pyridines with malononitrile in methanol, where the expected Knoevenagel reaction does not proceed. Instead, a solvent molecule drives a tandem reaction that affords three tricyclic N ‐heteroaromatic compounds. title: Steady-state parameter-space analysis for interpretable fault diagnosis of centrifugal pumps
abstract: This paper investigates a steady-state parameter-space approach for interpretable fault diagnosis of centrifugal pumps under controlled benchmark conditions. The analysis assesses whether physically interpretable coefficients derived from pump head and shaft-torque relations can provide an informative diagnostic representation within the tested steady-state scope. A semi-empirical model is formulated for the pump head and shaft torque, and six trial-wise coefficients are estimated by least squares from repeated steady-state measurements.
