title: Genomic epidemiology of Neisseria gonorrhoeae in ghana reveals a diverse recombinant pathogen population driven by plasmid acquired and mutational resistance
abstract: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a major sexually transmitted pathogen and an escalating public health threat due to its rapid acquisition of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Despite a high estimated burden of gonorrhea in Africa, genomic surveillance data from West Africa remain scarce. Establishing localized, evidence-based genomic baselines is vital to appropriately inform national treatment guidelines, improve antimicrobial stewardship, and support public health intervention programs. title: Integrating cortical microtubules into plant gravity signaling: dynamics, tubulin phosphorylation, and growth regulation
abstract: Plant gravity responses depend on coordinated signaling and growth-control mechanisms that convert directional and mechanical stimuli into differential cell expansion. Cortical microtubules are central to the conversion: they pattern cellulose synthase trajectories, set cell-wall anisotropy, and are remodeled in altered-gravity and tubulin-mutant systems. Yet the cytoskeletal regulatory pathway remains only loosely connected to the canonical, auxin-centered picture of how plants perceive and respond to gravity. title: Dung Beetle Functional Response and Dung Removal Rates Along an Altitudinal Gradient in Neotropical Rainforests
abstract: ABSTRACT Dung beetles are a vital component of ecosystems, providing essential ecosystem services. However, the factors that regulate the functional response of dung beetles and dung removal across altitudinal gradients have been scantily explored. Along an altitudinal gradient in rainforests of the Talamanca Cordillera of Costa Rica, we assessed the structure, composition, functional diversity, and dung removal rates of the dung beetle assemblage. title: In the nodule or on the nodule? The hidden Frankia biodiversity in Casuarina nodules across continents
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Actinorhizal root nodule symbioses are formed between a diverse group of mostly woody dicotyledonous plants and nitrogen-fixing soil Actinomycetota of the genus Frankia . Some of the most ecologically relevant actinorhizal plants are Casuarina species, used widely in shelter belts and phytoremediation due to their high tolerance to abiotic stresses and ability to thrive on marginal soils. abstract: Apresentamos novos dados obtidos em um levantamento geológico de detalhe realizado em Tejuçuoca-CE. title: Evaluation of LiDAR‐based canopy trait estimation in Midwestern row crops
abstract: Abstract Stand count, the number of plants per unit ground area, and leaf area index (LAI), the ratio of leaf area to ground area, are critical traits for crop research but are traditionally measured using labor‐intensive methods. While new sensing technologies are being developed, quantifying improvement in measurement efficiency and data quality, relative to traditional techniques, is lacking. abstract: ABSTRACT Graphical abstract showing the assessment of EcoSan sustainability in Kabale District, Uganda, using a multi-criteria analysis approach based on health, technical, environmental, socio-cultural, economic and financial, and legal and institutional criteria. This study evaluated the sustainability of ecological sanitation (EcoSan) systems in Kabale Municipality, Uganda, using a multi-criteria analysis framework based on the analytical hierarchy process (AHP). title: Anti‐Inflammatory Activity of Cotula cinerea Essential Oil: Integrated Chemical, In Vivo, Histological, and Computational Evaluation
abstract: ABSTRACT The anti‐inflammatory activity of Cotula cinerea essential oil (EO) was evaluated using integrated chemical, in vivo, histological, and computational approaches. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) identified trans‐thujone (51.86%), santolina triene (10.60%), and sabinene (6.17%) as the most abundant constituents. title: Novel highly potent and environmentally benign molluscicides for Pomacea canaliculata control: Discovery, mechanism, and field validation
abstract: The Pomacea canaliculata is a globally invasive freshwater pest that poses significant threats to both agriculture and aquatic ecosystems; however, conventional molluscicides, such as niclosamide, exhibit high toxicity toward non-target organisms, leading to substantial ecological risks. To develop highly potent and environmentally benign molluscicides, we designed and synthesized a series of 15 novel compounds, among which D-1 emerged as the most promising candidate. title: Low-density ablator response to induction plasmatron aerothermal environments
abstract: Abstract The aerothermal response of low-density charring ablators for atmospheric entry is investigated in dissociated air and nitrogen plasmas. NASA’s Phenolic Impregnated Carbon Ablator, and its carbon preform, FiberForm, were subjected to aerothermal environments relevant to Earth and Titan atmospheric entry in the Plasmatron X inductively coupled plasma wind tunnel. title: Real-time process analysis and optimization of nitroguanidine synthesis in microflow using inline Raman spectroscopy
abstract: Non-contact inline Raman spectroscopy is used as a fast, flexible, and safe method for monitoring and optimizing continuous-flow processes involving highly hazardous and corrosive materials. The synthesis of nitroguanidine (NQ), an energetic material, was characterized and optimized as a model for hazardous reactions. The contactless, flexible, and real-time analysis in this environment was implemented using a clip-on adapter for a Raman probe downstream of the microflow reactor. title: Engineered probiotic biointerfaces: Construction principles, microscopic characterisation and biomedical functions
abstract: Engineered probiotic biointerfaces are the dynamic boundaries through which modified bacteria interact with their biological surroundings. They can improve bacterial survival, mucosal retention and therapeutic delivery, but the structural basis of these effects is often unclear. This review groups biointerfaces by their dominant role: barrier protection, recognition, responsiveness, interaction and renewal by living cells. title: How Socio-Cultural Structures Shape Strategies of Climate-Resilient Social Protection Pathways in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
abstract: Low-income households in Sub-Saharan Africa have limited resilience to climate change shocks despite the region's unique socio-cultural support structures. This article explores how socio-cultural structures such as gender norms, social networks, social cohesion, trust, indigenous knowledge, customs and traditions, and cultural values of reciprocity shape climate-resilient social protection pathways among low-income households. abstract: This study analyses the free vibration and thermal buckling of size-dependent, axially functionally graded Euler–Bernoulli nanobeams using a nonlocal thermo-elastic Fredholm integral model based on Eringen’s nonlocal elasticity. title: Weak and inconsistent associations between birch-feeding insects and pollution levels around two industrial towns during substantial emission decline (1988–2025)
abstract: Industrial emissions have historically altered terrestrial ecosystems, but their long-term effects on insect herbivores remain insufficiently understood, particularly during ecosystem recovery following emission decline. We analysed a dataset on the densities of 24 Recognisable Taxonomic Units (RTUs) of birch-feeding insects collected from 1988 to 2025 around two industrial towns in northwestern Russia previously identified as pollution hotspots. title: Aridity-driven shifts in plant–microbial diversity relationships across the arid and semi-arid grasslands of northern China
abstract: Abstract Climate change-driven aridification threatens above- and belowground biodiversity, yet how the relationships between plant diversity and soil microbial diversity change along aridity gradients remains unclear. Here, we conducted a 4,000-km field survey across arid and semi-arid grasslands in northern China. We show that soil conditions, plant diversity, and microbial diversity exhibit sequential threshold responses along the aridity gradient. title: Environmental Factors' Effect on Alpha and Beta Diversity of Butterflies in North‐East Algerian Forests
abstract: ABSTRACT The specific factors determining butterfly alpha and beta diversity in Algerian forests remain insufficiently understood; not a single study has yet addressed this issue. Most previous studies in the region have exclusively focused on richness and abundance without evaluating how environmental variables shape community diversity. To address this knowledge gap, we conducted a field survey from May 2019 to March 2021 across three forest massifs in North‐east Algeria. title: SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in Long COVID: an exploratory randomized phase 2a mechanistic trial
abstract: Abstract Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 has been proposed as a biological driver of Long COVID, a disabling chronic illness with no proven treatments. We conducted an exploratory, placebo-controlled, double-blind, 2:1 randomized mechanistic trial (NCT05877508) of the SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in 36 participants who met the World Health Organization case definition of Long COVID. title: Assessing Trust in Community Science Data From Multiple Perspectives to Understand System-Level Impacts
abstract: Despite advancements in the field, generation of community science data exceeds its application. To better understand what shapes data use at a system level, we examine perceptions of data quality and trust in data usage from the perspectives of volunteers and professionals by leveraging a community wildlife monitoring program. We surveyed 486 volunteers on their perceptions of the data before and after participation. title: Functional–Taxonomic Scaling Resolves Conflicting Average Genome Size Estimates Across Environmental Gradients
abstract: Community-level average genome size (AGS) is a key trait linking microbial diversity, functional potential, and eco-evolutionary strategy, yet estimates of AGS diverge markedly among common methods. Here, we introduce and validate a framework that adjudicates conflicting AGS estimates by testing which estimate yields a gap between scaled functional diversity and scaled taxonomic diversity that is consistent with the expected positive association between genome size and gene functional breadth. title: 32-bit SPI interface design between Texas Instruments MCU and Intel FPGA enabling real-time intelligent control applications
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) communication system between a Texas Instruments TMS320F28335 Microcontroller Unit (MCU) and an Intel Altera Cyclone V 5CSEMA5F31C6N Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). The system demonstrates high-speed, reliable, full-duplex communication between heterogeneous processing platforms for real-time intelligent control and embedded system applications. abstract: Purpose: This study examines the relationships between professionalism, mindfulness, and job satisfaction among airline pilots and explores the mediating role of mindfulness in the relationship between professionalism and job satisfaction. Design/methodology/approach: The study employs a quantitative survey design. The sample consists of 171 airline pilots. title: Soil-plant-animal properties and microbial reassembly distinguish cattle oral disease prevalence across converted Amazon pasture systems
abstract: Forest-to-pasture conversion can alter soil properties, forage composition, and microbial communities, but whether these changes are associated with bovine periodontitis remains unclear. We compared eight pasture systems in the Western Brazilian Amazon classified by high or low herd-level prevalence of periodontal lesions. title: Thermostability and pH Differentiation in Geobacillus Hydrolases: A Comparative Perspective
abstract: Thermostable enzymes are central to high-temperature industrial processes because they combine catalytic efficiency with structural resilience under demanding conditions. Among thermophilic bacteria, Geobacillus has emerged as a prominent source of industrially relevant enzymes, particularly hydrolases such as proteases, lipases, and carbohydrate-active enzymes. title: Genetic diversity in soybean [ Glycine max ( L .) Merr.] genotypes based on agro‐morphological traits using univariate and multivariate statistical techniques
abstract: Abstract Soybean [ Glycine max (L.) Merr.] is a versatile leguminous crop that plays a vital role in biodiesel production, livestock feed, and enhancing global food security. Soybean production and productivity in Ethiopia are low compared to the national potential, mainly due to the lack of high‐yielding genotypes. Substantial genetic variability is essential for developing high‐yielding, climate‐resilient soybean varieties. title: Infant-caregiver vocal contingency changes across varying interpersonal space
abstract: Vocal contingency between caregivers and infants is a fundamental building block for socio-communicative development. This paper investigates vocal contingency in home settings and how it varies as a function of the physical distance between infants and their caregivers. We recorded 61 mother-infant dyads when infants were 5-14 months old during long-form home recording sessions (M = 7.2 h; SD = 2.3; Range = 1-13), using wearable audio and proximity sensors. title: Nocturnal Lepidoptera Larvae in Mega‐Project: Habitat and Environmental Factors Over Construction Effects
abstract: Mega-projects are large-scale developments that profoundly transform landscapes while delivering infrastructure and socio-economic benefits. However, they are also major drivers of biodiversity loss through multiple direct and indirect impacts. Among these, artificial light at night (ALAN) is increasingly recognised as a threat to biodiversity, including nocturnal Lepidoptera, which play crucial ecological roles. title: Sentinel-2 NDVI as an indicator of apple orchard yield
abstract: Satellite data is increasingly being used as a basis for operational crop monitoring. However, satellite technologies for monitoring perennial crops remain underdeveloped. The aim of this study was to assess the relationship between apple yield and NDVI calculated using all available Sentinel-2 data for the growing seasons (March-November) from 2017 to 2024. abstract: ABSTRACT Visible/near‐infrared (Vis/NIR) spectroscopy offers a promising non‐destructive technique for assessing round eggplant ( Solanum melongena var. esculentum ) quality. For the purple‐black round eggplant samples examined here, however, dark pericarp coloration and multi‐layered tissue structure limit light penetration and accurate internal evaluation. abstract: Abstract We report on observations of the O I 6300 Å and O I 5577 Å nightglow using a wide‐field imaging spectrograph during geomagnetic quiet times from mid‐latitudes. title: Comparative Genomic Analysis Exposes Conserved Antimicrobial Resistance Elements and Diverse Secretion Systems in Serratia proteamaculans
abstract: Serratia proteamaculans is an environmentally widespread member of the genus Serratia isolated from aquatic animals, food products, plants, insects, environmental habitats and clinical sources. Ecologically broadly distributed, little is known about its genomic diversity and factors associated with antimicrobial resistance and virulence. The present study reports a comparative genomic analysis of 38 publicly available S. proteamaculans genomes to explore genomic diversity, antimicrobial resistance determinants, integrons, and bacterial secretion systems. title: Occupational branches of Japan’s ruling party: building linkages while hedging clientelist exposure
abstract: Abstract Reassessing the underappreciated grassroots of Japan’s Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), I argue that the party’s localized institutions not only mobilize votes but also mitigate the risks of clientelism. Informed by field research and relying on documentary evidence, descriptive statistics, and financial records, I identify mechanisms that link the party to citizens, even in the periphery. Such mechanisms have received too little scholarly attention due to persisting notions that membership in the LDP is spurious and that the party’s local linkages are weak or narrowly transactional. title: Brechas de interoperabilidad y adopción de salud digital en los establecimientos sanitarios del Perú
abstract: The digital transformation of the Peruvian healthcare system faces challenges relating to interoperability, infrastructure, connectivity and training, which limit the secure and timely exchange of clinical information. The coexistence of incompatible platforms between the Ministry of Health (MINSA), EsSalud, the Armed Forces, the National Police and the private sector fragments care, hinders longitudinal patient follow-up and contributes to the duplication of tests, diagnostic delays, clinical errors and administrative overload. title: Exploring factors influencing the use of internet in the household by women small-scale farmers in rural South Africa: evidence from GHS 2019
abstract: This study adds to the empirical evidence of information and communication technology (ICT) use by women smallholder farmers in South Africa. The study draws on quantitative data collected by Statistics South Africa. The General Household Survey (GHS) for 2019 was manipulated to meet study objectives. The GHS questionnaire was used to sample households, and special attention was given to women farmers who have access to buyers of agricultural products through internet access in the household. title: An intelligent real-time intrusion detection and prevention strategy for emergency response MANETs
abstract: Abstract In recent years, Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs) have emerged as a pivotal domain within wireless technologies. Emergency Response MANETs (ER-MANETs) support communication among emergency responders during critical scenarios. Ensuring the real-time integrity and availability of these highly dynamic networks requires robust security measures beyond traditional approaches. title: Grid-Connected PV Carport Feasibility at a University Campus: Techno-Economic and Environmental Assessment with 3D Near-Shading Analysis
abstract: Despite growing institutional interest in solar carports as land-efficient alternatives to ground-mounted photovoltaics, existing feasibility studies rarely combine zone-resolved three-dimensional near-shading modelling with comprehensive techno-economic and environmental assessment, particularly in developing-economy contexts marked by tariff volatility and fossil-fuel import dependency. title: Development and validation of a simple impulse-based method for inductor design in electromagnetically driven tools for high-speed material processing
abstract: Electromagnetically driven tools offer a promising way to accelerate conventional tools to high speeds in order to take advantage of the beneficial effects of high strain rates in material processing. However, the systematic design of inductors for such systems is still largely based on time-consuming coupled multiphysics simulations, which hinders industrial implementation. title: Overwintering Strategies Drive Climate Change Impacts on Body Mass in Northern Mammals
abstract: Climate change drives variable shifts in mammalian body sizes, yet the mechanisms underlying this variation remain unclear. Two explanations prevail: (1) higher temperatures reduce thermal constraints, favouring smaller bodies; or (2) warming enhances primary productivity, supporting larger bodies. We propose that species' overwintering strategies, which mitigate exposure to winter temperatures, determine which mechanism predominates. title: Optimization of ultrasonication-assisted decellularization of porcine liver for biomimetic scaffold fabrication
abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM)-based hydrogels in previous research demonstrated as promising biomimetic scaffolds. However, conventional decellularization protocols are commonly based on harsh detergents that disrupt ECM integrity. While milder detergents such as sodium lauryl ether sulfate (SLES) and physical methods like ultrasonication have been proposed to reduce these negative effects, their combined application and the influence of ultrasonication parameters remain insufficiently explored. title: Comparing wolf feeding ecology between historical ranges and recently colonized human-dominated lowlands
abstract: The recent spread of wolves into highly human-modified landscapes in Europe is an important example of large carnivore recovery and illustrates their ability to live in environments very different from those usually considered suitable for the species. This study aimed to evaluate how wolf feeding habits vary over time and across space by comparing diet composition, trophic niche breadth, and key prey consumption between the historical Apennine range and the recently colonized Po Plain in north-western Italy, based on scat samples collected between 2021 and 2025. title: Contextual Microplastic Impacts on Croplands From Field Trials and Global Synthesis
abstract: Microplastic accumulation is an increasingly widespread anthropogenic disturbance in agricultural soils, yet ecological risk assessments remain dominated by simplified laboratory assays that may not capture context-dependent responses under field conditions. Here, we combined a five-year experiment across four semi-arid cropland sites with a global synthesis restricted exclusively to outdoor field observations to quantify microplastic effects on crop yield, soil quality, and ecosystem multifunctionality. title: A Comprehensive Definition of the Archetype 1
abstract: Abstract Fifteen years of theorizing on the archetype has led me to a working definition that I contend not only clarifies what an archetype is and how it works but helps to sharpen a number of clinical and practical processes as I hope to show. The definition I propose is amenable to empirical inquiry, falsification, and modification, it pulls together many threads of thought on the archetype and helps, I argue, to eliminate the conceptual confusion that has plagued archetype theory. title: Spatial and Temporal Scale Sensitivity in NDVI-Based Greenness Exposure Assessment for Alzheimer’s Disease Incidence: A Miami-Dade County Medicare Cohort Study
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a leading cause of dementia, and neighborhood greenness may represent a protective environmental exposure. However, greenness-health associations may depend on how vegetation exposure is defined across spatial and temporal scales. We examined the influence of the modifiable areal unit problem (MAUP) and modifiable temporal unit problem (MTUP) on associations between Landsat-derived Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and incident AD among Medicare beneficiaries in Miami-Dade County, Florida. title: Behavior in asymmetric dominance pairings predicts physiology, neural response, and neurogenesis in a social cichlid fish
abstract: Introduction In a social dominance hierarchy, dominant and subordinate individuals can exhibit dramatic differences in behavioral, physiological, and neural phenotypes. Juveniles often also form social dominance hierarchies, but it is less explored how these hierarchies reflect, or are distinct from, those exhibited by adults. Methods In the present study, we housed juvenile social cichlid Astatotilapia burtoni for one week in an asymmetric size pairing. title: Courage, Passion, Fun and Recreational Flow Experience in University Students Studying Catamaran and Windsurfing
abstract: Catamaran sailing and windsurfing are nature-based sports that require physical risk-taking, balance, attention, and endurance. Participation in these activities may contribute not only to physical skill development but also to psychological experiences such as courage, passion, pleasure/fun, and flow. This study aimed to examine how these psychological experiences are shaped among university students receiving catamaran and windsurfing training and to determine the relationships among courage, passion, pleasure/fun, and recreational flow experience. title: Seroprevalence and the determinants of lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV) in cattle reared under smallholder production systems in northwestern Bangladesh
abstract: Lumpy skin disease (LSD) is a vector-borne transboundary disease that causes substantial productivity losses in cattle. This study was undertaken to determine the seroprevalence of LSD and the associated determinants of non-vaccinated cattle reared in smallholder production systems of northwestern Bangladesh. A cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2024 to January 2025 covering ten districts where a total of 450 non-vaccinated cattle were sampled across 100 smallholder farms. title: Phenology and Morphometric Parameters of Spiraea cantoniensis Lour. as Indicators of Climate Change in Urban Ecosystems
abstract: Abstract The identification of phenological patterns and morphological changes in Spiraea cantoniensis Lour. in urban ecosystems is essential for the optimal selection of taxa. Given that changes in vegetation dynamics are strongly associated with variability in climatic patterns, this study employed the extended BBCH scale, accumulated heat sums, and circular statistical methods to analyse phenological patterns, together with morphometric analyses of inflorescences, flowers, and fruits. title: QGIS-Based Mapping and Quantification of Riparian Bamboo as a Nature-Based Strategy for Erosion Control and Flood Resilience in Doña Remedios Trinidad, Bulacan
abstract: Riparian bamboo usually grows along rivers and is recognized for its effectiveness in controlling and managing erosion because of its strong root systems, which enhance flood control. In this study, the riparian bamboo identified and mapped was kawayan tinik (Bambusa blumeana). However, there is still limited information on its occurrence pattern in Doña Remedios Trinidad (DRT), Bulacan. journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews

title: The pattern of revisionist strategy: From Cyprus to Ukraine
abstract: Drawing on Türkiye’s illegal military invasion of the independent island Republic of Cyprus and occupation of Cypriot territory, classic strategic theory, and empirical war studies, this article delineates a pattern of revisionist strategy. Within this framework, an aggressor state alters existing borders and the regional balance of power through the erosion of sovereignty and incremental territorial annexation. title: Stage-specific shifts in bacterial and fungal amplicon profiles of garlic bulbs during cold storage
abstract: Garlic bulbs can remain externally intact while microbial and tissue changes develop during cold storage, so endpoint inspection may miss distinct intermediate states. We characterized cold-stored garlic across four storage stages by combining bacterial 16S rRNA gene and fungal internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon sequencing with culture, quantitative PCR (qPCR), photography, and cryo-scanning electron microscopy. title: iDNA-based mammal survey in the last large refuge of the giant armadillo in the Atlantic Forest
abstract: Abstract Sampling mammal diversity is effort-demanding in hyperdiverse biomes, such as the Atlantic Forest. Molecular tools for rapid biodiversity assessment, such as invertebrate-derived DNA (iDNA) metabarcoding, have emerged as promising approaches to complement traditional survey methods. Here, we assessed mammal diversity in a large Atlantic Forest remnant, Rio Doce State Park (PERD) in Minas Gerais state-Brazil, using iDNA metabarcoding from mosquitoes and flies during a short-term sampling effort. title: INVESTIGATION OF THE PARAMETERS OF A HYBRID WIND–SOLAR POWER PLANT FOR ENERGY SUPPLY OF REMOTE AUTONOMOUS CONSUMERS
abstract: This study investigates the operating parameters of a hybrid wind–solar power plant for autonomous electricity supply in the sharply continental climate of central Kazakhstan. The plant consisted of a 600 W wind turbine, four 200 W photovoltaic panels, a 12 V battery and a charge controller, the load being separated between alternating-current and direct-current circuits. Field measurements were carried out continuously during 2025 near Karaganda. title: Strategies for sustainable crop production in the Yangtze River Basin of China: insights from field experiments and farm surveys
abstract: Introduction Rice-based cropping systems in the Yangtze River Basin of China are diverse. Objectives However, most previous studies have focused primarily on improving the yield, resource use efficiency, or reducing the carbon emissions of individual systems, with few comprehensive comparisons across different systems. title: Field‐Driven Active Colloids as Distributed Micromachines: Bridging Physics, Control, and Function Across Length Scales
abstract: Field-driven active colloids offer a route to microscale machines whose behavior can be programmed by external electric and magnetic fields. At the micron scale, thermal fluctuations, hydrodynamic interactions, interparticle forces, and field-mediated actuation combine to connect active matter physics with control and function. title: Effects of DEM Resolution on Hectare‐Scale Potential Soil Loss Modelling: A Case Study Using a Spatially Distributed Erosion Model
abstract: ABSTRACT Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are essential in estimating soil erosion, yet the influence of DEM spatial resolution on model outputs remains uncertain, particularly at the scale of individual fields. This study investigates how raster cell size affects soil erosion estimates using a physical‐statistical soil erosion model (PSSEM) on a 2.8‐km 2 agricultural area in Northern England. abstract: ABSTRACT Changes in climate conditions and land‐use patterns exert significant influences on hydrological processes in agriculture‐dominated watersheds, with direct implications for regional water and food security. Although afforestation has been implemented in many agriculture‐dominated watersheds in the United States, the response of key hydrological processes to afforestation under future climate conditions remains poorly understood. title: Navigating global health futures under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
abstract: The Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) provide valuable insights to understand how future socioeconomic changes could alter the magnitude and pattern of climate-related risks across sectors, which might facilitate or hinder adaptation and mitigation responses. Many sectors have created SSP narrative extensions to specify insights for their domains. title: Cancer incidence in the Ecuadorian Amazon: A retrospective study (1990–2019)
abstract: BACKGROUND: There is a scarcity of cancer studies in the Amazon region. This study aimed to analyse trends in cancer incidence within the Ecuadorian Amazon between 1990 and 2019, identifying the most prevalent cancer types and assessing their provincial and temporal distribution. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted using data from the Quito population-based cancer registry, focusing on patients whose habitual residence was in the Amazonian provinces of Sucumbíos, Orellana, Napo, and Pastaza. title: Brand Matters: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Quality, Reputation, Pricing and Advertising on Generation Z's Purchase Decisions for Nike Footwear in Kathmandu Valley
abstract: Background: Nike has established itself as a globally recognized athletic and lifestyle brand, and its footwear enjoys strong appeal among Generation Z consumers even in emerging markets such as Nepal, where the brand maintains no official retail presence. In Kathmandu Valley, Nike's market standing is sustained largely through imported product quality, brand reputation, and exposure to global advertising, yet little empirical research has examined how these brand-related factors, together with pricing and brand loyalty, jointly shape Gen Z's purchase decisions in this context. title: Mapping multi-hazard flood and drought risk in a rapidly growing region: A ward-level assessment in the Bengaluru metropolitan region, India
abstract: A B S T R A C T Hydrological extremes, such as floods and droughts are becoming increasingly frequent and severe under the influence of climate change, with rapidly urbanizing regions like South Asia facing particularly high risks. Moreover, the occurrence of these extremes is becoming more common, amplifying their overall impact through compounding effects. title: Comparative Google Earth Engine Workflows for Flood and Landslide Diagnostics in Lower Silesia, Poland, and Batang Kali, Malaysia
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates Google Earth Engine (GEE) as the central computational environment for a unified, repeatable workflow for post-event geospatial diagnostics of two contrasting natural hazards: the September 2024 flood in Lower Silesia, Poland, and the December 2022 Batang Kali landslide in Selangor, Malaysia. Both cases followed the same analytical sequence: pre-event and post-event image selection, generation of a continuous change layer, threshold-based binary mask extraction, z-score standardization of change magnitude, point-based validation, and cartographic export. title: Tree-microbe-soil interactions affecting soil organic carbon fractions in Mediterranean forest soils
abstract: Abstract. Soil organic carbon (SOC) represents a major terrestrial carbon pool, yet the processes that regulate its storage remain uncertain, particularly in water-limited ecosystems. The behavior of SOC is informed by partitioning into mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC), considered more persistent, and particulate organic carbon (POC), which is more labile. abstract: This paper proposes a scheme for the statistical confidence interval inference of a subsurface electrical resistivity model in magnetotellurics and geomagnetic depth soundings. The method assesses the confidence interval of resistivity for a target block in optimal model obtained through inversion. title: Integrative analyses revealed the domestication history, genomic targets of breeding and the spatiotemporal expression patterns of fruit traits in Chinese bayberry ( Myrica rubra )
abstract: Abstract he Chinese bayberry (Myrica rubra) is an important fruit crop in southern China with a domestication history longer than 3000 years. It is the only domesticated fruit crop in the family Myricaceae. In this study, we sequenced genomes of more than 200 wild and cultivated individuals and proposed that M. rubra diverged firstly in Northeast Asia before spreading from southwest to southeast China where the primary domestication occurred. title: Determination of Certain Physicochemical Properties of Olive Oils Under Different Storage Conditions
abstract: Olive oil is a widely consumed vegetable oil known for its health-promoting properties. Unlike most other vegetable oils, it is obtained directly from the fruit and produced entirely through physical processes without chemical treatment, allowing it to be consumed in its natural form while preserving its vitamins, essential fatty acids, and other bioactive compounds. title: A self-assembled Dendrobium polysaccharide hydrogel with anti-aging activity via the FOXO signaling pathway
abstract: Faced with the complexity and diversity of skin aging, it is critical to investigate multi-target synergistic anti-aging products. Herein, a novel composite hydrogel with anti-aging activity was developed based on Dendrobium polysaccharide, hyaluronic acid (HA), and nicotinamide (NMN). title: SW1D: A Python package for seismic surface wave solutions in 1-D elastic media
abstract: We present SW1D, a Python version of a legacy code for the forward computation of Rayleigh and Love wave dispersion curves as well as synthetic seismograms, in elastic, isotropic, laterally homogeneous media. This code solves the surface wave eigenvalue problem for 1-D media using a propagator-matrix technique and subsequently obtains surface wave excitations, in the frequency domain, for a point source described by its moment tensor. title: Resummation-scale uncertainties in PDF determinations
abstract: We investigate the impact of resummation-scale variations on parton distribution function (PDF) determinations. These variations introduce an additional source of theoretical uncertainty related to the evolution of PDFs and strong coupling $α_s$ that has never previously been accounted for in PDF fits. Using the open-source xFitter framework, we quantify this uncertainty in fits to HERA deep-inelastic scattering data and examine its implications for predictions of top-quark pair production at the LHC. title: Phoenix: A Modular and Versatile Framework for C/C++ Pointer Analysis
abstract: We present Phoenix, a modular pointer analysis framework for C/C++ that unifies multiple alias analysis algorithms behind a single, stable interface. Phoenix addresses the fragmentation of today’s C/C++ pointer analysis ecosystem by cleanly separating IR construction, constraint generation, solver backends, and client-facing queries—making analyses easy to compare, swap, and compose while exposing explicit precision–performance trade-offs. title: Estimating High-Energy Neutrino Effective Areas from Muon Propagation
abstract: Neutrino telescopes observe neutrinos through the muons produced by charged-current interactions. Most of those muons are born kilometers outside the detector, and how much energy they lose on the way is stochastic. We show that we can compute analytically the distance a muon travels before it falls below the detection threshold, while describing the statistical properties of its losses. title: The LZ event with a two-state dark matter halo
abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported a single nuclear-recoil candidate at $E_R \simeq 248$keV. LZ interprets it in terms of inelastic dark matter that scatters endothermically from its ground state, $χ_1 N \to χ_2 N$. title: Design and Validation of an Antagonistic Tendon-Driven Dexterous Robotic Hand with Bidirectional Operation
abstract: Dexterous robotic hands typically reproduce human hand morphology but inherit its one-sided grasping workspace, requiring wrist or arm reorientation to grasp from the opposite side. Existing reversible hands generally rely on non-anthropomorphic, soft, or task-specific finger arrangements, whereas conventional five-digit anthropomorphic hands remain designed primarily for palmar-side grasping. title: Life-time patterns of reinfections: epidemic cohorts as traveling waves
abstract: Infectious disease models that allow for reinfection, such as the SIS or SIRS frameworks, typically treat all infections as exchangeable and independent, erasing the temporal structure of individual reinfection histories. Here, we introduce a minimal "chain SIR" model that resolves this limitation by indexing compartments by reinfection count and allowing transmission, recovery, and waning rates to depend on that count. abstract: Heterogeneous high--performance computing architectures expose numerical algorithms to perturbations arising from the non--associativity of floating--point arithmetic. title: Nucleon parton distribution functions from boosted correlations in the Coulomb gauge
abstract: A bstract Recently, a novel approach has been proposed to compute parton distributions through the use of boosted correlators fixed in the Coulomb gauge from lattice QCD, within the framework of Large-Momentum Effective Theory (LaMET). This approach circumvents the need for Wilson lines, potentially enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of lattice calculations. title: Safe Hypergraph Contraction via Capacity-Aware Repair Certificates
abstract: Multilevel partitioners shrink circuit hypergraphs through vertex contractions, yet a contraction that satisfies block capacity can still eliminate every optimal balanced bipartition. We develop certified safe coarsening (CSC) to identify contractions that preserve an optimum without computing that optimum.
